name: timer1_counted_delay_using_0a56
comment:
Stores R7 into XDATA 0x0A56 as a loop counter, clears bit 0 of 0x8E and of 0xAB, and calls 0x05E8. Per counter value it calls 0x0EE8, then spins until bit 7 of 0x8F is set (jnb 0x8F branches back on itself), clears bit 0 of 0x8E and bit 7 of 0x8F, decrements 0x0A56 and repeats; on reaching zero it calls 0x05EF and sets bit 3 of 0xAB. 0x8E/0x8F/0xAB are TCON.6/TF1, TCON.7 and IE.3, i.e. TR1/TF1/ET1, so this is a counted wait on Timer 1 overflow. The count's time units are not decoded.

(An earlier reading of this comment said "a stock 8051 places TC1 at 0x8E and TF1 at 0x8F". That is wrong and is left here because the function's own name already contradicted it: TCON is at 0x88, so 0x8E is TCON.6 = TR1 and 0x8F is TCON.7 = TF1, exactly as Ghidra's C has it, and ec/tools/disasm8051.py's bit_name() says the same. TC1 is not an 8051 register at all.)

name: clear_4c_bits_4_5_7
comment: Clears bits 4, 5 and 7 of the direct internal byte 0x4C: it loads 0x4C into A, applies ANL #0xEF, then ANL #0xDF, then ANL #0xBF, writing the accumulator back to 0x4C after each pass. The decompiled C folds the three passes into one AND with 0x8F, which is the same result. No other address is touched.

name: event_id_latch_and_bit_merge
comment: Stores R7 to XDATA 0x0A49, then on a two-call countdown at internal byte 0x90 copies internal byte (0x97 + 0x0A49) into 0x91 when that byte is 0, 3 or 4. It next branches on bit 0 of internal 0x8F, on internal 0x85, and on bits 0-2 of XDATA 0x1304: one arm stores the return of 0x3C0A in internal 0x8B and 0x33 in 0xAD, another ORs a byte fetched through 0x3B4E into XDATA 0x1304 at each of internal 0x88-0x8A whose bit 6 is set, and a third does the same over three code-pointer entries when 0x0A49 is 0, writing 0x17 through 0x3B22 and 0x3B3E. The listing ends in a call to 0x2BC1 with no ret, so what follows is not decoded here.

name: call_3894_then_jmp_2de3
comment: Calls 0x3894 and then, once that returns, jumps unconditionally to 0x2DE3. There is no ret in the listing, so whether 0x2DE3 returns for this entry or is itself a jump out is not shown, and neither callee is decoded here.

name: cascade_gate_170a_1709_1708
comment: Tests bit 3 of XDATA 0x170A, then of 0x1709, then of 0x1708, in that order, and on the first one set requires bit 2 of XDATA 0x1106 to be set, bit 2 of 0x1102 to be clear, and the matching cell 0x1702, 0x1701 or 0x1700 to equal 0x17 before calling 0x012F, 0x018C or 0x029B. On a match it sets R7 to 1; otherwise it returns with R7 at the 0 it was given on entry. The decompiled C keeps the same tests but omits every R7 = 1 write and drops the tiering, so the .asm is the reading used here.

name: write_10_2007_clear_1302_set_1300
comment: Writes 0x10 to XDATA 0x2007, executes eight NOPs, clears XDATA 0x1302 and writes 0x48 to XDATA 0x1300, then returns. The eight 0x00 bytes are real NOPs in the listing rather than padding this tool inserted. Nothing here identifies any of the three addresses.

name: stage_and_commit_0a56_block
comment: Stages R7, R5 and R3 into XDATA 0x0A56, 0x0A57 and 0x0A58, sets 0x0A5E to 0xEE, and clears 0x0A60 and the direct internal byte 0xAF, then branches to 0x451A when bit 7 of 0x0A57 is clear. Otherwise it clears that bit and pushes the values at 0x0A58 and 0x0A59 through the callee pairs 0x4AB8/0x4A69 and 0x4AEF/0x4A69, storing R7 back through DPTR each time, and when 0x0A5C is non-zero it additionally calls 0x4725 on bytes fetched by 0x4B44 with R6 as DPTR's high byte. When 0x0A57 equals 0x0C it repeats the fetch with DPTR incremented once and passes the result through 0x4B0F and 0x4A69. The listing stops at an sjmp to 0x4534 and the decompiled C continues far past that, so only the bytes here are described.

name: stage_0a54_0a55_then_dispatch
comment: Writes R5 to XDATA 0x0A54 and R3 to 0x0A55, then exchanges R1 through the accumulator twice so R1 ends up holding the caller's R7 while R3 is cleared. If that value is 0xFF it sets R7 to 0 and returns; otherwise it calls 0x4A76 and then 0x4A4D, which the decompiled C marks as not returning. The C reads the 0xFF test as a separate third parameter compared against the entry value, which the instruction sequence does not support.

name: dec_a_store_and_advance_dptr
comment: Three instructions: decrements the accumulator, stores it through the current DPTR into XDATA, then increments DPTR by one. The listing has no ret and its own header calls the boundary a hypothesis, so whether the routine continues at 0x4B21 is not shown; the decompiled C's call to a 16-bit add helper appears nowhere in these bytes.

name: stage_009a_dispatch_to_4bb0
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x009A and calls 0x05E8, then loads R4 with 0x4B and R5 with 0xB0 with A and R7 cleared and calls 0x1636 -- R4:R5 read as a big-endian CODE address is 0x4BB0, which is the very address it calls next after eight NOPs. It finishes with 0x4BB0 and a call to 0x05EF. Nothing in this listing says what 0x05E8, 0x1636 or 0x4BB0 do.

name: dispatch_to_4c5d
comment: Calls 0x05E8, then loads R4 with 0x4C and R5 with 0x5D with A and R7 cleared and calls 0x1636, then after eight NOPs calls 0x4C5D, the address that R4:R5 forms, and finishes with 0x05EF. It reads and writes no XDATA of its own. The same build-an-address-in-R4:R5-then-call-it shape is at 0x530E, 0x537F, 0x53AF, 0x541D, 0x549B and 0x54C2.

name: stage_0094_block_dispatch_4d96
comment: Writes R5 to XDATA 0x0094, R3 to 0x0095 and R7 to 0x0098, and copies XDATA 0x0A59 into 0x0096. It then calls 0x05E8, sets R4 to 0x4D and R5 to 0x96 and calls 0x1636, calls 0x4D96 -- the address that pair forms -- after eight NOPs, and finishes with 0x05EF. It has no branch: unlike 0x53AF there is a single target.

name: stage_009b_block_branch_dispatch
comment: Writes R6 and R7 to XDATA 0x009B and 0x009C, R5 and R3 to 0x0094 and 0x0095, and copies 0x0A5A into 0x0096, then calls 0x05E8. It picks one of three targets from 0x009D and 0x009E: 0x009D equal to 0xBF together with 0x009E equal to 0x01 takes 0x50DE, 0x009D equal to 0xBF alone takes 0x4FED, and any other 0x009D takes 0x4F3E. Each path calls 0x1636 with the matching R4:R5 address and then calls that address after eight NOPs, and all three rejoin at 0x05EF.

name: stage_009b_block_dispatch_51c8

The three-way target selection its sibling 0x53AF performs is absent; there is one target and no branch.

name: default_009d_bf_dispatch_4e2c
comment: If XDATA 0x009F is zero it writes 0xBF to 0x009D, then calls 0x05E8, loads R4 with 0x4E and R5 with 0x2C and calls 0x1636, calls 0x4E2C after eight NOPs, and finishes with 0x05EF. 0x009D is the same byte 0x53AF tests against 0xBF, and this routine is the one place in these listings that supplies that value; that is an observation about the two listings side by side, not a traced call from one to the other.

comment: Calls 0x05E8, loads R4 with 0x4E and R5 with 0xCD and calls 0x1636, calls 0x4ECD after eight NOPs, and finishes with 0x05EF, reading and writing no XDATA of its own. It is the shape of 0x5349 with a different address pair.

name: read_byte_by_tag_r3
comment: A two-arm dispatch on R3: when R3 is 0xFE it returns the XDATA byte at the address R1 points to via `movx A,@R1`, and otherwise it returns the CODE byte at the address in R2:R1 with the code index cleared. The decompiled C renders the first arm as an ordinary 16-bit pointer dereference, which is the same access here but hides that the two arms read different address spaces.

name: write_byte_by_tag_r3
comment: Dispatches on R3 and on the carry the caller left behind: R3=0x01 writes A to the XDATA address in R2:R1, carry set writes A to direct internal RAM at R1, and carry clear with R3=0xFE writes A to XDATA at R1, falling into the same ret, so a carry-clear R3 other than 0xFE writes nothing at all. The decompiled C reads the carry test as a second comparison against the same selector and so reports a write in the case that falls through here.

name: write_byte_offset_by_tag_r3
comment: The indexed form of the R3 and carry dispatch at 0x7049: R3=0x01 adds R1:R2 to the current DPTR and stores the saved A there in XDATA, carry set stores A in direct internal RAM at DPL+R1, and carry clear with R3=0xFE stores A in XDATA at DPL+R1. As at 0x7049 a carry-clear R3 other than 0xFE falls through to the ret and writes nothing. It saves the value in R0 before touching DPTR and restores it before the XDATA store.

name: normalize_sign_pair_4byte
comment: Clears the direct bit 0xD5, which is PSW bit 5, then when the top bit of R0 is set flips 0xD5 and computes a four-byte two's-complement negate of the quad R0:R1:R2:R3 with R0 most significant, as a subb chain through R3, R2, R1 and R0. It does the same for the quad whose top byte is R4, calling 0x7281 and then 0x71B9 before negating, and calls 0x71B9 alone when R4's top bit is clear. The listing ends on `jnb 0xd5`, so what the flag gates is not shown, and the representation of the two quads is not established by these bytes.

comment: Shared epilogue that cases 0x00 through 0x06 of the bank0 0x8038 table jump to: it calls 0xBB08 then writes 0x06 to XDATA 0x08E1 and post-increments the selector at 0x08E0 with 0x0822C-0x0822D before an ljmp to the default 0x8274. Only the listed bytes were read and the file claims no execution order

name: index_table_default
comment: Default arm of the bank0 0x8038 index dispatch: it decrements XDATA 0x08E1 and returns while that stays non-zero and when it is zero runs the longer body 0x827E-0x8293 which touches 0x1904 and 0x190C and calls 0xBCB1 before returning. The file says this is what the bytes decode to and not a claim that any of it executes

name: return_trampoline_8294
comment: A single RET. FUN_CODE_8294 ljmps here on both of its early-exit paths, the R7 > 6 reject at 0x829E and the R5 == 0 path at 0x833D, so it is that routine's shared return trampoline and not a routine in its own right.

name: ring_push_0990
comment: Reads the ring index at XDATA 0x09BF, zeroing it first if it has reached 0x2F, computes DPTR as 0x0990+index, stores R7 there, then increments the index and zeroes it again once it reaches 0x2F. The index therefore walks a 47-byte ring at XDATA 0x0990-0x09BE. The value left in A by the final subb/jc pair is not a stored result, so the decompiler's char return is a reading of those flags rather than of anything this routine returns.

name: sync_0788_and_07d4_from_09e9
comment: Returns at 0x849C immediately if XDATA 0x080F is non-zero or if 0xB9D8 returns non-zero. Otherwise it clears bit 6 of 0x07C5 and calls 0x163C with R5=0x85, copies 0x09E9 into 0x0788 and calls 0x163C with R5=0x83 when they differ, and -- only when bit 0 of 0x0743 (CTGP_DB_CTRL) is set -- copies 0x09EA and 0x09EB into 0x07D4 and 0x07D5, sets or clears bit 3 of 0x07C4 to follow bit 4, and calls 0x163C with R5=0x84, but only when bits 3 and 4 of 0x07C4 differ from each other or either byte of 0x07D4/0x07D5 differs from 0x09EA/0x09EB. 0x09E9, 0x09EA and 0x09EB have no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so what the copied values hold is not determined here.

name: return_trampoline_83ff
comment: A single RET, the early exit that FUN_CODE_83FF branches to from 0x8405, 0x840D, 0x843A and 0x8471. Nothing is read or written before it, so it is a return trampoline rather than a routine of its own.

name: clear_200b
comment: Loads A with 0, sets DPTR to XDATA 0x200B and issues movx @DPTR,A five times in a row. DPTR is never advanced, so all five stores land on the same byte 0x200B; the decompiled C shows a single assignment, which collapses the repeats but does not change the address written. 0x200B has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: seed_fan_table_base
comment: Seeds the fan-table CODE base as 0x60F2, a table of big-endian CODE pointer pairs from which the 0x888D handler copies; it is the routine called at 0xA828 inside the 0xA7C8 routine. The rest of this routine is not analysed in the file that establishes it

name: mode_tick_084c_07a5_09ee
comment: Calls 0xBE9C first: a zero result with XDATA 0x06E6 not equal to 1 zeroes 0x0780, sets PSW bits 0xD8 and 0xD9 and spins at 0x8761, while 0x06E6 equal to 1 tail-jumps to 0x8939. Otherwise it calls 0xB9D8 up to three times: on a zero result a non-zero 0x084C runs 0xDFDF and 0xE010, sets bit 5 of AP_OEM (0x0741) when both bytes of 0x0464/0x0465 and of 0x046C/0x046D are zero, and then decrements 0x084C; a non-zero result clears bit 5 of 0x0741, and a second non-zero result zeroes 0x1804, 0x0460, 0x0461, 0x0468, 0x0469, 0x075B, 0x1809, 0x085F and 0x0787 before returning. A later block compares CPU_TEMP (0x043E) against 0x51 and 0x5F and GPU_TEMP (0x044F) against 0x50 and 0x57 to set or clear bit 3 of 0x07A5, mirrors that bit into bit 0 of 0x09EE and calls 0xA73F with R7=0xBB when the two disagree, and the listing ends by calling 0x8653, 0xBB24 and ljmping to 0x893E with A=0x3C when 0x06C2 is non-zero. The .asm listing stops at 0x888A while the .c continues well past it, so the remainder of the decompiled body is not covered here.

name: fan_table_mailbox_handler
comment: Handler for the 0x0F5D-0x0F5F mailbox: requires 0x0F5D=0xFD and 0x0F5E=0xC9, reads table selector 0x0F5F (1 Turbo, 2 Gaming, 3 Office, the last chosen between two Office tables by 0x0782 bit 2) and copies 0x30 bytes from each of a CODE pointer pair to 0x0F00 and 0x0F30. The trigger found is explicit host request, and whether some other path also calls the copy is not something a site scan can rule out

name: store_200_via_dptr_then_8f09
comment: Two instructions: calls 0xBB22 and loads A with 200, then falls through into 0x893E, which stores A through the caller's DPTR and ljmps to 0x8F09. 0x8939 lies inside the range this repo lists for FUN_CODE_8931 (0x8931-0x8B11), so it is a byte-aligned entry inside that routine rather than one of its own; the single branch that reaches it in this shard, the ljmp at 0x8755, arrives with DPTR = 0x06E6, so the byte written is XDATA 0x06E6.

name: store_a_via_dptr_then_jump_8f09
comment: Two instructions: stores A to the XDATA byte the caller's DPTR addresses, then ljmps to 0x8F09, which is itself the three-instruction copy into XDATA 0x075C. 0x893E is inside FUN_CODE_8931's listed range (0x8931-0x8B11) and directly follows 0x8939, so both are entries into the middle of that routine. The address written is not decided by this listing; the only branch into 0x8939 in this shard supplies DPTR = 0x06E6.

name: ramp_1804_1809_toward_0461_0469
comment: Stores its incoming A into XDATA 0x0469, then picks a rate byte in R5 -- 3 by default, or 0x0787 masked with 0x7F when 0x0787 bit 7 and AP_OEM (0x0741) bit 0 are both set and those low seven bits are non-zero -- and copies either 0x0461 or 0x0469 into XDATA 0x0670, choosing between them on bit 7 of 0x0456 and the carry from 0xBBE6. It bounds 0x0670 against 0x0C and 0xE4, raises it to 0xA0 when it is below that and 0x0440 is zero, then leaves for 0x8DE0 unless bit 7 of 0x07C5, bit 0 of 0x0741 and bit 2 of 0x07C6 are all set. In that path it increments 0x070A, arms 0x0672 with 0x14 when 0x1804 is zero and 0x0461 is not, arms 0x0673 the same way for 0x1809 and 0x0469, and otherwise uses 0x0986 and 0x0989 as backoff bytes while stepping 0x1804 and 0x1809 by one per pass toward 0x0461 and 0x0469 with 0xC8 as the cap; every exit from those two ramps is an ljmp 0x8F03.

name: ramp_1804_toward_0670_and_set_1809
comment: First clamps XDATA 0x0670: a value of zero, or 0x3D and above, is written back as 0x3C, while 0x01-0x3C is left alone. If 0x1804 is zero and 0x0670 is not it arms 0x0672 with 0x14, and a non-zero 0x0672 sends the routine to 0xBEB4 and past the ramp; otherwise 0x0986 acts as a backoff byte, 0x070A is incremented, and 0x1804 moves one step toward 0x0670 with 0xC8 as the cap, but only on passes where 0x070A modulo the incoming R5 is zero. It then writes 0x1809 as either 0 or 0x1804-0x14, the choice made by a four-way comparison of XDATA 0x0460 and 0x0468 against 0x04 with 0x07 or 0x08 depending on bit 7 of MANUAL_FAN_CTRL (0x0751), and falls through into the separately listed 0x8F03.

name: call_bb28_on_1804
comment: Two instructions: loads DPTR with XDATA 0x1804 and calls 0xBB28. The decompiled C also has this entry copying 0x1804 into XDATA 0x075C, but no such store appears in the listing; it may be inside 0xBB28 or past this function's boundary, and this listing does not show which.

name: copy_dptr_byte_to_075c
comment: Three instructions: reads the XDATA byte the caller's DPTR addresses into A, points DPTR at XDATA 0x075C and writes A there. Nothing else is read or written. 0x075C is entered in ec/annotations/registers.yaml as MAIN_FAN_R_DUTY, the vendor's ADDR_EC_MAIN_FAN_R_DUTY_BYTE (issue #123); this copy is how a value reaches it, and the repo's 0x8939 row shows 200 arriving here on the fan-flat-out path.

name: return_trampoline
comment: A single RET. It is the target of the ljmp 0x8F0E at 0x89AB inside FUN_CODE_8931's listed range and of the branch the 0x8F20 chain takes when 0x0768 bit 2 is set, so it functions as a shared do-nothing exit. Nothing is read or written before it.

name: store_a_to_dptr_then_075c_and_notify
comment: Writes the incoming A through the caller's DPTR, reads that byte straight back, copies it into XDATA 0x075C, then calls 0xA73F with R7=0xA7 and again with R7=0x43 before returning. What the two 0xA73F command codes select is not decoded here. 0x075C is entered in ec/annotations/registers.yaml as MAIN_FAN_R_DUTY (issue #123), which also carries the 0x1804/0x1809 scratch bytes this routine copies between; 0xA73F has no entry there and is still open.

name: state_0817_dispatch
comment: If either byte of the 16-bit big-endian value at XDATA 0x081E/0x081F is non-zero it adds 0xFFFF to it through 0x70E4, and it then leaves for 0x8FDB unless bit 0 of 0x0815 is set. With that bit set it calls 0xC1B1 and, if R7 comes back non-zero, either exits at 0x9040 when 0x0817 is zero or clears 0x0817 and tail-calls 0xC2A2 and 0xC478. When R7 is zero it dispatches on 0x0817: value 0 requires 0x081E/0x081F to be zero, then writes 0x0A to 0x081F (0x28 instead when 0x0440 is zero), sets 0x0817 to 1 and jumps to 0xC48F; value 1 checks the same pair and jumps to 0x902A; value 2 calls 0xC349 and 0xC2AA, clears bit 0 of the byte at the DPTR that 0xBC14 leaves behind, and unless 0x073C is exactly 0x01 writes 0x02 to XDATA 0x0A59 and 0x00 to 0x0A5A, 0x0A5B and 0x0A5C before ljmping to 0x445E with R3=0x5A, R5=0x88 and R7=1. Any other 0x0817 value exits at 0x9040, and the listing ends at that ljmp.

name: state_0817_fallthrough
comment: Calls 0xC356; when R7 comes back non-zero and XDATA 0x06C5 is zero it exits at 0x9040 if 0x0817 is zero, otherwise clears 0x0817, calls 0xC48F and tail-jumps to 0xC2AA. Otherwise it dispatches on 0x0817: value 1 requires 0x081E/0x081F to be zero or it exits at 0x9040, and both 0 and 1 then fall into the shared block at 0x9031, which calls 0xC1BE, exits at 0x9040 if R7 is non-zero, and otherwise calls 0xC478 and 0xBC14 and sets bit 0 of the byte at the DPTR 0xBC14 leaves. Values of 2 and above reach 0x9031 only by falling through from the failed comparisons, and the listing ends at 0x903F. The .c orders these paths differently and adds writes to 0x081E, 0x081F and 0x0817 that are not in this listing.

name: ljmp_703d
comment: A single LJMP 0x703D. 0x9000 lies inside the range this repo lists for FUN_CODE_8FDB (0x8FDB-0x903F), so it is a byte-aligned entry inside that routine rather than a separate function, and no branch to it appears in the instructions listed for 0x8FDB. The decompiler renders it as a thunk to FUN_CODE_703D; 0x703D's own body is not in this listing and is not shown to be the routine the .c calls be16_add at 0x70E4.

name: read_dptr_byte
comment: A single MOVX A,@DPTR: reads the XDATA byte the caller left in DPTR into A. It is the head of the 'if the first byte is zero, read the next one' idiom that recurs at 0x8F22, 0x8F66, 0x8F93 and 0x9020, and it lies inside FUN_CODE_8FDB's listed range (0x8FDB-0x903F), so it is a byte-aligned entry within that routine. The timer-restart body the decompiled C attaches to it is not in this listing.

name: word_nonzero_check_tail
comment: Four instructions that complete the 16-bit non-zero test begun at 0x9006: if the byte already in A is non-zero it skips the reload, otherwise it advances DPTR and reads the next byte, and it branches to 0x9040 if that byte is non-zero too. Falling out of the listing at 0x900B therefore means both bytes read as zero. It lies inside FUN_CODE_8FDB's listed range, so it is a byte-aligned entry within that routine, and the writes the .c attaches to it are not in this listing.

name: clear_081e_after_c2a2
comment: Calls 0xC2A2, then loads DPTR with XDATA 0x081E, clears A and stores zero there. The listing ends there; the writes that follow it -- 0x081F = 0x14 and 0x0817 = 1 -- are the separately listed 0x9015, 0x9016 and 0x9018, which the decompiler folds into one body. 0x900D lies inside FUN_CODE_8FDB's listed range (0x8FDB-0x903F), making it a byte-aligned entry within that routine.

name: advance_dptr_to_081f
comment: A single INC DPTR. Entered with DPTR on XDATA 0x081E it advances DPTR to 0x081F, so that the movx @DPTR,A at 0x9018 lands on the low byte of the 16-bit value; it writes nothing itself. It lies inside FUN_CODE_8FDB's listed range (0x8FDB-0x903F) and is one of three single-instruction census entries inside the write sequence at 0x900D-0x9018, not a routine of its own.

name: load_constant_14
comment: A single MOV A,#0x14, loading the constant that the movx @DPTR,A at 0x9018 stores through the caller's DPTR. It writes nothing itself and lies inside FUN_CODE_8FDB's listed range (0x8FDB-0x903F), so it is a byte-aligned entry inside that routine's write sequence rather than a routine of its own.

name: store_14_then_select_0817
comment: Two instructions: writes A -- 0x14, as loaded at 0x9016 -- through the caller's DPTR, which the preceding sequence has advanced from 0x081E to 0x081F, then loads DPTR with XDATA 0x0817. The store of 1 into 0x0817 that the decompiled C shows in the same body is not in this listing, and 0x9018 is a byte-aligned entry inside FUN_CODE_8FDB's listed range (0x8FDB-0x903F) rather than a routine of its own.

name: write_1_to_dptr
comment: Two instructions: loads A with 0x01, writes it to XDATA at whatever address the caller left in DPTR, and returns. The listing never loads DPTR itself, so the destination is the caller's choice; the decompiled C's *param_1 is a pointer the decompiler invented, not a 8051 calling convention.

name: write_2_to_0817
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0817, loads A with 0x02 and writes that single byte to XDATA 0x0817. No read, no call, and no effect on any register the caller can see beyond DPTR. 0x0817 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: bare_ret_9040
comment: A single ret instruction. Nothing is read or written, and the accumulator, DPTR and carry are handed back exactly as the caller left them, so whether this is a deliberate no-op landing pad or a false positive of the call-target byte scan that proposed this boundary is not determinable from the listing.

name: store_r7_to_0850_then_jump_1648
comment: Writes the caller's first stack argument byte, R7, to XDATA 0x0850, then long-jumps to 0x1648 instead of returning, so 0x0850 is handed on as an input rather than consumed. 0x1648's body is not decoded in this listing, and 0x0850 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: countdown_0806_and_branch_on_0490
comment: Reads flag byte 0x0490 (bits 0 and 2), 0x0398 and 0x06E6. If either bit 2 of 0x0490 is set together with 0x0398 == 0xA5, or 0x06E6 == 0x05, it calls 0xC363 and 0xC371; otherwise, if bit 0 of 0x0490 is set it calls 0xC36A, clears 0x0806 and returns. On the remaining path a 0x06E6 of 0x03 calls 0xC36A and reloads 0x0806 with 0x64, then a non-zero 0x0806 is decremented and the same 0xC363/0xC371 pair fires again when it reaches 0x0A. The decompiled C's outer condition does not match the jump at 0x904D and should not be relied on; none of these addresses has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: update_flag_bits_in_0985
comment: Returns immediately if bit 3 of 0x045B is set. Otherwise it sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x0985 when bit 0 of 0x0490 is clear and XDATA 0x0622 is 7 or more, and clears it otherwise; it then sets bit 3 of 0x0985 when 0x0806 has reached 0x0A while bit 0 of 0x0490 is still clear, and clears it otherwise. It finishes at 0xC124 when 0x0780 == 0xA2, or when both 0x0985 and 0x09E7 are zero, and at 0xC12C otherwise. The decompiled C reads the 0x0806 threshold as 0x0B where the instructions at 0x90C6 compare against 0x0A. ec/annotations/registers.yaml now carries 0x045B and 0x0985 as XDATA_045B and XDATA_0985, EC-side sites found with their meanings not established, and 0x09E7 as XDATA_09E7; 0x0622 and 0x0806 have no entry there, and 0x0780 appears there only in a passing note about the 0x0780-0x07FF range.

name: update_flag_bits_in_0723
comment: Sets or clears bit 1 of XDATA 0x0723 according to bit 0 of 0x0490 and whether XDATA 0x0622 is 7 or more, then sets or clears bit 5 of the same byte according to whether 0x0806 is non-zero while bit 0 of 0x0490 is clear. It ends at 0xC49F when 0x0780 == 0xA2, when bit 0 of 0x0490 is set with 0x0723, 0x09E6 both zero, or when 0x06E6 is neither 0x84 nor has that bit set; otherwise it tail-jumps to 0xC497. ec/annotations/registers.yaml now carries 0x0723 as XDATA_0723, an EC-side site found with its meaning not established, and 0x09E6 as XDATA_09E6; 0x0622, 0x0806 and 0x06E6 have no entry there.

name: gate_on_074c_then_dispatch
comment: Three gates, each exiting to the empty stub at 0x924B: bit 4 of XDATA 0x074C must be set, the value 0xB9D8 returns must be zero, and bit 5 of 0x074C must be clear. Past them it sets bit 5 of 0x074C, calls 0x7151 with the low nibble of 0x074C, then acalls 0x94AF and 0x94B5 and jumps to 0x9091. The listing ends at that jump and does not show 0x9091's body; the decompiled C's switch_case_dispatch is the call to 0x7151. 0x074C has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: config_init_from_ba36_ba46
comment: Calls 0xBA46, ORs 0x03 into the byte it returns in A, and writes that to XDATA at the address 0xBA46 left in DPTR. Two calls to 0xBA36 then gate two blocks: a 0x03 result writes 0x00 to 0x083A, 0x0D to 0x083B, 0x18 to 0x08B8 and sets bit 3 of 0x0832; a 0x04 result, or the low nibble of the byte 0xBA36 left in DPTR being 6, clears bit 1 of 0x1611, bit 3 of 0x1613 and bit 6 of 0x1616, each masked with a fresh 0xBDFA result. It finishes by calling 0x94D0 with R7 = 0 and then 0x8653; neither callee is decoded here, so what the scattered 0x08xx bytes are for is not established by this listing. None of the addresses involved has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: bare_ret_924b
comment: A single ret instruction, and the common target of the three ljmp 0x924B failure exits in 0x9167, so it acts as that routine's no-op path. Nothing is read or written. Whether it is a deliberate empty stub or a byte-scan artefact of the proposed boundary is not determinable from the listing.

name: set_0838_0839_0832_on_049f_bit2
comment: Does nothing at all unless bit 2 of XDATA 0x049F is set. When it is, the routine clears that bit, calls 0x9277, then writes 0x50 to XDATA 0x0838 and 0x0A to the next byte, 0x0839 - or 0x54 to 0x0838 instead when bit 5 of 0x08E2 is set - and finally sets bit 2 of 0x0832. ec/annotations/registers.yaml documents 0x049F bit 1 (BIOS_INFO_3, Turbo supported); bit 2 of that byte, 0x08E2, 0x0832, 0x0838 and 0x0839 have no entry there.

name: seed_tcc_defaults_from_ba36
comment: Zeroes XDATA 0x098C and returns unless 0x06E6 == 0x01 and 0x0440 is non-zero. Otherwise it saves 0x098C into 0x0A4A, and three calls to 0xBA36 each choose a constant pair written at 0x0A47/0x0A48: 0x61/0x62 when the call returns zero or the low nibble of the DPTR byte is 5, 0x61/0x7A on a return of 0x08 or a nibble of 9, 0x61/0x86 on 0x03 or 7, and 0x61/0x6E otherwise. A call to 0xB93D then leaves indexed CODE-table bytes in 0x07D8, 0x07D9 and 0x07DA - the three addresses ec/annotations/registers.yaml documents as MODE_TCC_OFFSET_DEFAULTS - and XDATA 0x0A49 is set to 0x02, 0x00 or 0x01 from bit 7 of 0x0751, from bit 1 of 0x049F together with 0xBB40 returning 0x10, and from the default. The .asm listing stops mid-instruction-sequence at 0x948B, so the 0x044F comparison, the calls to 0xBC0E and 0xBE02 and the 0x098C/0x0463 write that 9334.c decompiles are not covered by it and are not decoded here.

name: load_r7_into_a
comment: The listing holds one instruction, mov A, R7, with no ret, so control falls straight into 0x93FF, whose own listing continues the routine. No XDATA or CODE address is touched here and nothing is written; the byte that ends up in A is whatever the caller left in R7, so the value the rest of the routine tests is not determined by this listing.

name: select_table_byte_against_044f
comment: Tests the A that 0x93FE loaded from R7. When it is zero the routine calls 0xB987 then 0xBC0E with XDATA 0x0A49 as the argument and tail-enters 0x948D with A = 0x03. Otherwise it calls 0xB93D and 0xBC0E twice, each time reading byte 0 and then byte 1 of the CODE table 0xBC0E leaves pointed at by DPTR into R4 and comparing R4 against XDATA 0x044F: if 0x044F is at or below byte 0 it calls 0xBE02 and enters 0x948D with A = 0x02, if 0x044F is above byte 1 it calls 0xBE02 and enters 0x948D with A = 0x03, and otherwise it copies 0x098C to 0x0A4A and jumps into the middle of 0x948D at 0x9492. ec/annotations/registers.yaml documents 0x044F as GPU_TEMP; 0x0A49, 0x0A4A and 0x098C have no entry there.

name: code_byte_to_0a4a_then_push_r7
comment: Reads the CODE byte at DPTR+A and writes it to XDATA 0x0A4A. If bit 7 of XDATA 0x0786 and bit 0 of 0x0741 are both set, 0x0A4A is then replaced by 0x0786 with bit 7 cleared, which is the seven-bit offset ec/annotations/registers.yaml documents for that address. It loads 0x0A4A into R7 and falls straight into 0x94AF with no ret of its own, so the store into 0x098C and 0x0463 belongs to 0x94AF. 0x0A4A, 0x098C and 0x0463 have no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: store_r7_to_098c_and_0463
comment: Compares XDATA 0x098C with R7 and does nothing when the two are equal. When they differ it writes R7 to 0x098C and R7 with bit 7 set to XDATA 0x0463, in that order. The 0x80 is the only difference between the two writes; whether bit 7 of 0x0463 is a change flag is suggested by the pattern but is not established by this listing, and 0x098C, 0x0463 and 0x0A4A have no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_07c4_bit4_from_r7
comment: A read-modify-write of XDATA 0x07C4 driven by R7: a non-zero R7 ORs 0x10 into the byte, a zero R7 ANDs it with 0xEF. The other seven bits keep their values, and the routine returns without touching DPTR's successor or any other XDATA address. 0x07C4 is in ec/annotations/registers.yaml as GPU_DYNAMIC_BOOST_STATUS (issue #183).

name: copy_code_table_into_0730_07a7
comment: Stores R7 into XDATA 0x0A50, then picks a two-byte seed pair at 0x0A51/0x0A52: 0x61/0xFE or 0x61/0xC8 when the high nibble of 0x07D3 is 0x30 and the two 0xBA36 calls agree, and 0x61/0x92 in every other case. A non-zero 0x0A50 tail-jumps to 0x95DD; a zero one calls 0xB93D, which leaves a CODE pointer in R6:R7, and copies indexed bytes of that table into 0x0730, 0x0731, 0x0732, 0x0733, 0x07A7, 0x07A8, 0x07A9 and 0x07AA, restoring R6:R7 into DPTR before each read and routing four of the bytes through 0xB939. Bit 2 of 0x0782 selects an 8/9/10/11 or a 4/5/6/7 index group, and the chosen byte is copied to 0x0735 and 0x0737 through 0xBEC8, 0xBED2 and 0xB939; the R7 value 0xB8C0 leaves behind then selects between jumping to 0x9A0D and writing the fixed bytes 0x64, 0x64, 0x2D, 0x3C and 0x01 to 0x07A7, 0x07A8, 0x0730, 0x0731 and 0x0737. ec/annotations/registers.yaml documents 0x0730-0x0737 and 0x07A7-0x07AA as the per-mode PL1/PL2/PL4/D-state defaults; 0x0A50, 0x0A51 and 0x0A52 have no entry there, and 0x07D3 is there as GFID (issue #183).

name: fill_08xx_from_code_table
comment: Calls 0xB984, which leaves a CODE pointer in DPTR, and copies byte 0x1A of that table to XDATA 0x08EA. It then branches on the result of 0xBB40 and bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490: when either is not taken it selects a table through 0xB93A and copies bytes 0-3 of it into 0x08BB via 0xBBB3, 0xB935 and 0xBBBD, calls 0xB8C0, and on a non-zero R7 writes 0x2D to 0x08C0 and 0x3C to 0x08C1; the other branch at 0x9623 tests bit 1 of 0x049F and 0xBB40 == 0x10 and writes 0x08C0, 0x08C1, 0x08BB and 0x08EA. From 0x9669 the same table copy repeats with a 4-7 or 8-11 index group chosen by bit 2 of 0x0782, and 0x08BB is cleared outright when R7 is non-zero. When that comparison does not borrow it sets bit 2 of 0x741, tests 0x73C for bit 0 set, bit 1 clear and bits 3-7 clear, and then either calls 0xA4D6 or sets bit 3 of 0x86F; on the sibling path reached from 0xA99E it clears bit 2 of 0x741 first and then either tail-jumps to 0xA747 or sets bit 2 of 0x86F. The meaning of 0x6E6, 0x86F and the 0x8A5/0x8A6 pair is not decoded here.

When 0x440 is zero it writes 0 to 0xD14 and returns, and otherwise it walks the byte at 0xD14 through compares against 0xF0, 0xFE, 0x10, 0x11 and 0x18, writing 0xFE or 1 on some branches and incrementing it on others. The only condition tested at each step is R7 as returned by 0xC31F; when 0xD14 is in 0x11-0x17 and that call returns zero it calls 0xAA90 and clears 0xD14.

It then calls 0xC412 and, if the returned R7 is non-zero, clears bit 0 of 0x6E2 and returns; if R7 is zero it sets bit 0 of 0x6E2 only when that bit was previously clear, and in that case calls 0xAB9E. name: set_0751_and_07a6_bits
comment: If bit 1 of 0x782 (BIOS_OEM_2) is set, it requires 0x440 non-zero, 0xB9D8 to return zero and 0xC1CB to return 1, then flips bit 6 of 0x751 (MANUAL_FAN_CTRL) with an xor. Otherwise it sets bit 0 of 0x7A6 (OEM_4), and if bit 0 of 0x741 (AP_OEM) is set it tail-jumps to 0xA73F with R7=0xB0; if that bit is clear it calls 0xBB40 and either sets bit 7 of the XDATA byte at the DPTR that call leaves, or, when 0xBB40 returns 0x80, clears bit 7 and sets bit 4 of 0x751, and on any other return clears bits 4 and 7 of 0x751. The address modified on the 0xBB40-returns-zero path is not fixed by this listing.

name: dispatch_on_0751_bits
comment: Requires XDATA 0x6E6 to be 1 and 0x440 non-zero; otherwise it calls 0xC307 and tail-jumps to 0xC317. Inside that gate, bit 4 of 0x751 (MANUAL_FAN_CTRL) together with bit 1 of 0x49F (BIOS_INFO_3) chooses between calling 0xC30F then 0xC2FF and calling 0xC317 alone. It then tests bit 7 of 0x751: set, it calls 0xC307 and tail-jumps to 0xC317; clear, it calls 0xB8C0 and finishes at 0xC2FF when the returned R7 is zero or tail-jumps to 0xC307 when it is not.

name: toggle_08e2_bit4
comment: Returns immediately unless 0xB9D8 returns zero and XDATA 0x73C is not exactly 0x01 (bit 0 set, bit 1 clear, bits 2-7 clear). It then sets bit 4 of 0x8E2 when bit 0 of 0x741 (AP_OEM) is set; otherwise, if bit 4 of 0x8E2 was already set, it clears that bit, clears 0x826 when bit 0 of 0x490 is clear, and sets bit 2 of 0x86F.

name: write_0a47_from_r7
comment: Writes the incoming R7 to XDATA 0xA47, then writes the constant 3 to XDATA 0xA4A. The listing contains no return instruction, so how control leaves this entry is not shown here; the .c attributes a dispatch on the value just stored to this address, but that dispatch is not part of this listing.

name: dispatch_on_0a47
comment: Reads XDATA 0xA47 and dispatches on it through a chain of subtract-and-test: 0x01 goes to the code at 0xAE13, 0x10 tail-jumps to 0xAE87, 0x20 to 0xAEC0, 0x30 to 0xAF27, 0x00 falls through to the block at 0xADD1, and every other value tail-jumps to 0xAF7D. The 0x00 block calls 0xBBFE, 0xB955, 0x445E, 0xBEFE, 0xB008, 0xB994, 0xB958, 0xAFCE and 0xB012, stores 0xB012's return in 0x79D, and branches to 0xAE6D or 0xAE79 on whether 0x79A is zero. The 0x01 block runs the bytes at 0xA4B and 0xA4C through add-0xD0 / SWAP / mask arithmetic into a single byte at 0x79A -- a BCD-shaped transform whose intent is not decoded further -- and then sets 0xA4B to 1.

name: set_08ec_bit0_clear_bit4
comment: Sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x8EC and then clears bit 4 of the same byte, in two separate read-modify-write passes, and returns.

name: set_08ec_bit4_clear_bit0
comment: Sets bit 4 of XDATA 0x8EC and then clears bit 0 of it, before tail-jumping to 0xAF7D. The listing has no ret of its own.

name: build_0791_0793_0794_then_branch
comment: Calls 0xAF8A and 0xB012, then with DPTR=0x790 calls 0xB947 and 0xB01C and stores the latter's return in 0x791. It repeats that pattern for 0xA4C with the constant 0x47, storing the return in 0x793, copies 0xA4C into 0x794, and finally tail-jumps to 0xAF66 when 0x790 is non-zero or to 0xAF72 when it is zero.

name: build_0795_0799_then_set_08ec
comment: Writes 0x40 to 0xA48, then calls 0xBC06, 0xB955, 0xAFF2, 0xB958 and 0xB026 with the constants 3, 0x28 and 3, re-reads the XDATA byte at whatever DPTR 0xB026 left, and stores the returns of the 0xB947/0xB038 pair into 0x796, of the 0xB994/0xB958/0xB038 triple into 0x798, and 0xA4C into 0x799. It then branches on 0x795: non-zero sets bit 2 and clears bit 6 of 0x8EC and returns, while zero sets bit 6 and clears bit 2 of 0x8EC and tail-jumps to 0xAF7D.

name: fill_0790_0791_0793_via_calls
comment: Calls 0xAF8A then 0xB026, re-reads the XDATA byte at the DPTR 0xB026 left, and with DPTR set to 0x790 and then 0x791 calls 0xB994, then 0xB958 with 0x22, then 0xB02F, then 0xB994 again, then 0xB958 with 0x21 and 0xB02F. It then calls 0xB990, 0xB958 with 0x26 and 0x445E with R5=8, copies 0xA4B into 0x793, and ends on a test of 0x790 whose branch to 0xAF72 is the last instruction in the listing -- the not-taken path is not shown here.

name: set_08ec_bit1_clear_bit5
comment: Sets bit 1 of XDATA 0x8EC and then clears bit 5 of the same byte, in two read-modify-write passes, and returns.

name: set_08ec_bit5_clear_bit1
comment: Sets bit 5 of XDATA 0x8EC and then clears bit 1 of the same byte. The listing has no ret, so control continues into the code at 0xAF7D.

name: decrement_0a4a_then_redispatch
comment: Decrements the byte at XDATA 0xA4A and writes it back, returning if the result is zero and otherwise tail-jumping to 0xADAE. The counter's initial value and its meaning are not established by this listing.

name: init_0a48_and_0a59_blocks
comment: Writes a fixed byte pattern: 0x54 to 0xA48, 3 to 0xA49, 0 to 0xA4B, and 0, 0x0A, 0x4B, 0 to 0xA59-0xA5C. It then calls 0x445E with R3=0x54, R5=0x88 and R7=3, loads R7 from 0xA49 and R3 from 0xA48+1, rewrites 0xA59-0xA5C as 0x28, 0x0A, 0x4B, 0, and returns. The values written are not decoded further here.

name: copy_0a4b_0a4c_to_079b_079c
comment: Calls 0x445E with R5=0x0C, then copies XDATA 0xA4B to 0x79B and XDATA 0xA4C to 0x79C. It then loads R7 from 0xA49 and R3 from 0xA48+1, leaves DPTR pointing at 0xA59, and returns that incremented byte in A; nothing in this listing consumes the register values.

name: call_445e_40_88_then_load_0a49
comment: Sets R3 = 0x40 and R5 = 0x88 and lcalls 0x445E, which is not decoded here. It then reads XDATA 0x0A49 into R7 and XDATA 0x0A48 + 1 into R3, leaving DPTR = 0x0A59. Returns with no value in A; the boundary is a call-target-scan hypothesis, so this may not be the whole routine.

name: read_0a4b_after_call_445e_0c
comment: Sets R5 = 0x0C, lcalls 0x445E, then loads XDATA 0x0A4B into A and returns it. 0x0A4B is read only here and never written by these five instructions.

name: read_0a4b_after_call_445e_08
comment: Sets R5 = 0x08, lcalls 0x445E, then loads XDATA 0x0A4B into A and returns it. Same shape as 0xB008 with a different R5 constant.

name: read_0a4b_after_call_445e_0c_b01c
comment: Sets R5 = 0x0C, lcalls 0x445E, then loads XDATA 0x0A4B into A and returns it. The five instructions are identical to 0xB008 and to 0xB038; nothing in this listing distinguishes the three.

name: set_dptr_0a4b_after_call_445e_08
comment: Sets R5 = 0x08, lcalls 0x445E, then points DPTR at XDATA 0x0A4B and returns. Unlike 0xB012 it does not read that byte, so the loaded DPTR is the only result.

name: set_dptr_0a4b_after_call_445e_08_b02f
comment: Sets R5 = 0x08, lcalls 0x445E, then points DPTR at XDATA 0x0A4B and returns. The four instructions are identical to 0xB026; nothing in this listing distinguishes the two.

name: read_0a4b_after_call_445e_0c_b038
comment: Sets R5 = 0x0C, lcalls 0x445E, then loads XDATA 0x0A4B into A and returns it. The five instructions are identical to 0xB008 and to 0xB01C; nothing in this listing distinguishes the three.

name: clear_16f1_bit5_then_store_0x80_pair
comment: Clears bit 5 of XDATA 0x16F1 (read-modify-write with mask 0xDF), then writes 0x80 to XDATA 0x1649 and the same byte to XDATA 0x164A. No byte is read back and nothing else in the listing distinguishes the three writes; the two 0x80 bytes are stored in adjacent addresses, not as one 16-bit value, and neither address is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: ten_count_gate_then_set_1300_and_200f
comment: Requires XDATA 0x0440, 0x06DB and 0x06E6 to be non-zero, 0x06E6 to equal 0x01, 0x047E to equal 0xEC, 0x06DB to be below 5, and bits 0 and 1 of XDATA 0x1304 to be 1 and 0; any other combination jumps to the exit at 0xB0DB. It then increments the direct byte 0xBD and returns unless the incremented value reaches 10, clearing 0xBD and calling 0x3AD6 and 0x2896 once it does. It then copies bit 1 of XDATA 0x1304 into bit 2 of it, and if bits 4, 2 and 0 of 0x1304 are 1, 0 and 1 it sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x1300, bit 4 of 0x1304, and writes 1 to XDATA 0x200F; otherwise it returns. The decompiled C reads the two bit 1/bit 2 decisions as direct-bit flags at 0x02, 0x04 and 0x00; the .asm shows all three are bits of XDATA 0x1304.

name: sync_0983_bit5_against_support_2_bit4
comment: Calls 0xB9D8 and returns immediately if it returns non-zero, or if XDATA 0x0440 is zero. Otherwise it forms R7 from bit 4 of SUPPORT_2 at XDATA 0x0766 and R6 from bit 5 of XDATA 0x0983, and if the two differ it XORs 0x20 into 0x0983 (toggling bit 5) and calls 0xA73F with R7 = 0xB6. The meaning of 0x0983 is not established by this listing.

name: check_0xB112
comment: First early-return gate of charge_target_update. What it tests was NOT decoded; the name is the one charge-target-derating.md uses for it and nothing more is claimed.

name: manual_ctrl_profile_gate
comment: Sets CHARGING_PROFILE in FAN_CTRL then, if AP_OEM ENABLE_MANUAL_CTRL is clear, masks OEM_4 bits 4-5 to force the profile back to High Capacity. The tick that runs it is not identified; the file notes uniwill-laptop clears that bit at shutdown so the reset fires on every module unload by design

name: charge_target_update
comment: Sets the charger's constant-voltage target. Reached by a conditional branch from 0xB141 (jb acc.1 on XDATA 0x0490 bit 1) and not by any call, so the direct-call census in bank-call-targets.csv cannot seed it; this row is what puts it in the project.

name: charge_stress_update
comment: Age-derating section: the seconds/minutes counters at XDATA 0x09C7/0x09C8 and the stress accumulator at 0x09C9, tiered by pack temperature. The worked acceptance target for this pipeline per ec/ghidra/README.md.

name: charge_target_minus_r3_times_0a47
comment: Takes its argument in R3, loads the 16-bit multiplier from XDATA 0x0A47, and forms the 16-bit product R3 x 0x0A47 with the 16x16 multiply at 0x707D (result in R7:R6). It subtracts that product from the big-endian 16-bit value at XDATA 0x0A50/0x0A51 and writes the little-endian difference to CHARGE_TARGET_MV at 0x0523 (high) and 0x0522 (low). The low byte at 0x0522 is then recomputed with an 8-bit MUL AB of R3 and 0x0A47, which yields the same low product byte, and the read of 0x0A50 immediately before that block is overwritten and has no effect. registers.yaml records 0xB378/0xB389 as one of the two writers of this byte.

name: unresolved_b38d
comment: A single RET and nothing else. The .c for this address is an empty void body, so no behaviour can be read from either file; the listing may be a genuine empty stub or the call-target-scan boundary may have cut a longer routine short, and this row records that rather than guessing.

name: step_1802_toward_bf12_limited_by_09cd
comment: Reads bit 5 of XDATA 0x0456: when it is clear the routine calls 0xB3E4 (which clears bit 0 of XDATA 0x0984) and then 0xC01C and returns. When it is set and XDATA 0x0440 is non-zero, bit 0 of 0x0984 clear causes 0xC468, 0xC016 and 0xBF12 to run and the 0xBF12 result to be stored in XDATA 0x1802 with that bit then set. On every pass it calls 0xBF12 again and moves 0x1802 one step toward the new result, incrementing while 0x1802 is below XDATA 0x09CD and decrementing once it is at or above it; a match returns with no change. None of 0x0456, 0x09CD, 0x1802 nor 0xBF12's result is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: call_c470_then_clear_0984_bit0
comment: Calls 0xC470, then clears bit 0 of XDATA 0x0984 (read-modify-write with mask 0xFE). The address 0xB3E4 is the shared continuation that 0xB38E reaches from three different branches, so it is entered both on its own and as a tail.

name: rewrite_dptr_byte_ff_at_f0_else_count_0988
comment: The entry executes INC R1 and then tests R0, returning immediately when R0 is zero. Otherwise it reads the XDATA byte at DPTR twice: a value of exactly 0xF0 is overwritten with 0xFF and the routine returns, a value below 0xF0 increments XDATA 0x0988 and returns, and a value above 0xF0 leaves both the byte and 0x0988 untouched. There is no return value, and what R0 and R1 carry in is not decoded here.

name: zero_xdata_block_ptr_r6r7_count_r4r5
comment: Takes a 16-bit XDATA destination pointer in R6:R7 and a 16-bit count in R4:R5, staging them at XDATA 0x0A56/0x0A57 and 0x0A58/0x0A59 and copying the pointer into the direct-byte pair 0xB7/0xB8. It clears a 16-bit index at XDATA 0x0A5A/0x0A5B and loops while that index is below the count, writing 0 through the pointer, advancing the pointer, and lcalling 0xBADE after each byte. The RET at 0xB460 leaves A holding the borrow-adjusted low byte of the last index-minus-count subtraction, which the caller does not use. The .c reads the direct pair 0xB7/0xB8 as the arguments and 0x0A5A as the argument to 0xBADE; the .asm has the roles the other way round.

name: zero_96_bytes_at_0f00
comment: Sets R5 = 0x60, R4 = 0x00, R7 = 0x00 and R6 = 0x0F, then tail-jumps to 0xB40C, so the callee sees the destination 0x0F00 and the count 0x0060. Net effect is that 96 bytes of XDATA from 0x0F00 upwards are zeroed. No return of its own; the RET belongs to 0xB40C.

name: clear_08eb_bit5_09e6_09e7_08a1_089c_089d
comment: Clears bit 5 of XDATA 0x08EB, bit 0 of XDATA 0x09E6, and bit 0 of XDATA 0x09E7 (each a read-modify-write), then writes 0 to XDATA 0x08A1. The bytes at 0xB5CD-0xB5D1 store A to XDATA 0x089C and 0x089D and are the same instructions that form the whole of 0xB5CC, so the .asm listing for this entry stops at 0xB5CB and only the .c shows those two stores; with A = 0 on entry from 0xB4A8 they store zero. Nothing is read back.

name: store_a_to_089c_and_089d
comment: Six instructions: loads DPTR with 0x089C, stores A, increments DPTR and stores A again, so the accumulator goes to both XDATA 0x089C and 0x089D. The following RET at 0xB5D2 is the next entry in the census, so this listing has no return of its own and falls straight into it. Callers set A first (0xB4A8 arrives with A = 0), so this is a 16-bit store in most of its uses, but the listing itself has no arithmetic.

name: unresolved_b5d2
comment: A single RET. It is the return path of the six-instruction store at 0xB5CC and also the destination of the ljmp instructions at 0xB51F, 0xB533 and 0xB53B in 0xB4A8, so its only established role is as an exit; the .c for this address is an empty void body and nothing further can be read from either file.

name: clear_08eb_bit3_09e6_09e7_08a2_089e_089f
comment: Clears bit 3 of XDATA 0x08EB, bit 1 of XDATA 0x09E6, and bit 1 of XDATA 0x09E7 (each a read-modify-write), then writes 0 to XDATA 0x08A2. The bytes at 0xB730-0xB735 store A to XDATA 0x089E and 0x089F and are the same instructions that form the whole of 0xB730, so the .asm listing for this entry stops at 0xB72F and only the .c shows those two stores; the clr a at 0xB72B is one instruction ahead of both, so they store zero whatever A was on entry. Same shape as 0xB5B2 with the bit 3 / bit 1 pair instead of bit 5 / bit 0. 0xB5F8 tail-jumps here on the USER-clear arm of the 0x0751 test at 0xB5EA, but that is one of three gates in and not the only one: 0xB5E7 reaches the same 0xB5F8 when XDATA 0x06E6 is not 1, before 0x0751 has been read at all, and 0xB5F5 falls into it when XDATA 0x07C5 bit 4 is set, so the USER-set arm runs this clearing too. Read in ec/annotations/manual-fan-ctrl-0751.md 8a. The seven bytes it writes are in ec/annotations/registers.yaml at present-untested and none of them is read back.

name: store_a_to_089e_and_089f
comment: Six instructions: loads DPTR with 0x089E, stores A, increments DPTR and stores A again, so the accumulator goes to both XDATA 0x089E and 0x089F. The following RET at 0xB736 is the next entry in the census, so this listing has no return of its own. The same six bytes are also the tail of 0xB716.

name: unresolved_b736
comment: A single RET. It is the return path of the six-instruction store at 0xB730 and also the destination of the ljmp instructions at 0xB66F, 0xB67D, 0xB68D, 0xB6FA, 0xB706 and 0xB714 in 0xB5D3, so it is established only as the failure exit of that state machine; the .c is an empty void body and nothing further can be read from either file.

name: clear_08eb_bit6_and_zero_08a0
comment: Clears bit 6 of XDATA 0x08EB (read-modify-write with mask 0xBF) and writes 0 to XDATA 0x08A0. It is the destination of the ljmp at 0xB758 in 0xB737, and the RET at 0xB83A is the shared exit that 0xB737's own listing also falls into, so both entries return through the same byte. Four branches reach 0xB758 and only one of them is the USER bit: 0xB73A when the call to 0xB9D8 at 0xB737 returns non-zero, which is before 0x0751 is read at all, 0xB740 the USER-clear arm, and 0xB747 and 0xB74E two early exits inside the USER-set arm (XDATA 0x0490 bit 0 clear, XDATA 0x04AB not 0x64). A fifth gate, 0xB755 on XDATA 0x07C5 bit 4, is a jnb acc.4 whose target is the lcall 0xba36 at 0xB75B, so it reaches 0xB758 by fall-through when the bit is set rather than by a branch. The byte it zeroes is a count rather than a flag: 0xB7E8 on the USER-set path increments XDATA 0x08A0 and compares it against 0x0A with the carry-in set by the setb c at 0xB7EF, so 0xB7F2 retires at 0x0A or below and the block past it runs from 0x0B, setting bit 6 of 0x08EB at 0xB7F8, so clearing the bit and zeroing the count are one reset. 0xB7D8 and 0xB7FC reach 0xB835, these same three instructions, without passing this entry point at all. Read in ec/annotations/manual-fan-ctrl-0751.md 8a; nothing is read back.

name: 09ee_bit1_edge_drives_0897_countdown
comment: Tests bit 2 of XDATA 0x07A4: when it is set and bit 1 of XDATA 0x09EE is clear, it sets that bit and tail-jumps to 0xC191, and when bit 1 is already set it falls to the shared RET at 0xB8BF. When bit 2 of 0x07A4 is clear and bit 1 of 0x09EE is set, it clears that bit, sets XDATA 0x0897 to 1 and returns; otherwise it decrements 0x0897 and calls 0xC199 when the decrement reaches zero. Nothing here establishes what 0x07A4 bit 2 or 0x09EE bit 1 represent.

name: test_0770_equals_04
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0770 and returns 1 in R7 if the byte equals 0x04, 0 if it does not. No write, no call, no other XDATA access. The decompiled C shows two bare returns and drops the R7 result entirely, so the .asm is the only statement of the result. 0x0770 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so what the value selects is not determined here.

name: test_0770_equals_08
comment: Same 13-byte shape as 0xB8C0: reads XDATA 0x0770 and returns 1 in R7 if it equals 0x08, 0 otherwise. It is one of nine adjacent routines at 0xB8C0-0xB928 that each compare the same byte against a different constant; 0x0770 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: test_0770_equals_18
comment: Same 13-byte shape as 0xB8C0: reads XDATA 0x0770 and returns 1 in R7 if it equals 0x18, 0 otherwise. 0x18 is the largest of the nine constants the routines at 0xB8C0-0xB928 compare against that byte; the set tested is 0x04, 0x06, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0C, 0x0E and 0x18.

name: test_0770_equals_09
comment: Same 13-byte shape as 0xB8C0: reads XDATA 0x0770 and returns 1 in R7 if it equals 0x09, 0 otherwise. The decompiled C again drops the R7 result, leaving only the comparison visible.

name: test_0770_equals_0c
comment: Same 13-byte shape as 0xB8C0: reads XDATA 0x0770 and returns 1 in R7 if it equals 0x0C, 0 otherwise. The decompiled C again drops the R7 result, leaving only the comparison visible.

name: test_0770_equals_06
comment: Same 13-byte shape as 0xB8C0: reads XDATA 0x0770 and returns 1 in R7 if it equals 0x06, 0 otherwise. The decompiled C again drops the R7 result, leaving only the comparison visible.

name: test_0770_equals_07
comment: Same 13-byte shape as 0xB8C0: reads XDATA 0x0770 and returns 1 in R7 if it equals 0x07, 0 otherwise. The decompiled C again drops the R7 result, leaving only the comparison visible.

name: test_0770_equals_0e
comment: Same 13-byte shape as 0xB8C0: reads XDATA 0x0770 and returns 1 in R7 if it equals 0x0E, 0 otherwise. The decompiled C again drops the R7 result, leaving only the comparison visible.

name: test_0770_equals_0a
comment: Same 13-byte shape as 0xB8C0: reads XDATA 0x0770 and returns 1 in R7 if it equals 0x0A, 0 otherwise. It is the last of the nine adjacent routines in this run and ends at 0xB934, immediately before the differently shaped code at 0xB935.

name: movc_lookup_set_dptr_08c1
comment: Two instructions: reads the CODE byte at (DPTR + A) into A with MOVC, then loads DPTR with 0x08C1. The listing contains no return, so the store that would use 0x08C1 is in the listing at 0xB939; the decompiled C's write of 0x08C1 and its return of 0x0A52 are not in these two instructions.

name: store_a_to_dptr_b939
comment: One instruction: writes the incoming A to the XDATA byte addressed by DPTR. The listing has no return, and nothing in it sets DPTR, so the address written is supplied by the caller. The decompiled C's return of 0x0A52 is not in this listing.

name: set_dptr_0a51_b93a
comment: One instruction: loads DPTR with 0x0A51. The listing contains no return, so it falls straight into 0xB93D, which continues by reading two consecutive XDATA bytes through DPTR. Whether 0xB93A is a one-byte entry point or the head of the routine 0xB93D completes is not determinable from this listing.

name: load_dptr_be16_from_xdata
comment: Reads the byte at DPTR into R6, increments DPTR, reads the next byte into A and R7, then sets DPH from R6 and DPL from A, so the two consecutive XDATA bytes are loaded into DPTR with the first byte read as the high byte. Returns with DPTR holding that address and A still holding the low byte. The decompiled C's `*(param_1 + 1)` reading does not match these instructions.

name: load_r3_r7_from_0a48_store_a
comment: Writes the incoming A to the XDATA byte at the caller's DPTR, then reads XDATA 0x0A49 into R7, reads XDATA 0x0A48 into A, increments A and leaves it in R3, and finally loads A with the constant 0x46. So the two registers carry XDATA 0x0A48+1 in R3 and XDATA 0x0A49 in R7, not a plain 16-bit read of that pair. The listing ends there with no return, and 0x46 is not stored in it.

name: set_dptr_0a59_b955
comment: One instruction: loads DPTR with 0x0A59. The listing contains no return, so the four stores that follow it are in the listing at 0xB958. Whether 0xB955 is a one-byte entry point or the head of the routine 0xB958 completes is not determinable from this listing.

name: write_4_bytes_ending_0a_4b_00
comment: Writes the incoming A to the XDATA byte at DPTR, increments DPTR and writes 0x0A, increments again and writes 0x4B, increments again and writes 0x00, then returns. Four consecutive XDATA bytes; the first is caller-supplied and the base address is not set in this listing. The decompiled C's param_2[0..3] form matches these four relative stores.

name: add_r6_r7_to_0a58_pair_then_halve
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's DPTR into A and stores it to XDATA 0x0A58, then adds R7 to the byte at 0x0A59 and R6 plus the carry to the byte at 0x0A58, shifts that 16-bit sum right by one through the carry (clr CY then two rrc), writes the result back to 0x0A58 and 0x0A59, and returns the new high byte in A. So the pair at 0x0A58/0x0A59 becomes ((old pair + R6:R7) >> 1) with R6 the high byte. Neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: store_a_to_dptr_b983
comment: One instruction: writes the incoming A to the XDATA byte addressed by DPTR. The listing has no return, and nothing in it sets DPTR, so the destination is supplied by the caller.

name: set_dptr_0a51_b984
comment: One instruction: loads DPTR with 0x0A51. The listing contains no return, so it falls into 0xB987, which continues by reading the byte at DPTR into R6. Whether 0xB984 is a one-byte entry point or the head of the routine completed at 0xB989 is not determinable from this listing.

name: read_dptr_byte_into_r6
comment: Two instructions: reads the byte at DPTR into A and then into R6. The listing has no return; the low byte, the DPH/DPL load and the return are in the listing at 0xB989. Whether 0xB987 is a two-byte entry point or the head of the routine 0xB989 completes is not determinable from this listing alone.

name: finish_dptr_be16_load
comment: Increments DPTR, reads that byte into A, sets DPL from it and DPH from R6, and returns. Together with the R6 loaded at 0xB987 this forms a 16-bit XDATA pointer from two consecutive bytes, the first read as the high byte. The decompiled C's `*(param_1 + 1)` reading does not match these instructions.

name: read_dptr_byte_then_set_dptr_0792
