comment: Loads B with 0x04 and tail-jumps to the common routine at 0x7110, which does mul AB and adds the product to DPTR. With B fixed at 4 the effect is DPTR += 4 * (the accumulator on entry); A is not set here, so the stride base comes from the caller. Nothing is read from or written to XDATA by this listing.

name: init_0817_081e_081f_read_0815
comment: Clears XDATA 0x0817, writes 0x00 to 0x081E and 0x08 to 0x081F, then returns the byte read from XDATA 0x0815 in A. Straight-line, no branch and no call; none of the four addresses has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: copy_0a53_to_0873_and_0a54_to_087b
comment: Copies XDATA 0x0A53 to 0x0873, then XDATA 0x0A54 to 0x087B, and returns. Two independent single-byte copies in the order shown; none of the addresses has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: code_byte_sub_from_044c
comment: Reads the CODE byte at (caller's DPTR + caller's A) into R7, reads XDATA 0x044C, and returns 0x044C minus that CODE byte in A. The SUBB also subtracts the carry inherited on entry, so the decompiled C's added PSW term has the wrong sign; ec/annotations/registers.yaml now carries 0x044C as XDATA_044C, an EC-side site found with its meaning not established.

name: store_a_then_clear_0824_bit7_and_0768_bit2
comment: First instruction stores the caller's A to whatever XDATA address the caller left in DPTR, then clears bit 7 of XDATA 0x0824 and bit 2 of XDATA 0x0768, both by read-modify-write, and returns. registers.yaml documents 0x0768 as SWITCH_STATUS (super-key lock on bit 0); the bit cleared here is bit 2, and 0x0824 has no entry in that file.

name: fan_table_base_offset_helper
comment: Helper called by the 0x888D handler when the 0x0F5F table selector is 2, annotated in the listing as yielding base + 0x00. Its own body is not decoded there, so the role is read off the call site only

name: inc_09e4_and_return_new
comment: Increments the byte at XDATA 0x09E4, writes it straight back and returns the new value in A. The INC sets no carry, so 0xFF wraps to 0x00; 0x09E4 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: store_code_byte_to_08ac_then_reload_dptr
comment: Reads the CODE byte at (caller's DPTR + caller's A) and writes it to XDATA 0x08AC, then loads DPTR with the caller's R6:R7 pair and returns. The pointer is reloaded from R6:R7, not incremented, and nothing outside 0x08AC is written; 0x08AC has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: read_0434_keep_0435_in_r4
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0435 into R4, then returns the byte at XDATA 0x0434 in A. The 0x0435 read has no other effect in this listing beyond the R4 hand-off; both addresses are the BAT_CURRENT_MA pair in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, little-endian mA there, with the byte order resting on three independent sources.

name: load_dptr_0a47_then_nothing
comment: Three bytes only: MOV DPTR,#0x0A47, and the listing ends at the next census entry 0xBC7E whose first instruction is the MOVX @DPTR,A that performs the store. Read as a fragment of one routine that writes the caller's A to XDATA 0x0A47, but as a function in its own right its role is not determinable.

name: store_a_then_read_086c_set_cy
comment: Stores the caller's A to the XDATA address the caller left in DPTR (0x0A47 if entered from the preceding fragment at 0xBC7B), then reads XDATA 0x086C into A, sets the carry with SETB CY and returns. The carry is left set for a following SUBB; 0x086C has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: clear_08a9_and_08aa
comment: Writes 0x00 to XDATA 0x08A9 and then to 0x08AA, and returns. No other effect; neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: cfg_cell_count_selector
comment: Yields 0xC0 or 0x80, which charge_target_update turns into a 4S/3S cell count. What configures it is not known.

name: table_632d_index_times_4
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's XDATA DPTR, uses it as an index into a byte table at CODE 0x632D (MOVC @A+DPTR), doubles the result twice and returns it in A. The table contents are not decoded here and 0x632D is not an address in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: mul_0826_by_dptr_byte
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's XDATA DPTR into R7, reads XDATA 0x0826, and multiplies the two with MUL AB. The 16-bit product comes back in A (low) and B (high); the decompiled char return shows only the low byte. 0x0826 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: clear_08a5_and_08a6
comment: Writes 0x00 to XDATA 0x08A5 and then to 0x08A6, and returns. No other effect; neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: load_dptr_08e1_and_a_06_then_nothing
comment: Four bytes only: MOV DPTR,#0x08E1 then MOV A,#0x06, and the listing ends at the next census entry 0xBCB6 whose first instruction is the MOVX @DPTR,A that stores 6 to 0x08E1. As a function in its own right its role is not determinable.

name: store_a_then_clear_08e0
comment: Stores the caller's A to the XDATA address the caller left in DPTR (0x08E1 if entered from the preceding fragment at 0xBCB1), then writes 0x00 to XDATA 0x08E0 and returns. Neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: dptr_r5_times_2_tail_call_705b
comment: Forms DPTR = R5 * 2 with MUL AB (B loaded with 0x02, product high byte into DPH), loads A with R7, and tail-jumps to 0x705B with no return of its own. What 0x705B does with that pair is not decoded in this listing.

name: store_be16_of_08e6_and_arg_to_0a47
comment: Saves the caller's A into R6, reads XDATA 0x08E6, adds the carry inherited on entry with ADDC A,#0x00, and writes that byte to XDATA 0x0A47; it then writes the saved argument byte to 0x0A48. The pair is a big-endian 16-bit store whose high byte carries the entry carry; no branch and no call.

name: x0f10_table_indexed_by_0460
comment: Reads the index byte at XDATA 0x0460, builds DPTR = 0x0F10 + index (DPL = index + 0x10, DPH = 0x0F plus the carry out of that add, which yields the same 16-bit address either way), and returns the byte at that XDATA address in A. There is no bounds check on the index and no other XDATA access; the table base is not documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: read_first_code_byte_pair_frag
comment: Clears A, reads the CODE byte at the caller's DPTR into R6, then loads A with 0x01; the listing ends at the next census entry 0xBCEE, which reads the CODE byte at DPTR+1 and assembles the two into DPTR. The pair reads a big-endian 16-bit CODE constant into DPTR, but 0xBCE9 on its own has no determinable role.

name: dptr_from_code_be16
comment: Reads the CODE byte at the caller's DPTR + 1 into R7, writes it to DPL and the caller's R6 to DPH, and returns. Net effect is DPTR = the big-endian 16-bit value stored at CODE[DPTR]; the R7 store is a copy of the same byte and nothing outside DPTR is touched.

name: stress_headroom
comment: Computes 65000 minus the stress counter minus 1, so the caller can skip the increment on borrow.

name: clear_0741_bit0_and_08e2_bit4
comment: Clears bit 0 of XDATA 0x0741 and bit 4 of XDATA 0x08E2, both by read-modify-write, and returns. registers.yaml documents 0x0741 as AP_OEM (ENABLE_MANUAL_CTRL, bit 0, status confirmed-working); 0x08E2 has no entry in that file.

name: read_x0b68
comment: Loads R7 with the immediate 0x68 (MOV R7,#0x68, an immediate load, not the internal-RAM read the decompiled C renders), builds DPTR = 0x0B68 from it, and returns the byte at that XDATA address in A. 0x0B68 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: store_044b_then_read_08e2
comment: Writes the caller's A to XDATA 0x044B, then reads XDATA 0x08E2 and returns it in A. 0x08E2 is the byte whose bit 4 the routine at 0xBD03 clears; ec/annotations/registers.yaml now carries 0x044B as XDATA_044B, an EC-side site found with its meaning not established; 0x08E2 has no entry there.

name: set_r5_and_1_plus_carry_frag
comment: Copies the caller's A into R5, then computes A = 1 + the carry inherited on entry (CLR A then ADDC A,#0x01); the listing ends at the next census entry 0xBD2D, which moves that value into R4 and then subtracts R4:R5 from R6:R7. As a function in its own right its role is not determinable.

name: sub16_r6r7_minus_r4r5
comment: Copies A into R4, clears the carry, then subtracts R5 from R7 and R4 from R6 with two SUBBs. Returns the low byte of (R6:R7) - (R4:R5) in A with the borrow in CY; neither operand is loaded here, so the entry state comes from the caller or from the preceding fragment at 0xBD29.

name: sub_dptr_byte_from_0867
comment: Copies the byte at the caller's XDATA DPTR into R7, reads XDATA 0x0867, clears the carry and returns that byte minus R7 in A with the borrow in CY. 0x0867 is recorded in ec/annotations/registers.yaml as XDATA_0867, units not determined.

name: sub_dptr_byte_from_0868
comment: Copies the byte at the caller's XDATA DPTR into R7, reads XDATA 0x0868, clears the carry and returns that byte minus R7 in A with the borrow in CY. Same shape as the routine at 0xBD34 one byte away; 0x0868 is recorded in ec/annotations/registers.yaml as XDATA_0868, units not determined.

name: be16_08a9_08aa_minus_0321
comment: Sets the carry, subtracts 0x20 from XDATA 0x08AA, then subtracts 0x03 from XDATA 0x08A9 through the borrow chain. The net effect is the big-endian 16-bit pair {0x08AA,0x08A9} minus 0x0321, low byte in A and borrow in CY; 0x08A9/0x08AA are the two bytes the routine at 0xBC85 clears, and nothing in this listing says what the constant compares against.

name: store_be16_b
comment: The second of the two big-endian 16-bit store helpers; see the note on 0xBB90.

name: be16_0464_0465_minus_100
comment: Clears the carry, subtracts 0x64 (100) from XDATA 0x0465, then subtracts 0x00 from XDATA 0x0464 through the borrow chain. The net effect is the big-endian 16-bit pair {0x0465,0x0464} minus 100, low byte in A and borrow in CY; neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: be16_046c_046d_minus_100
comment: Same shape as the routine at 0xBD5D but over XDATA 0x046D/0x046C: clears the carry, subtracts 0x64 from 0x046D, then subtracts 0x00 from 0x046C through the borrow. Returns the low byte of {0x046D,0x046C} minus 100 in A with the borrow in CY; neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: tail_call_7110_with_b6
comment: Two instructions: loads B with 0x06 and tail-jumps to 0x7110, passing the caller's A through unchanged. Nothing is read or written before the jump, and 0x7110's own behaviour is not decoded in this listing.

name: store_a_then_tail_call_7110_b6
comment: Writes the incoming A to XDATA at the caller's DPTR, then loads DPTR with R6:R7, B with 0x06 and A with R5 before tail-jumping to 0x7110. The tail target is not decoded in this listing.

name: tier_250_eligible
comment: One of the comparisons behind the 250 mV-per-cell derating tier (stress > 18144).

name: tier_200_eligible
comment: One of the comparisons behind the 200 mV-per-cell derating tier (stress > 14808).

name: set_cy_fallthrough_to_bda6
comment: A single instruction: sets the carry flag. The listing contains no ret, so execution falls straight into 0xBDA6, whose movc/subb pair subtracts with that carry already set. Whether 0xBDA5 is a one-byte entry point or the head of the routine that 0xBDA6 completes is not determinable from the byte-scan function boundary alone.

name: sub_code_byte_from_x0875
comment: Reads the CODE byte at DPTR+A into R7, reads XDATA 0x0875, and returns 0x0875 minus that CODE byte minus the incoming carry. The carry is the one the immediately preceding 0xBDA5 sets, which is why the decompiled C shows the +1 form. 0x0875 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: copy_x1907_to_x0a57
comment: Reads XDATA 0x1907 and writes that byte to XDATA 0x0A57, then leaves DPTR pointing at 0x1908. Only the single byte 0x1907 is copied; 0x1908 is loaded into DPTR but not read or written here.

name: copy_x190a_to_x0a57
comment: Reads XDATA 0x190A and writes that byte to XDATA 0x0A57, then leaves DPTR pointing at 0x190B. Same destination as 0xBDAE and 0xBDC6, a different source byte each time.

name: copy_x190d_to_x0a57
comment: Reads XDATA 0x190D and writes that byte to XDATA 0x0A57, then leaves DPTR pointing at 0x190E. One byte in, one byte out; no 16-bit value is formed here.

name: read_x0a59_and_x0a5a
comment: Reads the two bytes at XDATA 0x0A59 and 0x0A5A: the first is left in R6 and the second is returned in A. The two addresses are separate single-byte accesses; this listing does not establish them as one 16-bit register.

name: store_code_byte_to_0a49_0a4a
comment: Reads the CODE byte at DPTR+A, then writes the caller's incoming R7 to XDATA 0x0A49 and that CODE byte to XDATA 0x0A4A. Clears A and R7 before returning, so the return value is 0 and the CODE byte is no longer reachable in a register.

name: gpu_temp_minus_xdata_byte
comment: Copies the byte at the caller's DPTR into R7, reads GPU_TEMP at XDATA 0x044F, and returns it minus that byte minus the incoming carry. The carry in is whatever the caller left; these instructions do not set it, and the borrow out is left for the caller.

name: write_40_then_read_x1601
comment: Writes the constant 0x40 to XDATA at the caller's DPTR, then loads DPTR with 0x1601 and returns the byte stored there. The destination of the 0x40 write is caller-supplied and is not identified by these instructions.

name: tail_call_7110_with_b4
comment: Loads DPTR with R6:R7, B with 0x04 and A with R5, then tail-jumps to 0x7110. No XDATA or CODE access of its own; the tail target is not decoded in this listing.

name: set_bit6_in_x0723
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0723, ORs bit 6 (0x40) into it and writes the byte back unchanged otherwise. ec/annotations/registers.yaml now carries 0x0723 as XDATA_0723, an EC-side site found with its meaning not established, so what that bit gates is not determined from these instructions.

name: x0449_minus_x08ea_minus_1
comment: Reads XDATA 0x08EA into R7 and XDATA 0x0449 into A, sets the carry so the following subb subtracts one extra, and returns 0x0449 - 0x08EA - 1. 0x0449 is XDATA_0449 in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, an EC-side site found with its meaning not established; 0x08EA has no entry there.

name: write_a_to_x1805_and_x1808
comment: Writes the incoming A to XDATA 0x1805 and then to XDATA 0x1808. Two separate single-byte stores three bytes apart; the listing does not present them as one register.

name: write_64_91_pair
comment: Writes 0x64 to XDATA at the caller's DPTR, increments DPTR, and writes 0x91 to the following byte. The two constants are stored as two adjacent bytes; what the pair encodes is not determined here.

name: write_64_c7_pair
comment: Writes 0x64 to XDATA at the caller's DPTR, increments DPTR, and writes 0xC7 to the following byte. Same shape as 0xBE2A, 0xBE3A, 0xBE42 and 0xBE4A with a different second constant.

name: write_64_d9_pair
comment: Writes 0x64 to XDATA at the caller's DPTR, increments DPTR, and writes 0xD9 to the following byte. Same shape as 0xBE2A, 0xBE32, 0xBE42 and 0xBE4A with a different second constant.

name: write_64_b5_pair
comment: Writes 0x64 to XDATA at the caller's DPTR, increments DPTR, and writes 0xB5 to the following byte. Same shape as 0xBE2A, 0xBE32, 0xBE3A and 0xBE4A with a different second constant.

name: write_64_a3_pair
comment: Writes 0x64 to XDATA at the caller's DPTR, increments DPTR, and writes 0xA3 to the following byte. Same shape as 0xBE2A, 0xBE32, 0xBE3A and 0xBE42 with a different second constant.

name: copy_x00c0_pair_to_iram_67_68
comment: Reads XDATA 0x00C0 and 0x00C1 and stores them into internal-RAM direct addresses 0x67 and 0x68 respectively. Returns nothing in A, and the meaning of the copied pair is not determined here.

name: add_20_carry_to_r6_r7
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's DPTR, adds 0x20, leaves the low byte in R7 and the carry out of that add in R6 (clr A followed by rlc A copies carry into A), then loads DPTR with 0x0A47 and returns. So the 9-bit sum lands in R6:R7 and the function returns an address rather than a byte; the decompiled C's boolean reading does not match these instructions.

name: x0469_minus_x1809
comment: Copies XDATA 0x1809 into R7, reads XDATA 0x0469, and returns 0x0469 minus 0x1809 minus the incoming carry. These instructions do not set the carry first, so the caller's flag is part of the result. Neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: write_a_then_zero_at_0a47_0a48
comment: Writes the incoming A to XDATA 0x0A47, increments DPTR, writes 0x00 to XDATA 0x0A48, then leaves DPTR at 0x08B8. Whether 0x0A47/0x0A48 form one 16-bit value is not established by these instructions.

name: write_9f_to_x1904
comment: Writes the constant 0x9F to XDATA 0x1904 and leaves DPTR pointing at 0x1906. Only that one byte is written; 0x1905 is not touched here.

name: write_9f_to_x1909
comment: Writes the constant 0x9F to XDATA 0x1909 and leaves DPTR pointing at 0x190C. One single-byte store; no other address is read or written.

name: write_9f_to_x190c
comment: Writes the constant 0x9F to XDATA 0x190C and leaves DPTR pointing back at 0x1904. Same constant and same shape as 0xBE7E and 0xBE88, applied to a different address.

name: read_x0780_xor_a2
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0780 and returns it exclusive-ORed with the constant 0xA2, without writing anything back. 0x0780 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: x044c_minus_r7
comment: Reads XDATA 0x044C, clears the carry so no extra borrow is taken, and returns 0x044C minus the caller's R7. ec/annotations/registers.yaml now carries 0x044C as XDATA_044C, an EC-side site found with its meaning not established.

name: sub_33_from_09e4_low7
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x09E4, masks off bit 7, and returns the masked value minus 0x33 in A. The setb CY before the subb is what makes it subtract 0x33 and not 0x32, so the carry left on exit says whether the masked value was below 0x33. 0x09E4 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: dec_dptr_byte_and_set_1804
comment: Decrements the byte the caller left selected in DPTR (movx A,@DPTR; dec A; movx @DPTR,A), then writes the constant 0x3C to XDATA 0x1804. DPTR is left pointing at 0x1804; which byte the caller's DPTR selects is not decided here. 0x1804 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: mod_070a_by_r5
comment: Loads the byte at XDATA 0x070A into A, sets B to R5, and executes div AB, which leaves the quotient in A and the remainder in B; the routine then moves B into A and returns it, so the result is 0x070A modulo R5. There is no zero test on R5 in this listing, and div AB with B clear is undefined on this part, so the decompiled C's if (param_1 != 0) guard corresponds to no instruction. 0x070A has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: load_code_byte_to_0734
comment: Reads the CODE byte at (incoming DPTR + A) with movc, writes it to XDATA 0x0734, then restores DPTR from R7:R6. 0x0734 is the first byte of the Office profile default block per ec/annotations/registers.yaml (status present-untested), and this listing is a writer for it. The CODE base and index come from the caller's DPTR and A and are not set here.

name: load_code_byte_to_0736
comment: Same shape as the routine at 0xBEC8: reads the CODE byte at (incoming DPTR + A) with movc, writes it to XDATA 0x0736, and restores DPTR from R7:R6. 0x0736 is the third byte of the Office profile default block per ec/annotations/registers.yaml (status present-untested). The CODE base and index are the caller's.

name: load_code_byte_to_08c4
comment: Reads the CODE byte at (incoming DPTR + A) with movc, writes it to XDATA 0x08C4, then restores DPTR from R5:R4. 0x08C4 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so what the stored byte means is not decoded here.

name: load_code_byte_to_08c6
comment: Reads the CODE byte at (incoming DPTR + A) with movc, writes it to XDATA 0x08C6, then restores DPTR from R5:R4. Only the single byte 0x08C6 is written, though 0x08C4 is the same shape and adjacent. Neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: read_0a4a_minus_carry
comment: Loads the byte at XDATA 0x0A4A into A and executes subb A,#0x00, which is the identity on the value apart from subtracting whatever carry the caller left set. The masked value and the carry it inherits both go back to the caller, and this listing does not say what the flag held on entry. 0x0A4A has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_089a_to_3c
comment: Writes the constant 0x3C to XDATA 0x089A and returns, leaving DPTR at 0x089A. Nothing is read and no condition is tested, so the byte is set unconditionally. 0x089A has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: read_be16_0a48
comment: Loads XDATA 0x0A49 into R7, then loads XDATA 0x0A48 into A and returns it, so the 16-bit value at 0x0A48/0x0A49 comes back big-endian across A and R7. Neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: sub_0a4e_against_4d_with_borrow
comment: Loads the byte at the caller's DPTR and subtracts 0x61 with subb, discards that result, then loads XDATA 0x0A4E and subtracts 0x4D, also with subb, so the first subtraction's borrow decrements the second. The value returned in A is 0x0A4E minus 0x4D minus one when the caller's byte was below 0x61, with the final borrow in CY, and no branch is taken on either. 0x0A4E has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: copy_043d_to_09cd_and_return_09cd
comment: Copies the byte at XDATA 0x043D to XDATA 0x09CD, then reads 0x09CD back into A and returns it. The asm returns the destination, not the source as the decompiled C says. 0x043D is XDATA_043D in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, an EC-side site found with its meaning not established; 0x09CD has no entry there.

name: init_xdata_from_code_table_64fd
comment: Writes 0x18 to XDATA 0x1674, then loops 90 times with a counter in direct RAM at 0x69 running from 0x00 to 0x59. Each iteration reads a three-byte record from CODE at 0x64FD + 3*i — the first two bytes big-endian as the XDATA destination, the third as the value — and writes the value to that destination; both offsets come from lcall 0x7110, which adds A*B to DPTR with B set to 3. DPTR is left pointing wherever the last record sent it, and the table's contents are not decoded here. 0x1674 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: clear_1610
comment: Writes 0x00 to XDATA 0x1610 and returns, leaving DPTR at 0x1610. Nothing is read and no condition is tested. 0x1610 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_1610_40_and_clear_1601_bit0
comment: Sets XDATA 0x1610 to 0x40, then clears bit 0 of XDATA 0x1601 by reading that byte, masking it and writing it back. The callee at 0xC4F0 writes 0x40 through the caller's DPTR and then repoints DPTR at 0x1601 without restoring it, so the masked value lands on 0x1601 — not on 0x1610, which is where the decompiled C puts it. Neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_1615_40_and_clear_1807
comment: Writes 0x40 to XDATA 0x1615 and 0x00 to XDATA 0x1807, leaving DPTR at 0x1807. Both writes are unconditional and nothing is read. Neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_16xx_40_and_clear_1601_bits_1_3_6
comment: Makes three passes, each calling 0xC4F0 to write 0x40 through the caller's DPTR and returning XDATA 0x1601 in A, masking one bit off that byte and storing the result: bit 1 while 0x1611 is set to 0x40, bit 3 while 0x1613 is set to 0x40, bit 6 while 0x1616 is set to 0x40. Because the callee leaves DPTR at 0x1601, all three masked writes land on 0x1601, not on the three 0x16xx bytes the decompiled C shows. None of the four addresses has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: clear_1611_1613_and_1616
comment: Clears XDATA 0x1611, 0x1613 and 0x1616 in turn, reusing the A cleared once at the top, and leaves DPTR at 0x1616. Nothing is read and no condition is tested. None of the three addresses has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_1608_bit5
comment: Reads XDATA 0x1608, ORs in 0x20 and writes the byte back, i.e. sets bit 5 and leaves every other bit as it was. 0x1608 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: clear_1608_bit5
comment: Reads XDATA 0x1608, ANDs with 0xDF and writes the byte back, i.e. clears bit 5 and leaves every other bit as it was. 0x1608 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_1601_bit4
comment: Reads XDATA 0x1601, ORs in 0x10 and writes the byte back, i.e. sets bit 4 and leaves every other bit as it was. 0x1601 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: clear_1601_bit4
comment: Reads XDATA 0x1601, ANDs with 0xEF and writes the byte back, i.e. clears bit 4 and leaves every other bit as it was. 0x1601 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: dispatch_1608_bit5_on_06e3

name: test_1606_bit4_inverted

name: nop_stub_c333

name: test_1667_bit0
comment: Loads A from XDATA 0x1667 and leaves 1 in R7 if bit 0 is set, 0 if it is clear: JNB on bit 0 jumps to the R7=0 return. 0x1667 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so the bit is not named. C356 immediately after is the same test on the same bit with the polarity inverted.

name: test_1667_bit0_inverted

name: write_40_to_1641
comment: Writes the constant 0x40 to XDATA 0x1641 and returns. The whole byte is overwritten; there is no read-modify-write. 0x1641 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so the value's meaning is not decoded further.

name: write_80_to_1641
comment: Writes the constant 0x80 to XDATA 0x1641 and returns, replacing the whole byte rather than merging bits. Pairs with C363, which stores 0x40 to the same address. 0x1641 is not in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: clear_1607_bit1
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x1607 into A, clears bit 1 (ANL A,#0xfd) and writes it back. No other address is touched. 0x1607 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so the bit is not named.

name: clear_1607_bit2
comment: Reads XDATA 0x1607, clears bit 2 (ANL A,#0xfb) and writes the byte back. Same one-bit read-modify-write shape as C371, C39E and C3A6, which all operate on this same byte. 0x1607 is not in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_1607_bit6
comment: Reads XDATA 0x1607, sets bit 6 (ORL A,#0x40) and writes the byte back. The counterpart of C3A6, which clears the same bit. 0x1607 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: route_074c_nibble_to_160a_and_1608
comment: Calls C4F8, which returns XDATA 0x074C & 0x0f and leaves DPTR pointing at 0x074C. If that nibble is 4 or 6 the function clears bit 5 of XDATA 0x160A and returns; otherwise it calls C4F8 a second time and, if the nibble is 0 or 3, sets bit 3 of XDATA 0x1608, else clears bit 3. Both nibble tests re-read the same byte at 0x074C (DPTR is not reloaded between them), not two different registers. 0x074C is not in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so what the nibble encodes is not decoded further.

name: test_1668_bit4
comment: Loads A from XDATA 0x1668 and leaves 1 in R7 when bit 4 is set, 0 when it is clear: JNB on bit 4 jumps to the R7=0 return. 0x1668 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so the bit is not named.

name: set_1609_bit0_and_write_44_to_2006
comment: Sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x1609 with a read-modify-write (ORL A,#0x01), then overwrites XDATA 0x2006 with the constant 0x44. Two independent XDATA addresses in one call, and nothing else is touched. Neither 0x1609 nor 0x2006 is in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: clear_1609_bit0_and_write_04_to_2006
comment: Clears bit 0 of XDATA 0x1609 (ANL A,#0xfe), then overwrites XDATA 0x2006 with the constant 0x04. Same pair of addresses as C43F with both values changed. Neither address is in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_1609_bit2
comment: Sets bit 2 of XDATA 0x1609 with a read-modify-write (ORL A,#0x04) and returns; no other XDATA or CODE address is touched. 0x1609 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so the bit is not named.

name: clear_1609_bit2
comment: Clears bit 2 of XDATA 0x1609 with a read-modify-write (ANL A,#0xfb) and returns; the counterpart of C468 on the same bit. 0x1609 is not in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_160a_bit0_unless_b8f4_and_08eb
comment: Calls B8F4 and tests the R7 it leaves: if R7 is 0, or R7 is non-zero and bit 7 of XDATA 0x08EB is clear, it sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x160A. The only case in which 0x160A is left untouched is R7 non-zero together with bit 7 of 0x08EB set. 0x08EB is not in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, and what B8F4's R7 encodes is not decoded here.

name: clear_160a_bit0
comment: Reads XDATA 0x160A, clears bit 0 (ANL A,#0xfe) and writes the byte back. 0x160A has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so the bit is not named.

name: set_160a_bit1
comment: Reads XDATA 0x160A, sets bit 1 (ORL A,#0x02) and writes the byte back. 0x160A is not in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_160a_bit2
comment: Reads XDATA 0x160A, sets bit 2 (ORL A,#0x04) and writes the byte back. 0x160A is not in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: test_166a_bit7_inverted
comment: Loads A from XDATA 0x166A and leaves 1 in R7 when bit 7 is clear, 0 when it is set: JB on bit 7 jumps to the R7=0 return. 0x166A has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so the bit is not named.

name: write_40_to_dptr_then_read_1601
comment: Writes 0x40 to whatever XDATA address DPTR holds on entry -- DPTR is not assigned anywhere in this listing, so the target is whatever the caller left there -- then loads DPTR with 0x1601, reads that byte into A and returns it. The decompiled C renders the first store as *param_1, an inferred pointer argument rather than a decoded one. Neither 0x1601 nor the caller's DPTR value is in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: read_074c_low_nibble
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x074C, reads the byte, masks it with 0x0f and returns the low nibble in A. DPTR is left pointing at 0x074C, which is why C3AE can re-read the same byte after calling this. 0x074C has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so the nibble is not named.

name: select_0027_0028_from_five_probes
comment: Calls 0xB8CD, 0xB8DA, 0xB8C0, 0xB8E7 and 0xB8F4 in that order, each returning a flag in R7, and writes a constant pair to XDATA 0x0027/0x0028 for the first one that returns non-zero: 0xB8CD gives 0x66/0x8B, 0xB8DA 0x67/0x8B, 0xB8C0 0x67/0x0B, 0xB8E7 0x68/0x0B, 0xB8F4 0x68/0x8B. If all five return zero it writes 0x66/0x0B. No return value is set and no other XDATA is touched; each of the five probes is a 13-byte compare of XDATA 0x0770 against one constant, and neither 0x0027, 0x0028 nor 0x0770 has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: kbd_status_from_0826_low_bits
comment: Masks KBD_STATUS at XDATA 0x078C with 0x0F so only its low nibble survives, then ORs in bits 2..0 of XDATA 0x0826 shifted up to positions 7..5: the swap/rlc/and-0xE0 sequence reduces to exactly that, and the bit the rotate carries in from the earlier anl is discarded by the 0xE0 mask. Returns XDATA 0x0826 plus 0x3B in A. 0x0826 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_support2_bit5_and_bios_oem2_bit6
comment: Read-modify-writes bit 5 of SUPPORT_2 at XDATA 0x0766 and bit 6 of BIOS_OEM_2 at XDATA 0x0782, setting both unconditionally; no other byte is read or written and nothing is branched on. registers.yaml records 0x0782 bit 6 as ENABLE_CHINA_MODE upstream but attaches no bit meaning to 0x0766, and gives both bytes status present-untested.

name: clear_kbd_status_bit1_return_0826
comment: Clears bit 1 of KBD_STATUS at XDATA 0x078C with an AND of 0xFD, then loads DPTR with 0x0826, reads that byte into A and returns it. It is the complement of 0xC9FF, which writes the same byte. 0x0826 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: dptr_from_r7_plus_00d0
comment: Loads A with 0xD0, adds R7, writes the low byte to DPL and the overflow carry (as 0 or 1) to DPH, then returns with A holding that carry, so DPTR becomes 0x00D0+R7 and the caller can read through it. It touches no XDATA and calls nothing. Its two callers at 0xC6A8 and 0xC6E5 both use the returned pointer immediately.

name: dptr_from_a_with_carry_as_high_byte
comment: Takes A as the low byte of a pointer: writes A to DPL, then writes the current carry as 0 or 1 to DPH, and returns with A equal to that carry. It reads and writes no XDATA, calls nothing, and never sets the carry itself, so the high half is whatever the caller left. Reached directly from 0xC6B5 and 0xC6F2, and by falling through from 0xCA39.

name: read_0490_and_leave_dptr_0826
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0490, reads that byte into A, then immediately overwrites DPTR with 0x0826 and returns. The decompiled C drops the second DPTR write, so the .asm is the only statement that the caller sees DPTR pointing at 0x0826 on return; the three callers at 0xC5AB, 0xC609 and 0xC84B read through it. Neither 0x0490 nor 0x0826 has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: read_fan_mode_bits_4_and_7
comment: Reads MANUAL_FAN_CTRL at XDATA 0x0751, masks it with 0x90 and returns bits 4 and 7 unchanged -- FAN_MODE_TURBO and FAN_MODE_USER in upstream's naming, per registers.yaml. No other byte is read or written. registers.yaml gives this address status present-untested and records that the six live mode switches each wrote it alone, with nothing else in XDATA moving.

name: tick_06ea_against_period_in_0a56
comment: Stores the incoming R6:R7 pair big-endian into XDATA 0x0A56/0x0A57, then calls 0x70E4 to add 0x0001 to the big-endian 16-bit counter at 0x06EA/0x06EB. It reloads 0x0A56/0x0A57 and subtracts it from the counter with a borrow chain; if the counter has reached or passed it, both halves of 0x06EA/0x06EB are zeroed and R7 is set to 1, otherwise R7 is set to 0. The period is supplied by the caller in R6:R7, and neither address pair has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: init_clear_00f5_and_1304_bit2
comment: Clears XDATA 0x00F5, clears bit 2 of XDATA 0x1304 with an AND of 0xFB, clears direct byte 0x02, calls 0x397D and then tail-jumps to 0xD3C8, so it never returns to its own caller. It shares its body with the separate entry at 0xCC51, which runs the same two subroutines in the opposite order and also sets bit 4 of 0x1304. Neither 0x00F5 nor 0x1304 has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: init_set_1304_bit4_and_clear_bit2
comment: Calls 0xD3C8, then rewrites XDATA 0x1304 twice -- clearing bit 2 with 0xFB and then setting bit 4 with 0x10 -- clears direct byte 0x02, and tail-jumps to 0x397D, so it never returns to its own caller. The entry at 0xCC3D performs the same two calls in the opposite order and does not set bit 4. 0x1304 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: init_06e6_1_clear_0743_07c5_and_07d5_ff
comment: An initialisation pass that writes 1 to 0x06E6. It clears bits 0 and 1 of CTGP_DB_CTRL at 0x0743 with an AND of 0xFA, clears bit 5 of 0x07C5 with an AND of 0xDF, writes 0xFF to 0x0788 and then to DBAP at 0x07D5, sets bits 7, 6 and 3 of 0x200D in three read-modify-writes, calls 0x2896, writes 0x01 to 0x06E6 and then to 0x0988, calls 0xCC51, 0x189A, 0xC4C9 and 0xB461, zeroes 0x0787 and CPU_TCC_OFFSET at 0x0786, writes 0x19 to 0x09CE, then sets or clears bit 4 of 0x08EB according to the bit of 0x0490 read immediately before it, zeroes 0x08A5 and 0x08A6, and returns. The branch that picks between setting and clearing bit 4 of 0x08EB is a jb acc.1, but DPTR was reloaded to 0x08EB before it while A still held the byte read from 0x0490, so the bit tested belongs to 0x0490 and not to 0x08EB. The entry is reached through the common-area bank-select trampoline that sets DPTR to this entry and jumps to the bank-0 select stub; the exact thunk is cited in the evidence. The 1 written to 0x06E6 is the discriminator that separates this entry from its two siblings, which write 3 and 5; what the three values select is not shown here. 0x07C5, 0x0787, 0x0788, 0x200D, 0x08A5, 0x08A6, 0x0490, 0x06E6 and 0x0988 have no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: power_on_init_and_two_hang_paths
comment: Writes 5 to XDATA 0x06E6, calls 0xCC3D, 0x18AC, 0xC4D1, 0xD084 and 0x2896, then clears bit 6 of OEM_4_CHARGING_PROFILE at 0x07A6, bit 7 of 0x07C5, bit 2 of AP_OEM_6 at 0x07C6, bit 1 of 0x1106, bit 3 of 0x08E2 and bit 2 of 0x08EB. If bit 2 of 0x08EB was set on the read before it was cleared, it writes 0x18 to 0x1063, calls 0xD065, writes 0x55/0xAA/0x5A to 0x07FE/0x07FF/0x07FD, and then spins forever on an sjmp to itself. If instead 0x077E reads 0xA5 and 0x077F reads 0x78, it zeroes both, calls 0xD73D, 0x5597 with R7=0, 0xD6F4, 0x0EA2 with R7=0x0A and 0xD065, and also spins forever; with neither condition it returns. 0x07C5, 0x1106, 0x08E2, 0x1063, 0x077E/0x077F and the 0x07FE-0x07FF triple have no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml; 0x08EB is now carried there as XDATA_08EB.

name: walk_index_06e7_up_to_1e_table_6bca
comment: Loops on the index byte at XDATA 0x06E7: a value of 0x1F or more returns index minus 0x1F. Below that it forms DPTR = 0x6B00 + index*5 + 0xCA and movc's a byte from CODE there; a non-zero byte branches to 0xCE1A, a zero byte calls 0xCFF6 (which loads a 16-bit table field into 0x06E8/0x06E9), then 0xD029 and 0xD041, and a zero result jumps back to the top. The 0xCE1A path calls 0xD038 and 0xD029; on a non-zero R7 on return it zeroes 0x06EA/0x06EB, calls 0xCFF6 and increments XDATA 0x06E7. What the CODE table holds is not decoded here, and none of 0x06E7, 0x06E8/0x06E9 or 0x06EA/0x06EB has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: walk_index_06e7_up_to_17_table_6c65
comment: Loops on the index byte at XDATA 0x06E7: a value of 0x18 or more returns index minus 0x18. Below that it forms DPTR = 0x6C00 + index*5 + 0x65 and movc's a byte from CODE there; a non-zero byte branches to 0xCE77, a zero byte calls 0xD038, 0xD005, computes 0x6C00 + index*5 + 0x61, then calls 0xD029 and 0xD041, and a zero result jumps back to the top. The 0xCE77 path calls 0xD038 and 0xD029; on a non-zero R7 on return it zeroes 0x06EA/0x06EB, calls 0xD038 and 0xD005, and stores the returned value plus one through the pointer 0xD005 leaves at 0x06E7. What the CODE table holds is not decoded here, and none of 0x06E7, 0x06E8/0x06E9 or 0x06EA/0x06EB has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: load_index_06e7_head_of_cea2_loop
comment: Two instructions: loads DPTR with XDATA 0x06E7 and reads the index byte into A, then falls straight into the entry at 0xCEA2. The 0xCEA2 listing is this same instruction stream read from four bytes further in, and the jz at 0xCED0 branches back to this address, so 0xCE9E is the loop head rather than a separate operation. Its only reference is the ljmp at 0xCF87; what the loop does is described on the 0xCEA2 row.

name: walk_index_06e7_up_to_0d_table_6cdd
comment: The body of the loop whose head is at 0xCE9E: a value of 0x0E or more at XDATA 0x06E7 returns index minus 0x0E. Below that it forms DPTR = 0x6C00 + index*5 + 0xDD and movc's a byte from CODE there; a non-zero byte branches to 0xCED3, a zero byte calls 0xD01A (which falls into the indirect jump at 0xD029), 0xD038, 0xD005 and 0xD045, and a zero result jumps back to 0xCE9E. The 0xCED3 path calls 0xD01A and checks R7 on return; on a non-zero result it calls 0xD038 and 0xD005, then stores the returned value plus one through the pointer 0xD005 leaves at 0x06E7. What the CODE table holds is not decoded here, and none of 0x06E7, 0x06E8/0x06E9 or 0x06EA/0x06EB has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: walk_index_06e7_up_to_10_table_6d23
comment: Loops on the index byte at XDATA 0x06E7: a value of 0x11 or more returns index minus 0x11. Below that it forms DPTR = 0x6D00 + index*5 + 0x23 and movc's a byte from CODE there; a non-zero byte branches to 0xCF28, a zero byte calls 0xD038, 0xD029, 0xD038, 0xD005 and 0xD045, and a zero result jumps back to 0xCEE9. The 0xCF28 path calls 0xD038 and 0xD029 and checks R7 on return; on a non-zero result it calls 0xD038 and 0xD005, then stores the returned value plus one through the pointer 0xD005 leaves at 0x06E7. What the CODE table holds is not decoded here, and none of 0x06E7, 0x06E8/0x06E9 or 0x06EA/0x06EB has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: dispatch_06e6_after_counting_down_06e8_pair
comment: Reads the big-endian 16-bit counter at XDATA 0x06E8/0x06E9; while it is non-zero it calls 0x70E4 to subtract 0x0001, re-reads it and returns if it is still non-zero, so the dispatch runs only once the counter has reached zero. It then dispatches on XDATA 0x06E6: 0x82 tail-jumps to 0xCE9E, 0x83 to 0xCEE9, 0x84 to 0xCE37, 0x81 clears bit 7 of AP_OEM at XDATA 0x0741, clears XDATA 0x0816 and tail-jumps to 0xCDE4, and any other value clears 0x06E6 and returns. registers.yaml documents bit 7 of 0x0741 as the BIOS overclock-recovery request and notes that which EC code sets it was not traced there; 0x06E6, 0x06E7, 0x06E8/0x06E9 and 0x0816 have no entry.

name: arm_index_06e7_for_dispatch_06e6
comment: Writes 1 to XDATA 0x06E7, clears both halves of the 16-bit pair 0x06E8/0x06E9, and stores the incoming R7 into XDATA 0x06E6 -- that is, it sets the index and the countdown that the routine at 0xCF48 consumes. The one caller in this bank passes R7 = 0x81 from 0xCFA9, which is the value 0xCF48 dispatches on. No other byte is read or written, and none of 0x06E6, 0x06E7 or 0x06E8/0x06E9 has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: bank1_switch_thunk_to_81c5
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x81C5 and jumps to the shared trampoline at 0x1114, which pushes the return address and DPH:DPL, stores 0x1E in direct byte 0x08, and drives P1 bits 0-2 to 1, 0, 0. A pure tail thunk: no XDATA is read or written here, and the CODE address 0x81C5 it names is in bank 1 and is not decoded in this listing.

name: bank1_switch_thunk_to_823a
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x823A and jumps to the shared trampoline at 0x1114, which pushes the return address and DPH:DPL, stores 0x1E in direct byte 0x08, and drives P1 bits 0-2 to 1, 0, 0. A pure tail thunk: no XDATA is read or written here, and the CODE address 0x823A it names is in bank 1 and is not decoded in this listing.

name: bank1_switch_thunk_to_8261
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x8261 and jumps to the shared trampoline at 0x1114, which pushes the return address and DPH:DPL, stores 0x1E in direct byte 0x08, and drives P1 bits 0-2 to 1, 0, 0. A pure tail thunk: no XDATA is read or written here, and the CODE address 0x8261 it names is in bank 1 and is not decoded in this listing.

name: init_ccfc_then_bank1_thunk_818a
comment: Two instructions: calls the long initialisation routine at 0xCCFC, then tail-jumps to 0x18C4, the bank-1 thunk that loads DPTR with 0x818A and jumps to the shared switch trampoline at 0x1114. It never returns to its own caller, and nothing is read or written here outside those two transfers.

name: collect_two_flags_into_0816_then_raise_ap_oem_bit7
comment: Runs three iterations of a counter held in R5; each iteration calls 0xD078 twice, and a first return of 0x14 sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x0816 while a second return of 0x32 from the same call sets bit 1 -- the two calls sit at the same point in the loop, so both tests see the same value. After the loop, if XDATA 0x0816 reads exactly 3 it sets bit 7 of AP_OEM at XDATA 0x0741, which registers.yaml documents as the BIOS overclock-recovery request. What address 0xD078 reads is not determined from this listing, and 0x0816 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: load_stride5_table_word_into_06e8_pair
comment: Forms DPTR = 0x6B00 + (XDATA 0x06E7 * 5) + 0xC8 and then falls straight into the entry at 0xD005, which movc's the two CODE bytes at that address, storing the first at XDATA 0x06E8 and the second at 0x06E9, before returning XDATA 0x06E7 in A. The export splits the routine only because 0xD005 is itself a call target; entered at 0xCFF6 the two listings are one operation, and both of its callers are inside the walker at 0xCDE4. None of these addresses has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: movc_two_code_bytes_into_06e8_06e9
comment: Takes the high half of a code pointer in A and the low half already in DPTR, movc's the byte at DPTR into R7 and the byte at DPTR+1 into A, then stores them to XDATA 0x06E8 and 0x06E9 in that order (first code byte at the lower address) and returns XDATA 0x06E7 in A. Its six callers all build the pointer from that same index. Neither address pair has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: indirect_code_jump_via_stride5_table_6cd9
comment: Forms DPTR = 0x6C00 + (XDATA 0x06E7 * 5) + 0xD9 and then falls straight into the entry at 0xD029, which movc's the two CODE bytes at that address and jumps to the address they spell. The export splits the routine only because 0xD029 is itself a call target; entered at 0xD01A the two listings are one operation, and its two callers are both inside the walker at 0xCEA2.

name: code_jump_to_two_bytes_at_dptr
comment: Takes the high half of a code pointer in A and the low half already in DPTR, movc's the byte at DPTR into R6 and the byte at DPTR+1 through R2, leaves the pair in R2:R1 and tail-jumps to 0x7177, which starts by loading DPTR from R2:R1. What 0x7177 then does with it is not decoded further: its own .c reports an unrecoverable jump table at 0x717C, and its listing is a run of register exchanges and direct-byte writes ending in xch A,0x82 / ret. R1, R2 and R6 are all clobbered, and all six callers are inside the XDATA 0x06E7 table walkers in this bank.

name: mul_06e7_by_5
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x06E7 into A, loads B with the constant 5 and executes MUL AB, so the 16-bit product is left in A:B with A the low byte. No other XDATA byte is read or written and nothing else is touched.

name: read_06e7
comment: The listing for this entry is only MOV DPTR,#0x06E7 followed by MOVX A,@DPTR, so as labelled it just fetches that byte into A. The bytes at the next entry, 0xD045, continue the same stream and increment the value there, so the increment the .c reports for this function belongs to that continuation; the split between 0xD041 and 0xD045 is a boundary hypothesis, not something the listing shows.

name: inc_06e7_clear_06ea_eb_read_06e8
comment: Increments A and stores it back through the caller's DPTR, which the preceding 0xD041 entry has set to 0x06E7, so the byte at 0x06E7 is incremented. It then clears 0x06EA and 0x06EB to zero, reads the byte at 0x06E8 into A and returns it.

name: add2_06e7
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x06E7, increments it, writes it back, then reads it again, increments it a second time and writes it back: a net +2 modulo 256 on that one byte. Nothing else is read or written.

name: set_06ec_1
comment: Writes the constant 1 to XDATA 0x06EC and leaves the same value in A and R7 before returning. No byte is read and no other location is touched.

name: init_1f01_1f06_1f07
comment: Writes three constants unconditionally and in order: 0x20 to XDATA 0x1F01, 0x01 to 0x1F06 and 0x5A to 0x1F07. Nothing is read, so none of the three values is derived from existing state.

name: set_0988_1
comment: Writes the constant 1 to XDATA 0x0988 and returns. No byte is read and no other location is touched.

name: dispatch_on_0860
comment: Early-out gates: the byte at XDATA 0x0860 being 0x00 or 0xFF, or bit 0 set in 0x1C00, 0x1C11 or 0x1C29, each ljmp to 0xD2BE, which is a bare RET. Otherwise it copies six bytes (0x1C04, 0x1C05, 0x1C15, 0x1C16, 0x1C39, 0x1C3A) into 0x0866-0x086B, and writes 0x48 to 0x0865 when 0x0860 is one of 0x06/0x16/0x36/0x07/0x17/0x37, 0x4C when it is one of 0x08/0x18/0x38/0x09/0x19/0x39, and 0 otherwise; it then calls 0x7151 with A holding the byte at 0x0860. CORRECTION 2026-09-24, issue #180: the 40 bytes from 0xD14B are a CODE table, not code. This supersedes the earlier reading of the same bytes as ACALLs to 0xD673, 0xD698, 0xD6C0 and 0xD6EF interleaved with INC and DEC of @R0, @R1, R0 and R1, SETB of bit addresses 0x21, 0x4E and 0x89, and two NOPs, and the "not settled by the listing" that closed it. The island is the inline table the 0x7151 reader consumes -- the same reader the table at 0x8038 uses, which pops the return address this function's lcall at 0xD148 pushed. Read as (big-endian address, case byte) triples it is 12 well-formed entries at file 0x0D14B-0x0D16E, a 0x0000 terminator at 0x0D16F, and a default of 0xD289 at 0x0D171, which is clear_0860. The case values are exactly the twelve the comparison chain above tests: 0x06 and 0x08 reach 0xD173, 0x07 and 0x09 reach 0xD198, 0x16 and 0x18 reach 0xD1C0, 0x17 and 0x19 reach 0xD1EF, 0x36 and 0x38 reach 0xD221, and 0x37 and 0x39 reach 0xD24E. Re-derived with `ec/tools/decode_index_table.py ec/firmware/GMxMGxx_11.800 --at 0xD148`, which checks the entry layout against the reader rather than against a linear disassembly, and reports the table well-formed. Note that the .asm's linear decode of the same bytes -- the ACALLs and SETBs named in that superseded reading -- is that data read as instructions and is not a reading of the table; the targets it names are 0x500 higher than the table's. Per-address table: ec/annotations/xdata-086x-dispatch.md. The tail writes 0x0863 to 0x1C04, calls 0xD2CB on the byte at 0x0864, ANDs the result with 0xFE and passes it to 0xD2DA, spins on 0xD2BF until it returns non-zero, then branches on 0xD319: a zero result stores A through the then-current DPTR and ljmps to 0xD28E, a non-zero result ljmps to 0xD284.

name: poll_d6c2_then_branch
comment: The entry's first byte pair decodes as SETB of bit address 0x54, which is bit 4 of internal RAM byte 0x2A; A is then copied to R6 and 0xD304 is called. It then loops, loading DPTR with 0x1C35 and calling 0xD2C2 until that call returns non-zero, and calls 0xD319 once. A zero result stores A through the current DPTR and sjmps to 0xD28E, a non-zero result sjmps to 0xD284. The store of the constant 1 that the .c shows as _a_4 is not in the listing.

name: store_dp_to_0864_then_d289
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's current DPTR, stores it to XDATA 0x0864 and sjmps to 0xD289. The entry contains no return of its own; the value stored is the byte at whatever address the caller left in DPTR.

name: set_0860_ff_then_d284
comment: The listing for this entry is a single MOV DPTR,#0x0860. The bytes at the next entry, 0xD284, load A with 0xFF, store it through that DPTR and sjmps to 0xD28E, so on a fall-through reading this entry is one way to reach the 0x0860 = 0xFF store; whether it is a genuine entry point or a mis-split boundary is not shown by the listing.

name: write_ff_to_dptr_then_d28e
comment: Loads A with 0xFF, stores it through the caller's current DPTR and sjmps to 0xD28E. The address that receives the 0xFF is therefore whatever XDATA location the caller left in DPTR, which this listing does not fix.

name: clear_0860
comment: The listing is CLR A, MOV DPTR,#0x0860, MOVX @DPTR,A: it writes zero to XDATA 0x0860 and has no return of its own. The six stores to 0x1C04, 0x1C05, 0x1C15, 0x1C16, 0x1C39 and 0x1C3A that the .c attributes to this function are the block at 0xD28E, into which this entry falls.

name: copy_0866_86b_to_1c04_1c3a
comment: Copies six bytes, each read with MOVX A,@DPTR and written back with MOVX @DPTR,A: 0x0866 to 0x1C04, 0x0867 to 0x1C05, 0x0868 to 0x1C15, 0x0869 to 0x1C16, 0x086A to 0x1C39 and 0x086B to 0x1C3A. The listing ends at 0xD2BD with no return; the next entry, 0xD2BE, is the RET that follows.

name: set_dptr_1c00_then_d2c2
comment: The listing for this entry is a single MOV DPTR,#0x1C00. The bytes at the next entry, 0xD2C2, read the byte at that address, copy it to XDATA 0x086C and return it masked with 0x7E, which is the body the .c reports for this function.

name: copy_dp_to_086c_return_masked_7e
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's current DPTR, stores it to XDATA 0x086C, re-reads it from 0x086C, masks it with 0x7E and returns the result in A. The source address is the caller's choice: 0xD236 calls it with DPTR = 0x1C35, and the fall-through reading of 0xD2BF reaches the same block with DPTR = 0x1C00.

name: store_a_to_1c05_then_d2d2
comment: Stores A to XDATA 0x1C05 and then loads DPTR with 0x1C00, where the listing ends. The bytes at the next entry, 0xD2D2, write 0xFF through that DPTR, read 0x0861 and return it, which is the behaviour the .c reports for this function.

name: write_ff_to_dptr_return_0861
comment: Loads A with 0xFF and stores it through the caller's current DPTR, then reads XDATA 0x0861 into A and returns that value. The 0xFF store lands on whatever address the caller left in DPTR.

name: stage_1c03_1c02_1c01
comment: Stores A to XDATA 0x1C03, then copies 0x0862 to 0x1C02 and 0x0865 to 0x1C01, and returns. It reads two XDATA bytes and writes three, with no branching.

name: mask_dp_byte_7c_reset_dptr_0860
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's current DPTR, masks it with 0x7C and leaves the masked value in A. As a side effect it reloads DPTR with 0x0860 before returning, so a caller that relies on DPTR surviving the call is affected. What the surviving bits 0x7C represent is not decoded.

name: tick_dd_da_dc
comment: If the byte at XDATA 0x00DD is non-zero it is decremented and the function returns immediately. Otherwise, if 0x00DA is non-zero, 0xD567 is called, 0x00DD is set to 0x14 and 0x00DC is incremented. Otherwise 0xD6D4 is called and, if it returns non-zero, 0xD358 is called; 0x00DA is then re-read and, if it is still non-zero, 0xD567 is called again and 0x00DD is set to 0x02. No other location is touched.

name: advance_d9_and_set_1500_20
comment: Calls 0xD6D4; a zero return goes straight to the RET. Otherwise it copies the byte at XDATA 0x00D9, read after a call to 0xD6DF, to 0x00DA and then to 0x00DE, and if 0x00DA is non-zero it ORs 0x20 into the byte at 0x1500. It then increments 0x00D9 and clears it to zero once the incremented value has reached 7; the value left in A is the incremented byte minus 7 in that case and 0 otherwise, which is what the .c returns as cVar3.

name: store_r7_at_d8_advance_index
comment: Increments the byte at XDATA 0x00DF, then sets DPTR to 0x00D8, calls 0xD6DF and stores R7, not A, into 0x00D8. It increments 0x00D8 and clears it to zero when it reaches 7, then compares 0x00D8 with 0x00D9; on a match it increments 0x00DB and sets 0x00D8 to 7 if it is 0, otherwise it decrements 0x00D8 by one.

name: zero_d0_d7_and_state
comment: R7 is set to 8 and a loop clears eight consecutive XDATA bytes starting at 0x00D0, DPTR incrementing between the MOVX @DPTR,A stores. It then clears 0x00D8, 0x00D9 and 0x00DA, ANDs 0x20 out of the byte at 0x1500, clears the direct address 0x6D, which is internal RAM and which the .c labels _d_5, and returns.

name: ret_only_d433
comment: A single RET and nothing else: no register, flag or XDATA byte is touched. It appears as a function entry in the call-target census, but which callers reach it is not visible from this listing.

name: forward_to_1906
comment: A single LJMP to 0x1906 in the common area: there is no body here and no return path, so the function is a pure jump stub. The decompiler's C instead reads the instruction as a call to bl51_bank_select_1(0x8652), but 0x8652 does not appear in these bytes and the opcode is a jump, not a call.

name: set_bits_0_and_4_of_3206
comment: Read-modify-writes the XDATA byte at 0x3206 four times, setting bit 4, clearing bit 0, setting bit 4 again and finally setting bit 0, so the byte is left with bits 0 and 4 set and the other six unchanged. Each write is preceded by a fresh read of the same address, which only matters if 0x3206 has write-1-to-clear or write-0-to-clear bits. 0x3206 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: read_xdata_0400_plus_r7
comment: Stores 0x04 to internal RAM 0xB7 and the incoming R7 to 0xB8, builds DPTR as 0x0400+R7 (DPH hard-set to 0x04, DPL loaded from R7), reads the byte at that XDATA address into internal RAM 0x69 and returns it in R7. The two internal-RAM stores are a side effect of the call and nothing in the listing says what they are for. The value in R7 is not decoded here, so the XDATA address cannot be tied to any register in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: write_r5_to_0400_plus_r7
comment: Stores 0x04 to internal RAM 0xB7 and R7 to 0xB8, reads the 0xB7 value back into R4, loads DPTR with 0x0400+R7 and writes R5 to that XDATA address, then tail-jumps to 0x1936 with no RET of its own. The decompiler's C reads 0xB7 as a pointer and dereferences it, but the instruction at 0xD594 is a direct store to internal RAM 0xB7, so the C's pointer dereference is not what the bytes do. The value in R7 is not decoded here, so the address written cannot be tied to any register in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: write_33_to_1501_join_loop_d5db
comment: Loads DPTR with XDATA 0x1501, loads A with 0x33 and jumps into the middle of the 0xD5DB loop at 0xD607, where the byte is stored, internal RAM 0x0B is cleared and control rejoins the loop head. That is the whole function: the large body in its .c is the code at 0xD5DB and beyond, which the call-target census attributes to other entries. 0x1500-0x1504 and 0x1510-0x1514 include no entry for these addresses in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: write_5a_to_1f07_then_spin
comment: The leading MOVX @DPTR,A completes a 0x01 write to XDATA 0x1F06 that the bytes before 0xD6C0 set up, so the call-target boundary splits one store across two entries. It then writes 0x5A to XDATA 0x1F07 and executes SJMP 0xD6C7, a jump to its own address that spins forever with no RET. Neither 0x1F06 nor 0x1F07 is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: call_0ea2_twice_with_fa
comment: Calls 0x0EA2 twice with R7=0xFA loaded before each call, then returns, with no register or memory access of its own. DPTR is not set here, so each call operates on whatever address the caller left in it, and the two calls are only equivalent if DPTR is unchanged between them, which this listing does not show. No absolute address appears in these five instructions.

name: xor_00d8_00d9
comment: Reads XDATA 0x00D8 into R7, reads XDATA 0x00D9 and returns the exclusive OR of the two in A. It touches no other address and calls nothing, so it is a pure two-byte comparison whose result the caller has to interpret. Neither 0x00D8 nor 0x00D9 is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: add_d0_to_dptr_low_byte
comment: Takes the byte at the caller's DPTR, adds 0xD0 to it, puts the low result in DPL and the carry out of that add into DPH via CLR A followed by ADDC A,#0, and returns. The caller's own DPH is not preserved: the new high byte is only 0 or 1, so this is a low-byte-plus-carry pointer step rather than a 16-bit add, and the value read at @DPTR affects nothing but the carry. No absolute XDATA address appears here, and the .c's comparison-and-return body describes instructions these bytes do not contain.

name: write_a_to_dptr_set_1f06
comment: Writes A to the XDATA address in the caller's DPTR, clears A and loads DPTR with 0x1F06, then falls into the next census entry at 0xD6EF, whose first instruction performs the store of that zero to 0x1F06. The listing has no RET, so this entry never returns on its own account. 0x1F06 is not documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: write_a_to_dptr_set_1f09
comment: Writes A to the XDATA address in the caller's DPTR, loads DPTR with 0x1F09 and returns, leaving that address in DPTR for the caller. The first instruction is the store that finishes the 0x1F06 write set up at the end of 0xD6EA, so the call-target boundary splits that store in two. Neither 0x1F06 nor 0x1F09 is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: zero_0a59_0a5a_then_call_series
comment: A fixed series of eight calls with two XDATA writes between them: it calls 0x5349, 0x549B, 0x530E with R7=0, 0x549B again, writes 0 to XDATA 0x0A59, calls 0x537F with R3=0xF0, R5=0x01 and R7=0xD7, then 0x54C2 and 0x549B, sets DPTR to 0x0A5A and calls 0xD889, which zeroes that address and returns R3=0xF0, R5=0x01, R6=0x02, R7=0x00, then calls 0x53AF with those registers live and tail-jumps to 0x54C2, so there is no RET here. Only 0x0A59 and 0x0A5A are addressed directly; the bytes the callees write through the caller's DPTR are not visible from this listing, and nothing here says what the sequence accomplishes. None of 0x0A59 or 0x0A5A is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: zero_0a4b_then_tail_jump_541d
comment: Loads DPTR with XDATA 0x0A4B, calls 0xD889, which writes 0 to that address and returns R3=0xF0, R5=0x01, R6=0x02, R7=0x00, and tail-jumps to 0x541D with those register values live, so there is no RET here and control never comes back to this address. What 0x541D does with them is not shown in this listing. 0x0A4B is not documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: scatter_0200_to_table_6d74
comment: Loops 14 times with R7 running from 0 to 13. Each pass calls 0xD894 to set DPTR to XDATA 0x0200+R7, saves the byte found there in R6, calls 0xD872 to replace DPTR with a 16-bit address read big-endian from the CODE table at 0x6D74+2*R7, and writes the saved byte to that address, so it scatters the 14 bytes at XDATA 0x0200-0x020D into the 14 addresses the table holds. Which addresses those are is not decoded here. The .c renders the same loop but types the table as a C pointer into the function's own frame, which the instructions do not do.

name: gather_0200_from_table_6d74
comment: Loops 14 times with R7 running from 0 to 13, and is the mirror image of 0xD72B: each pass calls 0xD872 to set DPTR to a 16-bit address read big-endian from the CODE table at 0x6D74+2*R7, saves the byte read there in R6, calls 0xD894 to set DPTR to XDATA 0x0200+R7, and writes the saved byte to it, so it gathers 14 bytes from the table's addresses into XDATA 0x0200-0x020D. Which addresses those are is not decoded here.

name: write_33_to_1511_then_loop
comment: Loads A with 0x33, writes it to XDATA 0x1511, sets R3=0x00 and falls straight into the polling loop at 0xD757, which is the whole of this function. The large body in its .c belongs to 0xD757 and the addresses after it, which the call-target census attributes to other entries. 0x1511 is not documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: load_code_ptr_from_table_6d74
comment: Computes 0x6D74 + 2*R7, fetches the two CODE bytes at that address with MOVC and loads them into DPTR as a big-endian 16-bit pointer, the first byte going to DPH and the second to DPL, then returns. R7 is left unchanged, so the caller's index survives the call. What the table's entries point at is not decoded here.

name: zero_dptr_and_load_regs
comment: Writes 0 to the XDATA byte at the caller's DPTR, then loads R6=0x02, R7=0x00, R3=0xF0 and R5=0x01 and returns, so those four register values are the function's real output. The .c shows only the zeroing store and drops the register loads entirely.

name: set_dptr_0200_plus_r7
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0200 + R7: R7 goes to DPL and the carry out of that add becomes DPH through CLR A followed by ADDC A,#2. R7 is left unchanged, and no memory location is read or written, so the routine only computes a pointer for its caller.

name: store_r4_r5_into_record_6e65
comment: Stores R4 to XDATA 0x0A5B and R5 to 0x0A5C, then uses two XCH instructions to leave R3 holding the incoming R7 and A holding R5, and calls 0xDB3E to load DPTR from a big-endian 16-bit entry in the CODE table at 0x6E65 + 6*R3. It writes 0x80 to that XDATA address, then writes the byte at 0x0A5B to the address the table holds at 0x6E67 + 6*R3 and the byte at 0x0A5C to the address at 0x6E69 + 6*R3, and finally writes 0x00 back to the first address, so the two argument bytes land in fields 1 and 2 of a six-byte record and field 0 is set to 0x80 and then cleared again. Neither 0x0A5B nor 0x0A5C is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: nop_stub_d9d2
comment: Eight NOP instructions followed by RET: the function has no observable effect, and nothing in these bytes indicates what it is for. Its role is not determinable from this listing.

name: ret_stub
comment: A single RET and nothing else. The header of the .asm records that this boundary came from a call-target byte scan, so something in the image branches here, but that single byte gives no way to tell what the caller expected the function to do, so the role is not determinable.

name: select_0825_or_0827_into_0826
comment: Presets XDATA 0x0825 to 0x03 and 0x0827 to 0x00, calls 0xC1E7, and copies one of those two bytes into XDATA 0x0826, taking 0x0827 if 0xC1E7 returned 0 in R7 and 0x0825 otherwise. The .c makes the same branch on a value it calls param_1, but the instruction at 0xD9EA is MOV A,R7, so the selector is the callee's return value and not an argument. None of 0x0825, 0x0826, 0x0827 is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: rec_ptr_from_index_6e65
comment: Treats R3 as a 6-byte-stride table index: DPL = 0x65 + R3*6 (MUL AB by 6, then ADD #0x65) and DPH = 0x6E plus the carry of that low-byte add, the high byte of the product being dropped. It then reads the two CODE bytes at that address with MOVC and loads them into DPTR, first table byte as DPH and second as DPL. The .c collapses the DPTR into a one-byte return with an 'n'-based expression, which the .asm does not support; what the pointer is used for is not in this body.

name: stash_code_pair_to_0b7_0b8
comment: Entry takes DPH from A, which the caller has already computed, then reads the two CODE bytes at DPTR with MOVC and stores them into internal RAM 0xB7 and 0xB8, low address first. It ends with MUL AB of R7 by 3, so A:B holds R7*3 on return. Neither the 0xB7/0xB8 pair nor the R7*3 product has a decoded consumer in this body.

name: store_r7_to_table_addr
comment: Entry takes DPH from A, reads the two CODE bytes at DPTR with MOVC into R4 and A, reassembles them as DPTR with the first table byte as the high byte, then writes R7 to that XDATA address with MOVX @DPTR. One unconditional byte store to an address that comes out of the CODE table; the address is not decoded further here.

name: copy_code_byte_to_r4_r5
comment: Entry takes DPH from A, reads one CODE byte at DPTR with MOVC (A cleared first), writes that byte to the XDATA address held in R4:R5, then increments R7 and returns R7+1 in A. A one-byte CODE-to-XDATA copy; neither address is decoded further in this body.

name: stream_code_bytes_to_1201
comment: Calls 0xDC60, stores its 0 result in internal RAM 0x65 as a loop counter and walks a 16-bit CODE pointer R6:R7 starting at 0x6EAD. Each of 0x26 (38) iterations writes 0 to XDATA 0x1200, copies the CODE byte at the pointer into XDATA 0x1201, spins on bit 2 of XDATA 0x1205 until it reads clear, calls 0xDC8D (which writes 1 to 0x1200), copies the next CODE byte to 0x1201, spins on 0x1205 bit 2 again, and then increments the pointer and the counter. On exit it calls 0xDC77, then 0xDBE2, then tail-jumps to 0xDC17. What the 0x1200-0x1205 block is and what the 38 table bytes mean is not decoded here.

name: write_consts_105a_105e_1076_1079
comment: Writes nine fixed constants and reads nothing: XDATA 0x105B=0x00, 0x105C=0x40, 0x1076=0x70, 0x1077=0xC0, 0x105D=0x36, 0x105E=0x25, 0x1078=0x15, 0x1079=0x16 (an INC A on the 0x15 just stored to 0x1078) and 0x105A=0x0F. 0xDB96 calls it once after its loop, so it reads as a one-shot setup of the 0x105x/0x107x block, but what that block is not decoded here.

name: write_1201_seq_07_05_30
comment: Fixed command sequence over the XDATA 0x1200/0x1201/0x1205 block: after calling 0xDC60 it writes 0x00 to 0x1200, then 0x07 to 0x1201, and spins on bit 2 of 0x1205; it calls 0xDC8D, writes 0x05 to 0x1201 and spins; it writes 0x00 to 0x1200, then 0x30 to 0x1201 and spins; it calls 0xDC8D again, writes 0x00 to 0x1201 and spins, then calls 0xDC77. Every spin is a JB on bit 2 of a freshly read 0x1205. What the block does with these bytes is not decoded here; 0xDB96 tail-jumps into this routine.

name: set_bit0_1202_1204_1205
comment: Read-modify-write on three XDATA bytes, setting bit 0 in each with ORL #0x01: 0x1202, then 0x1204, then 0x1205. Leaves A=0 on return, which 0xDB96 stores as its loop counter. 0xDC77 is the same three bytes with bit 0 cleared; what the bit gates is not decoded here.

name: clear_bit0_1202_1204_1205
comment: Read-modify-write on XDATA 0x1202, 0x1204 and 0x1205 clearing bit 0 in each with ANL #0xFE, with no other effect. 0xDC60 sets the same three bits. Nothing about what those bits select is decoded here.

name: write_1_to_1200
comment: Writes the constant 0x01 to XDATA 0x1200 and returns; that is the whole body. 0xDB96 and 0xDC17 both call it between writes to 0x1201, while they write 0x00 to 0x1200 directly, but this two-instruction body does not show what the byte is for.

name: set_r7_1_tail_3fa4_a
comment: Loads R7 with 0x01 and tail-jumps to 0x3FA4 in the common area, so the only argument passed is the value in R7. The body at 0x3FA4 is outside this shard, so what the argument selects is not decoded. Byte-identical to 0xDCCB, 0xDCD0 and 0xDCF5, which differ from 0xDC99 only in loading 0x02.

name: set_r7_2_tail_3fa4
comment: Loads R7 with 0x02 and tail-jumps to 0x3FA4, the same two-instruction shape as 0xDC94 and its three byte-identical siblings; the 2 is the only difference. 0x3FA4 is outside this shard and what the argument selects is not decoded.

name: de4d_d991_ea0_tail_e256_a
comment: Calls 0xDE4D, then loads R4=0xE2, R5=0x56 and R7=0x01 and calls 0xD991, clears the EA SFR (opcode C2 AF, the global interrupt-enable bit) and tail-jumps to 0xE256. There is no RET of its own. Byte-identical to 0xDCBA, 0xDCFA and 0xDD10; the constants' meaning is not decoded here.

name: bank1_trampoline_a694

name: read_0454_tail_3f9d

name: de4d_d991_ea0_tail_e256_b
comment: Calls 0xDE4D, loads R4=0xE2, R5=0x56 and R7=0x01, calls 0xD991, clears the EA SFR and tail-jumps to 0xE256. Byte-identical to 0xDC9E, 0xDCFA and 0xDD10, so the _b suffix records position, not a behavioural difference.

name: set_r7_1_tail_3fa4_b

name: set_r7_1_tail_3fa4_c
comment: Loads R7 with 0x01 and tail-jumps to 0x3FA4. Byte-identical to 0xDC94, 0xDCCB and 0xDCF5; the _c suffix records position, not a behavioural difference. The 0x3FA4 body is outside this shard and the argument's meaning is not decoded.

name: read_0455_tail_3f9d

name: set_bit0_045b

name: clear_bit0_045b

name: read_0459_tail_3f9d
