name: set_r7_1_tail_3fa4_d
comment: Loads R7 with 0x01 and tail-jumps to 0x3FA4. Byte-identical to 0xDC94, 0xDCCB and 0xDCD0; the _d suffix records position, not a behavioural difference. The 0x3FA4 body is outside this shard and the argument's meaning is not decoded.

name: de4d_d991_ea0_tail_e256_c
comment: Calls 0xDE4D, loads R4=0xE2, R5=0x56 and R7=0x01, calls 0xD991, clears the EA SFR and tail-jumps to 0xE256. Byte-identical to 0xDC9E, 0xDCBA and 0xDD10, so the _c suffix records position, not a behavioural difference.

name: de4d_d991_ea0_tail_e256_d
comment: Calls 0xDE4D, loads R4=0xE2, R5=0x56 and R7=0x01, calls 0xD991, clears the EA SFR and tail-jumps to 0xE256. Byte-identical to 0xDC9E, 0xDCBA and 0xDCFA, so the _d suffix records position, not a behavioural difference.

name: bank1_trampoline_a69f
comment: Loads DPTR with 0xA69F and tail-jumps to 0x1114; the decompile renders it bl51_bank_select_1(0xa69f), the same Keil cross-bank trampoline shape as 0xDCAF which passes 0xA694. Neither target address is decoded here.

name: call_d57b_with_0d32_tail_3f9d
comment: Loads R7 from internal RAM 0x32, calls 0xD57B with that value in R7, then tail-jumps to 0x3F9D; there is no RET of its own. The value's meaning and what 0x3F9D does with it are not decoded here.

name: copy_0d32_or_call_0d58e
comment: Branches on internal RAM 0x31: if it equals 0x02, copies internal RAM 0x32 into 0x33 and returns; otherwise loads R5 from internal RAM 0x32, R7 from 0x33, calls 0xD58E and returns. The two internal RAM bytes and the value branched on are not identified anywhere in this shard, so what the split selects is not decoded.

name: store_0d32_to_045d_0704
comment: Writes internal RAM 0x32 to XDATA 0x045D and then to XDATA 0x0704, reloading DPTR for each, and returns. Both stores are unconditional and no other location is touched; neither byte's meaning is decoded here.

name: or_intmem_32_low_nibble_into_045a
comment: Reads XDATA 0x045A, masks the low nibble off and writes it back so the high nibble survives, then ORs the low nibble of internal-RAM byte 0x32 into it and writes 0x045A again. Net effect: XDATA 0x045A = (old & 0xF0) | (internal 0x32 & 0x0F).

name: store_32_to_0458_then_tailcall_1954
comment: Copies internal-RAM byte 0x32 to XDATA 0x0458 and then LJMPs (not LCALLs) to 0x1954, so 0x1954 returns straight to this function's caller. No other address is touched here.

name: init_0046_to_64_and_clear_af
comment: Writes 0x64 to XDATA 0x0046, then executes CLR 0xAF, which is CLR direct on the whole internal-RAM byte 0xAF (the decompiled C renders it as a bit write to EA, which the opcode C2 does not support).

name: read_code_byte_at_ptr_0a35_0a36
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0A35 into R6 and XDATA 0x0A36 into A, then loads DPTR from them with 0x0A35 as DPH and 0x0A36 as DPL, i.e. a big-endian 16-bit CODE pointer. With A cleared it fetches CODE[DPTR] via MOVC and returns that byte in A and R7.

name: init_163e_16f1_300e_3008
comment: Clears XDATA 0x163E, sets bit 4 of XDATA 0x16F1, writes 0x03 to XDATA 0x300E, and rewrites XDATA 0x3008 as (old & 0xF8) | 0x01. No branch and no return value.

name: stage_0a47_then_call_de83_r5_1a
comment: Points DPTR at XDATA 0x0A47 and calls 0xE02D, points DPTR at 0x0A47 again and calls 0xE03F, moves the returned A into R7, sets R5 to 0x1A and calls 0xDE83. It returns 0xDE83's carry unchanged: CY set returns at 0xDF32, CY clear falls through to a redundant CLR CY and RET. The only difference from 0xDF35 is the R5 constant (0x1A here, 0x1B there).

name: stage_0a47_then_call_de83_r5_1b
comment: Identical to 0xDF1E except that R5 is loaded with 0x1B before the call to 0xDE83. Calls 0xE02D and 0xE03F with DPTR pointing at XDATA 0x0A47, moves 0xE03F's A into R7, calls 0xDE83 and returns its carry unchanged.

name: scale_r7_by_8_then_set_09c1_09c3
comment: Multiplies R7 by 8 with MUL AB (B set to 8) and keeps the low product byte in R7, then points DPTR at XDATA 0x0A47 and calls 0xE033. It next writes (XDATA 0x0A47 | 0x80) to XDATA 0x09C1, 0x00 to 0x09C2 and 0x00 to 0x09C3, sets R2 = R3 = 0, R5 = 0x3C and R7 = 0, calls 0xDE83, and returns that call's carry unchanged.

name: gate_06e6_then_store_0464
comment: Reads XDATA 0x06E6 and returns immediately unless it equals 0x01. On that path it loads R7 from XDATA 0x181F and R5 from XDATA 0x181E, calls 0xDFA0 with that 16-bit pair, and writes the returned R6 to XDATA 0x0464 and R7 to XDATA 0x0465 in that order.

name: load_06e6
comment: Loads XDATA 0x06E6 into A and stops; the listing has no RET. This is the head of a larger routine: the comparison on that byte, the load of XDATA 0x1821/0x1820, the call to 0xDFA0 and the store of R6:R7 to XDATA 0x046C/0x046D all continue at 0xE014 and end at the RET at 0xE02C, so the entry's callers and wider purpose are not visible from this address alone.

name: branch_on_06e6_eq_1
comment: Compares A (the byte 0xE010 loaded from XDATA 0x06E6) against 0x01 and jumps to the RET at 0xE02C when they differ. On equality it loads R7 from XDATA 0x1821 and A from XDATA 0x1820 and falls into 0xE020, which moves A into R5 and calls 0xDFA0. The listing ends mid-routine; the shared tail at 0xE024 stores R6:R7 to XDATA 0x046C/0x046D.

name: move_a_to_r5_and_call_dfa0
comment: Moves A into R5 and LCALLs 0xDFA0. A at this point is the byte 0xE01C read from XDATA 0x1820, and 0xDFA0 returns its 16-bit result in R6:R7. The listing has no RET of its own; the shared tail at 0xE024 does the storing.

name: store_r6_r7_to_046c_046d
comment: Writes R6 to XDATA 0x046C and R7 to XDATA 0x046D, then returns. This is the shared tail of the routine whose head is at 0xE010, not a function of its own.

name: mul_r7_by_8
comment: Multiplies R7 by 8 using MUL AB with B preloaded to 8, and keeps the low byte of the product in R7 (the high byte stays in B). The listing has no RET: the continuation at 0xE033 is what writes B and R7 out, so the product is not consumed here.

name: set_09c1_09c3_from_dptr
comment: Reads the XDATA byte at the caller's DPTR, ORs 0x80 into it and writes the result to XDATA 0x09C1, then writes 0x20 to XDATA 0x09C2 and 0x00 to XDATA 0x09C3, leaving R2 and R3 both zero. Callers set DPTR to 0x0A47 immediately before the call.

name: store_a_to_dptr_e054
comment: Writes A to the XDATA byte at DPTR and returns. DPTR is left entirely to the caller and nothing else appears in the two-instruction listing, so which address is written cannot be determined from this function alone.

name: copy_043e_to_1511
comment: Sets CY from the complement of bit-addressable bit 0x05, loads DPTR with 0x043E (CPU_TEMP in ec/annotations/registers.yaml), and jumps to 0xE091 rather than 0xE090, which deliberately skips the INC DPTR there and so makes 0x043E itself, not 0x043F, the byte copied. 0xE091 reads that byte and falls into 0xE09D, which writes it to XDATA 0x1511 and returns. The carry computed at the start is never consumed by the shared tail.

name: copy_dptr_to_1511_discard_arith
comment: Increments the direct byte at 0x90, adds R7 and the carry into A, then jumps to 0xE091, the shared tail that reloads A from XDATA[DPTR] and stores it to XDATA 0x1511. The arithmetic in A is therefore discarded before the store, so the only observable effect is the copy of XDATA[DPTR] to 0x1511. Whether 0x90 is a port register or plain internal RAM on this part is not settled by the listing, and the decompiled C's 'P1' is an assumption.

name: copy_dptr_plus_1_to_1511
comment: Increments DPTR, reads the XDATA byte at the new address and jumps to 0xE09D, which writes it to XDATA 0x1511 and returns. This entry therefore copies XDATA[DPTR+1] to 0x1511, with DPTR supplied by the caller. The jump target 0xE09D is shared with the entries at 0xE064 and 0xE06F.

name: store_a_or_3c_at_dptr
comment: Writes A to the XDATA byte at DPTR, loads internal-RAM byte 0x3C into R6 through R7, ORs that into the byte just written and writes the result back. It then increments DPTR, reads XDATA at DPTR+1 and writes the same value back, so the last read/write pair changes nothing.

name: inc_indirect_then_store_3c_at_dptr
comment: Increments the internal-RAM byte addressed indirectly by R0, calls 0xE149 (which leaves DPTR holding a code address assembled from XDATA 0x0D04/0x0D05), then writes internal-RAM byte 0x3C to XDATA[DPTR] and returns. Whether the increment is meant to affect the location 0xE149 ends up pointing at is not determinable from this listing.

name: load_dptr_from_0d04_0d05
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0D04 and XDATA 0x0D05, stages them through internal-RAM bytes 0xB7 and 0xB8 (exchanging the accumulator with R7 to do it), then loads DPTR from that pair with 0x0D04 as DPH and 0x0D05 as DPL. It returns with A holding the low byte, XDATA 0x0D05. The internal-RAM staging is real work in the listing and is not what the decompiled C shows.

name: read_code_pair_at_dptr_into_r2_r1
comment: Takes DPH from A and DPTR from the caller, then fetches two consecutive CODE bytes with MOVC: the byte at DPTR is captured in R6 and exchanged into R2, and the byte at DPTR+1 ends up in R1. The 16-bit result is therefore R2 (first byte) and R1 (second byte), an unusual register pair for this firmware.

name: dispatch_on_0046_copy_status_to_0083
comment: Clears XDATA 0x0083, then, if XDATA 0x0046 is 0x64, 0x66 or 0x6C, writes 0xFA to XDATA 0x1306, 0x1501 or 0x1511 respectively. It then loops on XDATA 0x0046: for 0x64 it reads XDATA 0x1304 and requires bit 1 (JNB bit address 0xE1) and bit 3 (JB bit address 0xE3) before copying XDATA 0x130A into XDATA 0x0083; 0x66 does the same with XDATA 0x1500 and 0x1504, and 0x6C with XDATA 0x1510 and 0x1514. A clear bit 1 spins back to the loop head, bit 3 clear stores the second byte and loops back, and bit 3 set stores it and falls through to the 0x0083 tests, which are also reachable directly when 0x0046 is none of the three codes. Finally, if XDATA 0x0083 reads 0x95 the routine writes 0x33 to XDATA 0x0045, calls 0x1978 and jumps to 0x0200; if it reads 0xAF it writes 0xAF to XDATA 0x1036, clears bit 3 of XDATA 0x1121, writes 0x08 to 0x1120, sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x2011, sets bit 0 of the direct bytes 0xD8 and 0xD9, and then spins forever on the SJMP to itself at 0xE31A. What the selector codes 0x64/0x66/0x6C and the result codes 0x95/0xAF denote is not established by the listing.

name: load_164b_and_80
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x164B and A with 0x80, then stops; the listing has no RET. The stores are the following block at 0xE37B, which writes A to 0x164B and then 0x80 to XDATA 0x164C, 0x164D and 0x164E before returning, so this entry and 0xE37B are one four-byte-store routine split by the call-target scan.

name: store_a_to_dptr_then_164c_164e
comment: Writes A to the XDATA byte at the caller's DPTR, then writes the same A to XDATA 0x164C, 0x164D and 0x164E and returns. Entered from 0xE376 with DPTR = 0x164B and A = 0x80, the whole run fills XDATA 0x164B through 0x164E with 0x80.

name: load_0434_0438_pairs_mul16_and_tailcall
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0435 into A with DPTR = 0x0434 and calls 0xE3C4, which leaves the pair in R6:R7; that pair is written to 0x0A50/0x0A51. It repeats the same read for 0x0439/0x0438 into 0x0A52/0x0A53, then reloads both pairs as R4:R5 and R6:R7 and calls 0x707D. Finally it calls 0xE3C9, which tail-jumps to 0x708F with R4 = 0 and R5 = 0x64. 0x707D is the 16x16 multiply in the common area; where its 32-bit result goes is not visible in this listing.

name: set_r6_from_a_r7_from_dptr
comment: Four instructions: R4 takes the incoming A, R7 takes the byte at XDATA[DPTR], and R6 then takes the saved A. There is no call and no write, so it is the second half of a 16-bit XDATA read whose first byte the caller has already put in A, as 0xE389 does with 0x0434/0x0435. The decompiled C for this address reports a call to 0x708F that is not in these bytes.

name: tail_jump_708f_r4_0_r5_64
comment: Loads R4 = 0x00 and R5 = 0x64 and tail-jumps to 0x708F. It is two argument-setup instructions for that routine, not a call of its own, and what 0x708F does with the registers is not in this listing.

name: write_103f_through_0a56_pointer
comment: Saves XDATA 0x103E to 0x0A58 and 0x1063 to 0x0A59. If the byte at 0x0A53 is 0 it sets 0x103E = 0x40; if that byte is 1 it clears 0x103E and clears bit 0 of 0x1063; any other value returns at once. It then loops while the big-endian 16-bit counter at 0x0A54/0x0A55 is non-zero, writing the byte read from 0x103F to the address held in 0x0A56/0x0A57, advancing that pointer by one (0xF10F, which adds 1 through 0x70E4) and decrementing the counter by one (0x70E4 with A and B both 0xFF, after an R3/R5/R1 increment chain whose purpose is not clear), and finally restores 0x103E and 0x1063 from 0x0A58/0x0A59. None of 0x103E, 0x103F, 0x1063 or 0x0A53-0x0A59 has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: copy_bytes_between_two_16bit_bases
comment: Stores the destination base R6:R7 to 0x0A52/0x0A53, the source base R4:R5 to 0x0A54/0x0A55 and the limit R2:R3 to 0x0A56/0x0A57, and starts a counter at zero. Each pass reads XDATA at (source base + counter), writes that byte to (destination base + counter), and adds 1 to the counter through 0xF10F. The loop test compares 0x0A58/0x0A59 against 0x0A56/0x0A57 as a big-endian 16-bit value while the address arithmetic adds them as 0x0A58 + 256*0x0A59; the two byte orders do not agree and which is intended is not decoded here. Normal exit is the ret at 0xE4B8 with A holding 0x0A58 minus 0x0A56, which is 0.

name: init_0a4d_block_and_count
comment: Writes R6 to XDATA 0x0A4D, R7 to 0x0A4E and the constant 2 to 0x0A4F, raising that byte to 3 when 0x0A4D is non-zero. It then calls 0x5597 with R7 = 1, reloads R7 from 0x0A4F and R5 from 0x0A4E, and writes 1 to 0x0A53 and 0x0A54, 0 to 0x0A55, with R2 = 2 and DPTR now at 0x0A56. The listing stops at 0xE4EE with no ret and one byte short of the next entry; the decompiled C goes on to a call to 0xE3D0 that is not in these bytes, so what the prepared block is used for is not shown here.

name: jump_to_f0a3
comment: Three bytes: an ljmp to 0xF0A3, with nothing else in the listing. The decompiled C inlines the code at 0xF0A3 (a branch on A, then 0x0F and 0x60 to 0x0A56/0x0A57 and 4 into the next byte), which this listing does not contain, so the jump target's behaviour is not decoded here.

name: write_fe_r7_to_0f61_62
comment: 0xF151 writes 0xFF to XDATA 0x0F60 and leaves DPTR at 0x0F61; the routine then writes A-1 (0xFE) to 0x0F61 and R7 to 0x0F62. It calls 0xF107 (inc DPTR), 0xF08B and 0x4777 with R3 = 4 and R7 = 1, and returns R7 = 1 if 0x4777 leaves R7 non-zero, else 0. Other listings in this range (0xE624, 0xE64A, 0xE670, 0xE6B1, 0xE7CA) set R7 to a small constant before calling it, and 0x0F60-0x0F62 have no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: write_ff_fa_r5_r7_to_0f60_63
comment: 0xF151 writes 0xFF to XDATA 0x0F60, then the routine writes 0xFA to 0x0F61, R5 to 0x0F62 and R7 to 0x0F63 (the last through 0xF108, which also leaves the byte at 0x0FA0 in R5). It calls 0xF08B and 0x4777 with R3 = 4 and R7 = 1 and returns R7 = 1 if 0x4777 leaves R7 non-zero, else 0. 0x0F60-0x0F63 have no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so the block's meaning is not determined here.

name: call_e4fe_2_clear_0f60_retry
comment: The declared entry 0xE567 is mid-instruction: the byte there decodes as addc A,R5, and the body runs 0xE544-0xE56F in this listing. It calls 0xE4FE with R7 = 2 and, when that returns non-zero, clears XDATA 0x0F60 and calls 0xF107, 0xF0F3, 0xF0DC with A = 0x10, and 0x4777, returning R7 = 1 or 0 from that. It then calls 0xF159 and jumps back to 0xE544 while carry is set, returning R7 = 0 when carry is clear. 0x0F60 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: probe_c0_c1_expect_88_51_or_53
comment: Clears XDATA 0x0A4D and loops: calls 0xE5B1 with R7 = 0xC0, and if that returns non-zero stores XDATA 0x0A4F into 0x2270 and requires it to equal 0x88; it then calls 0xE5B1 with R7 = 0xC1, stores 0x0A4F into 0x2271, and accepts 0x51 or 0x53, returning R7 = 1. On any mismatch it calls 0xF159 with DPTR = 0x0A4D and retries while carry is set; 0xF159 increments that byte and returns carry while the incremented value is below 3, so the body runs three times before it gives up and returns R7 = 0. Neither 0x2270 nor 0x2271 has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: forward_e896_with_fixed_args
comment: Loads R1 = 0x4F, R2 = 0x0A, R3 = 1 and R6 = 0xFF, calls 0xE896 and returns its R7 unchanged. It reads and writes no XDATA of its own; the four argument bytes are constants in the instruction stream and what 0xE896 makes of them is not in this listing.

name: write_ff_f8_a5_5a_and_retry
comment: Clears XDATA 0x0A4D, then in a loop: 0xF151 writes 0xFF to 0x0F60 and the routine writes 0xF8 to 0x0F61, 0xA5 to 0x0F62 and 0x5A to 0x0F63 (the last through 0xF108), then calls 0xF08B and 0x4777 with R3 = 4 and R7 = 1, returning R7 = 1 if 0x4777 leaves R7 non-zero. Otherwise it calls 0x0ECC with R7 = 0x78, calls 0xF159 on the counter at 0x0A4D and repeats while carry is set, which is three passes, then returns R7 = 0. 0x0F60-0x0F63 have no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: write_ff_f8_00_and_retry
comment: Clears XDATA 0x0A4D, then in a loop: 0xF151 writes 0xFF to 0x0F60, the routine writes 0xF8 to 0x0F61 and 0x00 to 0x0F62, calls 0xF107, 0xF08B and 0x4777 with R3 = 4 and R7 = 1, and returns R7 = 1 if 0x4777 leaves R7 non-zero. Otherwise it calls 0x0ECC with R7 = 0x78, calls 0xF159 on 0x0A4D and repeats while carry is set, then returns R7 = 0. This is the same shape as 0xE5BE with the 0xA5/0x5A pair replaced by a single zero byte and 0xF107 in place of 0xF108.

name: gate_04_09_then_0f80_bit1_set
comment: Calls 0xE4FE with R7 = 4 and then with R7 = 9, returning R7 = 0 if either returns zero. On success it calls 0xF0C4 and 0x4777, requires R7 non-zero, then reads XDATA 0x0F80 and returns R7 = 1 only if bit 1 is set (jnb ACC.1 exits with 0). 0x0F80 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: gate_05_09_then_0f80_bit1_clear
comment: Calls 0xE4FE with R7 = 5 and then with R7 = 9, returning R7 = 0 if either returns zero. On success it calls 0xF0C4 and 0x4777, requires R7 non-zero, then reads XDATA 0x0F80 and returns R7 = 1 only if bit 1 is clear (jb ACC.1 exits with 0). Apart from the first identifier and the polarity of the bit test it is the same shape as 0xE624. 0x0F80 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: gate_poll_0f80_bit4
comment: Clears R5, calls 0xE51E and then 0xE4FE with R7 = 6, and returns R7 = 0 if either returns zero. It then clears XDATA 0x0A4D and loops: with DPTR = 0x0F60 it writes 0xFF through 0xF0C8 and calls 0x4777, returning R7 = 0 if that leaves R7 zero; otherwise it reads XDATA 0x0F80, sets 0x0A4D = 1 when bit 4 is clear, and repeats the send until that bit is set, then returns R7 = 1. Neither 0x0A4D nor 0x0F80 has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: init_args_then_e51e_e4fe_16
comment: Stores R5 in XDATA 0x0A4F and R6/R7 in 0x0A4D/0x0A4E, clears 0x0A51 and sets it to 0x40 when all three argument bytes are zero. It calls 0xF17E (which loads R7 from 0x0A4E and A from 0x0A51) and then 0xE51E, tail-jumping to 0xE7C7, which sets R7 = 0 and returns, if that fails; it then clears 0x0A50, calls 0xE4FE with R7 = 0x16 with the same failure exit, and writes the byte returned by 0xF189 to the address left in DPTR. The listing ends at 0xE6F3 and the next entry, 0xE6F4, continues the same routine, so this is a fragment of it.

name: r7_zero_ret_2
comment: Two instructions: loads R7 = 0 and returns. It is the failure exit that 0xE6B1 tail-jumps to when 0xE51E or 0xE4FE returns zero.

name: init_0a50_2_then_start_0x13_block
comment: Stores R5 in XDATA 0x0A4F and R6/R7 in 0x0A4D/0x0A4E, sets 0x0A50 = 2, clears 0x0A51 and sets it to 0x40 when all three argument bytes are zero. It calls 0xE51E with R5 = 0x0A51 and then 0xE4FE with R7 = 0x13, exiting to 0xE893, which returns R7 = 0, if either fails. On success it clears 0x0F60, calls 0xF107, loads R3 from 0x0A50, calls 0xF0F3 (which writes 0x0F to 0x0A56 and 0x60 to 0x0A57) and starts the block with A = 0x10 aimed at 0x0A58. The listing stops at 0xE820; the store that completes the 0x0A56-0x0A5A block and everything after it is the separately listed 0xE822.

name: r7_zero_ret_3
comment: Two instructions: loads R7 = 0 and returns. It is the failure exit that 0xE7CA tail-jumps to when 0xE51E or 0xE4FE returns zero, and it is byte-identical to the exits at 0xE7B8 and 0xE7C7.

name: write_0f60_0f61_then_0x7049
comment: With DPTR = 0x0A50 it calls 0x713C, then writes R6 to XDATA 0x0F60 and R5 to 0x0F61, calls 0xF0CA (which stores further bytes and leaves the byte at 0x0FA0 in R5) and then 0x4777. If 0x4777 leaves R7 non-zero it reads XDATA 0x0F80 into R7, calls 0x711C with DPTR = 0x0A50 and 0x7049 with A = R7, and returns R7 = 1; otherwise it returns R7 = 0. 0x0F60, 0x0F61 and 0x0F80 have no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: write_r6_r7_r5_to_0f60_62
comment: Loads A from R7, writes R6 to XDATA 0x0F60, R7 to 0x0F61 and R5 to 0x0F62 (the last through 0xF108, which also leaves the byte at 0x0FA0 in R5). It then calls 0xF08B and 0x4777 with R3 = 3 and R7 = 1 and returns R7 = 1 if 0x4777 leaves R7 non-zero, else 0. The same 0x0F60-0x0F62 block and the same 0xF08B/0x4777 sequence appear at 0xE4FE, 0xE51E and 0xE5BE with different leading constants; none of these addresses has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: mask_1603_and_wait_tf1
comment: Stops Timer 1 (0x8E) and clears its interrupt enable (0xAB), loads TH1 = 0xB2 and TL1 = 0x19, clears TF1 (0x8F) and starts the timer. It then clears bits 0 and 3 of XDATA 0x1603, keeps that value in R0, and precomputes R1 = R0|0x06, R2 = R0|0x02 and R3 = R0|0x04, then the loop from 0xE911 stores R1, then R2, then R3, then R0 back to 0x1603 (each as three identical movx @DPTR,A instructions) until TF1 is set, but the bytes from 0xE915 to 0xE94C decode to repeated add A,B / div AB / mov A,0x01 sequences that are not coherent 8051 code here, so what the loop actually computes is not decoded. On exit it stops Timer 1, clears TF1, sets ET1 and calls 0x05EF and then 0xF118 with A = 0. 0x1603 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: rmw_1603_and_wait_tf1_2500_times
comment: Sets bits 0x90 in XDATA 0x1C34, stops Timer 1 (0x8E), clears ET1 (0xAB), calls 0x05E8 and 0xF116, and clears bits 0 and 3 of XDATA 0x1603. The loop then runs R7 = 0x64 times for each of R6 = 0x19 outer passes (2500 in total), and each pass reads 0x1603, complements ACC bit 0 and branches on it, complements ACC bit 1 and writes A back to 0x1603, then reloads TH1 and TL1 with 0xFF and spins until TF1 (0x8F) is set before stopping the timer. On exit it clears bits 0x90 in 0x1C34 again. Why the accumulator bits are complemented and written back to 0x1603 is not decoded; neither 0x1603 nor 0x1C34 has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: three_calls_then_4777_r3_04
comment: Calls 0xF189 then 0xF0FE then 0xF08B; loads R3=0x04 and R7=0x01 and calls 0x4777; returns 1 if R7 is non-zero and 0 if it is zero. No XDATA address is touched directly here and none of the three helpers is decoded in this listing.

name: set_dptr_0f60_then_4777_r3_03
comment: Sets DPTR to 0x0F60 and calls 0xF0FE then calls 0xF08B; loads R3=0x03 and R7=0x01 and calls 0x4777; returns 1 if R7 is non-zero and 0 if it is zero. Same shape as the entry at 0xEA94 apart from the 0x0F60 pointer and the R3 value; what 0xF0FE does with that pointer is not shown here.

name: forward_to_8648_after_1978_c43f
comment: Calls 0x1978 then calls 0xC43F then jumps to 0x8648 with ljmp. Whatever 0x8648 leaves in its return register is what this entry returns; no XDATA address is named in this listing.

name: dispatch_on_0a4b_via_7151
comment: Fall-through continuation of 0xEADA: calls 0x1510; loads DPTR=0x0A4B; reads that byte and calls 0x7151 with it in A. Whatever 0x7151 returns in R3/R4 is then adjusted (R3 is decremented) and control jumps to 0xE8EC with A holding R4. The table 0x7151 indexes and the targets at 0xE8EC are not decoded in this listing.

name: store_r7_to_0a4c_and_branch_on_1_or_2
comment: Calls 0xE64A and returns via 0xED47 if it reports zero; otherwise calls 0xF12F then 0xE7CA with R5=0x01 and stores the returned R7 at XDATA 0x0A4C. If R7 is 1 it sets DPTR=0x0A49 calls 0xF10F and then writes 0x0A4B=0x04 when @0x0A49==1 and @0x0A4A==0 or 0x0A4B=0 otherwise; if R7 is 2 it writes @0x0A49 back to itself clears bits 0-1 of 0x0A4A and sets 0x0A4B=0; any other value just returns via 0xED47. The decompiled C names R7 a parameter; the asm shows it is 0xE7CA's return value. 0x0A4C is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml as a charge-target derating tier but the values written here are 0 1 or 2 rather than the 150-550 cycle counts recorded there so its role in this function is not established.

name: gate_a4b_eq_9
comment: Loads DPTR=0x0A4B compares the byte there with 0x09 and jumps to 0xED52 when they are equal; otherwise it jumps to 0xEBD5. The 0x1C41/0x08FE/0x08FF/0x1601 stores that the decompiled C attributes to this address are not in this listing - they belong to 0xED52 which follows.

name: write_1c41_12_copy_0a49_0a4a_clear_1601_bit4
comment: Writes 0x12 to XDATA 0x1C41; copies the bytes at 0x0A49 and 0x0A4A to 0x08FE and 0x08FF; and clears bit 4 of 0x1601. The listing ends on that store; the next entry at 0xED6E follows immediately and does call 0xEAD1 set R7=0 and return - whether control is meant to reach it from here is not shown.

name: forward_to_ead1_return_0
comment: Calls 0xEAD1 then loads R7=0x00 and returns. The bytes are the fall-through tail of the preceding entry at 0xED52 so the boundary between the two is a hypothesis.

name: write_0a59_block_then_445e
comment: Sets R7=0x14 and calls 0x0EA2; loads R3 from XDATA 0x0A48; writes 0xB6 0x00 0xC0 0x00 to 0x0A59-0x0A5C; then calls 0x445E with R5=0x0C and R7=0x01 and returns 0x445E's R7 unchanged. 0xEADA writes the same 0x0A59-0x0A5C block and makes the same 0x445E call with R3=@0x0A48.

name: call_0ea2_with_0xfa
comment: Loads R7=0xFA and calls 0x0EA2; the listing then shows a second mov R7 0xFA at 0xEDA0 and stops there. The matching second call and the return are not in this listing so the repetition the decompiled C shows is not confirmed from the asm; what 0x0EA2 does with 0xFA is not decoded here.

name: mov_c_from_bit_0x22
comment: Two bytes only: mov C with bit address 0x22 (bit 2 of internal RAM byte 0x24) with no return instruction in the listing so execution falls through into the next entry at 0xEDA6. The decompiled C for this address instead shows a call to 0xE8C4 which is not present in these bytes; the role of this entry is not determinable from the listing.

name: call_e8c4_with_r6_0xff_return_r7
comment: Loads R6=0xFF calls 0xE8C4 and returns its R7 in A. This is the same code the decompiled C attributes to the preceding entry at 0xEDA4; that attribution is not supported by 0xEDA4's own bytes.

name: four_calls_then_4777_flag
comment: Calls 0xF121; calls 0xF177 with A=0x04; calls 0xF07F with A=0x03; calls 0xF128; then calls 0x4777 and returns 1 if R7 is non-zero and 0 if it is zero. No XDATA address appears in this listing and none of the five helpers is decoded here.

name: write_4_bytes_after_f121_then_chain
comment: Calls 0xF121 - which sets DPTR but is not decoded here - then writes 0x05 0x00 0xFF 0xFF to four consecutive XDATA bytes starting at DPTR+1 so the base address is whatever 0xF121 left in DPTR. It clears A then calls 0xF083 then 0xF128 then 0x4777; on a non-zero result it calls 0x0EA2 with R7=0x14 then 0xF09F then 0x4777 then 0xEDBC and returns 1 only if all three report success and 0 at the first failure.

name: send_0x12_via_f078_then_chain
comment: Calls 0xF121 then 0xF078 with A=0x12 then 0xF128 then 0x4777 and returns 0 if 0x4777 reports zero. On success it calls 0x0EA2 with R7=0x14 then 0xF09F then 0x4777; requires the byte at XDATA 0x0F81 to be non-zero; then calls 0xF0ED 0xF138 and 0xF0B3 and 0x4777; and finally calls 0xEDBC. It returns 1 only if every one of those steps reports success and 0 at the first failure.

name: write_3_bytes_after_f121_then_chain
comment: Calls 0xF121 then writes 0x06 0x00 0x00 to three consecutive XDATA bytes starting at DPTR+1 and calls 0xF081; the base address comes from 0xF121 and is not shown here. The rest is the same chain as 0xEE0F: 0xF128 then 0x4777 then 0x0EA2 with R7=0x14 then 0xF09F then 0x4777 then a non-zero test of XDATA 0x0F81 then 0xF0ED 0xF138 0xF0B3 and 0x4777 then 0xEDBC - returning 1 only if all of it succeeds.

name: send_0x07_via_f078_then_chain
comment: Same shape as 0xEE0F but sends A=0x07 to 0xF078 instead of 0x12; the remaining chain (0xF121 0xF128 0x4777 0x0EA2 with R7=0x14 0xF09F 0x4777 the XDATA 0x0F81 non-zero test 0xF0ED 0xF138 0xF0B3 0x4777 0xEDBC) is identical instruction for instruction and it too returns 1 only on full success.

name: send_0x10_via_f079_then_chain
comment: Same shape as 0xEE0F but loads A=0x10 and calls 0xF079 instead of 0xF078; the rest of the chain is identical. The listing ends on the jz after the 0xEDBC call so the success path's return value is not shown - unlike 0xEE0F the mov R7 1 bytes are missing from it.

name: ajmp_0xe822
comment: One instruction: ajmp 0xE822. It reads and writes nothing and leaves the return address on the stack so it is an absolute jump rather than a call; the body the decompiled C shows for this address belongs to 0xE822 and not to this entry.

name: call_f0a1_with_d6_then_4777_flag
comment: Loads A=0xD6 calls 0xF0A1 then 0x4777 and returns 1 if R7 is non-zero else 0. No XDATA address is named in this listing and 0xF0A1's use of 0xD6 is not decoded here.

name: toggle_0fc0_bit1_unless_r6r7_zero
comment: Forms A = R6 OR R7 and then tests R7; when both are zero it jumps to 0xF077. Otherwise it reads XDATA 0x0FC0 XORs it with 0x02 and writes it back - bit 1 of that byte is toggled. Nothing else in this listing touches a location.

name: call_ee96_then_xor_0fc0_04
comment: Calls 0xEE96 and jumps to 0xF077 if it returns zero. Otherwise it reads XDATA 0x0FC0 XORs it with 0x04 and writes it back - bit 2 of that byte is toggled. This is 0xEF60's shape with one extra call and a different bit.

name: call_ef17_then_copy_0f80_to_0fb1
comment: Calls 0xEF17 and jumps to 0xF06B if it returns zero. On success it copies XDATA 0x0F80 to 0x0FB1 and then sets DPTR to 0x0F81; the listing stops there so the copies of 0x0F81-0x0F83 that the decompiled C shows are not in it.

name: store_dptr_byte_to_0fb2_copy_0f82
comment: Loads A from the XDATA address the caller left in DPTR and stores it at 0x0FB2; then copies XDATA 0x0F82 to 0x0FB3 and starts reading 0x0F83 at 0xF000 where the listing ends. The rest of the body - the 0x0A43-0x0A46 computation and the 0x0FC3/0x0FC0 stores that the decompiled C shows - is not in this listing.

name: store_16bit_sum_to_0a43_0a44
comment: Completes a 16-bit addition: adds R6 and the carry into R4 stores the low byte at XDATA 0x0A43 and the earlier accumulator value (R7) at 0x0A44 and then reads XDATA 0x0FB2 into A. The listing opens with add A 0x00 which changes nothing but the carry so the entry point is mid-expression and where the two addends came from is not shown here.

name: rotate_16bit_pair_and_range_check_0fc3
comment: Masks its incoming A with 0x0F into R6; reads XDATA 0x0FB3 and masks it with 0xFC; forms a 16-bit sum in R6:R7; then runs a two-iteration rotate-right-through-carry over that pair - each iteration reloading the carry from bit address 0xE7 - and stores the result big-endian at 0x0A45 (high) and 0x0A46 (low). It then compares that 16-bit value against 0x0190 and if it is not below it compares 0x0A43:0x0A44 against 0x0145. Falling below either bound jumps to 0xF06B; otherwise it sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x0FC3 and jumps to 0xF072 which zeroes 0x0FC0.

name: clear_0fc3_bit0_and_zero_0fc0
comment: Clears bit 0 of XDATA 0x0FC3 then falls into 0xF072 which writes 0 to XDATA 0x0FC0. It is the failure target of 0xF022 and 0xEFDC and 0xF072 is also the join point 0xF022's sjmp reaches on success.

name: ret_immediately
comment: A single `ret`. No XDATA address is loaded, no register is read or written, nothing is called; the decompiled C is an empty void function to match. What this address is for is not determined by these bytes, and the file's own header records the function boundary as a hypothesis.

name: store_a_0_1_zeros_at_dptr_plus1
comment: Increments DPTR and stores the incoming A at the new address, then writes 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 to the six addresses after it: eight bytes spanning the caller's DPTR+1 to DPTR+8. It then loads DPTR with 0x0A56 and writes 0x0F, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00 to XDATA 0x0A56-0x0A5A, then returns. The .asm slice for this address stops at F07D; the later stores are the decompiler's reading of the same run. None of 0x0A56-0x0A5A has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: store_a_0_1_zeros_at_dptr
comment: Stores the incoming A at DPTR without advancing first, then writes 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 to the next seven addresses: the same eight-byte run as F078, one byte earlier in the buffer. It then loads DPTR with 0x0A56 and writes 0x0F, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00 to XDATA 0x0A56-0x0A5A. The .asm slice stops at F07D. None of 0x0A56-0x0A5A has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: store_a_plus1_then_five_zeros
comment: Increments A, stores it at DPTR, then clears A and writes 0 to the next five addresses (DPTR+1 to DPTR+5), followed by the 0x0F, 0x60, 0, 0, 0 block at XDATA 0x0A56-0x0A5A. Its .asm slice begins partway through the byte run that F078's slice starts, and the file's own header records the function boundary as a hypothesis, so whether this address is a callable entry or a mid-routine label is not established here.

name: store_a_then_five_zeros
comment: Stores the incoming A at DPTR, then clears A and writes 0 to the next five addresses (DPTR+1 to DPTR+5), then loads DPTR with 0x0A56 and writes 0x0F, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00 to XDATA 0x0A56-0x0A5A. One caller-supplied byte followed by five zero bytes. The .asm slice for this address is a single `movx @DPTR, A`; the rest is the decompiler's reading of the run.

name: store_five_zeros_at_dptr_plus1
comment: Clears A and writes 0 to five consecutive addresses starting at DPTR+1, then loads DPTR with 0x0A56 and writes 0x0F, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00 to XDATA 0x0A56-0x0A5A. It stores nothing at DPTR itself. Its .asm slice is a single `clr A` and the file's header records the function boundary as a hypothesis, so whether this is a callable entry or a mid-routine label is not established here.

name: store_a_five_times
comment: Increments DPTR and writes the incoming A, then repeats four more times, so A lands in five consecutive addresses (DPTR+1 to DPTR+5). It then loads DPTR with 0x0A56 and writes 0x0F, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00 to XDATA 0x0A56-0x0A5A. The .asm slice covers only the first of the five stores. None of 0x0A56-0x0A5A has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: store_a_four_times
comment: Increments DPTR and writes the incoming A, repeating three more times, so A lands in four consecutive addresses (DPTR+1 to DPTR+4). It then loads DPTR with 0x0A56 and writes 0x0F, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00 to XDATA 0x0A56-0x0A5A. The .asm slice shows three of the four stores; the fourth falls in F089's slice. None of 0x0A56-0x0A5A has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: store_a_once_at_dptr_plus1
comment: Increments DPTR, stores the incoming A there, then loads DPTR with 0x0A56 and writes 0x0F, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00 to XDATA 0x0A56-0x0A5A. Only one payload byte is written. Its .asm slice is two instructions and the file's header records the function boundary as a hypothesis, so whether this is a callable entry or a mid-routine label is not established here.

name: set_0a56_to_0f_60_00_00_00
comment: Loads R6 with 0x0F, sets DPTR to 0x0A56, writes 0x0F, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00 and 0x00 to XDATA 0x0A56-0x0A5A, and returns. It writes nothing to the caller's DPTR. The .asm slice covers only the R6 load and the `mov DPTR, #0x0a56`; the five stores are the decompiler's reading of the same run. None of 0x0A56-0x0A5A has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: write_0f_60_00_00_00_at_dptr
comment: Loads A with 0x0F and stores it at DPTR, then loads A with 0x60; the following instructions store that byte and three zeros into the next four addresses. Read as an entry this writes 0x0F, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00 at DPTR to DPTR+4. Its .asm slice is three instructions inside the same byte run that F08B's slice starts, and the file's header records the function boundary as a hypothesis, so whether this is a callable entry or a mid-routine label is not established here.

name: store_a_then_three_zeros

name: set_0f60_84_and_0a56_block

name: trampoline_to_c118
comment: Loads DPTR with 0xC118 and ljmp 0x1100, the stub this repository's decompiled output names bl51_bank_select_0; no instruction here reads or writes any XDATA address itself. 19A8.c is the decompiler rendering that as a call to the stub with 0xC118 as the argument. 0xC118 is not an instruction boundary: it is the immediate byte of `anl A,#0xf3` at 0xC117, the second-to-last instruction of FUN_CODE_c0a8 (ec/decompiled/bank1/C0A8.asm, 116 bytes, 0xC0A8-0xC11B), so an annotation row seeding a function there resolves to nothing and the build reports `0xC118 in bank1.bin: no function at this address`. Decoded from this address the four bytes are `movx @R1,A` (0xF3), `orl A,R5` (0x4D), `movx @DPTR,A` (0xF0) and `ret` (0x22), the last three being the same tail 0xC119-0xC11B that FUN_CODE_c0a8 reaches from its own mask, and none of the four writes R7. The census counts where the targets fall in the committed listings and is reproducible from them: take the `imm16` of each bank1 `mov DPTR,#imm16` + `ljmp 0x1100` listing and test it against the instruction-start addresses of the committed .asm files. What the 22 mean is not settled here. Those listings are byte-exact against the image (`ec/tools/verify_reassembly.py --check`), so the imm16 values are not in question; whether these are entries the linear listing frames differently from the code the linker placed, or targets that are not entries at all, is a question the listings cannot answer. Issue #255 asks it of bank1's 0xC10C, and on this count it is 22 addresses wide, not one. name: tick_06f9_and_dispatch_table_8a80
comment: Increments the byte at XDATA 0x06F9, writes it back, masks the new value with 0x07, and jumps through the table at CODE 0x8A80 at offset (value & 7) * 3 (`ADD A,R0` twice then `JMP @A+DPTR`), so the eight entries are three bytes each. Those entries are `LJMP` instructions whose targets are 0x8AA7, 0xABE2, 0xABE9, 0xABEA, 0x8ABB, 0x8AA7, 0x8AA7 and 0x8AA7 in order, which agrees with the decompile's switch; the table bytes themselves are not part of this listing. Nothing is passed to the target other than the incremented counter left in A.

name: clear_06f9_bits_0_3_then_call_abee
comment: Reads XDATA 0x06F9, XORs it with 0x08, masks it with 0xF8 and writes it back, which forces bits 0-3 of that byte to zero and leaves bits 4-7 as they were. The `JB 0xE3` at 0x8AB0 then tests accumulator bit 3, which the preceding `ANL A,#0xF8` has just cleared, so the branch is never taken: 0xABEE is called unconditionally and the `LCALL 0xABFB` at 0x8AB7 is unreachable as the bytes stand. The decompile tests the pre-mask value, which is why it shows both calls.

name: probe_159a_19f0_0983_then_dispatch
comment: Calls 0x159A and returns through 0x8B31 if R7 is non-zero; otherwise it calls 0x19F0, and carry set jumps into the middle of the routine at 0x8B35. It then tests bit 0 of the byte at XDATA 0x0983 and tail-jumps to 0x8B8F if that bit is set, else calls 0x1990 and branches to 0x8B0C when R7 is non-zero. The listing stops at 0x8AFF because the call-target scan also found entries at 0x8B01 and 0x8B04; the bytes there continue the same body, and the 0x8AE5 decompile covers all of it, working on XDATA 0x097F, 0x06C0, 0x0980, 0x06E1, 0x0459, 0x0495, 0x045D and 0x0704.

name: load_dptr_097f
comment: The listing at this address is the single instruction `MOV DPTR,#0x97F`, immediately followed at 0x8B04 by the `MOVX A,@DPTR` that reads the byte it points at. It sits inside the body of the routine that starts at 0x8AE5, and no `lcall` or `ljmp` to 0x8B01 appears in the generated .asm listings, so the entry-point boundary here is the call-target byte scan's hypothesis and the function-level role is not determined.

name: countdown_06c0_latch_097f_bit0
comment: This is the body of the routine that starts at 0x8AE5, whose decompile at this address covers these bytes. It tests bit 0 of the byte DPTR already points at, XDATA 0x097F, and tail-jumps to 0x8B8F if set; otherwise it tests bit 3 of XDATA 0x0459 and, when that is clear, clears bit 7 of 0x06E1, calls 0x1762, and falls into the shared block at 0x8B25 that writes 0x14 to XDATA 0x06C0 and 0x19 to 0x0980. After calling 0x199C it returns to 0x8B25 if bit 7 of XDATA 0x0495 or of XDATA 0x06E1 is set, and otherwise zeroes XDATA 0x045D and 0x0704 and decrements 0x06C0, returning at 0x8B31 unless the decrement reaches zero, in which case it calls 0x1990 and then either 0x8BD1 (setting bit 0 of 0x097F when that returns carry clear) or 0x19BA followed by 0x198A and, if R7 and XDATA 0x0756 and 0x0845 are all zero, 0x1996.

name: return_with_carry_cleared
comment: The listing is `CLR CY` followed by `RET`, so its only effect is to return with the carry flag cleared. It is reached by `LJMP` from 0x8DB9, 0x8D80 and 0x8DE1 and by local branches inside the body at 0x8B04, so it acts as a shared exit stub. It writes no XDATA byte and calls nothing.

name: return_with_carry_set
comment: The listing is `SETB CY` followed by `RET`, so its only effect is to return with the carry flag set. It is the complement of the stub at 0x8B31 and is reached by `LJMP` from 0x8DB6 and 0x8DD8. It writes no XDATA byte and calls nothing.

name: clear_0480_bit4_set_0459_01_06e1_a0
comment: Clears bit 4 of the byte at XDATA 0x0480, writes 0x01 to XDATA 0x0459, clears bit 0 of XDATA 0x097F, and sets bits 7 and 5 of XDATA 0x06E1. It then calls 0x19AE followed by 0x199C and returns with the carry flag set. No caller-supplied value is read and no XDATA address outside that list is touched. It is reached by `LJMP` from 0x8B09 and 0x8AF8 and by `LCALL` from elsewhere in the bank, including 0xA4CF and 0xA3F7.

name: set_0480_50_zero_048f_0459_02_06e1_a0
comment: Sets bits 4 and 6 of the byte at XDATA 0x0480, writes 0x00 to XDATA 0x048F, writes 0x02 to XDATA 0x0459, and sets bits 7 and 5 of XDATA 0x06E1. It then calls 0x19AE and returns with the carry flag set. Compared with the routine at 0x8B8F it sets rather than clears bit 4 of 0x0480 and writes 0x02 rather than 0x01 to 0x0459, and it does not touch 0x097F or call 0x199C. No `lcall` or `ljmp` to 0x8BB2 appears in the generated .asm listings, so how control reaches it is not shown here.

name: select_probe_address_and_return_carry
comment: Calls 0x198A and returns with the carry flag clear through 0x8CDB if R7 is non-zero. If bit 0 of both XDATA 0x0497 and XDATA 0x097B is set it clears bit 0 of 0x097B; otherwise it copies XDATA 0x0514 into 0x04AB and, when 0x0514 is below 7, returns with the carry flag set through 0x8CDD. Failing both, it loads DPTR with 0x0502, calls 0x8886, then calls 0x8863 with R4:R3 = 0x0CE4, substituting 0x0D48 or 0x0D16 when XDATA 0x0398 reads 0xA5 or XDATA 0x030D reads 0x10 or 0x11. Carry set from that probe returns via 0x8CE3, carry clear repeats the pattern for 0x09F6 and 0x0ABE and carry clear from that also returns via 0x8CE3, while carry set from it leads to a third 0x8863 call, preceded by 0x8886 with DPTR = 0x0506, whose R4:R3 argument is 0x2328, 0x2EE0 or 0x1770 chosen by bits 6-7 of XDATA 0x0491, with the outcome returned as carry set via 0x8CDD or carry clear via 0x8CDB.

name: return_with_carry_clear
comment: The listing is `CLR CY` followed by `RET`, so its only effect is to return with the carry flag cleared. It is reached by `LJMP` from 0x8BD7 inside the routine at 0x8BD1 and by fall-through from the `JNC` at 0x8CD9, which is that routine's carry-clear return. It writes no XDATA byte and calls nothing.

name: write_0a_to_07f2_fall_into_8ce3
comment: Writes 0x0A to XDATA 0x07F2 and then falls straight into the next entry at 0x8CE3, which clears bit 0 of XDATA 0x0983, sets the carry flag and returns; there is no `RET` inside this listing. The decompile's second statement is that fall-through rather than code at 0x8CDD. It is reached by `LJMP` from 0x8BFD and by the `JNC` at 0x8CD9, both inside the routine at 0x8BD1.

name: clear_0983_bit0_return_carry_set
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0983, clears bit 0 with `ANL A,#0xFE`, writes the byte back, sets the carry flag and returns. It is used as a return path at three places: `LJMP` from 0x8C50, a `JNC` from 0x8CA1, and the fall-through from the store at 0x8CDD. No `LCALL` to 0x8CE3 appears in the generated .asm listings.

name: gate_then_copy_2200_to_075f
comment: Returns immediately at 0x8D0F unless XDATA 0x06C2 is zero and bit 7 of XDATA 0x06E1 is clear. It then requires 0x8D25 to leave the carry clear, 0x159A to return zero in R7, and 0x19F0 to set the carry; if any of those does not hold it calls 0x1762 and returns at 0x8D0F. When they all hold it zeroes XDATA 0x045D and XDATA 0x0704, copies the byte at XDATA 0x2200 into XDATA 0x075F, and calls 0x1768.

name: combine_0490_0495_049d_flags_into_carry
comment: Returns with the carry flag clear if 0x198A or 0x19A8 returns a non-zero R7. Otherwise, if bit 7 of XDATA 0x0490 is set, the carry is set when bit 0 of XDATA 0x049E or bit 5 or bit 3 of XDATA 0x049D is set. If bit 7 of 0x0490 is clear, the carry is set when bit 0 of XDATA 0x0496 or bit 5 or bit 3 of XDATA 0x0495 is set. The decompile carries a `Type propagation algorithm not settling` warning and models only one of the two flag groups, so it does not show the 0x0490 bit 7 path.

name: write_30_to_0679_and_14_to_0678
comment: Writes 0x30 to XDATA 0x0679 and 0x14 to XDATA 0x0678, then tail-jumps to 0x8B31 with an ljmp, so no return address of its own is pushed. Nothing in this listing reads the two bytes back, so what they hold is not decoded here.

name: count_down_0678_0679_pair
comment: Returns immediately to the 0x8B31 exit unless XDATA 0x06C2 reads as zero. With it zero, bit 7 of XDATA 0x06E1 or bit 1 of 0x0459 jumps to 0x8D74; otherwise XDATA 0x0678 is decremented, reloaded with 0x14 on underflow while 0x0679 is decremented, and when 0x0679 also reaches zero 0x8D74 is called, bit 6 of 0x06E1 is cleared and control tail-jumps to 0x8B33. Every other path tail-jumps to 0x8B31.

name: write_05_to_06c4_after_1984_check
comment: Exits through 0x8B31 at once if bit 7 of XDATA 0x0800 is set. Otherwise, when bit 6 of XDATA 0x0801 is set and XDATA 0x0630 is zero, it calls 0x1984 and tail-jumps to 0x8B33 if the returned R7 is zero; every other outcome writes 0x05 to XDATA 0x06C4 and then tail-jumps to 0x8B31. The decompiler's param_1 is the R7 result of 0x1984, not an argument passed in.

name: dispatch_on_0490_0495_0496_0498
comment: Falls through to the ret at 0x8E4B unless bit 7 of XDATA 0x0800 is clear, bit 6 of 0x0801 is set, 0x1984 returns non-zero in R7, XDATA 0x06E6 is not 0x84 and XDATA 0x06C3 is zero. A non-zero 0x06C3, bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490, or a non-zero XDATA 0x06DA jumps to 0x8ECC. With those clear, bit 6 of 0x0490 selects a second level: clear reads 0x0495, 0x0560 and 0x0496 and ends in an R4 code of 0xB1, 0xF1 or 0x15 handed to 0x8E3B with R6 = 1 (with 0x14 or 0x1A sent to 0x8F37/0x8F54 on the way), set reads 0x0498 and ends in 0xB3 to 0x8E3B with R6 = 3, or 0x3A to 0x8F37/0x8F54. The listing stops at 0x8E8F and the .c continues past the separate 0x8E91 and 0x8ECC entries, so that tail is reported from the .c and not decoded here.

name: write_r4_to_047f_then_047e_fc
comment: Copies R4 to XDATA 0x047F, loads R7 with 0x84, calls 0x19A2, then writes 0xFC to XDATA 0x047E and returns. The value 0x19A2 returns in R7 is not tested here, and R4 is the only input consumed.

name: dispatch_on_049d_049e_05e0
comment: Loads R4 = 0xB2 and R6 = 2, then tail-jumps into 0x8E3B with that R4 if XDATA 0x049D & 0xC4 is non-zero, if XDATA 0x05E0 & 0xF0 equals 0xF0 (R4 becomes 0xF2), or if bit 4 of XDATA 0x049E is set (R4 is 0x25 at that point). Bit 3 of 0x049E sends R4 = 0x24 to 0x8F37 and XDATA 0x049D & 0x28 sends R4 = 0x2A to 0x8F54, both then jumping to 0x8ECC, which is also where control goes when neither bit is set. The listing ends at 0x8ECA and the .c continues to 0x8EF8, past the separate 0x8ECC entry, so the CPU_TEMP comparison in that tail is reported from the .c and is not decoded here.

name: select_r4_from_cpu_temp_and_0620_0626
comment: Sets R4 = 0xCF and R6 = 4, then compares CPU_TEMP (XDATA 0x043E) against 0x57 when XDATA 0x0458 & 0x70 equals 0x10 and against 0x6E otherwise; a CPU_TEMP at or above the limit tail-jumps to 0x8E3B. Otherwise R4 = 0xC5 and XDATA 0x0620 equal to 0xCC also tail-jumps to 0x8E3B; R6 becomes 5 and XDATA 0x068A & 0xF0 equal to 0xF0 sends R4 = 0x1C there, XDATA 0x06D1 equal to 0 with 0x0620 equal to 0xC1 sends R4 = 0xC1 to 0x8F37, XDATA 0x0626 equal to 0xCC sends R4 = 0xC3 to 0x8E3B and 0x0626 equal to 0xC1 sends R4 = 0xC2 to 0x8F37. No XDATA byte is written on any of these paths, and the chosen R4 reaches 0x8E3B as an argument the caller cannot see.

name: write_047f_and_arm_06d1_fa
comment: Writes R4 to XDATA 0x047F and calls 0x19A8; if that returns zero in R7 the routine returns immediately. With R7 non-zero and XDATA 0x06D1 zero it calls 0x88F0 with R5 = 0x27 and writes 0xFA to XDATA 0x06D1, so that byte is set only on the first qualifying call. The decompiler's second parameter is the R7 result of 0x19A8, not an argument passed in.

name: write_047f_and_arm_06d2_fa
comment: If XDATA 0x06D2 is non-zero it returns without touching anything. Otherwise it writes R4 to XDATA 0x047F, calls 0x88F0 with R5 = 0x0A and writes 0xFA to XDATA 0x06D2, so the store pair runs only on the first call after 0x06D2 has been read as zero.

name: store_a_to_xdata_at_dptr
comment: The whole listing is one instruction, movx @DPTR, A, storing A to whatever XDATA address DPTR already holds; the .c for this address decompiles the same single store. Nothing in the listing loads DPTR or shows a caller, and the file header states the function boundary is a hypothesis, so which address is written and why is not decoded here.

name: ret_only_fragment
comment: The whole listing is a single ret, so the code at this address does nothing observable in its own frame. The file header notes that the boundary is a hypothesis, so whether this is an entry point or the return of a routine entered elsewhere is not decoded from this pair of files.

name: load_dptr_06ce
comment: The whole listing is one instruction, mov DPTR, #0x6CE, and the byte that would consume DPTR is not in this file. The .c for this address decompiles a much longer body than the one instruction listed, so the two disagree about where the function starts and what this instruction contributes is not decoded here.

name: store_a_to_xdata_at_dptr_2
comment: The whole listing is one instruction, movx @DPTR, A; the .c for this address decompiles a long flag-and-counter body rather than this single store. Whether 0x06CE is the target here cannot be read off this listing, since nothing in it loads DPTR, so the role is not decoded.

name: update_06cf_countdown_and_06e1_bits
comment: Clears bit 3 of XDATA 0x06E1, then decrements a non-zero XDATA 0x06CF and returns. At zero it tests whether XDATA 0x06E6 equals 0x03 or bit 1 or bit 3 of XDATA 0x0472 is set; if so and bit 2 of 0x06E1 is set it calls 0x1768, then 0xA57E with R5 = 0x09, then 0x1762, and clears bit 2 of 0x06E1. Otherwise it loads XDATA 0x06CE and 0x06CF with 0x64 and, when bit 4 of 0x06E1 is clear, sets bit 4 and calls 0x88F0 with R5 = 0x16 if XDATA 0x0440 is non-zero (then clearing bit 2 of 0x06E1) or calls 0x19F6 if 0x0440 is zero. Whether this address is an entry point or the continuation of the routine at 0x8F6B is not shown by the listing.

name: count_down_06e4_and_toggle_06e3
comment: If XDATA 0x045F equals 0xDB and bit 5 of XDATA 0x04FF is set it calls 0x9178 and returns. Otherwise a non-zero XDATA 0x06E4 is decremented and control jumps to 0x90B8; at zero, XDATA 0x06E3 is XORed with 0x01 and stored back, and if the new value's bit 0 is set the next address is 0x90B2 while otherwise 0x0E is written to XDATA 0x06E4. The listing stops at 0x90AF, so the code at 0x90B2 and the rest of the 0x06E4/0x084E sequencing the .c shows are reported from the .c and not decoded here.

name: forward_to_90b8
comment: The whole listing is a single sjmp 0x90B8, so control passes to the routine at 0x90B8 without a call and no return address is pushed here. The decompiler renders it as a thunk of that routine.

name: step_counter_084e_dispatch
comment: When bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490 is clear, bit 5 of XDATA 0x0476 is set and XDATA 0x06E6 is 0x01, it increments XDATA 0x084E and branches on the new value: 0x01 calls 0x1738, 0x19FC and 0x1A02, 0x0B calls 0x1A08, 0x1A02 and 0x1A0E, 0x15 falls through to the reset and any other value goes to the 0x476 bit 5 test. Otherwise it zeroes 0x084E and, unless bit 4 of XDATA 0x0466 is set while XDATA 0x06E6 has bit 7 set, calls 0x1A14. The closing block reads XDATA 0x0480, 0x0472, 0x06E6 and 0x06E3 to decide whether to call 0x19A8, and calls 0x1990 only when 0x06E6 is neither 0x01 nor 0x03. The decompiler's param_1 is the R7 return of 0x1984, not an argument passed in.

name: call_1738_1a0e_1a1a
comment: Calls 0x1738, then 0x1A0E, then 0x1A1A, in that order, and returns. No XDATA byte is read or written here and no return value is tested, so what the three calls accomplish is not visible in this listing.

name: add_two_xdata_bytes_to_r1r2_and_halve
comment: Reads two consecutive XDATA bytes at DPTR and DPTR+1 into R3 and R4, adds them to the 16-bit value held in R1 (low) and R2 (high) with carry, then shifts that sum right by one bit through the carry and leaves the result in R1:R2. DPTR is left pointing one byte past the second byte read.

name: store_r1_r2_to_xdata_at_dptr
comment: Writes R1 to the XDATA address in DPTR, increments DPTR and writes R2 to the next address, so the 16-bit register pair R1:R2 goes out low byte first. Nothing else is read or written and no return value is produced.

name: gate_1984_19a8_then_count_06cc
comment: Calls 0x1984 and 0x19A8 and, if either returns zero in R7 or bit 5 of XDATA 0x0801 is set or bit 7 of XDATA 0x0471 is set, calls 0x17FE and returns. Otherwise it decrements a non-zero XDATA 0x06CC and then calls 0x17FE, or, when 0x06CC is already zero, calls 0x1A20 instead. The decompiler's param_1 does not correspond to anything passed in.

name: dispatch_062e_counter_via_table_91d0
comment: Increments XDATA 0x062E, stores it back, masks the new value with 0x07 and jumps indirectly: DPTR is loaded with 0x91D0, R0 takes the index, A is doubled into it twice and jmp @A+DPTR transfers to 0x91D0 plus three times the index, so the table is a sequence of three-byte long jumps. The table entries and their targets are not in this listing; the decompiled C reads the eight cases as 0x91FA, 0x9202, 0xC352, 0x92F7, 0x9373, 0x91FA, 0x91FA and 0x91FA.

name: clear_062e_and_jump_94a8
comment: Writes 0x00 to XDATA 0x062E, the counter 0x91E8 dispatches on, and then tail-jumps to 0x94A8 with an ljmp. Nothing is read here and no return value is produced, so what 0x94A8 does with the cleared counter is not visible in this listing.

name: step_0628_nibble_against_92dc_table
comment: Returns unless XDATA 0x06E6 equals 0x01. It then reads CPU_TEMP (XDATA 0x043E) into R6, takes the low nibble of XDATA 0x0628 as R7, calls 0x92DC to obtain a CODE table address in R2:R1 and compares table[R7], then table[0x10+R7], against CPU_TEMP, incrementing R7 when table[R7] is at or below CPU_TEMP and decrementing it when table[0x10+R7] is at or above CPU_TEMP and R7 is not zero, with both ends of the 0x00-0x0F range clamped; the new R7 is stored back to 0x0628. It reads table[0x20+R7] into R6 and stores that byte to XDATA 0x0620, reloading XDATA 0x0894 with 0x14 when the byte is non-zero and decrementing a non-zero 0x0894 while leaving 0x0620 untouched when it is zero. The listing jumps from 0x9209 to 0x926C, so 0x9211-0x926B is not decoded here and the table contents at 0x920C and 0x923C live outside this file.

name: clamp_a_to_7_and_set_0723_08e2
comment: Returns A+1 when the incoming A is below 0x07, the comparison being A - 0x07 with the carry cleared. Otherwise it sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x0723 and bit 3 of XDATA 0x08E2, calls 0x19BA and returns 0x07. The input arrives in the accumulator; no other register is read.

name: select_table_920c_or_923c_by_074c
comment: Reads XDATA 0x074C and masks the low nibble: a non-zero nibble loads DPTR with 0x923C and a zero nibble loads 0x920C, in both cases copying DPH then DPL into R2 and R1 and returning. No XDATA is written, so this is purely a selector of a CODE address for the caller to index, and the tables themselves are not in this listing.

name: write_057b_057c_057d_and_call_888c
comment: Writes 0x0A, 0x08 and 0x1F to XDATA 0x057B, 0x057C and 0x057D, then overwrites 0x057D with 0x11 unless bit 0 of XDATA 0x0497 is set and XDATA 0x0539 equals 0x01, or bit 0 is clear and XDATA 0x0403 is below 0x14. If bit 7 of XDATA 0x0490 is set it calls 0x8886 with DPTR = 0x05B2 and 0x888C with DPTR = 0x0646. Otherwise it calls 0x9354 and then branches on the carry flag that call leaves in place, loading DPTR with 0x2AF8 when carry is set and 0x1770 when it is clear, passing that address in R2:R1 to a final 0x888C with DPTR = 0x0646.

name: gate_030a_030b_then_8892_887a
comment: Returns with the carry flag cleared unless XDATA 0x030A is 0x03 and XDATA 0x030B is 0x02. When both match it reads XDATA 0x0318, calls 0x8892 with that value in A, then calls 0x887A with R1 = 0xE0 and R2 = 0x2E and returns, leaving whatever carry 0x887A set for the caller to test.

name: gate_0456_80_and_06e6_01
comment: Checks bit 7 of XDATA 0x0456 and requires XDATA 0x06E6 to equal 0x01; if both hold it tail-jumps to 0x9416, otherwise it returns immediately. No XDATA byte is read or written here, so all the work is in the routine at 0x9416, which is not decoded in this listing.

name: adjust_0627_index_against_gpu_temp
comment: Reads GPU_TEMP at XDATA 0x044F and picks one of three CODE tables -- 0x9386 when the low nibble of 0x074C is nonzero, otherwise 0x93E6 if bit 7 of MANUAL_FAN_CTRL (0x0751) is set and 0x93B6 if it is not -- then indexes the chosen table with the low nibble of XDATA 0x0627. The entry at that offset, when less than or equal to GPU_TEMP, increments 0x0627 but only if bit 3 of the incremented value is clear; the entry 0x10 further on, when greater than or equal to GPU_TEMP, decrements 0x0627 if it is nonzero. The entry at offset +0x20 is copied to XDATA 0x0626; when that entry is zero and 0x0895 is nonzero, 0x0895 is decremented and 0x0626 is left alone, and when the entry is nonzero 0x0895 is reloaded with 0x14.

name: lookup_94a0_table_by_0620_low3
comment: Returns immediately if bit 7 of XDATA 0x04FF is set, if bit 3 of 0x08E2 is set, or if 0x085B is nonzero. Otherwise it passes the values of XDATA 0x0621, 0x0622, 0x0623 and 0x081D in R0 to four separate calls of 0x88A4, stores the byte read from 0x0620 to XDATA 0x045C, and uses the low three bits of that same value to index a CODE table at 0x94A0, writing the result to both XDATA 0x0874 and 0x087C before a final call to 0xC6B8. The decompiler's C turns the 0x04FF test into a signed comparison; the listing's jb on bit 7 is a plain bit test.

name: magic_55aa_and_0704_countdown
comment: Calls 0x1984, and if R7 is zero and XDATA 0x07FE/0x07FF hold 0x55/0xAA, clears both and then either jumps to 0x95B7 when 0x07FD is 0x5A or clears XDATA 0x0045, 0x07FD and 0x1F07. It then copies a nonzero XDATA 0x0470 into 0x06F1, clears 0x0470, and sets 0x06F7 to 0x80 and 0x06F2 to 1. If 0x045F is 0xAA it increments XDATA 0x06D0 and, once that reaches 2, calls 0x88F0 with R5 = the byte at 0x045E and clears 0x06D0, 0x045F and 0x045E; any 0x045F other than 0xDB also clears 0x04FE and 0x04FF. Finally, when 0x045D is nonzero and the R7 tests after 0x1984 and 0x19A8 and bit 5 of 0x0801 do not all force an early return, it jumps to 0x95B7 if XDATA 0x0704 is zero and otherwise decrements 0x0704.

name: copy_045d_to_0704
comment: Reads XDATA 0x045D and writes it unchanged to XDATA 0x0704. Nothing else is touched.

name: load_0704_from_045d_then_branch
comment: Calls 0x95AE (which copies XDATA 0x045D to 0x0704) and then 0x9ED4 with A = 0xE6, followed by 0x1984. If R7 is zero it calls 0x8B8F and returns; otherwise it calls 0x19A8, returns if R7 is nonzero and XDATA 0x06E6 is not 2, and calls 0x1768, 0xA567 with R5 = 0xC8, and 0x1762 when 0x06E6 is 2. The bodies of 0x1984, 0x19A8 and 0x9ED4 are not in this listing, so only the R7 branch is observable here; the decompiler's C folds this body into 0x94FA, whose listing does not contain it.

name: set_0476_bit1_then_branch_on_r7

Otherwise it calls 0x1984 and, if R7 is still nonzero, 0x19A8 and then 0x159A again, branching on R7 a second time. name: decrement_0980_then_run_19b4_198a
comment: Does nothing unless bit 0 of XDATA 0x97F is set, then calls 0x1A08. If 0x980 is non-zero it is decremented in place and the function returns unless the result is zero; on zero it calls 0x19B4, clears bit 0 of 0x983, calls 0x198A, and calls 0x1A6E only when the R7 that 0x198A returns is zero. The decompiler's param_1 is that R7, not an argument passed in.

name: tick_09e3_countdown
comment: Reads XDATA 0x09E3 and returns at once if it is zero. With bit 7 set it takes the abort route: it calls 0x8B8F, calls 0x9ED4 with 0xE8, then clears 0x09E3. With bit 7 clear the low seven bits are decremented and stored back; on reaching zero it writes 0xE9 to 0x047E, sets bit 7 of 0x09E3, calls 0x19A2 with R7 = 0x84 and 0x9ED4 with 0xE9, and on reaching 0x1C it calls 0x1A74 and returns.

name: tick_0750_countdown
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0750 and returns at once if it is zero; otherwise it first calls 0xA43B, which may clear 0x0750 by tail-jumping to 0xA44C, after which the re-read of 0x0750 below sees the cleared value. With bit 7 of 0x0750 set it calls 0x8B8F and 0x9ED4 with 0xE8, then tail-jumps to 0xA44C to clear 0x0750, but only when bit 7 of 0x6E6 is clear. With bit 7 clear the low seven bits are decremented and stored, and on reaching zero it writes 0xE9 to 0x047E, sets bit 7 of 0x0750, calls 0x19A2 with R7 = 0x84 and 0x9ED4 with 0xE9. Unlike 0xA3B2 it has no 0x1C test.

name: scan_0b00_for_byte_1c
comment: Walks XDATA upward from 0x0B00, incrementing DPL only, comparing each byte against 0x1C. The walk stops once DPL reaches 0xFD, so the bytes at 0x0B00 through 0x0BFC, 253 of them, are examined and DPH never changes. On a match it tail-jumps to 0xA44C, which clears 0x750; with no match it returns without touching 0x750. What 0x1C signifies in the 0x0B00 region is not decoded here.

name: clear_0750
comment: Writes 0x00 to XDATA 0x0750 and returns. It reads no other location and calls nothing.

name: map_0763_through_f13f_table
comment: Runs only while XDATA 0x762 holds 0xFF and 0x763 does not hold 0x0D. It takes the byte at 0x763 as an unsigned index into a CODE table at 0xF13F with movc, masks the fetched byte with 0x1F, passes it to 0xA476, stores the returned byte in 0x762, and then increments 0x763. The table's own bytes are not part of this listing, so what each index maps to is not decoded here.

name: gate_value_against_045a_bits
comment: Copies the incoming accumulator into B and, for the six values 0x01, 0x05, 0x08, 0x0E, 0x0F and 0x15, returns that value only if the matching bits of XDATA 0x45A are set: 0x01 needs 0x45A & 0x60 non-zero, 0x05 needs bit 7, 0x08 needs bit 4, 0x0E needs bit 5, 0x0F needs bit 6, and 0x15 needs 0x45A & 0xE0 non-zero. When the required bits are clear it returns 0, in the masked cases because the mask itself is what remains in the accumulator. Any other value is returned unchanged out of B, and no XDATA is written.

name: send_ea_to_9ed4_when_06e6_eq_05
comment: Requires XDATA 0x6E6 to equal 0x05, then calls 0x1984 and 0x19A8 in turn and returns if either leaves a zero value in R7. It also returns if 0x047E holds 0xCD or 0xFC; otherwise it calls 0x9ED4 with 0xEA and then 0x8B8F. The decompiler's param_1 is not an argument: the R7 it tests is the return value of each of the two calls.

name: forward_to_a501
comment: Two instructions: lcall 0xA501 followed by ret, so it is a tail call with no work of its own. 0xA501 is not in this listing and was not read, so what it does is not decoded here.

name: gate_0442_06e6_before_call_1a7a
comment: Tests bit 0 of the byte at XDATA 0x0442 and returns at once if it is set. Otherwise reads XDATA 0x06E6 and calls 0x1A7A only when that byte is 0x05 or 0x00; any other value returns without the call. Both gate reads and the single call target are in the listing; what 0x1A7A does is not.

name: code_table_scatter_to_xdata
comment: Loop runs R2 times. Each pass pushes the incoming DPTR, reads three CODE bytes at the source pointer, pops the first two of them back into DPH and DPL so they form a big-endian XDATA address, writes the third CODE byte there with movx, restores the pushed destination and advances it by three. The .c reads the same bytes as a plain byte copy and does not show the address being built from the two leading table bytes. The seven call sites all pass a literal DPTR and R2 and the tables are enumerable from committed CODE: 0x83B7 walks 0x8453 for 0x43 records, 0x841D 0x851C for 0x17, 0x82FD 0x8561 for 0x11, 0x82C9 0x8594 for 1 -- the first three contiguous, 108 records over 0x8453-0x8596 -- then 0xC740 0xC6E2 for 0x0A, 0xC7AC 0xC7A1 for 2 and 0xC7F2 0xC7BD for 0x10. Three of those records store 0x00 to XDATA 0x0440, at CODE 0x8453 record 0, 0x8453 record 2 and 0x851C record 9. The general search that found this, and the fifteen call sites of the caller-supplied-DPTR helpers it does not resolve, are in ec/annotations/xdata-0440-readers.md.

name: write_0_to_200b_7_times
comment: Loads R5 with 7, then runs a loop body that loads DPTR with 0x200B and writes the constant 0 there, decrementing R5 each pass, so seven stores are made and R5 is left at 0. That single XDATA address is the only one the listing touches.

name: write_0_to_200b_335_times
comment: Two nested counters, R5 = 0x43 and R6 = 5, drive 335 executions of a body that writes 0 to XDATA 0x200B. A and direct address 0x06 are pushed on entry and popped before returning, so both survive; R5 is left at 0. No other address appears in the listing.

name: write_0_to_200b_r5_times_330
comment: The incoming R5 is copied into A and becomes the outer counter; each pass runs an inner R6 = 5 by R5 = 0x42 loop, 330 writes of 0 to XDATA 0x200B, so the store count is 330 times the entry value of R5. A and direct address 0x06 are pushed and popped around the inner loop on every pass including the first, and the original R5 is not restored. Nothing beyond the store count is decoded here.

name: mul_partial_products_r0_r1_r2_r3
comment: Uses MUL AB on the pairs R0xR2, R0xR3, R2xR1 and R3xR1 and threads the carry through R4, which are the four partial products a 16x16 unsigned multiply needs. It finishes by storing the low accumulation in R0 with R1 forced to 0, the R3xR1 product plus carry in R2:R3, and popping the two direct-byte slots 0x00 and 0x04 that it pushed. The .c returns a single char and models none of the register results, so the final 32-bit layout is not decoded further.

name: mul_16_round_shift_subtract
comment: Clears R7 and R6, sets B to 0x10, then runs 16 rounds. Each round shifts R1, R2, R6, R7 and then R0, R5 left with carry cleared, and compares R6:R7 against R3:R4, replacing R6:R7 with the difference whenever the subtract produced no borrow. On exit it copies R5 to R2, R0 to R1, R7 to R4 and R6 to R3. Which register holds which operand is not decoded further, and the .c drops the conditional subtract.

name: zero_xdata_block_at_dph00
comment: Clears A, then picks a count: R0 = 0xFD (253) when R1 == 7 and R0 = 0 otherwise. With DPH inherited from the caller and DPL loaded from A (zero), it writes 0 to XDATA at (DPH:0x00), increments DPTR and repeats while R0 is nonzero, so 253 bytes are zeroed in the R1 == 7 case and one byte otherwise. The .c reads the same bytes as a 3-or-0-byte clear on a pointer derived from a parameter, which the listing does not show.

name: dispatch_0832_event_bits
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0832 and tests bit addresses 0xE1, 0xE0, 0xE2, 0xE3, 0xE4, 0xE5 and 0xE6 in that order. The first three tests fall into inline blocks that clear the matching bit, set R3/R4/R5, load R6:R7 from a pair of XDATA addresses and call 0x19D2 and 0x859B; bits 3, 4, 5 and 6 tail-jump to 0xA7D8, 0xA7F7, 0xA7F7 and 0xA816. If no test is taken it writes 0 to XDATA 0x0832 and jumps to 0xA835. On the instruction stream the test operands are bit addresses in internal RAM 0xE0, not masks on the byte just read into A; the .c reads them as masks, and this listing does not settle which the hardware means.

name: flag_0832_bit3_send_12_3f_8c
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0832 into A, executes clr 0xE3, and writes A back to the same address; clr 0xE3 is a bit-address clear in internal RAM 0xE0 and does not change A, so the byte stored is the one just read. It then sets R3 = 0x12, R4 = 0x3F, R5 = 0x8C, R6:R7 from XDATA 0x083A/0x083B, calls 0x19D2 and 0x859B, and tail-jumps to 0xA835. The .c renders the same three instructions as clearing bit 3 of 0x0832.

name: flag_0832_bit5_send_12_3b_8c
comment: Same shape as the bit-3 handler: read XDATA 0x0832, clr 0xE5, write A back unchanged, set R3 = 0x12, R4 = 0x3B, R5 = 0x8C and R6:R7 from XDATA 0x0830/0x0831, call 0x19D2 then 0x859B, tail-jump to 0xA835. The dispatcher at 0xA750 sends both bit 4 and bit 5 here, while the clear it performs is on bit address 0xE5, so the two bits are not distinguished by these bytes.

name: flag_0832_bit6_send_12_12_8c
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0832 into A, executes clr 0xE6, writes A back unchanged, sets R3 = 0x12, R4 = 0x12, R5 = 0x8C and R6:R7 from XDATA 0x083C/0x083D, calls 0x19D2 and 0x859B, then sjmp 0xA835. As in the sibling handlers the store is the value read, not a masked one, and what 0x19D2 or 0x859B do with the registers is not decoded here.

name: write_5_to_0680
comment: Four instructions: load DPTR with 0x0680, load A with 5, write it, return. It is the common tail of the 0xA750 dispatch group and of the A7D8, A7F7 and A816 handlers. Nothing in this listing reads 0x0680 back, so what the value 5 means to the hardware is not decoded here.

name: dispatch_086f_event_bits
comment: Reads XDATA 0x086F and tests bit addresses 0xE0, 0xE1, 0xE2, 0xE3, 0xE4, 0xE5 and 0xE7 in that order, tail-jumping to 0xA873, 0xA88D, 0xA8A7, 0xA8C5, 0xA8DA, 0xA8DF and 0xA8E4; bit 6 (0xE6) is never tested here. If no test is taken it writes 0 to XDATA 0x086F and jumps to 0xA8E9. As at 0xA750 the operands are bit addresses in internal RAM 0xE0, which the .c instead renders as masks on the byte just read.

name: flag_086f_bit0_send_5a_01_88
comment: Clears bit address 0xE0, writes the value already in A back through DPTR (still 0x086F from the dispatcher), then calls 0x1A80 with R3 = 0x5A, R4 = 0x01, R5 = 0x88, R6 = 0x00, R7 = 0x00, calls 0x85AE, calls 0x88F0 with R5 = 0x77, and tail-jumps to 0xA8E9. The store to 0x086F puts A back unchanged, so on the instruction stream it rewrites the byte; the .c shows it as clearing bit 0.

name: flag_086f_bit1_send_5a_01_88_ff
comment: Same shape as the bit-0 handler, clearing bit address 0xE1 and passing R6 = 0xFF, R7 = 0x00 to 0x1A80 with R3 = 0x5A, R4 = 0x01, R5 = 0x88, then 0x85AE, then 0x88F0 with R5 = 0x78, and tail-jumping to 0xA8E9. A is again written back to XDATA 0x086F unchanged.

name: flag_086f_bit2_send_5a_02_88_table
comment: Clears bit address 0xE2, writes A back to XDATA 0x086F, then reads XDATA 0x0826 into R6 and uses that byte as an index into a CODE table based at 0xA83C (DPTR = 0xA83C, movc A,@A+DPTR), passing the table byte in R6 with R7 = 0x00 to 0x1A80 after R3 = 0x5A, R4 = 0x02, R5 = 0x88. Calls 0x85AE and tail-jumps to 0xA8E9. The table's length and contents are not decoded here.

name: clear_bit_e4_then_tail_a8e9
comment: Three instructions after the entry point: clr 0xE4, movx @DPTR,A with DPTR still 0x086F and A the value read by the dispatcher, then sjmp 0xA8E9. No call and no register set-up, unlike the 0xA873 to 0xA8C5 handlers which do the same store and then call 0x1A80 and 0x85AE. The .c ends the function at the store and shows the clear as a mask on 0x086F.

name: write_5_to_068b
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x068B, loads A with 5, writes it and returns. It is the common tail of the 0xA841 dispatch group: 0xA8DA and 0xA8DF jump to its first instruction and 0xA8E4 jumps to its ret. Nothing in this listing reads 0x068B back.

name: clamp_0623_level_into_080e
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0623, masks bit 2 down to 0 and keeps the result in R1, forcing R1 to 4 if that value is 5 or more. Reading XDATA 0x0476, bit 5 set forces R1 to 0. It then reads XDATA 0x080E and, because cjne A,0x01 compares against direct address 0x01 (R1) rather than the immediate 1, returns without writing when the stored byte already equals R1 and otherwise writes R1 to XDATA 0x080E.

name: clamp_078b_level_into_0804
comment: Four gates, each returning via 0xA9B3 unless all pass: bit 4 of XDATA 0x08EB clear, XDATA 0x0440 non-zero, XDATA 0x080D zero, bit 4 of XDATA 0x0442 clear. It reads XDATA 0x078B, decrements it into R1, and keeps R1 only if the result is below 5, otherwise setting R1 to 0. Nine XDATA bytes (0x080E, 0x080C, 0x0808, 0x0805, 0x0626, 0x08AC, 0x08BA, 0x08A1, 0x08A2) are each loaded into R0 and passed to 0x88A4. R1 is then clamped to 4 and written to XDATA 0x0804 unless 0x0804 already equals it, and if bit 7 of XDATA 0x0456 is set it calls 0x88F0 with R5 = R1 + 0xD1.

name: return_stub
comment: A single ret. It is the target of five ljmp instructions inside 0xA916, where it serves as that function's common exit: the four early gates, the case where XDATA 0x0804 already holds the computed value, and the case where bit 7 of XDATA 0x0456 is clear. Nothing else is decoded in these bytes.

name: step_state_0845
comment: Returns at once unless XDATA 0x06C2 is zero and XDATA 0x06E6 is 0x05. It then calls 0x19F0 and takes a short path writing 0x0A to XDATA 0x0845 if that call returns carry set, and otherwise requires 0x1984 (skipped when XDATA 0x047E is 0xEC), 0x198A and 0x1990 each to leave R7 zero, plus bit 0 of XDATA 0x097C clear, returning if any of these fails. A non-zero XDATA 0x0845 is decremented by one and written back, returning at once unless the old value was 1. Otherwise it calls 0x1A86, 0xA567 with R5 = 1, 0x198A and, when R7 is zero and XDATA 0x0756 and 0x0845 are both zero, 0x1996; then it calls 0xA567 with R5 = 0x64 and 0x1A74 and writes 0xF0 to XDATA 0x0845 if bit 3 of XDATA 0x160A is clear, or 0x0A if that bit is set.

name: step_counters_0756_0757
comment: Returns immediately if XDATA 0x0756 is zero, otherwise calls 0xAAA2 first. If bit address 0xE7 is clear it masks the low seven bits of 0x0756, decrements them and writes the result back, and on reaching zero calls 0x1A86, 0xA567 with R5 = 0x64 and 0x1A74, then 0x8E3B and 0x1A92, sets bit 7 of XDATA 0x0756, writes 5 to XDATA 0x0757 and calls 0x9ED4 with A = 0x30. If bit address 0xE7 is set it decrements XDATA 0x0757 when that byte is non-zero, and when 0x0757 is zero calls 0x1A8C, 0x1A86, 0xA567 with R5 = 0x64 and 0x1A74, clears bit 7 of 0x0756, then calls 0x8B8F and 0x9ED4 with A = 0x81. On the instruction stream 0xE7 is a bit address in internal RAM 0xE0 rather than a mask on the byte just read, so the two arms do not depend on the high bit of XDATA 0x0756.

name: clear_0756_when_1c_found_in_b00_fc
comment: Walks XDATA from 0x0B00 upward, comparing each byte with 0x1C and stopping the loop when DPL reaches 0xFD, so the range scanned is 0x0B00 to 0x0BFC inclusive, 253 bytes. On the first match it writes 0 to XDATA 0x0756 and returns immediately; if the range is scanned out with no match it returns without touching 0x0756. No other address is referenced.

name: write_083c_083d_and_0832_bit6
comment: Tests bit address 0xE0 and then 0xE2, and only if both are taken requires (XDATA 0x0491 & 0xC0) == 0xC0 before choosing 0x83; every other combination chooses 0x81. Both paths write 0x18 to XDATA 0x083C, the chosen constant to XDATA 0x083D, and OR 0x40 into the byte read from XDATA 0x0832 and write it back. As at 0xA750 the two tests are on bit addresses in internal RAM 0xE0, so on the instruction stream the choice does not depend on the bytes read from XDATA 0x0490 immediately before them.

name: write_0830_0831_and_0832_bit5
comment: Tests bit address 0xE0: when it is set 0x02 is written to XDATA 0x0831, when it is clear 0xC2 is. Both arms write 0x10 to XDATA 0x0830 and OR 0x20 into the byte read from XDATA 0x0832. The read of XDATA 0x0490 immediately before the test does not affect the branch on the instruction stream, because 0xE0 is a bit address in internal RAM 0xE0 and not a mask on A; the .c reads it as a mask on 0x0490.

name: latch_0983_b2_from_0442_b3
comment: Copies bit 3 of the byte at XDATA 0x442 into bit 2 of XDATA 0x983, in both directions. On the 0-to-1 transition it first writes 0x0A to XDATA 0x80F, 0x0A to XDATA 0x80D and 0x20 to XDATA 0x806, then sets the bit; on the 1-to-0 transition it only clears the bit. If the two bits already agree nothing is written. None of 0x983, 0x442, 0x80F, 0x80D and 0x806 is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so no meaning is claimed for the values written.

name: write_0680_03_or_04_from_04fe_0490
comment: Reads bit 4 of the byte at XDATA 0x4FE. If that bit is set it writes 0x04 to XDATA 0x680 and returns; if it is clear it then reads bit 2 of XDATA 0x490, and on that bit set it tail-jumps to 0xE100 with no store in this frame, otherwise it writes 0x03 to XDATA 0x680. What 0xE100 does is not decoded here. None of 0x4FE, 0x490 and 0x680 is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so no meaning is claimed for the values written.

name: write_1c00_ff_and_0680_04
comment: Tests two bits of the byte at XDATA 0x490. Only when bit 1 is set and bit 2 is clear does it tail-jump to 0xDE3C, with no write in this frame; in every other case it writes 0xFF to XDATA 0x1C00, writes 0x04 to XDATA 0x680, and returns. What 0xDE3C does is not decoded here. None of 0x490, 0x1C00 and 0x680 is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_0681_bit7
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x1C00; if bit 2 is set it returns without writing anything. Otherwise it reads the byte at XDATA 0x1C0A and, if that byte is not 0x07, reads XDATA 0x681, ORs 0x80 into it and writes it back, so bit 7 is set. The listing ends at that store on 0xAC82 with no ret, and the next census entry 0xAC83 is a bare ret, so the return this path takes is not in this listing. None of 0x1C00, 0x1C0A and 0x681 is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: ret_only_ac83
