Nothing is read, written or compared here, so its role is not determinable from these instructions.

name: ten_step_check_1aaa_889e
comment: Tail-jumps to 0xDB0B when bit 0 of XDATA 0x497 is set. Otherwise it runs ten steps: each loads R3 = 0x16, R4 = one of 0x08, 0x0F, 0x18, 0x19, 0x0D, 0x09, 0x3C, 0x3D, 0x3E, 0x3F and R5 = 0x0C and calls 0x1AAA, bailing out with CY set if that call returned carry, and on carry clear sets DPTR to the matching XDATA address (0x502, 0x518, 0x52A, 0x52E, 0x514, 0x506, 0x53A, 0x53C, 0x53E, 0x540 in that order) and calls 0x889E. After the sixth step it reads XDATA 0x491, masks it with 0xC0 and branches on the result: 0x80 skips the 0x3C step, 0x40 skips both the 0x3C and 0x3D steps, and any other value runs the 0x3C step, so the 0x3E and 0x3F steps and the 0x540 DPTR are on every path. The full-success path returns with CY clear. What 0x1AAA, 0x889E and 0xDB0B do, what the R4 constants mean, and what the XDATA slots hold are not decoded here; none of those addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: round_robin_dispatch_on_0566
comment: Increments the byte at XDATA 0x566, masks it with 0x07, multiplies the result by three and jumps indirectly through the eight three-byte entries starting at CODE 0xAD50 (jmp @A+DPTR with DPTR = 0xAD50). The table itself is not in this listing; the .c's switch reads those eight targets as 0xB56C, 0xADFD, 0xAF06, 0xAD8B, 0xB2D5, 0xB33B, 0xC245 and 0xC245, so index 6 and index 7 land on the same routine. None of the eight targets is decoded here.

name: forwarder_to_b56c
comment: Three bytes: ljmp 0xB56C, with nothing executed here. AD77.c is the decompiler following that tail jump, so the XDATA addresses 0x548, 0x43A, 0x436 and 0x0490 and the calls to 0x8886, 0x8892, 0x8863 and 0x888C that it shows belong to 0xB56C and are reported from the .c, not decoded from these bytes.

name: forwarder_to_adfd
comment: Three bytes: ljmp 0xADFD, with nothing executed here. AD7A.c is the decompiler following that tail jump, so the test of bit 2 of XDATA 0x0490, the index byte 0x056A and the indirect jump it reports belong to 0xADFD and are read from the .c, not decoded from these bytes; the .c also carries a warning that the jump table at 0xAE15 was not recovered.

name: forwarder_to_af06
comment: Three bytes: ljmp 0xAF06, with nothing executed here. AD7D.c is the decompiler following that tail jump, so the tests of bit 2 of XDATA 0x0490 and bit 3 of XDATA 0x04FF and the XDATA addresses 0x0503, 0x0505, 0x0502 and 0x04A2 that it shows belong to 0xAF06 and are reported from the .c, not decoded from these bytes.

name: forwarder_to_ad8b
comment: Two bytes: sjmp 0xAD8B, with nothing executed here. AD80.c is the decompiler following that jump, so the tests of XDATA 0x0490, 0x0492, 0x04A0, 0x0524, 0x0494, 0x0518, 0x0546 and 0x0497 that it shows belong to 0xAD8B and are reported from the .c, not decoded from these bytes.

name: forwarder_to_b2d5
comment: Three bytes: ljmp 0xB2D5, with nothing executed here. AD82.c is the decompiler following that jump, so the copies from 0x0514 and 0x0516 and the rest of the body it shows belong to 0xB2D5 and are reported from the .c, not decoded from these bytes.

name: forwarder_to_b33b
comment: Three bytes: ljmp 0xB33B, with nothing executed here. AD85.c is the decompiler following that jump, so the 140-line body it shows belongs to 0xB33B and is reported from the .c, not decoded from these bytes.

name: forwarder_to_c245
comment: Three bytes: ljmp 0xC245, with nothing executed here. AD88.c is the decompiler following that jump, so the switch on XDATA 0x0490 and the writes to 0x0432 and 0x04F2 that it shows belong to 0xC245 and are reported from the .c, not decoded from these bytes.

name: update_0492_from_0490_0524
comment: Masks XDATA 0x0490 with 7: any value other than 7 writes 0 to 0x0492 and returns. With 7 it reads 0x0492, and if that is 0 it loads 0x04A0 into R1 (unused in this listing) and, when 0x0524 equals 1, writes 0x20 to 0x0492. When 0x0492 is non-zero it requires bit 5 of 0x04A0 to be clear and 0x0494 to be 0, loads 0x0518/0x0519 into R3:R4 and 0x0546/0x0547 into R1:R2, calls the 16-bit compare helper at 0x8863, and on carry clears bit 7 of 0x0497 and tail-jumps to 0xB937. None of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, and what 0xB937 does is not decoded here.

name: dispatch_on_056a_low3
comment: Returns immediately unless bit 2 of XDATA 0x0490 is set, then masks 0x056A with 7, multiplies the result by three by adding R0 to A twice, and jumps indirectly through 0xADE2 plus that offset, so the eight three-byte entries of the table at 0xADE2-0xADF9 select the handler. The table's own bytes are not in this listing, so the eight target addresses are not decoded here; Ghidra reports the same failure to recover the jumptable at 0xAE15. 0x0490 and 0x056A are not documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_056a_1_on_carry_from_ae2b
comment: Loads R6 with 0 and tail-jumps to 0xAE6F if bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490 is set. Otherwise it calls 0xAE2B and tail-jumps to 0xAE6F on carry clear, or writes 1 to 0x056A and returns on carry set. The listing ends at the ret on 0xAE2A; the write to 0x0496 that the .c shows next is in the separate entry at 0xAE6F, not in these bytes. Neither 0x0490 nor 0x056A is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: cmp_0436_0437_against_040a_040b
comment: Five instructions: loads the 16-bit value at XDATA 0x0436/0x0437 into R3:R4 (0x8892), loads the 16-bit value at 0x040A/0x040B into R1:R2 (0x8886), calls the 16-bit compare helper at 0x8863 and returns its A and carry unchanged. The helper sets carry when R4:R3 is below R2:R1, which is what the callers at 0xAE16 and 0xAE42 branch on; none of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: chain_probes_update_056a_0_1_2
comment: Loads R6 with 1 and tail-jumps to 0xAED9 if bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490 is set. Otherwise it calls 0xAE2B and, on carry clear, jumps to 0xAE3B which writes 0 to 0x056A; on carry set it calls 0xAE5F and, on carry clear, tail-jumps to 0xAE6F, or writes 2 to 0x056A. The three instructions at 0xAE3B-0xAE41 that open the listing are the target of that first branch, not part of this entry. None of 0x0490 or 0x056A is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: cmp_0436_0437_against_0544_0545
comment: The same five-instruction shape as 0xAE2B, but the second operand is the 16-bit value at XDATA 0x0544/0x0545: 0x0436/0x0437 goes into R3:R4, 0x0544/0x0545 into R1:R2, then the compare helper at 0x8863 and ret. None of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: or_r6_into_0496_low5
comment: Three reads and one write: loads XDATA 0x0496, clears its low five bits with `anl A,#0xe0`, ORs in R6 and writes the byte back. R6 is not set here; the callers that tail-jump to this entry load it with 0, 1, 3, 7, 0x0F or 0x1F (0xAE16, 0xAE42, 0xAE78, 0xAEA2, 0xAEE2, 0xAEF3), but that is an inference from those listings, not from these bytes. 0x0496 is not documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: chain_probes_update_056a_1_3
comment: Loads R6 with 3 and tail-jumps to 0xAED9 if bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490 is set. Otherwise it calls 0xAE5F and, on carry clear, jumps to 0xAE24 which writes 1 to 0x056A; on carry set it calls 0xAE92 and, on carry clear, jumps to 0xAE6F, or writes 3 to 0x056A. The block at 0xAE24 is outside this listing, and 0xAE6F is a tail call, not a call. Neither 0x0490 nor 0x056A is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: cmp_0436_0437_against_040c_040d
comment: The same five-instruction shape as 0xAE2B, with the second operand at XDATA 0x040C/0x040D: 0x0436/0x0437 into R3:R4, 0x040C/0x040D into R1:R2, the compare helper at 0x8863, ret. None of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: chain_probes_update_056a_2_4
comment: Loads R6 with 7 and tail-jumps to 0xAED9 if bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490 is set. Otherwise it calls 0xAE92 and, on carry clear, jumps to 0xAE58 which writes 2 to 0x056A; on carry set it calls 0xAEBC and, on carry clear, jumps to 0xAEE0 (an sjmp to 0xAE6F), or writes 4 to 0x056A. The sjmp at 0xAEE0 closes this listing but is a separate three-byte entry, not part of this routine. Neither 0x0490 nor 0x056A is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: cmp_0436_0437_against_1_or_test_0514
comment: If bit 0 of XDATA 0x0497 is set, reads 0x0514, clears carry and subtracts 1, so the carry it returns is set exactly when 0x0514 is 0 and A is 0x0514-1. Otherwise it loads 0x0436/0x0437 into R3:R4, sets R2=0 and R1=1, and calls the compare helper at 0x8863, returning its A and carry. None of 0x0497, 0x0514 or 0x0436 is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: store_0_to_056a
comment: Three instructions: loads DPTR with 0x056A, writes 0 to it and returns. It is the shared tail target of the bit-0 test on XDATA 0x0490 in 0xAE16, 0xAE42, 0xAE78, 0xAEA2, 0xAEE2 and 0xAEF3, and 0x56A is also the byte 0xADFD indexes on, which is why it is called the state here; 0x056A is not documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_056a_3_or_0496_low5_0f
comment: Loads R6 with 0x0F and tail-jumps to 0xAED9 if bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490 is set. Otherwise it calls 0xAEBC and, on carry clear, jumps to 0xAE8B which writes 3 to 0x056A; on carry set it tail-jumps to 0xAE6F to OR 0x0F into the low five bits of 0x0496. The .c renders the R6 load as an argument to the call (`FUN_CODE_aebc(0xf)`); the instructions put 0x0F in R6 before the 0x0490 test, so that reading is wrong. Neither 0x0490 nor 0x056A is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_056a_3_or_0496_low5_1f
comment: Tail-jumps to 0xAED9 if bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490 is set. Otherwise it calls 0xAEBC and, on carry clear, jumps to 0xAE8B which writes 3 to 0x056A; on carry set it loads R6 with 0x1F and tail-jumps to 0xAE6F to OR it into the low five bits of 0x0496. Neither 0x0490 nor 0x056A is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: gate_0490_04ff_0505_then_call_b0d1
comment: Reaches 0xB0D1 by one of three routes. If bit 2 of XDATA 0x0490 is clear it calls 0xAF32 and tail-jumps to 0xB0D1 from 0xAF4E; if that bit is set and bit 3 of 0x04FF is set it tail-jumps to 0xB0D1 from 0xAF2E; and if both conditions hold with bit 3 of 0x04FF clear, it reads 0x0503 into R1, and a 0x0505 of 0 falls to the first route, a 0x0505 of 1 loads 0x0502/0x0503 into R1:R2 and stores them to 0x04A2/0x04A3 before the third route, and any other value returns at 0xAF31 without reaching 0xB0D1. The R1 load from 0x0503 is dead in this listing. None of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, and what 0xAF32 and 0xB0D1 do is not decoded here.

name: step_index_056b_update_0495_0493
comment: Uses the low nibble of XDATA 0x056B as a four-byte-per-entry index into one of four CODE tables at 0xAFF1, 0xAFB1, 0xB031 and 0xB071, chosen by bit 0 of 0x0497, by whether 0x0398 equals 0xA5, and by the byte at 0x030D (0x0F or 0x10 selects 0xAFF1, 0x11 selects 0xB031, anything else 0xAFB1). Entry bytes 3 and 2 are stored to 0x056E/0x056F and bytes 1 and 0 to 0x056C/0x056D through the store helpers at 0x889E and 0x888C, then 0x04A2/0x04A3 is loaded and compared against the entry's bytes 0 and 1 by the helper at 0x8863. Carry clear increments 0x056B and replaces it with 0x0F once bit 4 of the result is set; carry set re-loads 0x056E/0x056F and 0x04A2/0x04A3, compares again, and decrements 0x056B only if that second compare is also below and the byte is non-zero. Finally it ORs a byte indexed by the new low nibble from 0xAF91 or 0xB0B1 into 0x0495, keeping bits 0x43, and a byte from 0xAFA1 or 0xB0C1 into 0x0493, keeping bits 0x1F. None of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, and the table contents are not decoded here.

name: dispatch_0490_low3
comment: Masks XDATA 0x0490 with 7: 6 jumps to 0xB1F5, 7 jumps to 0xB224, and bit 1 set returns. Otherwise, if 0x043C is 1 it returns; if not, it stores 0xFFFF to 0x0436/0x0437, writes 1 to 0x043C and 0 to 0x0432, and stores 0x0000 to 0x0434/0x0435 and 0x0438/0x0439. The 0xB1F5 block loads 0x0436/0x0437 into R3:R4, sets R2:R1 to 0xFFFF and calls the compare helper at 0x8863 -- and the listing ends there, with no ret, so the write of 4 to 0x043C, the call to 0xB2A0 and the write of 1 to 0x0432 that the .c shows are not in this listing; those instructions are at 0xB202. None of the addresses here is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: carry_set_set_043c_4_call_b2a0
comment: Entry point that dispatches on the carry the caller left: carry clear jumps back to 0xB1D9, inside 0xB1B3, and carry set writes 4 to XDATA 0x043C, calls 0xB2A0 and writes 1 to 0x0432 before returning. The .c also shows the carry-clear arm writing 1 to 0x043C, 0 to 0x0432 and storing 0x0000 to 0x0434/0x0435 and 0x0438/0x0439; none of those instructions is in this listing, and they belong to 0xB1B3. None of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, and what 0xB2A0 does is not decoded here.

name: set_carry_if_0404_0405_is_0201
comment: Loads the 16-bit value at XDATA 0x0404/0x0405 into R3:R4 and the 16-bit value at 0x0436/0x0437 into R1:R2, then calls 0x887A, which sets carry exactly when R3 is 1 and R4 is 2 -- that is, when 0x0404 holds 0x01 and 0x0405 holds 0x02 -- and clears it otherwise. R1:R2 is loaded but not tested by these bytes; the four callers branch on the carry. None of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: cmp_0404_vs_0518_then_store_0436
comment: Calls 0xB214 and returns if that sets carry and bit 5 of XDATA 0x04A0 is clear. It then loads R1 from 0x0519 and returns unless 0x051B equals 1; otherwise it loads 0x0404/0x0405 into R3:R4 and 0x0518/0x0519 into R1:R2, compares them with the helper at 0x8863, and on carry clear sets R4=2 and R3=1. In every path it then stores R3:R4 to 0x0436/0x0437 and returns. None of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: copy_0514_0516_to_04ab_04ac_then_probe
comment: Copies XDATA 0x0514 to 0x04AB and 0x0516 to 0x04AC, calls 0xB6C9 with DPTR=0x0524, and if that leaves carry clear stores R1:R2 to 0x04A0/0x04A1. It then requires bit 0 and bit 2 of 0x0490 to be set and 0x04AB to be at least 2, calls 0xB6C9 with DPTR=0x051C and returns if that sets carry, otherwise loads 0x051C/0x051D into R1:R2 and 0x0404/0x0405 into R3:R4, compares them with the helper at 0x8863 and branches to 0xB321 if bit 0 of the helper's A is set. The 0xB321 block that the .c continues with (the 0x0497 and 0x0575 tests) is a separate entry and is not in this listing, and the .c's `FUN_CODE_b6c9(DAT_EXTMEM_04ab - 2,0x51c)` is a misreading: the instructions load DPTR with the constant 0x051C. None of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_0575_8_or_write_0404_and_call_88f0
comment: If bit 0 of XDATA 0x0497 is set it writes 8 to 0x0575 and returns. Otherwise it stores R1:R2 to 0x0404/0x0405, loads R5 with 6 and calls 0x88F0, whose body is not decoded here. R1:R2 is whatever the caller left; the .c's `FUN_CODE_888c(0x404)` with no operands reflects that. None of these addresses is documented in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: forwarder_to_b40e
comment: Two bytes: sjmp 0xB40E, with nothing executed here. B407.c is the decompiler following that jump, so the counter at 0x054D, the writes to 0x0495, 0x0514 and 0x0494 and the call to 0xCBF3 that it shows belong to 0xB40E and are reported from the .c, not decoded from these bytes.

name: set_dptr_1770_fallthru
comment: Loads DPTR with the 16-bit constant 0x1770 and then falls straight through into 0xB40E. The whole entry is two instructions (MOV DPTR,#0x1770 then SJMP 0xB40E); 0xB40E copies DPTR into R4:R3 and calls 0x8863, so this entry exists only to supply that constant.

name: cmp_dptr_to_r2r1
comment: Copies the caller's DPTR into R4:R3 and calls 0x8863, so the carry on return is the result of comparing that 16-bit address against the 16-bit value left in R2:R1. 0x8863 sets carry when (R4:R3) is less than (R2:R1) and returns A=0 instead of A=1 in the one case where (R4:R3) is exactly 0x0201. The listing is only these three instructions; the decompiled C for 0xB40E spans the whole block through 0xB4B6 and does not match this listing.

name: bump_counter_054d
comment: Branches on the carry from the caller: if it is set the code jumps to 0xB43B. Otherwise it reads the byte at XDATA 0x054D, increments it in A, and falls through into 0xB41C, which stores it. The listing stops after the INC A, so what 0xB41C does with the stored value is not shown here.

name: store_054d_set_bit_on_10
comment: Writes the incremented accumulator back to XDATA 0x054D (DPTR is still 0x054D from 0xB415) and compares it against 0x0A. If the value is 10 or more it sets bit 6 of XDATA 0x0495, and if bit 0 of XDATA 0x0497 is also set it clears XDATA 0x0514 and calls 0xCBF3. The listing ends at the SJMP to 0xB442, so the code there is not shown in this file.

name: derive_scaled_values_from_0404
comment: Takes the 16-bit little-endian value at XDATA 0x0404/0x0405 and stores value>>4 to 0x040A/0x040B and value>>5 to both 0x040C/0x040D and 0x040E/0x040F. It then stores (value>>5)+0x28 to 0x0544/0x0545, value-(value>>4) to 0x0546/0x0547 and value-(value>>5) to 0x0410/0x0411. The right shifts are 0x8844 (R7 counted down, R2:R1 rotated right through carry) and the two differences are 0x885B; the C reads the 0x8886 and 0x889E calls as writes, which they are not.

name: cmp_043a_0436_store_0548
comment: Loads the 16-bit little-endian value at 0x043A/0x043B and compares it against the one at 0x0548/0x0549 with 0x8863, returning immediately if the 0x043A half is exactly 0x0201 (the special case inside 0x8863). It then compares 0x043A against the 16-bit value at 0x0436/0x0437, with bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490 choosing which of the two is loaded into R4:R3 and therefore which operand the 0x0201 special case applies to. If the 0x043A value is not less than the 0x0436 value it is written back to 0x0548/0x0549; otherwise the function returns without writing.

name: dispatch_043c_04fc_bits
comment: If XDATA 0x05F6 is non-zero it is decremented and the function returns. Otherwise it reads XDATA 0x043C and XDATA 0x04FC, applies SWAP A to the 0x04FC byte, ORs the two together, and dispatches on bits 0, 2 and 6 of the result to 0xB666, 0xB679, 0xB68C, 0xB6A8 or 0xB652. The paths reaching 0xB637 call 0xB6A8, then 0x896A with R7=0xAB, then 0x88F0 with R5=7, then 0x159A, and pass R5=0x16 or 0x19 to 0x88F0 depending on whether 0x159A left R7 at zero. The listing ends at 0xB650 with an SJMP into the shared tail at 0xB65C, and the body of the 0xB65C tail is not in this file.

name: arm_05f6_with_88f0_06
comment: Calls 0xB6A8, then 0x896A with R7=0xAB, then 0x88F0 with R5=6, and finally writes 3 to XDATA 0x05F6. The disassembly in this listing starts at 0xB655: the first instruction of the entry, the LCALL 0xB6A8 at 0xB652, is in the C and in the firmware bytes at 0xB652 but is not in the .asm, so it is reported from those two sources rather than from the listing.

name: gate_0572_bit0_clear
comment: Tests bit 0 of XDATA 0x0572 and jumps to the arming path at 0xB637 if it is clear. If it is set it tests bit 2 of the same byte and, when that is set, bit 2 of XDATA 0x0574; a clear bit 2 in either goes to 0xB652 and both set goes to 0xB68C. This is one arm of the bit tree rooted at 0xB5AF; the code at those three targets is not in this listing.

name: gate_0572_bit0_set
comment: Same shape as the 0xB666 arm but with the sense of bit 0 of XDATA 0x0572 inverted: if that bit is set it jumps to 0xB637, otherwise bit 2 of 0x0572 and then bit 2 of XDATA 0x0574 are tested, a clear bit 2 going to 0xB652 and both set going to 0xB68C. The targets are outside this listing.

name: gate_0571_0573_eq_1
comment: Loads XDATA 0x0432 into R1 and requires XDATA 0x0571 to equal it; on a mismatch it jumps to 0xB652. If they match it reloads R1 with XDATA 0x04F2 and requires XDATA 0x0573 to equal that instead; both matches fall through to 0xB6A8 and a second mismatch jumps to 0xB652.

name: snapshot_0432_043c_04f2_04fc
comment: Four byte copies: XDATA 0x043C to 0x0572, 0x0432 to 0x0571, 0x04FC to 0x0574 and 0x04F2 to 0x0573. Each is a MOVX A,@DPTR into A followed by MOVX @DPTR,A into a freshly loaded DPTR. This is the routine the bit tree at 0xB5AF calls before it arms XDATA 0x05F6.

name: cmp32_hi16_lt_lo16_at_dptr
comment: Reads four bytes from the caller's DPTR upward into R3 (byte 0), R4 (byte 1), R1 (byte 2) and R2 (byte 3), so R4:R3 is the high half and R2:R1 the low half of a little-endian 32-bit value. It calls 0x8863 and returns with the carry set when the high half is less than the low half and clear otherwise, except that 0x8863 also treats a high half of exactly 0x0201 as not-less. No DPTR is loaded here; the caller sets it (0xB43B passes 0x050E).

name: clear_0610_bit5_and_dispatch
comment: Returns immediately unless bit 5 of XDATA 0x0610 is set, and when it is set that bit is cleared by writing the byte back. It then loads the 16-bit little-endian value at 0x060A/0x060B and compares it with the constant 0x03E8: if that value is 1001 or greater, or if it is 1000 or less but XDATA 0x0575 is non-zero, it calls 0xB841, then 0xB8E1, and clears bit 1 of XDATA 0x0480. Otherwise it calls 0xB784 then 0xB8E1 and leaves 0x0480 alone.

name: arm_05f5_countdown_0490_bit5
comment: Writes 3 to XDATA 0x05F5 and sets bit 1 of XDATA 0x0480, then returns if bit 5 of XDATA 0x0490 is already set. Otherwise it counts XDATA 0x05F4 down and, on reaching zero, sets bit 5 of 0x0490 while clearing bit 6 and writes 0 to XDATA 0x05E1 and 0x0A to 0x06DA. The listing contains no call instruction and touches no other address.

name: arm_05f2_countdown_0575_clears_0490
comment: Decrements XDATA 0x0575 if it is non-zero, then writes 3 to XDATA 0x05F2. If bit 1 of XDATA 0x0490 is clear it returns. Otherwise it counts XDATA 0x05F3 down and, when that reaches zero, clears bits 0, 1, 2 and 6 of 0x0490, calls 0xB88C and 0xB937, stores the 16-bit value 0x0000 to XDATA 0x04AE/0x04AF, calls 0xAF32, clears bits 0 and 1 of XDATA 0x0848 and jumps to 0xC751.

name: arm_05f4_countdown_0576_clears_0490
comment: Decrements XDATA 0x0576 if it is non-zero, then writes 3 to XDATA 0x05F4. If bit 5 of XDATA 0x0490 is clear it returns. Otherwise it counts XDATA 0x05F5 down and, when that reaches zero, clears bits 5 and 6 of 0x0490, calls 0xB91B and 0xB962, stores the 16-bit value 0x0000 to XDATA 0x04BE/0x04BF and calls 0xC613. The listing ends at 0xB91A.

name: zero_xdata_04b0_05ff_runs
comment: Three calls to 0x89F4, each zeroing a run that starts at the given address and wraps at 0xFFFF to end at low address 0x03: (R2,R1) = (0x05,0x80) covers 0x0580-0x05FF and then 0x0500-0x0503, (0x04,0xC0) covers 0x04C0-0x04FF and then 0x0400-0x0403, and (0x04,0xB0) covers 0x04B0-0x04FF and then 0x0400-0x0403. Nothing else is read or written, and R3 is not used by 0x89F4.

name: clear_0492_0496_0577_0578_0542
comment: Writes 0 to XDATA 0x0494, 0x0495, 0x0496, 0x0577, 0x0578 and 0x0492, masks XDATA 0x0491 with 0xC0 so that only bits 6 and 7 survive, and stores the 16-bit little-endian value 0x0000 to XDATA 0x0542/0x0543. The listing is a straight-line sequence of seven MOVX writes plus the 0x888C pair, with no branches and no calls.

name: clear_049a_049e_0579_057a_05c2
comment: Same shape as 0xB937 on the second flag group: writes 0 to XDATA 0x049C, 0x049D, 0x049E, 0x0579, 0x057A and 0x049A, masks XDATA 0x0499 with 0x80 so that only bit 7 survives, and stores the 16-bit little-endian value 0x0000 to XDATA 0x05C2/0x05C3. The listing is a straight-line sequence with no branches and no calls.

name: threshold_dispatch_0438_by_0491
comment: Returns immediately if bit 5 of XDATA 0x04FE is set, and calls 0xC59F before anything else. It continues only when XDATA 0x06C2 is 0, bit 0 of XDATA 0x0490 is set, and either bit 3 or bit 7 of 0x0490 is set; otherwise it masks XDATA 0x0499 with 0xC0 and jumps to 0xBD10, and on the continuing path it returns if bit 0 of XDATA 0x0497 is set while the low two bits of XDATA 0x0848 are not both 1. It then loads the 16-bit little-endian value at 0x0438/0x0439 and compares it with a constant picked by bits 6-7 of XDATA 0x0491 (0x1C20 for mask 0x80, 0x12C0 for 0x40, 0x2580 otherwise), branching to 0xBABF on a borrow; if it is not less and bit 2 of 0x0490 is set it makes a second comparison against 0x2EE0 for mask 0xC0, 0x1770 for 0x40 or 0x2328 otherwise, branching to 0xBA43 on a borrow and to 0xBBA4 otherwise. The listing stops at 0xBA40, so the 0xBA43-0xBAB1 block the C shows as a continuation is not in this file.

name: gate_chain_to_0491_bit0

comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x367 into A and then discards it: the next instruction, jnb 0xE2, tests bit 2 of the bit-addressable byte at 0xE0, not the value just read. With that bit clear it ljmps to 0xCBAB; with it set it calls 0xD22E, then 0xD235, then 0xCD80, and ljmps to 0xD23F. name: dispatch_03a3_low3
comment: Takes the low three bits of the byte at XDATA 0x3A3, multiplies them by three and jumps through the eight-entry ljmp table at 0xC90C. Cases 0-6 land on 0xC931, 0xC979, 0xC9BE, 0xCA1D, 0xCA3E, 0xCAB8 and 0xCB08, case 7 on 0xCB1E, which is a bare ret. Nothing is written to XDATA in this listing.

name: mul_0342_0514_into_0388_when_03d0_lt_0384

Otherwise it multiplies the byte at XDATA 0x342 by the byte at 0x514 and stores the 16-bit little-endian product at 0x388. Both paths then write 2 to XDATA 0x3A3.

name: count_0361_then_0362_toward_03a3
comment: With bit 2 of the bit-addressable byte at 0xE0 set it jumps to 0xCA16, which writes 7 to XDATA 0x3A3; the byte read from XDATA 0x367 immediately before that test is discarded. When the 16-bit pair at XDATA 0x834 is zero it increments XDATA 0x361 and jumps to 0xCA16 if the incremented value exceeds 0x7F. Otherwise it clears XDATA 0x361, compares the 16-bit value at 0x382 against XDATA 0x39A multiplied by ten, and on not-less falls through into 0xCA02 at XDATA 0xC9FF.

name: store_a_then_03a3_3_over_1f
comment: Stores A through @DPTR, which on the 0xC9BE path is XDATA 0x362 already holding that byte incremented, then adds 0xE0 to A. If the addition carries, that is A above 0x1F, it writes 3 to XDATA 0x3A3 and clears XDATA 0x362; otherwise it returns with the stored value left in place. 0xC9BE falls into this address and ec/annotations/bank-call-targets.csv also records an ljmp to it from 0xE7BB and an lcall to it from 0x039C, so A and DPTR on those entries are whatever the caller left.

name: add_03a6_plus_0388_into_039e
comment: Loads the 16-bit little-endian value at XDATA 0x3A6 into R3:R4, adds the 16-bit little-endian value at 0x388 with the helper at 0x8854, a 16-bit add that carries into the high byte, and stores the sum little-endian at XDATA 0x39E. It then clears XDATA 0x361 and writes 4 to XDATA 0x3A3.

name: count_0361_to_40_then_branch_on_0347

When the 16-bit pair at XDATA 0x834 is zero it increments XDATA 0x361 without storing on overflow, and at 0x40 or more it tests XDATA 0x347: equal to 0x64 it compares the 16-bit values at 0x4AE and 0x168 and writes 5 or 7 to 0x3A3 by that borrow, otherwise it returns if bit 5 of the byte at 0xE0 is set and writes 7 to 0x3A3 if it is clear. When the 0x834 pair is non-zero it clears XDATA 0x361 and returns.

name: set_0575_08_when_03a1_low2_clear
comment: Tests bits 1-0 of XDATA 0x3A1 and returns without writing if either is set. With both clear it writes 0x08 to XDATA 0x575 and 7 to XDATA 0x3A3.

name: ret_only_cb1e
comment: A single ret and nothing else in the listing. The bank-call census records exactly one reference, the ljmp at 0xC921 that is case 7 of the jump table at 0xC90C used by 0xC924, so it is entered when the low three bits of XDATA 0x3A3 are 7. What that case was meant to do is not decoded here.

name: set_039b_039c_from_0404_div_100
comment: Divides the 16-bit little-endian value at XDATA 0x404 by 100 and, from the low byte q of the quotient, writes (q>>2)&0x3F to XDATA 0x39D, q+3 to XDATA 0x39B and, when q+3 is at least 6, q-3 to XDATA 0x39C, otherwise zero. If the call to 0xCB80 returns non-zero it recomputes XDATA 0x39B and 0x39C the same way from XDATA 0x39D instead, so the pair becomes 0x39D+3 and 0x39D-3 clamped at zero.

name: div_0343_by_31e_shifted_into_03a9
comment: Loads XDATA 0x31E into R3 and the 16-bit little-endian value at XDATA 0x343 into R1:R2; when the high byte at 0x344 is zero and neither 0x343 nor 0x31E has any of bits 7-5 set, it writes 0 to XDATA 0x3A9 and returns 0 in A. Otherwise it divides R1:R2 by R3:R4, that is by 0x31E shifted left eight bits, with the helper at 0xA5E6, and stores the low byte of the quotient in XDATA 0x3A9 and in A.

name: increment_0349_saturating
comment: Adds one to the byte at XDATA 0x349 and stores the result, but skips the store when the addition carries, so the byte saturates at 0xFF.

name: publish_0514_and_0342_product
comment: Copies XDATA 0x514 to 0x516, 0x4AB and 0x347, then multiplies it by the byte at XDATA 0x342 and stores the 16-bit little-endian product at each of 0x518, 0x51A and 0x345 in turn. If 0x514 is not 0x64 it also clears XDATA 0x524.

name: set_0397_from_0342_by_0514_band

Below 0x5F it compares 0x3D0 against 0x380 and on not-less clears XDATA 0x3B6, writes 0xFA to 0x397, writes 0 to 0x514 and calls 0xCBF3, while every other path writes 0x342 to 0x397 except the value-2-and-above path that, when bits 7-6 of XDATA 0x3BB are set, compares 0x382 against XDATA 0x39A times ten and then sets bits of the byte at 0xE0 with setb before storing XDATA 0x3A4 back. The read of XDATA 0x367 at 0xCCA0 is discarded because the test at 0xCCA4 addresses bit 0 of the byte at 0xE0, and the second jc at 0xCCCD re-tests the carry the first one at 0xCCCB already consumed.

name: dispatch_03f1_low3
comment: Increments XDATA 0x3F1, masks the result to three bits and jumps through the eight-entry ljmp table at 0xCDB3, whose entries in order are 0xCE2D, 0xCE78, 0xCEA9, 0xCEDA, 0xCF0B, 0xCF3C, 0xCF6D and 0xCFB1. The listing starts with that table at 0xCDB3-0xCDCA and the dispatch code follows at 0xCDCB, so the table is included in this item.

name: clamp_r1r2_against_const_from_0491
comment: Copies the caller's R3:R4 into R1:R2, then picks a 16-bit constant from bits 7-6 of XDATA 0x491: 0x8C23 when they are 0x80, 0xD417 when 0x40, 0x442F otherwise. It subtracts R1:R2 from that constant with the helper at 0x885B; on a borrow it puts the difference in both R1:R2 and R3:R4 and returns, and on no borrow it recomputes the same constant, re-reading 0x491, and returns with R3:R4 holding the constant and R1:R2 the caller's original value.

name: store_slot_for_index_0_and_7

If XDATA 0x3C3 is 7 it clears XDATA 0x3F6 and 0x3F7 and copies the word at 0x3E0 to 0x3F8, so the previous index, 7, publishes zero rather than its stored word at 0x3EE.

name: store_slot_for_index_1

If XDATA 0x3C3 is 6 it also stores R3:R4 at XDATA 0x3F8 and copies the word at 0x3E0 to XDATA 0x3F6, the previous index's slot.

name: store_slot_for_index_2

If XDATA 0x3C3 is 5 it also stores R3:R4 at XDATA 0x3F8 and copies the word at 0x3E2 to XDATA 0x3F6, the previous index's slot.

name: store_slot_for_index_3

If XDATA 0x3C3 is 4 it also stores R3:R4 at XDATA 0x3F8 and copies the word at 0x3E4 to XDATA 0x3F6, the previous index's slot.

name: store_slot_for_index_4

If XDATA 0x3C3 is 3 it also stores R3:R4 at XDATA 0x3F8 and copies the word at 0x3E6 to XDATA 0x3F6, the previous index's slot.

name: store_slot_for_index_5

If XDATA 0x3C3 is 2 it also stores R3:R4 at XDATA 0x3F8 and copies the word at 0x3E8 to XDATA 0x3F6, the previous index's slot.

name: store_slot_for_index_6

If XDATA 0x3C3 is 0 it stores R3:R4 at XDATA 0x3F6 and then writes 0xFF to both 0x3F8 and 0x3F9, and if 0x3C3 is 1 it stores R3:R4 at 0x3F8 and copies the word at 0x3EA to 0x3F6; any other value of 0x3C3 leaves only the 0x3EC store done.

name: step_03c3_and_reload_03bf

If 0x3F8 is less it decrements XDATA 0x3C3, and only if that is not already zero, masking to three bits; if instead 0x3F6 is less it does not touch 0x3C3. Either way it then reloads XDATA 0x3BF to 4, while when neither is less it counts 0x3BF down and, at zero, advances 0x3C3 by one from its low three bits, storing unless bit 3 of the bit-addressable byte at 0xE0 is set.

name: dispatch_on_03c3_low3

When that field is 3 or more it computes A = 3*field and jumps to 0xD000 + A, i.e. into a table with a 3-byte stride starting at 0xD000 (the five reachable addresses are 0xD009, 0xD00C, 0xD00F, 0xD012 and 0xD015). When the field is 0 to 2 it falls through to code past 0xD036 that is not part of this listing, so that path is not decoded here.

name: set_r1_0e_jump_d068

name: set_r1_0c_jump_d068

name: set_r1_08_jump_d068

name: set_r1_06_jump_d068

name: set_r1_04_jump_d068

name: set_r1_02_jump_d068

name: set_r1_00_jump_d068

name: scale_store_to_0397
comment: Takes bytes in R1, R5 and B and writes one byte to XDATA 0x0397. If R1 equals R5 it stores B; if R1 is greater it multiplies B by (R1 - R5), stores the low product byte, and stores 0xFF instead when the 16-bit product has a nonzero high byte (that store is the code at 0xD09F). If R1 is smaller it right-shifts B logically by (R5 - R1) positions and stores that, except that a shift of more than 3 positions is clamped to B >> 3.

name: store_ff_to_0397
comment: Writes 0xFF to XDATA 0x0397 and returns. It is the branch target reached from 0xD068 at 0xD090 when the 16-bit product of the multiply has a nonzero high byte.

name: store_03c3_to_0360_when_ge_3
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0360 into R0, which is then unused, and XDATA 0x03C3 into R1. If 0x03C3 is at least 3 the CJNE against 0 at 0xD0B6 is always taken and the function writes 0x03C3 into 0x0360 and writes 0 into 0x03B5 before returning. If 0x03C3 is below 3 it returns without writing anything.

name: update_0524_0526_4a0_and_0497_flags

The remaining path runs a chain of guards (0x8898 on 0x0834, 0xD1BC, bit 2 of 0x0367, 0x8886 on 0x0382 followed by 0x885B, and a second 0x885B on 0x0190 reached only when bit 0 of 0x0497 is set with 0x0539 == 1, or bit 0 clear with 0x0403 below 0x14), and every failure branch reaches 0xD16F, which writes 0x0A to 0x0648. On success it returns without writing if 0x0648 is already nonzero, otherwise it sets bit 5 of 0x0497; if 0x0514 then equals 0x64 it calls 0xCBF3 and, unless bit 5 of 0x0524 is set, writes 0x63 to 0x03C1 and 0x20 to 0x0524, 0x0526, 0x04A0 and 0x0492. When 0x0514 is not 0x64 it only sets bit 7 of 0x0497.

name: increment_0514_toward_0x64

Otherwise it compares XDATA 0x0514 with 0x64: on reaching exactly 0x64 it clears bit 5 of 0x0497 and jumps to 0xD14C, inside 0xD0C4, while 0x0514 is below 0x64 and XDATA 0x0368 is zero it increments 0x0514, calls 0xCBF3 and sets 0x0368 to 0x96. Every other combination ends at 0xD16F.

name: trampoline_to_d16f
comment: Calls 0xD16F and returns, doing nothing else. It is the target of the ljmp at 0xD0E3, taken when 0x198A returns zero in R7.

name: select_ptr_0491_c080_then_0506
comment: Masks XDATA 0x0491 with 0xC0 and selects a code pointer from it: 0x3F48 when the masked value is 0xC0, 0x2FA8 when it is 0x80, otherwise 0x1FA4. The selected pointer is moved into R2:R1 with DPTR addressing it, then 0x8892 is called with DPTR = 0x0506 followed by a call to 0x8863. What the two helpers do with these arguments is not decoded here.

name: set_0497_bit6_and_0394_to_5
comment: If bit 0 of XDATA 0x0497 is clear it returns immediately. Otherwise, when bit 6 is not already set, it calls 0xD37F and abandons the update if that returns with carry set; it then clears bit 7 and sets bit 6 of 0x0497, calls 0xE5A7 and writes 0x05 to XDATA 0x0394.

name: step_03c2_and_dispatch_four_ways

The decompiler's C labels those four cases 0xD22E, 0xD235, 0xD246 and 0xD23F, and its case-1 target 0xD235 is one byte before the 0xD236 listing in this shard.

name: call_cdcb_then_d0a6
comment: Calls 0xCDCB, then 0xD0A6, then returns. It performs no register or memory work of its own and passes nothing to either call.

name: call_d2a3_then_d274
comment: Decodes as `pop 0x18` writing the popped byte to internal RAM 0x18, then a call to 0xD2A3, a call to 0xD274 and a return; the decompiler's C reads the pop as a return-address byte stored into R0, which is what a mid-instruction entry would produce. The committed firmware image has 0x12 at 0xD235, so the real stream there is lcall 0xD018, lcall 0xD2A3, lcall 0xD274, ret, and the jump-table entry 1 reached from 0xD219 targets 0xD235 rather than 0xD236. The two calls to 0xD2A3 and 0xD274 are certain either way; the leading lcall to 0xD018 is the one reading not confirmed from this listing alone.

name: call_d34b_then_d32c
comment: Calls 0xD34B, then 0xD32C, then returns. It performs no register or memory work of its own and passes nothing to either call.

name: clear_0394_or_call_cd80
comment: Calls 0xC924 and then 0x198A. If 0x198A returns nonzero in R7, or bit 0 of XDATA 0x0497 is clear, it writes 0 to XDATA 0x0394 and returns. Otherwise it calls 0x1984 and returns if R7 is zero, else calls 0x19A8; both the zero and nonzero outcomes of 0x19A8 then call 0xCD80 and return, so within this listing the result of 0x19A8 does not change what happens.

name: div_23_minus_0386_by_034d_capped_15
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0386 into R1 and computes 0x23 minus it. If 0x0386 is above 0x23, equal to 0x23, or the byte at XDATA 0x034D masked with 0xFC is zero, it writes 0 to XDATA 0x03BA and returns. Otherwise it repeatedly subtracts the byte at 0x034D from that difference, counting the iterations in R7, and stops the loop once R7 reaches 0x0F; the count is written to 0x03BA.

name: derive_scale_from_034e_and_compute_from_044c

If bit 2 of XDATA 0x0367 is set it reads 0x0438 and then 0x0434 through 0x8886, combines them through helper 0xA5E6 (always called with a 0x0064 divisor) including a MUL of two intermediate bytes, and restores the pushed R3:R2 pair afterwards; if the bit is clear, A comes straight from XDATA 0x044C. The result minus 5, floored at 0, is passed to helper 0xA5A7 and the pair that returns is moved into R1:R2. The listing ends at 0xD320 setting R4 = 0 and R3 = 0x0A; the decompiler's C shows a following call to 0xA5E6 and then 0x888C with DPTR 0x03B8, but those instructions are not in this listing.

name: call_a5e6_then_888c_on_03b8
comment: Calls helper 0xA5E6 with whatever register values it was entered with, then sets DPTR to 0x03B8, calls helper 0x888C and returns. In this bank 0x888C is only ever called immediately after a computed 16-bit register pair, which is consistent with a 16-bit XDATA store, but its argument convention is not decoded here and is not asserted.

name: copy_0514_to_03c1_and_set_03a1_bit0
comment: Copies XDATA 0x0514 into R1 and reads XDATA 0x03C1; if 0x03C1 equals 0x01 it returns without writing. Otherwise it stores the copy of 0x0514 into 0x03C1 and, when bit 0 of XDATA 0x03A1 is clear, sets that bit and writes 0 to XDATA 0x03C4. If bit 0 was already set it stops after the 0x03C1 write.

name: bump_counter_mirror_to_04a6_04a7
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0349 and returns immediately unless that byte has reached 0xC8 or more. When it has, it clears 0x0349, increments the 16-bit big-endian counter at 0x0343 (high byte) and 0x0344 (low byte) using the carry out of the high byte into the low, and writes those two result bytes to 0x0528/0x0529 and to 0x04A6/0x04A7. registers.yaml documents 0x04A6/0x04A7 as BAT_CYCLE_COUNT, so this is where that pair is stepped.

name: scan_table_03de_down_stride2
comment: If bit 7 of XDATA 0x03A2 is clear it returns immediately with carry set. Otherwise it reads XDATA 0x0363 through 0x8892 and returns with carry clear when the resulting register pair is zero, then walks a table with R5 starting at 0xDE: each pass re-reads 0x03AC through 0x8892, reads the 16-bit value at code address 0x0300 + R5 (0x03DE descending) through 0x8886 and tests it with 0x885B, and on a failed test subtracts 0x0C from R7 and 2 from R5 and repeats while (R5 & 0x0F) is not 0x0E. On a passed test it stores R7 to XDATA 0x03AB, goes through 0x03FC and 0x03DE, picks one of three constant pairs from bits 0xC0 of XDATA 0x0491 (0xD8/0x40, 0xA2/0x30 or 0x6C/0x20) and tests it with 0x885B, scales through 0xA5E6 with 0x10 and adds the result to 0x03AB, while the not-first-iteration path uses 0x0C and masks its term with 0x0F. Both finished paths branch to 0xD473, the body of 0xD472, with the computed byte in A, and the exhausted-table path jumps to 0xD472 with A = 0.

name: store_r1_to_0514_03ab_if_gap_ok
comment: Entered at 0xD472 it forces A = 0; entered at 0xD473, as 0xD37F does, it takes the caller's byte in R1. It writes R1 into XDATA 0x03AB and 0x0514, calls 0xCBF3 and sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x03A1, but only when the guards allow: the write happens if 0x0514 is at least 0x1E and 0x0514 - 0x1E is at least R1, or if 0x0514 is below R1 and R1 exceeds 0x0514 + 0x1E (compared as 0x64 if that sum carries). A second guard requires XDATA 0x0308 to differ from 0x036D or XDATA 0x03FB to be zero, and otherwise the function returns with carry clear. The decompiler's C marks 0xD48B-0xD49A unreachable, but the JNC at 0xD489 falls through into it whenever the borrow is set, so that block is live.

name: counter_tick_03ae_0560
comment: Increments XDATA 0x03AE and, unless that wraps from 0xFF, stores it back, setting bit 0x02 of 0x0367 when bit address 0xE2 is set and bit 0x10 of 0x0494 when bit address 0xE4 is set. It then adds 2 to 0x0560: without a carry it calls 0xE2C3 and tail-jumps to 0xE27D, and with a carry it goes to 0xE1FB where 0x0367 is tested against 0x30 - when those two bits are not both set it adds 0x10 to 0x0367, calls 0x1ABC, and clears 0x0560, 0x03AE and bit 0x10 of 0x0494 before calling 0xE2C3 anyway. None of 0x03AE, 0x0367, 0x0494 or 0x0560 has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so the two counters and two flag bytes are named here only by address.

name: gate_1c00_init_defaults
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x1C00: zero and it writes 0x48, 0x01 and 0x9B to 0x1C01, 0x1C02 and 0x1C03 and returns; non-zero and it tests bit address 0xE1 and the mask 0x7C, falling through to 0xE1D7 when either test fails. When both pass it clears 0x0560, loads 0x1C04 into R1, and unless bit address 0xE3 is set it loads R2 from 0x0391 and R3:R4 from DPTR (so 0x91 and 0x03), calls 0x9EA1 with DPTR 0x03C7, and stores the returned byte to 0x0387. The decompiled C continues past 0xE27C with writes to 0x0680, 0x0681, 0x0683, 0x03A0 and 0x1C05 that this listing does not contain.

name: reset_1c00_group_and_toggle_03a0
comment: Writes 10 to XDATA 0x0683, 0 to 0x1C04, 0 to 0x1C05 and 0xFF to 0x1C00, then 4 to 0x0680, and finally exclusive-ORs 0x03A0 with 0x01 and stores it back. It reads nothing, so every value except the 0x03A0 byte is a constant. 0xE1D7 tail-jumps here.

name: setup_0975_0976_0978_0979_call_c54c
comment: Writes 0x9A to XDATA 0x0975, 0x09 to 0x0976 and 0x80 to both 0x0978 and 0x0979 - 0x0977 is left untouched - then calls 0xC54C. On a carry-clear return from that call it sets bit 0x02 of 0x0497; on carry it returns without touching 0x0497. The decompiled C renders the same branch as a test on PSW, which is the same thing read the other way. None of 0x0975, 0x0976, 0x0978, 0x0979 or 0x0497 has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: set_1c00_ff_clear_1c04_1c05
comment: Writes 0xFF to XDATA 0x1C00 and 0 to 0x1C04 and 0x1C05, then returns. All three values are constants and nothing is read, so this resets that three-byte group unconditionally; it is called from 0xE1D7, 0xE501 and 0xE54F in this shard.

name: set_036c_to_4_jump_e490
comment: Three instructions: writes 4 to XDATA 0x036C, loads DPTR with the code address 0xE454, and tail-jumps to 0xE490. Nothing is read and no register other than DPTR is touched. That 0xE490 uses DPTR as a code-table pointer indexed by 0x03C4 is established by 0xE490's own listing, not by this one.

name: copy_03cd_03ce_03cf_to_1c02_1c04_1c05
comment: Requires XDATA 0x045F to hold 0xDB and 0x1C00 to be zero; otherwise it falls through to 0xE409. On that path it copies 0x03CD to 0x1C02 and clears 0x03CD, then branches on bit 7 of 0x03A1: clear writes 0 to 0x1C04 and 0x1C05 and 0xA1 to 0x1C03, set copies 0x03CE to 0x1C04 and 0x03CF to 0x1C05 and writes 0xA0 to 0x1C03, and both write 0x48 to 0x1C01 and return. At 0xE409 it accepts the transfer only when bit address 0xE1 is set and bits 0x7C of 0x1C00 are clear, copying 0x1C04 to 0x03CE and 0x1C05 to 0x03CF and jumping to 0xE501; on the reject path it calls 0xE4E9 and then jumps to 0xE501.

name: stage_1c00_block_from_code_table_indexed_03c4
comment: Takes a CODE pointer in DPTR from the caller and uses XDATA 0x03C4 as an index into a three-byte record at that pointer: bytes 0 and 1 are assembled big-endian into a 16-bit XDATA address whose byte is copied to both 0x1C04 and 0x1C05, and byte 2 goes to 0x1C02 - a zero byte 2 jumps to 0xE501 instead. It then writes 0xA0 to 0x1C03 and 0x48 to 0x1C01, calls 0x8886 with DPTR 0x036E and 0x8854 with R3=1 and R4=0, and advances 0x03C4 by 3, wrapping it to 0 when the result would be 0x78. When XDATA 0x1C00 is non-zero on entry the listing branches to 0xE4E9 instead; the 0x03AF counter, the 0x03A1 bit clearing and the 0x0680 and 0x0681 writes that the decompiled C shows for that case are code this listing does not contain.

name: gate_1c00_bit1_then_1c00_ff
comment: Reads XDATA 0x1C00 and jumps to 0xE54F unless bit address 0xE1 is set and bits 0x7C of the byte are clear. On the accept path it loads 0xFF into A and sets DPTR to 0x1C00, and the listing here stops at that MOV DPTR - the store of the 0xFF and the following write of 4 to 0x0680 are the two instructions listed at 0xE4F9, not part of this file. The decompiled C attaches the rest of this routine to it (0x03C4 and 0x03AF resets, the call to 0xE2C3, and the 0x0680 and 0x0681 writes), but none of that is in the .asm for this address.

name: store_a_to_dptr_then_set_0680_4
comment: Two stores and a return: the byte in A goes to whatever XDATA address DPTR holds, then 4 is written to 0x0680. On the fall-through path from 0xE4E9 that means 0xFF to 0x1C00 followed by 4 to 0x0680, which is the accept branch of that routine's test - but ec/annotations/bank-call-targets.csv also records a jump to 0xE4F9 from 0xA944, so this address is not only the tail of 0xE4E9 and the value of the first store is the caller's there. The decompiled C reads it as *param_2 = param_1, which has the direction of that move backwards.

name: reset_03c4_03af_and_clear_03a1_bit
comment: Clears XDATA 0x03C4 and 0x03AF, then reads the low three bits of 0x036C and clears one bit of 0x03A1 selected by them: 1 clears bit 0, 2 clears bit 1, 3 clears bit 2 and 4 clears bit 3, using CLR on the bit addresses 0xE0 to 0xE3. It writes 0 to 0x036C, calls 0xE2C3 (which sets 0x1C00 to 0xFF and clears 0x1C04 and 0x1C05), and writes 4 to 0x0680.

name: increment_03af_clear_03a1_on_wrap
comment: Adds 1 to XDATA 0x03AF: on a carry out of 0xFF it clears 0x03A1 instead of storing the increment, and otherwise stores the incremented byte. It then calls 0xE2C3, writes 4 to 0x0680 and 1 to 0x0681. Nothing else is read, so the wrap-clears-mask behaviour is the only conditional in it.

name: push_r7_call_e5d6_pop_r7
comment: The listing for this address is a single instruction, PUSH direct 0x07, which saves bank-0 R7. The next two bytes are in no listing, but ec/annotations/bank-call-targets.csv records an lcall to 0xE5D6 at 0xE580, the decompiled C calls 0xE5D6 between the save and the restore, and the matching POP direct 0x07 sits at 0xE583 in the 0xE582 listing - read that way this is a register-preserving call to 0xE5D6. The byte at 0xE582 is both the target byte of that lcall and a decodable XCHD A,@R0, so 0xE582 cannot be an instruction boundary at the same time; the census also records an ljmp to 0xE582 from 0x9F03, so one of those two census entries is a false positive. Which entry the routine is actually reached through is not settled by this file pair.

name: read_code_pair_by_r7_index_then_call_889e
comment: The listing starts at 0xE582 with XCHD A,@R0, but that byte is also the third byte of the lcall 0xE5D6 that ec/annotations/bank-call-targets.csv places at 0xE580, so this first instruction is contested rather than established. From 0xE583 the decode is coherent: it restores bank-0 R7, forms an index of ((R7 XOR 7) AND 7) times 16, reads two CODE bytes through the caller's DPTR into R4 and R3, rotates R7 left and masks it to 0x0E, and calls 0x889E with DPTR set to 0x03E0 plus that masked value. R3 and R4 are not used again in this listing, so whether they are an argument to 0x889E or dead is not shown here. The decompiled C models this as a function returning a single byte, which the instruction stream does not do.

name: decrement_0365_and_0368_if_nonzero
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0365 and 0x0368 in turn and decrements each by 1, storing the result back only when the byte read was non-zero, so both behave as saturating down-counters that stop at zero. Nothing else is read or written and no register is passed on. Neither address has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, so what the two counters count is not established by this listing.

name: write_r1_to_tmod_and_jump_8801
comment: Two instructions: opcode A7 is MOV direct,@R1, so the byte pointed at by R1 is written to direct address 0x89 - TMOD in the 8051 SFR map, though this repository does not document it - and execution then tail-jumps to 0x8801. The decompiled C has the direction of that move reversed, reading 0x89 and storing it through a pointer. What 0x8801 does is not in this listing.

name: ret_no_op
comment: A single RET. It is a call target in ec/annotations/bank-call-targets.csv, so something reaches it, but the one instruction at this address has no side effects and returns immediately with whatever the caller left in the registers. What the caller expected from it is not shown in this file pair.

name: clamp_r2r1_to_0420_above_3c0b
comment: Compares the 16-bit pair R2:R1, R2 high and R1 low, against 0x3C0B in two steps: R2 not zero and R2 at least 0x0B, or R2 zero and R1 at least 0x3C. When the value is at or above that limit it overwrites the pair with 0x0420 through DPTR and returns; otherwise it returns leaving R1 and R2 as they were. The decompiled C drops the store-back entirely and returns a char that the listing never produces.

name: countdown_03a8_gated_by_0490_bit1
comment: Returns immediately if XDATA 0x03A8 is zero. Otherwise it reads 0x0490: with bit address 0xE1 set it clears 0x03A8 and returns, and with that bit clear it decrements 0x03A8, stores the result back, and on the transition to zero it copies XDATA 0x03FE into 0x036D. The copy happens exactly once, on the pass that takes the counter to 0x00, and the counter is left at 0x00 on every path out of the decrement branch. None of 0x03A8, 0x0490, 0x03FE or 0x036D has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: compute_097e_times_10_write_0386_0387
comment: The listing begins at 0xE89B, before this address: that block writes 0x1E to XDATA 0x097E and tail-jumps to 0xE931, and it is the target of the jnb at 0xE8A8. This address tests bit 0 of 0x0497 and takes that path when the bit is clear; otherwise it loads 0x097E into R5, substituting 1 for 0, and loops calling 0x8892 with DPTR 0x060A, 0xE924 with DPTR 0xE7B1 and 0x8863, decrementing R5 on a carry-clear result and running one extra incrementing pass on carry. It then stores R5 back to 0x097E, forms the 16-bit product R5 times 10 in R3:R4, calls 0x8854 with R1=0x46 and R2=0x0A, 0x889E with DPTR 0x0502 and again with 0x0504, and 0x885B with DPTR 0x0AAA. On carry from 0x885B it writes 0x00 to both 0x0386 and 0x0387; otherwise it loads the product into the bank-0 direct bytes 0x01 and 0x02, sets R3=0x0A and R4=0, calls 0xA5E6, and writes the returned R1 to both 0x0386 and 0x0387 before jumping to 0xE931, and no XDATA address in this listing has an entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: read_code_pair_at_r5_index
comment: Forms an index of (R5 AND 0x7F) shifted left one, reads CODE[DPTR + index] into R2 and CODE[DPTR + index + 1] into R1 through the movc at A+DPTR, using the DPTR the caller left. The listing has no RET: it ends at 0xE930 and falls through into 0xE931, which is a bare ret, so the pair R2:R1 is what this leaves behind. The decompiled C models it as a function returning a single byte, which the instruction stream does not do.

name: shared_return_point
comment: A single RET with no side effects. Three paths in this shard reach it: the ljmp at 0xE8A1 and the sjmp at 0xE922, both in 0xE8A4's listing, and the fall-through from the end of 0xE924. It therefore doubles as a shared return stub for those paths, and the register state it hands back is whatever each caller set up.

name: unresolved_byte_stream_e954
comment: The bytes decode to a register-only arithmetic stream - interleaved DEC R1/R2/R3, ADD, XRL and SUBB against the same few registers, writes to direct addresses 0x19 and 0x1A, and a final AJMP 0xEA19 that lands inside the 0xE9CE listing - with no branch target resolving back into this range and no coherent entry sequence at 0xE954. 0xE954 is a call target in ec/annotations/bank-call-targets.csv, so something reaches it, but these bytes do not decode as a routine that could be entered there. The decompiled C's pointer arithmetic over BANK3 registers is a reading of this stream, not behaviour the instructions support. Not decoded further.

name: unresolved_byte_stream_eac3
comment: The first instruction is a plausible lcall to 0x2A70 in the common area, after which the linear decode degenerates into the same register-only pattern as 0xE9CE, with JMP at A+DPTR at 0xEB11 and 0xEBE5 and the decompiler reporting an instruction at 0xEAFE overlapping the one at 0xEAFD. Three RETI instructions sit at 0xEB84, 0xEBAC and 0xEBAE, which is more characteristic of table bytes than of a routine, but this listing on its own does not establish that everything after the lcall is data rather than a mis-decoded entry point. 0xEAC3 is a call target in ec/annotations/bank-call-targets.csv. Nothing beyond that lcall is decoded.

name: data_run_1a_1e
comment: Not a function: the bytes here are part of an ascending run of small data values (0x1A-0x1E interleaved with what would be opcode bytes) that a linear sweep decodes as instructions, including a self-referencing cjne R3,#0x1e,0xED0F at 0xED0F. The single census hit for 0xED02, a reported ljmp 0xED02 at 0xE7B5, sits inside a descending 2-byte table (F9, ED, E2, D6, CA ...) in the firmware bytes, so it is a byte-pattern match rather than a branch. What the table holds is not decoded.

name: data_run_2e_3e
comment: Not a function: the bytes here continue the same ascending data run (0x2E-0x3E) that 0xED02 sits in, and decode as add A,Rn / dec Rn sequences over register numbers that increase with the byte values. The decompiler additionally reports overlapping instructions at 0xEE57/0xEE58, so its 345-line body is not a reading of code. No call in bank1 targets 0xED3A in the census; what the table holds is not decoded.

name: data_run_33_34
comment: Not a function: the bytes at 0xEF26-0xEF31 (33 C2 33 F4 34 26 34 58 34 8A 34 BC) are the tail of the same ascending data run that 0xED02 and 0xED3A sit in, and the real code starts at 0xEF32. The .c here is a verbatim copy of the 0xEF32 body, i.e. Ghidra attached that function to the earlier address, and no call in bank1 targets 0xEF26 in the census. What the table holds is not decoded.

name: xdata_request_dispatch_048c
comment: Reads the request byte at XDATA 0x048C and branches on three of its bits. Bit 0 copies two bytes out of the address formed by XDATA 0x048B:0x048A into XDATA 0x048D/0x048E (the first byte to 0x048D); bit 1 writes the single byte 0x048D back to that address; bit 3 stores the high nibble of XDATA 0x048D into direct byte 0x00 and dispatches through the three-byte ljmp table at 0xEFE8. When 0x048B is 0x30 the two byte accesses use mov A,@R1 / mov @R0,A, which touch internal RAM, not the XDATA the .c assumes. With all three bits clear the function jumps to the RET at 0xEFBC; otherwise it clears bits 0, 1 and 3 of 0x048C and sets bit 7.

name: ret_stub_no_request_bit
comment: A single RET, and the destination of the ljmp 0xEFBC at 0xEF3F, which is where 0xEF32 goes when XDATA 0x048C has none of bits 0, 1 or 3 set. It touches no register and no memory: a request byte with no request bit set does nothing and returns.

name: tick_097d_call_88f0_at_c8
comment: Tests bit 2 of the XDATA 0x048C request byte. If it is clear, XDATA 0x097D is zeroed and the function returns; if it is set, 0x097D is incremented, and when the incremented value is 0xC8 it loads R5 with 0x5E and calls 0x88F0 before zeroing 0x097D on the way out. Any other value leaves 0x097D holding the increment and returns.

name: dispatch_index_3x_from_byte_00
comment: Jump-table dispatcher: masks direct byte 0x00 with 0x0F, adds it to itself twice so A = 3 x index, folds any carry into DPH, then executes jmp @A+DPTR, so entries are three bytes each. With the mask in place A never exceeds 0x2D, so the inc DPH at 0xEFE5 cannot execute. The .c reports that it could not recover the jumptable; the tables are the ljmp rows at 0xF041, 0xF071, 0xF0A1 and 0xF0D1, and the wrappers at 0xF018/0xF022/0xF02C/0xF036 are what load DPTR before calling here.

name: table_efe8_row14_ljmp_f040
comment: A single ljmp 0xF040; it is row 14 of the sixteen three-byte rows at 0xEFE8, and rows 10-15 (the six ljmp 0xF040 entries at 0xF006-0xF015) all carry this same target. It is a table row reached through the 0xEFE8 dispatch, not a routine with behaviour of its own.

name: dispatch_via_table_f041
comment: Copies B into direct byte 0x00, loads DPTR with 0xF041 and calls 0xEFDA, so the low nibble of B selects one of sixteen three-byte ljmp rows at 0xF041 (0xF101, 0xF102, 0xF104, 0xF106, 0xF109, 0xF10C, 0xF10D, 0xF110, then 0xF113, 0xF116, 0xF119, 0xF11C, 0xF11F, 0xF122, 0xF123, 0xF126), then returns. It reads no XDATA itself, and what the targets do is not visible in this file pair.

name: dispatch_via_table_f071
comment: The same three instructions as 0xF018, with DPTR = 0xF071. All sixteen three-byte rows of that table are 02 F1 27, so every index the dispatcher can produce lands on 0xF127 whatever the low nibble of B is.

name: dispatch_via_table_f0a1
comment: Copies B into direct byte 0x00, loads DPTR with 0xF0A1 and calls 0xEFDA. Rows 0-4 of that table are ljmp 0xF128, row 5 is ljmp 0xF129, and rows 6-15 are ljmp 0xF13C, so the index selects between three targets.

name: operand_of_mov_dptr_f02f
comment: Not an instruction boundary and not a function: the bytes 0xF0 and 0xA1 at this address are the immediate operand of the mov DPTR,#0xF0A1 at 0xF02F, inside the 0xF02C wrapper. The census seeded this address from a byte-pattern match inside that instruction, which is why the .c describes a store through a pointer and a call to 0xF512 that do not correspond to these two bytes.

name: dispatch_via_table_f0d1
comment: Copies B into direct byte 0x00, loads DPTR with 0xF0D1 and calls 0xEFDA. Row 0 of that table is ljmp 0xF13D and rows 1-15 are ljmp 0xF13E.

name: mid_instruction_of_row_f053
comment: Not an instruction boundary: 0xF054 and 0xF055 are the high bytes of the three-byte ljmp 0xF10D row that starts at 0xF053, row 6 of the table at 0xF041. The census seeded this address from a byte-pattern match inside that row, and the .asm runs on from the acall it decoded at 0xF054 into the following table rows, so the .c's call to 0xF70D followed by a jump to 0xF246 is that continuation rather than a call at this address.

name: table_f071_row01_ljmp_f127
comment: A single ljmp 0xF127, the first row of the sixteen three-byte rows at 0xF071 that 0xF022 dispatches into. A table row, not a routine with behaviour of its own.

name: table_f071_row04_ljmp_f127
comment: A single ljmp 0xF127; row 4 of the table at 0xF071 (0xF071 + 3 x 4 = 0xF07D). A table row, not a routine with behaviour of its own.

name: table_f071_row05_ljmp_f127
comment: A single ljmp 0xF127; row 5 of the table at 0xF071. A table row, not a routine with behaviour of its own.

name: table_f071_row09_ljmp_f127
comment: A single ljmp 0xF127; row 9 of the table at 0xF071 (0xF071 + 3 x 9 = 0xF08C). A table row, not a routine with behaviour of its own.

name: mid_instruction_of_row_f08f
comment: Not an instruction boundary: 0xF090 and 0xF091 are the high bytes of the three-byte ljmp 0xF127 row that starts at 0xF08F, row 10 of the table at 0xF071. The census seeded this address from a byte-pattern match inside that row and the sweep read 0xF1 there as an acall, so the .c's call to 0xF727 then jump to 0xF127 is that continuation rather than a call at this address.

name: mid_instruction_of_row_f0e3
comment: Not an instruction boundary: 0xF0E4 and 0xF0E5 are the high bytes of the three-byte ljmp 0xF13E row that starts at 0xF0E3, row 6 of the table at 0xF0D1. The census seeded this address from a byte-pattern match inside that row, and the .asm continues into the following rows, so the .c's call to 0xF73E then jump to 0xF13E is that continuation.

name: last_byte_of_row_f0ec
comment: Not an instruction boundary: 0xF0EE is the last byte of the three-byte ljmp 0xF13E row that starts at 0xF0EC, row 9 of the table at 0xF0D1. The census seeded this address from a byte-pattern match inside that row, so the .c's addc A,R6 and jump to 0xF13E come from the sweep running on into the following bytes.

name: ret_stub_table_f041_row00
comment: A single RET with no register and no memory access. It is the target of row 0 of the table at 0xF041, so the jump into it from the 0xF018 dispatch is unconditional and the RET returns to whoever called 0xF018.

name: sjmp_f154
comment: A single sjmp +0x50, an unconditional branch to 0xF154, reached as row 1 of the table at 0xF041. The .c attached here is the decompilation of the branch target 0xF154, not of these two bytes.

name: sjmp_f160
comment: A single sjmp +0x5A, an unconditional branch to 0xF160, reached as row 2 of the table at 0xF041. The .c attached here is the decompilation of the branch target 0xF160, not of these two bytes.

name: ljmp_f18a
comment: A single ljmp 0xF18A, reached as row 3 of the table at 0xF041. The .c attached here is the decompilation of the branch target 0xF18A, not of these three bytes.

name: ljmp_f196
comment: A single ljmp 0xF196, reached as row 4 of the table at 0xF041. The .c's own header calls this thunk_FUN_CODE_f198, but the instruction in the .asm targets 0xF196, and the .c is the decompilation of 0xF196 rather than of these three bytes.

name: ret_stub_table_f041_row05
comment: A single RET with no register and no memory access. It is the target of row 5 of the table at 0xF041, so the jump into it from the 0xF018 dispatch is unconditional and the RET returns to whoever called 0xF018.

name: ljmp_f219
comment: A single ljmp 0xF219, reached as row 6 of the table at 0xF041. The .c attached here is the decompilation of the branch target 0xF219, not of these three bytes.

name: ljmp_f246
comment: A single ljmp 0xF246, reached as row 7 of the table at 0xF041. The .c attached here is the decompilation of the branch target 0xF246, not of these three bytes.

name: thunk_to_f275
comment: Three bytes only: ljmp 0xf275. No XDATA address is read or written by these bytes. F113.c is the decompiler following that jump, so the body it shows - the test of XDATA 0x0440, the OR of 0x80 into 0x06FF and the call to 0x896A with R7 = 0x35, or the XOR of 0x80 into 0x0471 - is 0xf275's code, not this slot's.

name: thunk_to_f290
comment: Three bytes only: ljmp 0xf290. F116.c is the decompiler following that jump; the body it shows (XDATA 0x06CD set to 0x02, 0x06FF OR 0x20, the call to 0x896A with R7 = 0x36, and 0x0471 masked with 0x7F) is 0xf290's code. The slot itself reads and writes nothing.

name: thunk_to_f2ad
comment: Three bytes only: ljmp 0xf2ad. F119.c is the decompiler following that jump; its body (XDATA 0x06CD set to 0x02, 0x06FF OR 0x40, the call to 0x896A with R7 = 0x37, and 0x0471 masked with 0x7F) is 0xf2ad's code. The slot itself touches no XDATA address.

name: thunk_to_f2ca
comment: Three bytes only: ljmp 0xf2ca. F11C.c is the decompiler following that jump; the 0x06C6 store, the call to 0x88F0 with R5 = 0x14 and the decrement of the low three bits of XDATA 0x0443 are 0xf2ca's code. This slot reads and writes nothing of its own.

name: thunk_to_f2f3
comment: Three bytes only: ljmp 0xf2f3. F11F.c is the decompiler following that jump; the 0x06C6 store, the call to 0x88F0 with R5 = 0x15 and the increment of the low three bits of XDATA 0x0443 are 0xf2f3's code. The slot itself touches no XDATA address.

name: bare_ret_f122
comment: A single ret instruction and nothing else: no XDATA, CODE or SFR byte is read or written, and A, DPTR and the flags are handed back as the caller left them. Whether this is a deliberate empty stub or an artefact of the call-target byte scan that proposed this boundary is not determinable from this listing.

name: thunk_to_f198
comment: Three bytes only: ljmp 0xf198. F123.c is the decompiler following that jump, so the tests of XDATA 0x0440 and 0x07F6, the 0x045A mask and the OR into 0x0720, 0x097A and 0x047B are 0xf198's code. The slot itself reads and writes nothing.

name: bare_ret_f127
comment: A single ret instruction: nothing is read or written, and the caller's A, DPTR and flags come back untouched. Whether this is a deliberate no-op stub or a false positive of the call-target byte scan that proposed this boundary is not determinable from the listing.

comment: A single ret instruction: nothing is read or written, and the caller's A, DPTR and flags come back untouched. Whether this is a deliberate no-op stub or a false positive of the call-target byte scan that proposed this boundary is not determinable from the listing.

name: store_00_ff_0d_to_0762_0764
comment: Three movx stores in sequence, DPTR reloaded before each: XDATA 0x0763 is written 0x00, XDATA 0x0762 is written 0xFF and XDATA 0x0764 is written 0x0D, then it returns. Nothing is read, so all three values are fixed constants rather than a copy. What the three bytes configure is not decoded here.

comment: A single ret instruction: nothing is read or written, and the caller's A, DPTR and flags come back untouched. Whether this is a deliberate no-op stub or a false positive of the call-target byte scan that proposed this boundary is not determinable from the listing.

name: bare_ret_f153
comment: A single ret instruction and nothing else: no XDATA, CODE or SFR byte is touched. It is the ljmp target of the nothing-to-do exits at 0xf1f5 in 0xf198 and at 0xf272 in 0xf246, so both of those routines deliberately land here; whether the call-target byte scan that proposed this boundary found a real empty routine is not determinable from the listing.

name: if_0440_nonzero_call_88f0_0a
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x0440 and returns immediately if it is zero. If it is non-zero the routine puts 0x0A in R5, calls 0x88F0, and returns. What R5 means to the callee, and what the byte at 0x0440 is, are not decoded here.

name: toggle_045b_bit0_set_0709_bit0
comment: Reads XDATA 0x06E6 and requires it to equal 0x01, requires XDATA 0x0440 to be non-zero and XDATA 0x070D to be zero, returning on any mismatch. It then complements bit 0 of the byte at XDATA 0x045B and writes it back - cpl 0xe0 operates on the accumulator's bit 0 - and sets bit 0 of XDATA 0x0709. The conjunction is 'some bit of the pair set in both bytes', not a bitwise AND: the 0x049D mask is only tested against zero and its value is discarded, and so is the R5 mask once 0x0498 has been set. From 0x0097 the body is a pair of `movc A,@A+DPTR` loops: the first copies CODE bytes into internal or external RAM on the carry, the second walks the same source doing bit manipulation through R0, and both run to a count in R7. 0x0091 and 0x0094 are a two-entry ljmp table to 0x00CF and 0x0200. This is Keil startup, not vendor code. The 0x0097 loops' caller, 0x00CF and 0x0200 are not decoded here.

Between them it calls six routines -- 0x14C8, 0x012F, 0x018C, 0x029B, 0x7110 and 0x7177 -- and the body of the frame between 0x012F and 0x029B tests a byte and branches on it, which is what makes this a dispatch rather than a straight-line sequence. name: timer1_target_splits_internal_ram_41_on_carry
comment: The timer 1 overflow handler, 48 bytes, with the same full save and restore of A, B, DPH, DPL and PSW. It calls 0x0E7D, copies internal RAM byte 0x41 into R7, swaps A, masks the low nibble and branches on ACC.0; if that bit is set it sets bit 2 of internal RAM byte 0x06 -- the bit address 0x32, which is the byte the .c prints as `_6_2` -- copies 0x41 into R7 again, clears bit 4 of 0x41, writes it back and calls 0x0E72. The byte at 0x05E5 is this function's own `reti`, which is what settles the framing of the two lone `reti` bytes after it: 0x05E6 and 0x05E7 are not its tail. 0x41 and 0x06 are not named in ec/annotations/registers.yaml and are not identified here.

name: serial0_target_is_one_byte_reti
comment: A single `reti` byte (0x32) and nothing else: the whole of what the serial 0 vector at 0x0023 reaches. It is not an epilogue split off a larger routine. The byte before it, 0x05E5, is the timer 1 handler's own `reti` -- 0x05B6's framed body is 48 bytes and ends exactly there -- and the byte after it, 0x05E7, is another lone `reti`, so no function body runs into this byte from either side. ec/ghidra/reassembly.csv records the address as a `match` and ec/tools/verify_reassembly.py --check confirms the listing is byte-exact, so the framing is settled by the bytes. Whether the EC services serial 0 is not established here: that is a question about the interrupt-enable and serial registers, which this address does not read, and 'the handler at the vector is one reti' is not the same claim as 'serial 0 is unimplemented'.

name: clear_low_nibble_of_1304
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x1304, reads the byte, ANDs it with 0x0F, writes it back, reads it again and leaves it in A on return. The listing opens with xch A,R5 / mov A,R7 / xch A,R5, a register shuffle whose result is discarded by the following movx and which the .c omits entirely. The .asm header flags this function boundary as a hypothesis, so the instructions shown may not be the whole function.

name: write_internal_ram_init_constants
comment: Writes constants into internal RAM by direct addressing: 0xB4=0x22, 0x96=0x2A, 0xB5=0x30, 0x25=0x0F, then zeroes 0x28 and 0x2A, computes 0xB0 = (0xB0 & 0xC3) | 0x28 and begins the same read-modify-write shape on 0xB2. The listing stops mid-sequence at 0x0F11; the .c continues with further read-modify-writes on 0xB1 and 0xB2 and clears of 0x20, XDATA 0x0019-0x001C and internal RAM 0x22, none of which the .asm covers, so that tail is reported from the .c and not decoded. The .asm header marks the boundary a hypothesis.

name: zero_xdata_200b
comment: Clears A, loads DPTR with 0x200B, then issues four consecutive movx @DPTR,A writes before returning, so XDATA 0x200B receives 0x00 four times. The .c shows a single write; the .asm shows four and the asm is the ground truth. Whether the repetition is a wider store that failed to advance DPTR or four deliberate writes is not determinable from these instructions.

name: bl51_bank_select_0
comment: Keil BL51 cross-bank switch stub that selects bank 0 in the common area: 350 of the 403 trampolines in 0x1150-0x1ABC route through it by loading DPTR with the target and jumping here. It carries the C0 08 74 prologue that occurs 4 times in the main EC image and 0 times in the PD image; nothing here is a claim about any register's behaviour

name: bl51_bank_select_1

The audit counts bank0 calling 61 bank-1 trampolines and bank1 calling 229 bank-0 ones but does not say how these 53 split between those callers so no caller is attributed to this stub

name: bl51_bank_select_2

It is the target of the table entry at 0x0007, one of five that reach this group, and it is a two-instruction thunk of the same shape as the hundreds of `mov DPTR,#imm16` + `ljmp 0x1100` trampolines elsewhere in the image. 0xBF1C lies in the 0x8000-0xFFFF banked CODE window. Ghidra's C names 0x1100 bl51_bank_select_0, and 0xBF57 lies in the 0x8000-0xFFFF banked CODE window.
