name: trampoline_bank0_c881
comment: One of the 403 BL51 trampolines in the common-area block 0x1150-0x1ABC: it loads DPTR with 0xC881 and ljmps to the bank-0 select stub at 0x1100. The audit's ajmp site at 0x15BA is the 0x81 low byte of that mov dptr immediate and is a scan phantom rather than a paged branch

name: set_direct_bit_0c_3
comment: Sets bit 3 of the direct internal byte 0x0C -- the bit address 0x63 -- and returns. Nothing else is touched, and nothing in these two bytes says what that bit means.

name: mul16
comment: 16-bit multiply, called by charge_target_update to get cells x 4100 and again for the final target arithmetic.

name: be16_add
comment: Big-endian 16-bit add, used to accumulate the temperature-weighted stress increment.

name: limit_65000_minus_x
comment: Called from 0xBCF5 to compute 65000 - stress - 1.

name: switch_case_dispatch
comment: The only subroutine in the main EC image opening d0 83 d0 82 f8: it pops the return address the preceding lcall pushed into DPTR to get the inline table's address and takes the selector in A; 15 lcall sites name it and it dispatches through jmp @a+dptr at 0x716B. Keil C51's own name for the idiom is ?C?CCASE but the file says that is a name for the shape and not a symbol read out of this image

name: ljmp_0056
comment: A single LJMP 0x0056. Nothing is read, written or computed at 0x0003 and there is no return of its own: the C body saved here shows the R0-R7 save and the call to 0x0050, but those belong to the target at 0x0056, not to this address.

name: ljmp_0094
comment: A single LJMP 0x0094, with no instruction of its own. The call to 0x0050 that the C body attributes to this address is executed by the target at 0x0094.

name: ljmp_00b2
comment: A single LJMP 0x00B2, with no instruction of its own. The R0-R7 save and the call to 0x0050 shown in the C body are the target's.

name: ljmp_00f0
comment: A single LJMP 0x00F0, with no instruction of its own. The call to 0x0050 that the C body attributes to this address is the target's.

name: ljmp_010e
comment: A single LJMP 0x010E, with no instruction of its own. The R0-R7 save and the call to 0x0050 shown in the C body are the target's.

name: call_10f1_then_jmp_1229
comment: Two instructions: LCALL 0x10F1, which reads three CODE bytes at DPTR into R3, R2 and R1, then LJMP 0x1229. The 0x1229 listing in this tree ends after MOV DPH,R2 / MOV DPL,R1, and that listing carries a boundary caveat, so what consumes R1:R2 after the tail jump is not shown here. 0x0050 itself touches no memory.

name: vector_wrapper_dp_0151
comment: Saves A, B, DPH, DPL and PSW, sets PSW=0x00, pushes R0 through R7, loads DPTR with the CODE address 0x0151, calls 0x0050, then pops everything in reverse and returns with RETI. Within this shard the three wrappers that set PSW=0x00 are exactly the three that also push R0-R7, while the two setting PSW=0x10 (register bank 1) do not. What the 0x0151 table entry selects is not decoded here.

name: vector_wrapper_dp_0154
comment: Saves A, B, DPH, DPL and PSW, sets PSW=0x10 to select register bank 1, loads DPTR with the CODE address 0x0154, calls 0x0050, then restores and RETIs. Unlike the PSW=0x00 wrappers it does not push R0-R7. What the 0x0154 table entry selects is not decoded here.

name: vector_wrapper_dp_0157
comment: Saves A, B, DPH, DPL and PSW, sets PSW=0x00, pushes R0 through R7, loads DPTR with the CODE address 0x0157, calls 0x0050, then restores and RETIs. It is byte-for-byte the same shape as 0x0056 apart from the three DPTR immediate bytes. What the 0x0157 table entry selects is not decoded here.

name: vector_wrapper_dp_015a
comment: Saves A, B, DPH, DPL and PSW, sets PSW=0x10 to select register bank 1, loads DPTR with the CODE address 0x015A, calls 0x0050, then restores and RETIs. It does not push R0-R7, matching 0x0094 rather than 0x0056. What the 0x015A table entry selects is not decoded here.

name: vector_wrapper_dp_015d
comment: Saves A, B, DPH, DPL and PSW, sets PSW=0x00, pushes R0 through R7, loads DPTR with the CODE address 0x015D, calls 0x0050, then restores and RETIs. It is byte-for-byte the same shape as 0x0056 and 0x00B2 apart from the three DPTR immediate bytes. What the 0x015D table entry selects is not decoded here.

name: dispatch_r5_write_083b_0300
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x083B and R5 to XDATA 0x0300, then reads XDATA 0x00E2 and returns at 0x0381 immediately if that byte equals 0x05. Otherwise a decrement chain dispatches on R5: 0 to 0x01B8, 1 to 0x01F2, 2 to 0x022C (which stores 0xE8 at XDATA 0x083D), 3 to 0x0234 (0xEC at the same byte), 4 to 0x023C, 5 to 0x0279, and any other value to 0x02CA, which copies XDATA 0x083D into XDATA 0x0301. Every arm calls 0xB154, 0xB156 or 0xB159 and then LCALL 0x104D, whose following 00 00 00 01 bytes are that routine's four inline argument bytes rather than the NOP/AJMP the linear decode shows; the instruction 0x104D returns to at 0x01C2 is not in this listing, and none of these XDATA addresses is resolved further here.

name: c_startup_idata_clear
comment: The ITE8850-PD image's own reset vector lands here and the head is the textbook Keil/SDCC IDATA clear: R0 counting 0x7F down to 0x00 with @r0 zeroed, then DPTR set to 0x0000. It is the evidence that 0x20000 is a second program, and it is PD-image code, not EC code

name: mul32_accumulate_r4_r7
comment: A 32-bit by 32-bit multiply built from a chain of MUL AB partial products that accumulates the low 32 bits in R4:R5:R6:R7. Both 16-bit halves R0:R1 and R4:R5 are first shifted right by 0x0721 (which folds sign bits into 0xD5 and leaves a flag in 0xE7), the accumulator is shifted by 0x0738 between bits, and the out-of-range paths return through 0x0756 or 0x0760. Which of the two register quads is the multiplicand and which the multiplier is not recorded here, and the .c's named parameters do not establish it.

name: shl32_16_iters
comment: A 16-iteration left shift of R4:R5:R6:R7, shifting R7, R6, R5 and then R4 in that order so R4's top bit reaches the carry first; a carry there exits early to 0x06DC instead of finishing the loop. The bit shifted out of the running A byte is stored at 0xD5, and when that bit is set the routine calls 0x0F00, which subtracts A from R4:R5:R6:R7. The early-exit arm at 0x06DC builds A from the remaining loop count in B plus 0x7E and rotates it right through the carry from 0xD5 into R4, R5, R6 and R7; the value that produces is not resolved here.

name: shift_right_2x16_sticky_d5
comment: Shifts R0:R1 and R4:R5 right by one bit, inserting a 1 into bit 0 of each half via SETB 0xE7 before each pair of RLCs, and folds the sign bits into 0xD5: 0xD5 takes bit 7 of the pre-shift R0 and is complemented at 0x0735 when bit 7 of the pre-shift R4 was set. Returns A holding the new low byte of R4 with the carry holding bit 7 of the pre-shift R4, and leaves 0xE7 and 0xD5 for the callers at 0x05A6 and 0x0738 to read. The .c for this address does not carry 0xD5 through at all.

name: shift_r3r4_right_1
comment: When bit 0xE7 is set it first increments R7, carrying through R6 and R5 into R3 - R4 is not on that chain - and jumps to 0x0760 if R3 then becomes zero. It then writes R4 = (R3 shifted right one) with the low bit of 0xD5 going into bit 7, and stores the carry out to 0xE7. R3, R5, R6 and R7 are otherwise left alone; the MOV A,R5 / MOV R5,A pair at 0x0751 and 0x0754 is a no-op on R5.

name: saturate_all_ones
comment: Loads 0xFF into A and stores it to R4, R5, R6 and R7 before returning, so the caller sees 0xFFFFFFFF in R4:R7. Within this shard it is entered only from 0x05C2 in the multiply at 0x05A6, on the path where a shifted operand half came out as 0xFFFF. Whether other callers exist elsewhere in the image was not checked.

name: clear_r4_r7_return_zero
comment: Clears A and jumps into the shared store at 0x0758, so R4, R5, R6 and R7 all become zero and the return value in A is 0. Within this shard it is entered from 0x05DB in the multiply at 0x05A6, the arm taken when the sign test at 0x05CE does not carry.

name: saturate_r4_from_d5_r5_80
comment: Loads bit 0xD5 into the carry, sets A = 0xFF and rotates it right through that carry, so R4 becomes 0xFF when 0xD5 is set and 0x7F when it is clear, then writes R5 = 0x80 and falls into the shared stores at 0x075A, which zero R6 and R7. Within this shard it is entered from 0x05D5 and 0x069A in the multiply at 0x05A6 and from 0x074A in 0x0738.

name: read_byte_by_tag_r3
comment: Reads one byte into A, selected by the R3 tag: R3=1 loads DPTR from R2:R1 and uses MOVX, R3=0 uses the non-MOVX indirect read @R1, R3=0xFE uses MOVX @R1 without touching DPTR, and any other value loads DPTR from R2:R1 and uses MOVC, reading the code space. The carry left by the CJNE at 0x0BAB is what identifies the R3=0 arm; the four addresses this selects are XDATA, internal RAM and CODE, and no memory outside the tag's own space is touched.

name: read_byte_at_dptr_plus_r1r2_by_tag
comment: The same four R3 tags as 0x0BAB, but the address is DPTR + R1:R2 rather than R1:R2 alone: R3=1 adds the pair into DPTR and reads with MOVX, R3=0 forms R0 = DPL + R1 and reads @R0 without MOVX, R3=0xFE forms the same R0 and reads it with MOVX, and any other value adds the pair into DPTR and reads with MOVC. DPTR is left modified on the R3=1 and default arms and untouched on the other two, and R0 is scratch on the R3=0 and R3=0xFE arms.

name: add_a_into_byte_by_tag_r3
comment: Adds the incoming A into the byte the R3 tag selects and returns the sum in A: R3=1 sets DPTR from R2:R1, reads with MOVX, adds and writes back, R3=0 and R3=0xFE add A into @R1 without and with MOVX respectively, and any other value reads the byte at the R2:R1 code address with MOVC and returns the sum without storing it. R0 holds the incoming A as scratch on three of the four arms, so the code-space arm is read-only and the other three update the byte in place.

name: write_byte_by_tag_r3
comment: Stores A to the single byte the R3 tag selects: R3=1 loads DPTR from R2:R1 and uses MOVX, R3=0 uses the non-MOVX indirect store @R1, and R3=0xFE uses MOVX @R1 without touching DPTR. Any other R3 value falls straight to the RET at 0x0C57 with nothing written, so the code-space case that 0x0BAB and 0x0BC4 read with MOVC has no store counterpart here.

name: write_byte_at_dptr_plus_r1r2_by_tag
comment: Stores the incoming A to the byte at DPTR + R1:R2 on the same three tags as 0x0C46: R3=1 adds the pair into DPTR and stores with MOVX, R3=0 forms R0 = DPL + R1 and stores @R0 without MOVX, and R3=0xFE forms the same R0 and stores it with MOVX. Any other R3 value returns at 0x0C79 with nothing written. A is moved to R0 at 0x0C58 on entry, so the value is held there while the address is formed and the two R3=0 arms swap it back out with XCH A,R0.

name: mul_r7_r5_r4_into_r6r7
comment: A three-term chain of MUL AB partial products written into R6:R7: R7 times R5 first, keeping the low byte in R7 and the high byte in R0, then the pre-shift R7 times R4 with its high byte added to R0, then the pre-shift R7 times R5 again with that sum folded into R6. R6's incoming value is overwritten and the result is truncated to 16 bits; the .asm carries a boundary caveat for this entry, so these instructions may not be the whole function.

name: div_u16_by_u16_or_u8
comment: Unsigned division of the 16-bit R7:R6, dispatched on which divisor bytes are zero. With R4=0 and R6=0 it does a single DIV AB of R7 by R5, leaving the quotient in R7 and the remainder in R5, with no zero-divisor test. With R4 nonzero it saves R4 into R0, reuses R4 as the 17th accumulator bit, and runs eight restoring shift-subtract iterations against the 16-bit divisor R4:R5, leaving the quotient in R7:R6 and the remainder in R4:R5. With R4=0 and R6 nonzero it first divides R6 by R5, jumping to the RET at 0x0CE0 with the result only in A and B if that division does not borrow, and otherwise stores quotient and remainder in R6 and R5 and runs the same eight iterations against the 8-bit divisor R5 held in R0.

name: read_two_bytes_by_ptr_kind
comment: Dispatches on R3: 1 reads two XDATA bytes at the 16-bit address in R1:R2, 0 reads two indirect internal-RAM bytes at @R1, 0xFE reads two indirect XDATA bytes at @R1, and any other value reads two CODE bytes at R1:R2 with movc. B receives the first byte and A the second. R1 is incremented and decremented around both indirect paths, so the pointer registers are left as found.

name: read_two_bytes_at_offset_by_ptr_kind
comment: The R3 dispatch of 0x0D0D with a 16-bit offset in R1:R2 added to the caller's DPTR. R3=1 adds the offset to DPTR and reads two XDATA bytes, R3=0 forms R0 = DPL + R1 and reads two internal-RAM bytes, 0xFE does the same through movx for XDATA, and the default path adds R2 to DPH and reads two CODE bytes at DPTR + R1:R2. B gets the first byte and A the second.

name: write_two_bytes_by_ptr_kind
comment: The store counterpart of 0x0D0D, taking the value in A:B. R3=1 writes A then B to XDATA at the 16-bit address in R1:R2, R3=0 writes them to internal RAM at @R1, and 0xFE writes them to XDATA at @R1. Any other R3 value reaches the ret with nothing written, so there is no CODE-space path.

name: write_two_bytes_at_offset_by_ptr_kind
comment: The store counterpart of 0x0D38. R3=1 adds the 16-bit offset R1:R2 to DPTR and stores A (saved in R0 on entry) then B to XDATA; R3=0 adds R1 to DPL and stores to internal RAM at R0; 0xFE does the same through movx. As in the reader, any other R3 value reaches the ret with nothing written.

name: add_32bit_r0r3_to_r4r7
comment: Adds the 32-bit value in R0:R3 to the 32-bit value in R4:R7 byte by byte, carrying upward, and leaves the sum in R4:R7. No memory is touched.

name: udiv_shift_subtract_core
comment: Shift-subtract unsigned division core whose four tails are chosen by testing the divisor bytes R0, R1 and R2 for zero in turn: 8 iterations at 0x0E18, 16 at 0x0EB3, 24 at 0x0E8A, or an 8-bit div AB on R4:R3 followed by 24 iterations at 0x0E6B. Each iteration doubles a five-byte register (DPL or R0 plus R4:R7) as one unit and, when the bit shifted out was set, subtracts the divisor R0:R3 and increments the low byte. Each tail ends by moving the surviving bytes into a different subset of R0:R3 and leaving one or two bytes in R7 and R6; which register holds the quotient and which the remainder is not determined from this listing.

name: and_32bit_r0r3_r4r7
comment: Four parallel AND operations: R7 &= R3, R6 &= R2, R5 &= R1, R4 &= R0. Returns immediately; no memory is touched.

name: or_32bit_r0r3_r4r7
comment: Four parallel OR operations: R7 |= R3, R6 |= R2, R5 |= R1, R4 |= R0, then ret. The .asm header notes that this function boundary came from a call-target byte scan and is a hypothesis, so the listing may not be the whole routine.

name: negate_32bit_r4r7
comment: Computes zero minus the 32-bit big-endian value in R4:R7 with a clr A / subb chain and writes the two's complement back into R4:R7. No memory is touched.

name: sub_or_cmp_r0_r7
comment: Subtract/OR comparison across R0-R3 and R4-R7 that changes A/B/flags and returns ordinarily; it is the routine branched on after CLR C at 0x4DA1. What it compares, and what the loaded values mean, is not identified here

name: shr_32bit_r4r7_by_r0
comment: Logical right shift of the 32-bit value in R4:R7 by the count in R0, zero-filling from the bottom: the carry is cleared once before the loop and each byte is shifted with rrc. A count of 0 jumps straight to the ret, so the value is returned untouched.

name: shl_32bit_r4r7_by_r0
comment: Logical left shift of the 32-bit value in R4:R7 by the count in R0, zero-filling from the top: the carry is cleared once before the loop and each byte is shifted with rlc. A count of 0 jumps straight to the ret, so the value is returned untouched.

name: read4_ptr_kind_dispatch
comment: Dispatches on R3 to a four-byte loader: 1 sets DPTR from R1:R2 and jumps to 0x0FAF, 0 sets R0 from R1 and jumps to 0x12B9, 0xFE sets R0 from R1 and jumps to 0x12C5, and anything else sets DPTR from R1:R2 and jumps to 0x0FBB. The default tail 0x0FBB is the CODE-space reader in this shard; the other three targets are outside this listing and are not decoded here.

name: read4xdata_to_r4_r7
comment: Four-byte XDATA reader relative to the entry pointer P: reads P..P+3 into R4..R7 with three INC DPTR and returns DPTR=P+3. It overwrites R4-R7 but not R3, and the later uses of the loaded values were not followed to any record meaning

name: read4_code_to_r4r7
comment: Reads four CODE bytes with movc at DPTR+0, +1, +2 and +3 into R4, R5, R6 and R7 in that order. No XDATA is touched. The decompiled C reports only the last byte, which is one reading of the same instructions but loses the three earlier loads.

name: load_xdata_to_r0_r1_r2_or_r3
comment: The routine 0x383A hands DPTR to; the head listed here is a 3-byte load into R0:R1:R2. The file records the 3-byte read as the same reading as its 0x10C8 table row, not as a traced caller | Four MOVX reads into R0-R3 with three INC DPTR, ending in an ordinary RET; it preserves R7 and does not touch R4-R7, which is what keeps the R7 index valid for 0xB2AE on the first reader path DISAGREEMENT: lightbar-bat-flow.md reads this as a 3-byte load into R0:R1:R2, pd-0x38-consumers.md reads it as four MOVX reads into R0-R3. Both are recorded; the decompile settles it. (cited from 2 files)

name: add_32bit_r4r7_into_xdata_at_dptr
comment: Adds the 32-bit value in R4:R7 into the four XDATA bytes at the incoming DPTR (R4 at DPTR+0 through R7 at DPTR+3), carrying upward and writing every byte back. R5 and R4 are both loaded from A before the add, and each step is an explicit DPL decrement with a DPH borrow rather than the pointer arithmetic the decompiled C shows.

name: write4xdata_from_r4_r7
comment: 4-byte store from R4:R5:R6:R7, rets at 0x104C. One handoff site (0x6610) uses it, which is how a 0x07E5 site reaches up to 0x07E8. Not one of the lcall 0x104D inline-argument routines that #36 owns | Four-byte XDATA writer relative to the entry pointer P: writes P..P+3 from R4..R7 and returns DPTR=P+3, preserving R4-R7. The stores are the MOVX instructions at 0x1042/45/48/4B, and this establishes a four-byte copy on one path, not a record width (cited from 2 files)

name: write4_inline_args
comment: Described here only as one of the lcall 0x104D inline-argument routines that issue #36 owns, a framing this file takes no position on; 0x1041 immediately before it is stated to be a separate routine. No role is claimed for it | Saves the destination halves, pops its caller's return address into DPTR, calls 0x1064 four times and finishes with CLR A; JMP @A+DPTR. A linear decode through the inline constants mistakes the argument bytes for instructions (cited from 2 files)

name: movc_byte_to_xdata
comment: Each invocation reads one CODE byte using MOVC, advances that pointer, swaps to the data destination for a MOVX store and increment, swaps back and returns; four calls account for exactly four inline argument bytes, not four executed caller instructions

name: add_full_product_to_dptr
comment: Keil index helper: multiplies A by B then adds the low byte of the product to DPL and the carry into DPH i.e. DPTR += A * B. The 0x07D0 sites reach it with B loaded from a record stride and DPTR loaded from an array base | The DPTR += A x B arithmetic helper in the same 0x10xx compiler-library neighbourhood as 0x10E8, 0x10C8 and 0x1041, but explicitly not one of them: it only adds to DPTR where those dereference it. The decode behind 0x04A6's handoffs belongs to pd-xdata-overlap.md; this file only cites the role | Adds the full A x B product to the incoming DPTR (MOV A,B retains the multiplication high byte for the ADDC into DPH), preserves R0-R7 and does no memory access, so the x2 its callers add is not truncated like the outer x0x38 term (cited from 3 files)

name: read3_xdata_to_r3r1_10c8
comment: Reads three consecutive XDATA bytes at DPTR, DPTR+1 and DPTR+2 into R3, R2 and R1 respectively, incrementing DPTR between each. DPTR is left pointing at the last byte read.

name: store_3byte_r3r2r1
comment: Stores R3 then R2 then R1 at DPTR with an inc dptr between each, rets at 0x10F0. Three of the eleven handoff sites reach it this way (0x5F03, 0x81A8, 0xB7A4), each writing three bytes of the 0x07Ex block

name: read3_code_to_r3r1
comment: The shape of 0x10C8 but reading CODE with movc: the three bytes at DPTR+0, +1 and +2 land in R3, R2 and R1. The .asm header notes that this function boundary came from a call-target byte scan and is a hypothesis, so the listing may not be the whole routine.

name: read3_ptr_kind_dispatch
comment: Dispatches on R3 to a three-byte loader: 1 sets DPTR from R1:R2 and jumps to 0x10C8, 0 sets R0 from R1 and jumps to 0x131B, 0xFE sets R0 from R1 and jumps to 0x132D, and anything else sets DPTR from R1:R2 and jumps to 0x10F1. All four targets are separate ljmps; no body is inlined here.

name: dispatch_code_table
comment: Complete dispatcher 0x119C..0x11C1: it consumes the return address as a CODE-table pointer, nonzero target pairs have a third selector byte and a matched selector leaves A=0 before 0x11AC, and a zero target pair selects the following default target. This framing rests on decoded dispatcher semantics plus table contents, not a raw target match

name: load_dptr_then_indirect_jump
comment: Loads DPTR from R1:R2 and then falls straight through into 0x122D, which clears A and jumps to DPTR; this listing has no ret of its own. The target address is not determined here, and the .asm header marks the function boundary as a call-target-scan hypothesis.

name: jmp_code_at_dptr
comment: Clears A and executes jmp @A+DPTR, so control transfers to the CODE address in DPTR. It is the tail that 0x1229 falls into after loading DPTR from R1:R2; no address is supplied by this two-instruction routine itself.

name: add_dptr_to_word_0d0e_ea_guard
comment: Adds the 16-bit value in DPTR to the direct internal-RAM word at 0x0E (low byte) and 0x0D (high byte). If the new high byte equals the old one, only 0x0E is stored; otherwise EA (direct bit 0xAF) is cleared around the two-byte store and set again if it had been set, so the pair is not seen half-updated by an interrupt.

name: add_word_0d0e_to_dptr
comment: Adds the 16-bit direct internal-RAM word at 0x0E (low) and 0x0D (high) to DPTR and returns the sum in DPTR. Nothing is written to memory.

name: fill_bytes_by_ptr_kind
comment: Fills a run of bytes with the value in R5, the count being the 16-bit pair R6:R7 tested from R7 upward: R7 or R6 being zero returns immediately, and R6 is incremented when R7 is non-zero. R3 selects the address space as in 0x0D0D: 1 stores through DPTR set from R1:R2 with movx, 0 stores to internal RAM at @R1, 0xFE stores to XDATA at @R1, and any other value stores nothing. R1 is saved in B and restored on both indirect paths.

name: read4_idata_to_r4r7
comment: Reads four consecutive internal-RAM bytes at @R0 into R4, R5, R6 and R7, incrementing R0 between each read. R0 is left pointing at the last byte read.

name: read4_xdata_to_r4r7
comment: Reads four consecutive XDATA bytes at @R0 into R4, R5, R6 and R7 with movx, incrementing R0 between each read. R0 is left pointing at the last byte read.

name: read3_idata_to_r3r1
comment: Reads three consecutive internal-RAM bytes at @R0 into R3, R2 and R1, incrementing R0 between each read. R0 is left pointing at the last byte read.

name: read3_xdata_to_r3r1_132d
comment: Reads three consecutive XDATA bytes at @R0 into R3, R2 and R1 with movx, incrementing R0 between each read. R0 is left pointing at the last byte read.

name: clear_0807_0808_dispatch_0805
comment: Sets DPTR to XDATA 0x803 and calls 0x393D, then clears XDATA 0x807 and 0x808. If direct bit 0xE4 is set and 0x1E9D returns zero and the byte at XDATA 0x805 XOR 0x10 is non-zero, it returns 1 or 2 in R7 according to 0x1E4B; otherwise it reads XDATA 0x805, passes it to 0x119C, decrements R6, increments R1 and jumps into the 32-bit XDATA adder at 0x1013. What the four callees do, and what direct bit 0xE4 gates, is not decoded further here.

name: store_r7_12_clear_bit_4d_tailcall
comment: Stores R7 to direct internal RAM 0x12, then tests and clears direct bit 0x4D -- the jbc target is the next instruction, so the result is discarded -- executes three nops, sets DPTR to XDATA 0x803 and calls 0x3720. It tail-jumps to 0x1CCE, which sets R5 to 5, calls 0x7CE0, and tail-jumps to 0x1E09, which sets R7 to 0 and returns; what those two callees do is not decoded here.

name: read_0803_and_invert
comment: Reads XDATA 0x803 into R7 and XDATA 0x804 into R5, sets R3 to 0x10, and calls 0xF407, whose body zeroes XDATA 0x84C and R1-R3 and calls 0x8814 and 0x821B. Returns the saved 0x803 byte with bit 0 inverted. Neither the 0x804 byte nor the R3 value is read again before the return.

name: flag_from_f4ee
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x803 into R7 and calls 0xF4EE, which leaves 0 or 1 in R7; the ret returns that R7, not the byte read. The decompiled C here returns the pre-call value, which the instructions do not.

name: invert_r7_after_f407
comment: Calls 0xF407, whose own body does not write R7 though its two callees 0x8814 and 0x821B are outside this listing, then returns R7 with bit 0 inverted. The value returned is the boolean NOT of the R7 the caller passed in.

name: read_byte_to_r3_stride_60_alt
comment: Handoff helper reached by 8 of the 0x07D0 sites and identical in its first three instructions to 0x357E: it reads the byte at DPTR copies it into R3 and loads B with 0x60. Only those three instructions are decoded here

name: load_b_60
comment: A single instruction, mov B,#0x60, with no ret, so this is not a self-contained routine and the use of the loaded B is not decoded here.

name: dph_plus_double_a_349b
comment: Doubles the byte in A, adds DPH, and writes the sum back to DPH, leaving DPL untouched and the new DPH still in A on return. No memory access and no other register touched.

name: read_byte_to_r7_base_0420
comment: Handoff helper reached by 6 of the 0x07D0 sites: it reads the byte at DPTR then points DPTR at 0x0420 and keeps the byte in R7. Only those three instructions are decoded here and 0x0420 is not otherwise identified

name: copy_a_to_r7_zero_r6
comment: Copies A into R7, clears A, and stores 0 into R6. The listing has no ret, so this is one piece of a longer sequence rather than a complete routine.

name: copy_a_to_r5_r4
comment: Copies A into R5 and then into R4. There is no ret, so what the pair is used for is not decoded here.

name: copy_a_to_r3
comment: A single mov R3,A with no ret, so the surrounding sequence is not decoded here.

name: r2_r1_r0_from_a_ljmp_0f0e
comment: Copies A into R2, R1 and R0, clears the carry, and tail-jumps to 0x0F0E. There is no ret, so whether this address is a real entry point or a split inside a longer routine cannot be told from the listing.

name: index_stride_5e_from_07d6
comment: Head of the routine whose tail at 0x34D9 is the stride-0x5E handoff entry: the head loads 0x07D6 where 0x34D9's callers load 0x07D0 and the two share the same multiply. This tail-sharing is the file's reason the entry addresses look unaligned

name: read_xdata_at_dptr_34d9
comment: One instruction, movx A,@DPTR, reading the byte at the caller-supplied DPTR into A. There is no ret, so what is done with that byte is not decoded here.

name: index_5e_fc
comment: With B set to 0x5E, MUL AB forms B:A = A*94, then 0xFC is added to the low byte into DPL and 8 plus the carry into DPH, leaving DPTR at 0x08xx, or 0x09xx on carry, with DPL = (A*94+0xFC) mod 256. It then tail-jumps to 0x0FAF, and the listing has no ret, so it is a fragment of a larger routine.

name: read_xdata_at_dptr_to_r7_34ed
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's DPTR into A and copies it to R7, then the listing ends with no ret. What happens to R7 next is not decoded here.

name: set_dptr_0424
comment: A single mov DPTR,#0x424 with no ret, so the pointer's use is not decoded here.

name: add_60a_to_dptr_34f2
comment: Loads 0x60 into B and tail-jumps to 0x10BC, whose body is mul AB, add A,DPL, mov DPL,A, mov A,B, addc A,DPH, mov DPH,A, ret, that is DPTR plus A*B with the carry propagated into DPH. With B = 0x60 this adds 96 times A to the incoming DPTR. There is no ret in this listing.

name: read_byte_to_r7_base_0408
comment: Handoff helper reached by 5 of the 0x07D0 sites: it reads the byte at DPTR keeps it in R7 and points DPTR at 0x0408 which is the base the file names for the 0x60-byte records. Only those three instructions are decoded here

name: add_60a_to_dptr_3500
comment: Loads 0x60 into B and tail-jumps to 0x10BC, whose body is mul AB, add A,DPL, mov DPL,A, mov A,B, addc A,DPH, mov DPH,A, ret, that is DPTR plus A*B with the carry propagated into DPH. With B = 0x60 this adds 96 times A to the incoming DPTR. There is no ret in this listing.

name: set_dptr_0a8b
comment: A single mov DPTR,#0xA8B with no ret; the listing does not show what the pointer is used for.

name: read_xdata_at_dptr_to_r7_3509
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's DPTR into A and copies it to R7, then the listing ends with no ret. What happens to R7 next is not decoded here.

name: index_5e_f4
comment: With B set to 0x5E, MUL AB forms B:A = A*94, then 0xF4 is added to the low byte into DPL and 8 plus the carry into DPH, leaving DPTR at 0x08xx, or 0x09xx on carry, with DPL = (A*94+0xF4) mod 256. Returns with that pointer in DPTR and the discarded high byte still in B. No memory is touched here.

name: write_3bytes_to_0a86
comment: Points DPTR at XDATA 0xA86 and calls 0x10E8, which the tree names store_3byte_r3r2r1 and which writes R3, R2 and R1 to three consecutive bytes from DPTR. The listing ends at the call with no ret, so it is a fragment, and nothing here shows where R3, R2 and R1 were set.

name: add_60a_to_dptr_353e
comment: Loads 0x60 into B and tail-jumps to 0x10BC, whose body is mul AB, add A,DPL, mov DPL,A, mov A,B, addc A,DPH, mov DPH,A, ret, that is DPTR plus A*B with the carry propagated into DPH. With B = 0x60 this adds 96 times A to the incoming DPTR. There is no ret in this listing.

name: zero_5_xdata_bytes
comment: Clears A, then stores it to five consecutive XDATA bytes, incrementing DPTR after each store and leaving DPTR five bytes on from where it started. The listing ends on the fifth inc with no ret and falls straight into 0x354F, which stores five more bytes and returns, so ten bytes are zeroed in total.

name: store_a_to_5_xdata_bytes
comment: Stores A to five consecutive XDATA bytes, incrementing DPTR after each, then returns. The entry state is the caller's: A holds whatever the caller left, which is 0 when control reaches this address by falling through from 0x3544.

name: dptr_0418_plus_60a
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's DPTR into A, saves it in R7, reloads DPTR with 0x418, then tail-jumps to 0x10BC, which adds A*B to DPTR. With B = 0x60 the resulting pointer is 0x418 plus 0x60 times the byte read. This listing stores nothing itself and has no ret.

name: read_byte_to_r3_stride_60
comment: Handoff helper reached by 12 of the 0x07D0 sites: its first three instructions read the byte at DPTR copy it into R3 and load B with 0x60 so on the file's index reading it prepares a stride-0x60 index. Only those three instructions are decoded here

name: dptr_0428_plus_60a
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's DPTR into A, saves it in R7, reloads DPTR with 0x428, then tail-jumps to 0x10BC, which adds A*B to DPTR. With B = 0x60 the resulting pointer is 0x428 plus 0x60 times the byte read. This listing stores nothing itself and has no ret.

name: store_2byte_r6r7_then_0x10c8
comment: 2-byte store from R6:R7, then reloads DPTR with 0x07D8 and calls 0x10C8 on it, before ljmp 0x0F45. Reached by lcall from the 0x6482 and 0x64AD sites, and what it then does with the 0x07D8 pointer is not read in this file

name: dptr_0400_plus_60a
comment: Reads the byte at the caller's DPTR into A, saves it in R7, reloads DPTR with 0x400, then tail-jumps to 0x10BC, which adds A*B to DPTR. With B = 0x60 the resulting pointer is 0x400 plus 0x60 times the byte read. This listing stores nothing itself and has no ret.

name: read_07d2_to_r3
comment: Points DPTR at XDATA 0x7D2, reads the byte there into A, and copies it to R3. The listing ends with no ret, so what is done with the value is not decoded here.

name: index_5e_f6
comment: With B set to 0x5E, MUL AB forms B:A = A*94, then 0xF6 is added to the low byte into DPL and 8 plus the carry into DPH, leaving DPTR at 0x08xx, or 0x09xx on carry, with DPL = (A*94+0xF6) mod 256. Returns with that pointer in DPTR and the discarded high byte still in B. No memory is touched here.

name: add_60a_to_dptr_3621
comment: Loads 0x60 into B and tail-jumps to 0x10BC, whose body is mul AB, add A,DPL, mov DPL,A, mov A,B, addc A,DPH, mov DPH,A, ret, that is DPTR plus A*B with the carry propagated into DPH. With B = 0x60 this adds 96 times A to the incoming DPTR. There is no ret in this listing.

name: add_r6_to_dpl
comment: Loads DPL into A and adds R6, leaving the sum in A. The listing has no ret, so the carry and any write-back of DPL are not part of it; the following bytes sit at 0x362A, a separate Ghidra function entry.

name: add_carry_into_dph
comment: Stores the byte in A into DPL, then adds the incoming carry into DPH: clr A leaves CY alone, so addc A,DPH yields DPH+CY and that goes back to DPH. No memory access and no other register touched. The five instructions here do not match the arithmetic the C at this address shows.

name: set_dptr_042f_then_fall_through
comment: One instruction: DPTR = 0x042F. The listing has no ret and the next address 0x3635 is mov B,#0x60 / ljmp 0x10BC, so control falls straight into that sequence and 0x3632 plus 0x3635 look like one routine split by the function boundary. The C's non-returning call to add_full_product_to_dptr is not contained in these three bytes.

name: tail_jump_10bc_with_b_60
comment: Loads B = 0x60 and jumps to 0x10BC without returning; 0x10BC is the address the export labels add_full_product_to_dptr. A and DPTR are whatever the caller left. Nothing in these two instructions shows what the callee does with B.

name: load_a_from_r7_then_tail_10bc
comment: Loads A from R7, sets B = 0x60, and jumps to 0x10BC (the export's add_full_product_to_dptr) with no return. DPTR is left as the caller set it. The C renders this as a call that returns, which the ljmp does not allow.

name: mul_by_17_add_2d_split_dpl
comment: Multiplies the byte in A by B = 0x17, adds 0x2D to the low byte and stores that in DPL, then leaves 0x0A plus the multiplication carry in A. The listing ends there with no ret, and 0x3655 begins with mov DPH,A, so this address and 0x3655 look like one routine cut in two. The C's call to read4xdata_to_r4_r7 and its second parameter appear nowhere in these instructions.

name: write_dph_call_0faf_return_r7
comment: Takes a high byte in A, stores it in DPH to finish the pointer 0x364A was building, calls 0x0FAF (the export's read4xdata_to_r4_r7), and returns the byte the call leaves in R7. The low byte of the pointer is the DPL that 0x364A wrote. What 0x0FAF itself reads is not shown in this listing.

name: scale_dptr_from_dptr_byte
comment: Reads the byte at the incoming DPTR into R7, then forms a new pointer from it: multiply by B = 0x5E, add 0xF3 to the low byte into DPL, and 0x08 plus the carry into DPH. Returns with DPTR rewritten and R7 holding the input byte; the new address is not dereferenced here. The C's return expression is not what these instructions produce.

name: write_xdata_then_set_r5_2
comment: Writes A to XDATA at the incoming DPTR, then zeroes R3 and R2, sets R5 = 0x02, and returns A = 0. The listing shows nothing reading the byte just written and gives no reason for R5 = 0x02. The C models the store through a pointer parameter, which the movx @DPTR,A does not show, and omits the register writes.

name: read_0a8b_then_tail_10bc
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0A8B, puts the byte in R7, sets DPTR = 0x0499 and B = 0x60, then jumps to 0x10BC (the export's add_full_product_to_dptr) with no return. Address 0x0A8B appears in this listing only, and what the byte there holds is not decoded here.

name: read_xdata_to_r3_set_dptr_0400
comment: Reads the byte at the incoming DPTR into R3 and A, sets B = 0x60 and DPTR = 0x0400, and returns that byte in A. The C drops both the B load and the DPTR constant and presents the input as a pointer.

name: read_0803_0804_to_r7_r5
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0803 into R7, increments DPTR to 0x0804, reads that byte into R5, and returns with the second byte also in A. Two adjacent XDATA bytes and no other access. The C returns 0x0804 as a constant and shows neither read.

name: read_07d6_tail_0c7a
comment: Reads XDATA 0x07D6 into R7, sets R6 = 0x00, R4 = 0x02 and R5 = 0x60, then jumps to 0x0C7A with no return. What the callee at 0x0C7A does with those four registers is not decoded in this listing.

name: call_0f1f_then_fall_through
comment: One instruction: lcall 0x0F1F. The listing has no ret of its own; the bytes that follow are the entry exported separately as 0x36E9, so the return the C shows is that function's, not this entry's. What 0x0F1F does, and which register its result lands in, is not shown here.

name: mask_r7_to_bit0_clear_r4_r5_r6
comment: Reduces R7 to its low bit (A = R7, anl A,#0x01, R7 = A), then clears R6, R5 and R4, and returns A = 0. No memory access. The C returns a constant 0 and shows none of the register writes.

name: setup_3byte_store_r3r2r1_at_0807
comment: Reads XDATA 0x07D2 into R7, sets R3 = 0x01, R2 = 0x07, R1 = 0xF3 and DPTR = 0x0807, then calls 0x10E8 (the export's store_3byte_r3r2r1). The three value bytes and the destination address are in this listing; the store itself happens in the callee, and there is no ret here.

name: set_r2_07_r1_d3_tail_10e8
comment: Sets R2 = 0x07 and R1 = 0xD3, then jumps to 0x10E8 (the export's store_3byte_r3r2r1) with no return. R3 and DPTR are left as the caller set them, so this listing fixes only two of the three bytes and not the destination.

name: read_xdata_to_r7_set_r3_r2
comment: Reads the byte at the incoming DPTR into R7 and A, sets R3 = 0x01 and R2 = 0x00, and returns the byte in A. R1 and DPTR are untouched, so unlike the 0x10E8 call sites this listing shows no destination for those two bytes. The C models it as a pointer dereference and omits R3 and R2.

name: scaled_lookup_from_07d2
comment: Reads XDATA 0x07D2 into R7, builds a pointer from that byte by multiplying by 0x5E, adding 0xF7 to the low byte and 0x08 plus the carry to the high byte, then reads the byte at that address and returns it in A. R7 keeps the index byte, not the result. The C's pointer expression matches the arithmetic but drops the final read.

name: call_0faf_0f00_then_jump_0dbc
comment: Three instructions: lcall 0x0FAF, lcall 0x0F00, then ljmp 0x0DBC, so there is no ret of its own. No register is set up and no XDATA address appears in the listing; all register and memory effects belong to the three callees, none of which is decoded here.

name: read_dptr_byte_then_tail_10bc_at_042c
comment: Reads the byte at the incoming DPTR into R7 and A, sets DPTR = 0x042C and B = 0x60, then jumps to 0x10BC (the export's add_full_product_to_dptr) with no return.

name: inc32_r4_r7_and_mul_r3_by_5e
comment: Increments the 32-bit little-endian value held in R4..R7 (R7 += 1, carry propagated through R6, R5 and R4 by the clr A / addc chain), then loads R3 into A, sets B = 0x5E, and returns the product in A:B. The multiplication leaves R4..R7 alone. The C reports only the multiply and loses the increment entirely.

name: load_r7_then_tail_10bc
comment: Loads A from R7, sets B = 0x60, and jumps to 0x10BC (the export's add_full_product_to_dptr) with no return. Same two instructions as 0x363E; only the address differs. Nothing here says what R7 holds at that point.

name: store_r7_at_dptr
comment: One of only two of the 25 handoff helpers that begins by storing rather than reading: 6 of the 0x07D0 sites hand DPTR to it so those sites are writes and not reads. The file does not trace the callers past the store

name: scale_dptr_from_dptr_byte_5e_f5
comment: Reads the byte at the incoming DPTR, multiplies it by B = 0x5E, adds 0xF5 to the low byte into DPL and 0x08 plus the carry into DPH, then returns. The pointer it builds is not dereferenced in this listing. The C's constant return is not what the instructions produce.

name: clear_r7_and_mask_r6_to_bit3
comment: Zeroes R7, then replaces R6 with R6 & 0x08 (A = R6, anl A,#0x08, R6 = A), and returns A = 0. Both writes are register-only, no memory is touched, and the surviving bit is not used again here. The C shows only the return.

name: unresolved_0x383A
comment: Unresolved: lcalls 0x0FCB with the DPTR it was given, clears carry and jumps to 0x0F0E. Remaining control flow not traced, for the same reason as 0xB1F2

name: call_0f1f_then_return_r7_and_3
comment: Calls 0x0F1F, then returns R7 & 0x03 in A. The masked value is R7 as the call left it, not the caller's input as the C has it. What 0x0F1F writes into R7 is not shown in this listing.

name: load_r0_r1_r2_r3_04_05_06_07
comment: Loads the immediate bytes 0x04, 0x05, 0x06 and 0x07 into R0, R1, R2 and R3 and returns. No memory access; A, B and DPTR are untouched, so it exists to set up four registers for the caller. The C is an empty body and shows none of the four writes.

name: read_xdata_to_r3_set_dptr_0418
comment: Reads the byte at the incoming DPTR into R3 and A, sets B = 0x60 and DPTR = 0x0418, and returns the byte in A. Same shape as 0x36B9 with a different constant pointer. The C shows only the dereference and drops B and the DPTR load.

name: read_be16_from_dptr
comment: Reads two consecutive XDATA bytes: the byte at the incoming DPTR into R4, then after inc DPTR the next byte into A, and finally moves R4 into B. Returns the pair in A:B, so the byte at DPTR+1 is the high byte. The C returns a single byte and drops the B load.

name: write_r7_r5_r3_to_consecutive_xdata
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA at DPTR, increments DPTR, writes R5, increments DPTR again, and writes R3, so three bytes go to consecutive addresses in that order. Leaves DPTR at the third address and A holding R3; R4, R6 and R7 are not written. The C's parameter order is the reverse of the register order.

name: read4xdata_and_clear_r7_bit0
comment: Calls 0x0FAF, which the decompile names read4xdata_to_r4_r7, so four XDATA bytes at DPTR land in R4:R7, then clears bit 0 of R7 and leaves the cleared value in R7, and returns R4 in A. The mask applies to the freshly read R7. The C shows the call and the return but drops the anl, so the value it reports is not what the instructions produce.

name: set_dptr_07fb_then_fall_through
comment: One instruction: DPTR = 0x07FB. There is no ret and the bytes run straight into 0x3977, which does movx A,@DPTR, so this entry plus 0x3977 look like one routine split by the function boundary. The C reports a return of XDATA 0x07D2, but no 0x07D2 access appears in these three bytes, so what this entry is for is not determined.

name: read_dptr_byte_then_07d2
comment: Reads the byte at the address the caller left in DPTR into R6, then sets DPTR = 0x07D2, reads that byte, and returns it in A. Only the 0x07D2 read is named by an address constant in this listing; the first address comes from the caller. The C shows just the 0x07D2 read and drops the R6 load.

name: read_byte_to_r7_set_r3_1
comment: Handoff helper reached by 4 of the 0x07D0 sites: it reads the byte at DPTR into R7 and loads R3 with 0x01. Only those three instructions are decoded here

name: set_dph_call_1041_r7_03
comment: Copies A into DPH, so the 16-bit XDATA address becomes A:DPL with DPL from the caller, then calls 0x1041, which this function's decompile names write4xdata_from_r4_r7, and overwrites R7 with 0x03 before returning. The four-byte write itself is inside 0x1041 and is not decoded here. The C shows the call but drops both the DPH store and the R7 overwrite.

name: set_args_r1_d3_r2_07_r3_01
comment: Loads R1 = 0xD3, R2 = 0x07, R3 = 0x01 and returns. No memory is touched and nothing is read to decide the values, so they are constants handed to whatever reaches this entry; it is also the fall-through target of 0x39E6, which adds R5 = A. What the triple represents is not determined here, and the C reports an empty body.

name: tail_jump_10bc_with_b_60_and_r7
comment: Loads B = 0x60, puts R7 into A, and ljmp 0x10BC, so control does not come back through this address. 0x10BC is the address the export labels add_full_product_to_dptr, and B = 0x60 is a constant the caller cannot change; what the callee does with either is not shown here.

name: read4xdata_and_return_r7_bit0
comment: Calls 0x0FAF, which the decompile names read4xdata_to_r4_r7, then returns bit 0 of the freshly read R7 in A. The mask is applied after the read, not to an argument: the C's return param_1 & 1 makes it look like a test on a parameter and is not what the instructions do.

name: store_a_then_multiply_r7_by_5e
comment: Writes A to the XDATA byte at DPTR, then loads R7 into A, multiplies by B = 0x5E, and returns with the low product byte in A and the high byte in B. The store uses whatever address the caller left in DPTR; no address constant appears in this listing.

name: clear_ram_07_08_then_call_10e8_at_0988
comment: Clears A, then direct internal RAM at 0x07 and 0x08, sets DPTR = 0x0988, and calls 0x10E8, which this function's decompile names store_3byte_r3r2r1. R1:R3 are not set here, so whatever the three-byte store used would come from the caller, but that store is inside 0x10E8 and the listing stops at the call, so these instructions alone do not show a write.

name: run_body_while_07cf_is_zero
comment: Zeroes the byte at XDATA 0x07CF and then loops while that byte is still zero, running the same sequence of calls each pass: 0x363E, 0x349B, 0xC2FA, 0x364A, 0x34C9, 0x8576, 0x35E8, 0x0FAF, 0x34CE, 0xF739, 0x3872, 0x3621, 0x3750, 0x36B9, 0x3497. It reads the byte pair at 0x0424/0x0425 and skips the 0xC2FA call unless the pair is 0x00/0x02 or 0x00/0x03, and the 0x07CF increment sits at 0x4800 and jumps back to 0x4408, the loop test. None of the callees is decoded in this shard, so what the loop drives is not determined.

name: increment_dptr_byte_and_jump_back_to_4408
comment: Ghidra's own output flags an overlap here: the cjne at 0x4801 straddles 0x4802, which is the ljmp 0x4802 tail of the loop at 0x4402, so this entry is a disassembly artefact rather than a clean function boundary. Reached at 0x4804 it increments the byte at XDATA[DPTR] and ljmp 0x4408, the re-test of that loop; 0x480B is a ret. How 0x4800 itself is reached, if at all, is not shown.

name: call_f739_then_return_dptr_07d0
comment: Calls 0xF739 and then loads DPTR with 0x07D0 before returning, so what the caller receives is a pointer to that XDATA byte. Nothing here reads or writes 0x07D0, and 0xF739 is not decoded in this shard, so the address is left unnamed rather than given a meaning this listing does not show.

name: dispatch_entry
comment: Prologue 0x4C27..0x4C37 immediately after RET at 0x4C26; its MOV A,R5 at 0x4C34 supplies the selector to LCALL 0x119C at 0x4C35. The framing is conditional on entry to 0x4C27: reset-to-0x4C27 reachability, all upstream callers, and occurrence of any selector are not established

name: dispatch_case_06
comment: Case 06 of the 0x119C CODE-table dispatcher (file 0x24C4A holds 4d6f06), separate from case 09 and not a successive execution region. It tests the bytes at 0x0834/0x0835 against #01, LCALLs 0xF75C and branches to 0x4DEE when the result is zero; 0x4D89 is the fallthrough of that last branch, not a separate entry

name: dispatch_case_09

It stores A=0 to XDATA[0x083A] at entry and the gate at 0x4E8F tests that same R7-source byte against 2; j<2 on the 0x4E96 arm is a local path condition, not a global index bound

name: scale_dptr_from_a_times_77_plus_73
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by 0x77, adds 0x73, puts the low byte in DPL and 0x08 plus the carry out of that add in DPH, so DPTR becomes 0x0800 + (A*0x77 + 0x73) and spans the 0x0800-0x09FF page. It returns without touching memory: the address is computed, not dereferenced. The C reduces the result to a single char, which these instructions do not produce.

name: store_a_then_scaled_lookup_from_r7
comment: Writes A to the XDATA byte at the caller's DPTR, then computes 0x0800 + (R7*0x77 + 0x6F) the same way, in the 0x0800-0x09FF page, and reads the byte there, returning it in A. The byte read is a table entry in this program's own XDATA; nothing here says what its contents mean, and the C's pointer return is a misreading of the computed DPTR.

name: read_xdata_0852
comment: Sets DPTR = 0x0852 and reads that byte into A. The listing ends there with no ret of its own, so what the caller receives is not shown. The C's arithmetic expression on 0x0852 does not correspond to these two instructions.

name: scale_dptr_from_a_times_77_plus_6e
comment: Multiplies A by 0x77, adds 0x6E, puts the low byte in DPL and 0x08 plus the carry in DPH, giving the address 0x0800 + (A*0x77 + 0x6E) in the 0x0800-0x09FF page, then returns. No memory is accessed, so this computes a pointer only and the C's single-char return is not what the instructions produce.

name: index_stride_77_addr_r1
comment: Stride 0x77 index helper returning the address halves in A:R1 - correction #74 supersedes the earlier R2:R1 reading - and the only one of the four multiply forms that keeps the full product: 0x089B + A * 0x77. No page term was resolved by this bounded decode

name: mul_dptr_byte_77_to_r4r5_and_arg_d7
comment: Reads the byte at the incoming DPTR, multiplies it by B = 0x77, and leaves the 16-bit product in R4:R5 (R4 high, R5 low). It then builds R1 = low + 0xD7, R2 = high + 0x08 + carry, R3 = 0x01 and returns. R4/R5 are the pair 0x58AB adds to, and what the product indexes is not determined here.

name: mul_dptr_byte_77_to_arg_6c
comment: Reads the byte at the incoming DPTR, multiplies it by B = 0x77, and builds R1 = low + 0x6C, R2 = high + 0x08 + carry (the high byte is still in B here, never copied out to R4), R3 = 0x01, then returns. Nothing in the listing says what the three-byte value addresses or is passed to.

name: arg_89_from_r4r5_then_store_at_0864
comment: Adds 0x89 to R5 and 0x08 plus the carry to R4, leaving the result in R1:R2, sets DPTR = 0x0864, and ljmp 0x10E8, which this function's decompile names store_3byte_r3r2r1. The store is therefore not in this listing, and R3 is left as the caller had it. What R4/R5 hold on entry, which this entry depends on, is not shown here.

name: scale_dptr_from_dptr_byte_77_plus_96
comment: Reads the byte at the incoming DPTR, multiplies it by B = 0x77, adds 0x96, and forms DPTR as 0x0800 + (value*0x77 + 0x96) in the 0x0800-0x09FF page, with DPL the low byte and DPH = 0x08 or 0x09, then returns. The byte read is not returned; the result is the pointer, and the C's char return does not match these instructions.

name: index_stride_77_r7
comment: Stride 0x77 helper reached from site 0xDA9B via 0xDAA3: it gives 0x0870 + low8(R7 * 0x77) so the high byte of the product is dropped while the low base addition still carries into the high byte

name: store_a_and_copy_07f4_masked_to_07f5
comment: Writes A to the XDATA address the caller left in DPTR, then computes XDATA 0x07F4 & 0x1F and writes that to 0x07F5. It finally reads 0x07D2 into R7, calls 0xF22E, and returns the 0x07D2 byte in A; the caller's DPTR is not restored. 0xF22E is not decoded in this shard.

name: call_122f_with_dptr_fffd_6f96
comment: Sets DPTR = 0xFFFD and calls 0x122F. The listing ends at that call with no ret of its own, so whether this is a tail call or a truncated export is not shown. Nothing else is touched here, and 0x122F is not decoded in this shard.

name: read_dptr_byte_into_r7
comment: Reads the byte at the XDATA address in DPTR into R7. The listing ends there with no ret of its own, so the value reaches the caller only if execution arrived by fall-through. The C's pointer arithmetic involving 0x5E does not match these two instructions.

name: scaled_lookup_from_a_times_5e_plus_f8
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by B = 0x5E, adds 0xF8, and uses the low byte plus the carry as a 16-bit XDATA address with DPH = 0x08 or 0x09, so it indexes the 0x0800-0x09FF page. It reads the byte there and returns it in A; no address is written. The page contents are not decoded here, so what each index denotes is not determined.

name: scaled_lookup_from_a_times_5e_plus_f7
comment: The same shape as 0x6FAF with a different addend: multiplies A by B = 0x5E, adds 0xF7, forms DPTR = 0x0800 + (A*0x5E + 0xF7) in the 0x0800-0x09FF page, and reads the byte there, returning it in A. Nothing is written, and the meaning of the indexed byte is not determined from this listing.

name: set_r5_then_fall_through
comment: One instruction: R5 = A. There is no ret, and the next entry 0x6FD5 loads B and DPTR before calling 0x10BC, so whether this is a real routine or a fragment the exporter split off is not determined here. The C claims a call to add_full_product_to_dptr at 0x0433, which is in the 0x6FD5 listing and not in these bytes.

name: call_10bc_with_b_60_and_dptr_0433
comment: Loads B = 0x60, sets DPTR = 0x0433, and calls 0x10BC, which this function's decompile names add_full_product_to_dptr. The listing ends at the call, so it may be a tail call; 0x10BC is not decoded in this shard, and 0x0433 is neither read nor written by these three instructions.

name: read_xdata_080d_and_set_r3_ff
comment: Sets DPTR = 0x080D, reads that byte into R7, and loads R3 = 0xFF. The listing stops there: R1 and R2 are never set and there is no ret, so what this entry hands on is not shown. The C's 0x0A86 address does not appear in these instructions.

name: set_dptr_0a86_and_call_10e8
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0A86 and lcalls 0x10E8. The listing ends without a ret, so execution falls through to 0x701A. The .c names the callee store_3byte_r3r2r1, but that routine's body is not in this file pair and its behaviour is not decoded here.

name: scale_5e_and_call_122f
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA[DPTR] into A, multiplies it by 0x5E into B:A, copies the product to R7 (low) and R6 (high), then packs the 24-bit value 0x010800 + 0x5E*x into R1:R2:R3, where x is the byte read: R1 = low + 0xF2, R2 = 0x08 + high + carry, R3 = 1. It loads DPTR with 0xFFFD and lcalls 0x122F; no ret here, so it falls through to 0x7038.

name: set_dptr_fffd_and_call_122f
comment: Loads DPTR with 0xFFFD and lcalls 0x122F, passing R0-R7 through unchanged. No ret in this listing, so execution falls through to 0x704B.

name: thunk_call_122f
comment: A single lcall 0x122F with no setup of its own: DPTR and R0-R7 are whatever the caller left. Nothing else is decoded from this address.

name: load_dptr_from_iram_0d_0e
comment: Loads DPH from internal RAM 0x0D and DPL from internal RAM 0x0E, i.e. DPTR = (IRAM[0x0D] << 8) | IRAM[0x0E], then returns. The .c renders this as a bare return and drops both moves.

name: call_1041_then_point_dptr_07d4
comment: Lcalls 0x1041, then loads DPTR with the XDATA address 0x07D4. No ret in this listing, so execution continues at 0x7069, whose first instruction is the read of that byte. What 0x1041 does is not decoded here.

name: read_07d4_into_r7
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA[DPTR] into A and copies it to R7. DPTR is not reloaded here; with the value set by the chunk at 0x7063 the address read is 0x07D4.

name: dptr_08e9_plus_5e_times_a
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by 0x5E, adds 0xE9 to the low byte and 0x08 plus carry to the high byte, and stores the result in DPTR: DPTR = 0x08E9 + 0x5E*A. A is the caller's, and no XDATA is read or written.

name: read_07d4_into_a
comment: Loads DPTR with the XDATA address 0x07D4 and reads that byte into A. No ret in this listing, so execution continues at 0x7095, which uses A as an index.

name: dptr_08ea_plus_5e_times_a
comment: Same shape as 0x706B: DPTR = 0x08EA + 0x5E*A, computed by MUL AB against 0x5E with the low byte offset 0xEA and the high byte 0x08 plus carry. A is the caller's and no XDATA is touched.

name: read_08ea_table_byte
comment: A single movx A,@DPTR, reading the byte at whatever XDATA address DPTR currently holds. With the DPTR from 0x7095 that address is 0x08EA + 0x5E*A. No ret in this listing.

name: dptr_08ed_plus_5e_times_a
comment: DPTR = 0x08ED + 0x5E*A, by the same MUL AB against 0x5E with the low byte offset 0xED and the high byte 0x08 plus carry. A is the caller's and no XDATA is touched.

name: read_08ed_table_byte
comment: A single movx A,@DPTR, reading the byte at the current XDATA address. With the DPTR from 0x70A4 that address is 0x08ED + 0x5E*A. No ret in this listing.

name: dpl_08f4_plus_5e_times_a_low_only
comment: Computes the low byte of 0x08F4 + 0x5E*A into DPL but leaves the high byte in A only: there is no mov DPH,A before the ret at 0x70C6, so DPH keeps whatever value the caller left. Whether that is intended is not determinable from this listing.

name: store_a_to_dptr
comment: A single movx @DPTR,A writing the accumulator to XDATA at the current DPTR. No ret in this listing, so it falls through to 0x70C8, which immediately overwrites DPTR from R7.

name: dptr_08e7_plus_5e_times_r7
comment: Takes R7 as the index rather than A: multiplies R7 by 0x5E and forms DPTR = 0x08E7 + 0x5E*R7, then returns. No XDATA is read or written.

name: read_dptr_to_r3_then_dptr_08fc
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA[DPTR] into A, copies it to R3, then multiplies A by 0x5E and forms DPTR = 0x08FC + 0x5E*A before returning. On return R3 holds the byte read from the caller's DPTR and DPTR points at the matching 0x5E-byte record.

name: call_0fcb_then_tail_jmp_0f0e
comment: Clears A, loads R4:R7 with 00 00 13 88, points DPTR at XDATA 0x080F and lcalls 0x0FCB; it then clears the carry and tail-jumps to 0x0F0E, with no ret of its own. What 0x0FCB and 0x0F0E do with that register set is not in this listing and is not decoded here.

name: read_dptr_to_r7_then_dptr_08f9
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA[DPTR] into A, copies it to R7, then forms DPTR = 0x08F9 + 0x5E*A and returns. Exactly one XDATA byte is read, from the address the caller left in DPTR.

name: set_dptr_0007_call_1253_tail_jmp_10c8
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0007, lcalls 0x1253, then tail-jumps to 0x10C8. There is no ret, so 0x10C8's own return is this function's return; the .c reports the two calls but drops the DPTR load.

name: read_08e8_record_byte_from_r7
comment: Computes DPTR = 0x08E8 + 0x5E*R7 from R7, reads the byte at that XDATA address into A and returns it in the accumulator. This is the only stub in the group that both computes the address and performs the read.

name: pack_0108e8_plus_5e_times_a_into_r1_r3
comment: Multiplies the caller's A by 0x5E and packs the 24-bit value 0x0108E8 + 0x5E*A into R1:R2:R3: R1 = low + 0xE8, R2 = 0x08 + high + carry, R3 = 1. No memory is touched; the packed value is left for a caller to use.

name: dptr_0a2d_plus_17_times_a
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA[DPTR] into A, then multiplies it by 0x17 and forms DPTR = 0x0A2D + 0x17*A before returning. The 0x17 stride here differs from the 0x5E stride the neighbouring stubs use; whether both index the same table is not shown by this listing.

name: dptr_08e4_plus_5e_times_a
comment: DPTR = 0x08E4 + 0x5E*A, computed by MUL AB against 0x5E with the low byte offset 0xE4 and the high byte 0x08 plus carry. A is the caller's and no XDATA is touched.

name: dptr_08e3_plus_5e_times_a
comment: DPTR = 0x08E3 + 0x5E*A, the same MUL AB shape as 0x715E with the low byte offset 0xE3. A is the caller's and no XDATA is touched.

name: set_dptr_ffff_tail_jmp_122f
comment: Loads DPTR with 0xFFFF and tail-jumps to 0x122F. There is no ret, so 0x122F's return is this function's return; the .c models it as a call that does not return.

name: pack_0108e3_plus_r6_r7_into_r1_r3
comment: Packs the 24-bit value 0x0108E3 + ((R6 << 8) | R7) into R1:R2:R3: R1 = R7 + 0xE3, R2 = 0x08 + R6 + carry, R3 = 1. Unlike 0x7140 the index is taken from R6:R7 directly rather than multiplied by 0x5E.

name: store_a_to_dptr_and_zero_r2_r3
comment: Writes A to XDATA[DPTR], then sets A to 0, copies that zero to R3 and R2, and sets R5 to 2 before returning. Nothing is read from XDATA.

name: count_07cb_up_to_3_over_07ca_records
comment: Seventy-four instructions ending in a plain `ret`, and no `mov DPTR` into 0xFF00-0xFFFF: the 0x07CA-0x07CE block it writes is reached by four `inc DPTR` off 0x07CA, and the one other XDATA address it names is the 0x04A5 index base handed to the stride helper 0x10BC. On entry it stores R7 at 0x07CA, zeroes 0x07CB, 0x07CC, 0x07CD and 0x07CE through three `inc DPTR`, and zeroes 0x07CB again as a counter. The loop calls 0x911C and 0x9028, returns early when bit 4 of 0x07CB is clear, stores the 0x07CA byte at 0x07CD, calls 0x9115/0x906D and the 0x04A5 index helper, writes 1 through the pointer 0x9177/0x9087/0x1041 build, then increments 0x07CB and repeats while it is at or below 2 -- so the counter runs 0, 1, 2 and stops. It is the second `FUN_CODE_` entry in pd-001 that the census could not classify by reading it, for the same reason as 0xEA67: nothing here reaches a 0xFFxx address, and a DPTR the caller set survives the three lcalls the loop body makes, which no read of the `.asm` can follow. What the 0x07CA-0x07CE record is not established here; the stride families are issue #75's and the 0x1253 pointer-add convention issue #69's.

name: set_07d2_and_return_r7_zero_or_one
comment: Sets XDATA 0x07D2 to R5 and calls 0xACF4 with DPTR = 0x07D1: a non-zero result takes a short path that calls 0x775C with R2 = 0x11 and R3 = 0x94 and returns 0 or 1 in R7, while a zero result calls 0xAD83 then 0xBECB with R3 = 1 and jumps to the second entry at 0x769E unless R7 equals 1. The main body calls 0xAD1E and 0xAD4D and hands R0-R3 plus the carry to 0x0F0E to compare against 0x82 and again against 0x0A; the shared block at 0x763D then calls 0xD83D (R4 = 0x13, R5 = 0x88), 0xAD9C, 0xE6C0, 0xAD83, 0xA0E6, 0xACE1, 0x0FAF, 0xAD09, 0xD013, 0xACE1, 0xADA4 and 0xAD09 before ending at 0xACBF and returning 1 in R7, and every exit path leaves R7 as 0 or 1. XDATA 0x07D1 is read repeatedly and DPTR is also loaded with 0x080F and 0x0815; the four-byte runs following each lcall 0x104D are not decoded here, and the disassembler's own byte alignment breaks around 0x762C-0x7639 and 0x7686-0x768E, so instruction boundaries in those two spans are not settled by this listing. The .c running puVar4 offset chain is not a data structure present in these bytes, and its control flow should not be relied on here.

name: call_f75c_with_07d1
comment: Loads the byte at XDATA 0x07D1 into R7, calls 0xF75C, and returns. Nothing after the call is read, so this is a one-way call that passes the byte in R7 and discards whatever the callee returns. The .c renders the same sequence as a call with the byte as its argument, which is consistent with the register setup here.

name: call_e4d0_return_r7
comment: Loads the byte at XDATA 0x07D1 into R7, calls 0xE4D0, then moves R7 into the accumulator and returns. The value returned is R7 as it stands after the call, not the byte read from 0x07D1; the .c caches the byte in a local before the call and returns that instead, which differs whenever 0xE4D0 alters R7.

name: reload_0a8b_call_f75c
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x0A8B into R7, calls 0xF75C, sets R3 to 0x07, then reads 0x0A8B a second time into R7 and returns. The .c omits the mov R3,#0x07 entirely, so that register side effect is visible only in the .asm. Nothing in this listing says what 0xF75C does with the value, and the byte is re-read rather than carried in a register, so a change made by the callee is what R7 ends up holding.

name: update_07d4_state
comment: Stores the caller's byte at XDATA 0x07D4, copies the byte 0x971B returns to 0x07D6, writes 0 to 0x07D7, then branches on individual accumulator bits returned by 0x96FE, 0x96ED and 0x97B9 (jnb ACC.3, jnb ACC.4, jb ACC.0) and on the carry left by 0x9784 and 0x9792. On those paths it clears bit 2, bit 4 and bit 5 of the byte at 0x07D4, sets bit 2 back, and calls 0x8210 with R5=2 and again with R5=0x40. It ends by storing three bytes at 0x07E0 through 0x10E8: the value {0x01, high, low} of (byte at 0x07D4) * 0x17 + 0x0A14, and the listing has no ret after that call.

name: call_dc29_with_07d4
comment: Sets R4=0, loads the byte at XDATA 0x07D4 into R7, and calls 0xDC29. R5 is left as the caller had it, so only two of the possible arguments are set here, and no result is read back. The .c renders it as FUN_CODE_dc29(0, DAT_EXTMEM_07d4), which matches R4=0 and R7=the byte.

name: fill_0849_0857_block
comment: Stores R7 to XDATA 0x0849 and R5 to 0x084A, sets R6=3, writes 1 to 0x0851, then reloads R5 from 0x084A and R7 from 0x0849, points DPTR at 0x042F and calls 0x9988 followed by 0x99C9, keeping the byte read back from 0x042F in R3. It writes R6 to 0x0855, copies 0x084C to 0x0856, reads three bytes from 0x084D through 0x10C8 and stores them at 0x0857 through 0x10E8, and the listing ends at that call with no ret. The .c lists the 0x0851 write first, assigns 0x0849 and 0x084A the other way round, and does not model the R6=3 that the 0x0855 store is built from.

name: step_state_07d0_07d1
comment: Stores the caller's byte at XDATA 0x07D0, clears 0x07D1, and calls 0x34DA and 0x36E9; if R7 is zero it runs a branch that reads 0x07D0 through 0x350B, calls 0x34D9/0x37ED/0x34CC and, when those succeed, hands 0x0420 and 0x60 to 0x3497. It then calls 0x3604 on 0x07D0 and, if bits 5 or 6 of 0x07D1 are set, calls 0x8D41. Later it recomputes 0x07D1 through 0xF5C3/0xF75C/0xF61C (or stores 0 into 0x07D1 when that path is not taken), continues only when the result is 1, 2 or 5 to write four bytes at 0x0A98 through 0x104D and call 0xCCB7, and finally calls 0x0FAF and 0x3750 and hands 0x040C and 0x60 to 0x3497 when 0x34CE returns non-zero. 0x07D0 and 0x07D1 are used here only as an index and a result byte; this listing gives them no vendor meaning.

name: call_f22e_with_07d0
comment: Loads the byte at XDATA 0x07D0 into R7, calls 0xF22E, then moves R7 into the accumulator and returns. The value returned is R7 as it stands after the call, not the byte read from 0x07D0; the .c caches the byte in a local before the call and returns that instead, which differs whenever 0xF22E alters R7.

name: store_3bytes_at_dptr_plus_1
comment: Increments DPTR and calls 0x10E8 (store_3byte_r3r2r1), which writes R3, R2 and R1 at DPTR and the two bytes after it. No address is loaded here, so the store lands wherever the caller left DPTR. The listing stops after the call with no ret, and the .c renders it as a non-returning store_3byte_r3r2r1(param_1+1) with a pointer argument this listing does not set up.

name: update_07d6_table_entries
comment: Stores the caller's byte at XDATA 0x07D6, builds DPTR = 0x0900 + byte*0x5E and writes four bytes there through 0x104D, then walks the two bytes at 0x08F6 + byte*0x5E, replacing the second with the first masked with 0xFE and the third with the old second masked with 0x03. It compares the 16-bit value 0x6FD4 returns against 0x1388 and loads R4, R2 and R3 with either (0x8C,0xCC,0xCD) or (0x99,0x99,0x9A) before calling 0x05A6 and 0x06EA, then writes four bytes at 0x0908 + byte*0x5E through 0x1041. It ends by storing three bytes at 0x0A86 through 0x10E8 with R3=0xFF and R1/R2 taken as 0x17/0xD6 or 0x21/0xD6 according to the byte 0x70BA returns, and the listing has no ret after that call. The .c drops the byte*0x5E striding that most of these addresses depend on.

name: call_f739_then_read_07d1
comment: Calls 0xF739, then loads the byte at XDATA 0x07D1 into the accumulator and returns it. The .c labels the call call_returns_with_dptr_loaded, but DPTR is set explicitly to 0x07D1 after the call rather than by it, and the return value of 0xF739 is not read here.

name: advance_07d2_counter_and_dispatch
comment: Stores the caller's byte at XDATA 0x07D2, runs 0x35AC, 0x349B, 0x3632, 0x349B and 0x3627, writes 0 to 0x07D2 and then 0xFF to it after 0x3760, and calls 0xEBE4 with R5=2. It then tests bits 7, 5 and 6 of the byte at 0x35FF's address plus one, and for each set bit masks a value with 0x7F, 0xDF or 0xBF, adds 0x25, 0x21 or 0x35 to build a 0x0900-block address with 0x3655, 0x3777 and 0x39DE, and calls 0x352C with (0x34,0xA8,0xFF), (0x47,0xA8) or (0x57,0xA8) followed by 0x366E with 0x12, 0x0F or 0x0B and then 0xF4AB. It finishes by incrementing the byte at 0x07D2 and choosing R3=5 or R3=1 for 0xCCB7 depending on whether the old value was below 3. The .c models that address as 0x07D3 and the bit tests as reads of 0x07D2/0x07D3, which this listing does not itself establish: the address comes from 0x35FF and only accumulator bits are tested.

name: call_7ce0_with_r5_0b
comment: Sets R5=0x0B, calls 0x7CE0, then loads the byte at XDATA 0x07D2 into R7, sets R3=0xFF and returns. Whatever 0x7CE0 returns in the accumulator is discarded. The .c omits both the R5 setup and the R3=0xFF, so the argument passed to 0x7CE0 and the register side effect are visible only in the .asm.

name: stub_set_r4_07
comment: A single instruction, mov R4,#0x07, with no ret and no other effect. The .c renders it as returning R7-3, which the one instruction does not contain. Whether a caller entering here expects DPTR, a value in A, or nothing cannot be determined from this listing; the bytes that follow belong to the separate 0x9023 entry.

name: make_dptr_r4_minus_3
comment: One instruction, mov A,R4, with no ret; the bytes after it belong to the separate 0x9024 and 0x9026 entries. Read as one block from 0x9023 the sequence is A=R4, R6=R4, A=1, R7=1, A=R4-3, DPL=R7, DPH=A, ret, so entering at 0x9023 with R4=n leaves DPTR = ((n-3) << 8) | 0x01. No XDATA is touched. The .c's return of param_1-3 does not match these instructions.

name: make_dptr_a_minus_3
comment: mov R6,A then clr A, with no ret; the add A,#0x01 that follows is the separate 0x9026 entry. Read as one block from 0x9024 the sequence ends with R7=1, A=A-3, DPL=R7, DPH=A and ret, so entering here with A=n leaves DPTR = ((n-3) << 8) | 0x01 and R6=n. R6 is left holding n, which the 0x9026 and 0x9028 tails go on to use as the row index, and no XDATA is touched. The .c's return of param_1-3 does not match these instructions.

name: make_dptr_r6_minus_3_9026
comment: A single add A,#0x01 with no ret; the seven instructions that follow are the separate 0x9028 entry. Read as one block from 0x9026 the sequence is R7=A+1, A=R6, addc A,#0xfd, DPL=R7, DPH=A, ret, so with A=c and R6=r it leaves DPTR = ((r-3+carry) << 8) | (c+1), where the carry is the one the add produced. Unlike 0x9023 and 0x9024 the column byte is caller-supplied and reaches DPTR through R7, and no XDATA is touched. The .c's return of param_2-3 does not match this instruction.

name: make_dptr_r6_minus_3_9028
comment: Takes the column byte in A and the row index in R6 and returns DPTR = ((R6-3) << 8) | A: it moves A to R7, does mov A,R6 and addc A,#0xfd, then DPL=R7 and DPH=A, with the single ret at 0x9030. No XDATA is touched. The other entries in this region (0x9021, 0x9023, 0x9024, 0x9026, 0x9066, 0x906D, 0x9076, 0x9078, 0x907E) are the same idiom with a different fixed column byte or a different register holding it, which is why this one is entered with a caller-set R6. The .c's return of param_1-3 does not match these instructions.

name: make_dptr_a_minus_3_col_12
comment: Saves the caller's A into R5 and R6, sets R7=0, loads A=0x12 and continues into the separate 0x906D entry. Read as one block from 0x9066 the sequence ends with R3=0x12, DPL=R3, DPH=A and a ret, so entering with A=n leaves DPTR = ((n-3) << 8) | 0x12 with R5=n and R7=0. Here A is the row index and 0x12 the fixed column, the opposite of the 0x9028 arrangement, and no XDATA is touched. The .c's return of param_1-3 does not match these instructions.

name: make_dptr_r6_minus_3_col_r3
comment: Moves A to R3, does mov A,R6 and addc A,#0xfd, then DPL=R3, DPH=A and ret, leaving DPTR = ((R6-3) << 8) | A with the column byte held in R3 rather than in R7 as at 0x9028. No XDATA is touched. The .c's return of param_1-3 does not match these instructions.

name: read_byte_at_dptr_to_r1
comment: Two instructions, movx A,@DPTR and mov R1,A, with no ret: it reads one XDATA byte at whatever address the caller left in DPTR and puts it in R1. The bytes that follow, from mov R7,#0x00 through mov DPH,A and ret, are the separate 0x9078 entry, which reuses the same value as a row index to build DPTR = ((byte-3) << 8) | 0x14. The .c's return of *param_1-3 does not match these two instructions.

name: make_dptr_a_minus_3_col_14
comment: Sets R7=0, saves the caller's A into R6, loads A=0x14 and continues into the separate 0x907E entry. Read as one block from 0x9078 the sequence ends with R5=0x14, DPL=R5, DPH=A and a ret, so entering with A=n leaves DPTR = ((n-3) << 8) | 0x14 with R7=0. It is the 0x9066 idiom with column 0x14 instead of 0x12 and R5 in place of R3, and no XDATA is touched. The .c's return of param_1-3 does not match these instructions.

name: make_dptr_r6_minus_3_col_r5
comment: Moves A to R5, does mov A,R6 and addc A,#0xfd, then DPL=R5, DPH=A and ret, leaving DPTR = ((R6-3) << 8) | A with the column byte held in R5. It is the 0x9028 idiom with R5 in place of R7, and the 0x906D idiom with R5 in place of R3. No XDATA is touched. The .c's return of param_1-3 does not match these instructions.

name: read_and_increment_32bit
comment: Moves A into DPH, with DPL supplied by the caller, calls 0x0FAF to read the four XDATA bytes at that address into R4-R7, then adds 1 with the carry propagated through R7, R6, R5 and R4, so the 32-bit value in R4:R7 is incremented and left in those registers. The .c reports only the four-byte read and a return of the parameter; neither the increment nor the DPH store appears there.

name: read_bit0_of_08fc_row
comment: Computes DPTR = 0x08FC + A*0x5E by multiplying A by 0x5E in B:A and adding 0x08FC with carry, calls 0x0FAF to read the four bytes there into R4-R7, then masks bit 0 of R7 and clears R6 before the ret at 0x90B0. The observable result is R6:R7 holding the low bit of the byte at 0x08FF + A*0x5E, with R4 and R5 left holding the two bytes below it. The .c returns a constant 0 and loses both the masking and the 0x08FC base.

name: store_4bytes_at_0a86
comment: A single instruction, mov R3,#0xFF, with no ret; the mov DPTR,#0x0a86 and the call to 0x10E8 that follow are the separate 0x90B3 entry. Read as one block from 0x90B1 the sequence writes R3=0xFF to 0x0A86, R2 to 0x0A87 and R1 to 0x0A88 through 0x10E8, then clears the byte at 0x0A89 and returns. The .c models only the 0xFF and calls the store non-returning, which the ret after the 0x0A89 clear contradicts.

name: store_3bytes_at_0a86
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0A86 and calls 0x10E8 (store_3byte_r3r2r1), writing R3, R2 and R1 to 0x0A86, 0x0A87 and 0x0A88. The listing ends at that call with no ret, and the .c reports the call as non-returning; the bytes following it in the image, which are not part of this listing, clear the byte at 0x0A89 and ret. R3 is the caller's here, unlike 0x90B1 which forces it to 0xFF before the same store.

name: read_xdata_00b0_plus_r4
comment: Adds R4 to 0xB0: the low byte goes to DPL, and clr A followed by rlc A leaves exactly the carry from that add in DPH, so DPTR = 0x00B0 + R4 as a 16-bit sum. Reads the XDATA byte there and returns it in A. The listing does not show what R4 holds or what the block at 0x00B0 contains.

name: dph_plus_double_a_90cf
comment: Doubles A, adds the current DPH and writes the result back to DPH, leaving A at twice its input value. DPL and every other register are untouched and there is no memory access, so this adjusts only the high byte of a pointer the caller has already started. The C shows the same arithmetic with DPH passed in as a second argument.

name: read_table_08f4_step_5e_minus_1
comment: Forms the address 0x08F4 + 0x5E * A (B = 0x5E, mul AB, add 0xF4 into DPL, then clr A / addc A,0x08 into DPH), reads the XDATA byte there, and returns that byte minus one: setb CY / subb A,0x01 leaves the carry set when the byte read was 0x00. The table being indexed and the reason for the minus one are not decoded here. The C's address expression is the same computation, but the final subtraction does not appear in it.

name: read_xdata_r6_minus_3_low_a
comment: Saves the incoming A into R7, then computes A = R6 + 0xFD + CY (R6 - 3, or R6 - 2 when the caller's carry is set) and stores it back into R6. R7 becomes DPL and the decremented R6 becomes DPH, and the XDATA byte at that address is read and returned in A. The carry this consumes is the caller's, and nothing in the listing fixes what the low byte or the address base means.

name: set_dptr_0004_then_fall_through
comment: One instruction: DPTR = 0x0004. The listing has no ret, so control continues at 0x90F6, which calls 0x1253 and then jumps to 0x10C8; the C's call of 0x1253 with the argument 4 is its reading of that pointer. No lcall or ljmp to 0x90F3 or 0x90F6 appears in the exported PD disassembly, and neither 0x1253 nor 0x10C8 is decoded here.

name: call_1253_then_jump_10c8
comment: Calls 0x1253, then jumps rather than calls 0x10C8, so whatever 0x10C8 returns to goes straight back to this function's caller. No register is set up here, so both callees see whatever the caller left. The C's call to 0x10C8 is wrong on that point: an ljmp pushes no return address.

name: call_0c46_then_dptr_0d0e
comment: One instruction: lcall 0x0C46. The listing has no ret of its own, so the bytes exported separately as 0x90FF run next, loading DPTR = 0x0D0E and returning; a call to 0x90FC therefore runs 0x0C46 and hands its caller that pointer. What 0x0C46 does is not shown in this listing.

name: set_dptr_0d0e_90ff
comment: Loads DPH = 0x0D and DPL = 0x0E, so DPTR = 0x0D0E, and returns without touching A, B or any R register. It dereferences nothing: the only observable effect is the pointer left for the caller, which the C's empty body does not show. What lives at that XDATA address in this program is not decoded here.

name: read_xdata_0a2c_step_17
comment: Builds the address 0x0A2C + 0x17 * A (B = 0x17, mul AB, add 0x2C into DPL, then clr A / addc A,0x0A into DPH), reads that XDATA byte and returns it in A, leaving B at the high byte of the product. The array being indexed and the meaning of the stride are not decoded here. The C's pointer expression is the same address arithmetic.

name: read_dptr_to_r5_r6_zero_r7
comment: Reads the byte at the incoming DPTR into R5, copies the same byte into R6, sets R7 = 0x00 and returns A = 0. The pointer is not set here, so the address read is whatever the caller left in DPTR, and the C's bare return 0 shows none of the three register writes.

name: read_xdata_07ca_into_r6
comment: Loads DPTR = 0x07CA, reads that XDATA byte into R6 and returns A = 0. One address and one read, with no write; the C's return 0 is right about A but hides both the read and the R6 store. What the byte at 0x07CA holds is not decoded here.

name: dpl_090d_plus_5e_times_a
comment: Multiplies A by B = 0x5E, adds 0x0D and stores the low byte in DPL, then returns 0x09 plus the multiplication carry in A. There is no mov DPH,A here, unlike the same shape at 0x90D6, so the computed high byte is only returned and DPH is left as the caller had it. The C returns the carry expression and drops the DPL store.

name: dpl_0931_plus_5e_times_a
