comment: Multiplies A by B = 0x5E, adds 0x31 and stores the low byte in DPL, then returns 0x09 plus the multiplication carry in A. As at 0x9123 there is no mov DPH,A, so DPH is left untouched and only the high byte comes back in A. The C returns the carry expression and drops the DPL store.

name: dpl_0929_plus_5e_times_a
comment: Multiplies A by B = 0x5E, adds 0x29 and stores the low byte in DPL, then returns 0x09 plus the multiplication carry in A. As at 0x9123 and 0x912F there is no mov DPH,A, so DPH is left untouched and only the high byte comes back in A. The C returns the carry expression and drops the DPL store.

name: load_r5_then_write_via_915f
comment: One instruction: A = R5. The listing has no ret, so control continues at 0x915F, which writes that A to the XDATA byte at the incoming DPTR, sets R6 = R4 and returns A = 0x06. The C folds that whole sequence into this address and shows only a pointer store and the constant 6.

name: write_a_to_dptr_set_r6_r4_ret6
comment: Writes A to the XDATA byte at the incoming DPTR, then loads R6 from R4, clears A, adds 0x06 and returns, so the return value is the constant 0x06. Entered by falling through from 0x915E the byte written is R5. Nothing in the listing shows what the constant or the R6 = R4 copy is for.

name: read_xdata_07c9_into_r6
comment: Loads DPTR = 0x07C9, reads that XDATA byte into R6 and returns A = 0. Same shape as 0x911C with a different address; the C shows only the zero return. What the byte at 0x07C9 holds is not decoded here.

name: set_b60_dptr_04a3_tail_10bc
comment: Loads B = 0x60 and DPTR = 0x04A3, then jumps to 0x10BC (the address the export labels add_full_product_to_dptr) with no return of its own, so 0x10BC returns straight to this function's caller. A is left as the caller had it. What 0x10BC does with B and DPTR is not shown in this listing.

name: dptr_07d1_then_scale_via_96ed
comment: One instruction: DPTR = 0x07D1. The listing has no ret, so control continues at 0x96EB, which reads that byte into R7, and then at 0x96ED, which builds DPTR = 0x0A13 + 0x17 * R7 and returns the high byte in A. A call to this address therefore leaves DPTR at 0x0A13 + 0x17 * the byte at XDATA 0x07D1; what that structure holds is not decoded here.

name: read_dptr_to_r7_then_scale
comment: Reads the XDATA byte at the incoming DPTR into R7 and A, then, with no ret of its own, continues at 0x96ED, which multiplies that byte by 0x17, adds 0x13 into DPL and 0x0A plus the carry into DPH, so DPTR becomes 0x0A13 + 0x17 * the byte just read. R7 keeps the input byte, not the result, and the address built is not dereferenced in this sequence. The C's pointer parameter is its rendering of that movx read; the DPL and DPH stores do not appear in it.

name: dptr_0a13_plus_17_times_a
comment: Multiplies the byte in A by B = 0x17, adds 0x13 to the low byte into DPL and 0x0A plus the multiplication carry into DPH, then returns, leaving DPTR = 0x0A13 + 0x17 * A and A holding the high byte of that address. No memory is touched: the pointer it builds is dereferenced by the caller. The C returns the high-byte expression and drops both pointer stores.

name: dptr_0819_then_scale_via_96ff
comment: One instruction: DPTR = 0x0819. The listing has no ret, so control continues at 0x96FE, which reads that byte into A, and then at 0x96FF, which builds DPTR = 0x0A27 + 0x17 * A and returns the high byte in A. A call to this address therefore leaves DPTR at 0x0A27 + 0x17 * the byte at XDATA 0x0819; neither that byte nor the structure it indexes is decoded here.

name: read_dptr_to_a_then_scale
comment: Reads the XDATA byte at the incoming DPTR into A, then, with no ret of its own, continues at 0x96FF, which sets DPTR = 0x0A27 + 0x17 * A and returns that address's high byte in A. R7 is left alone, unlike the sibling entry at 0x96EB. The C renders the multiply over a pointer parameter and shows neither the DPL nor the DPH store.

name: dptr_0a27_plus_17_times_a
comment: Multiplies A by B = 0x17, adds 0x27 to the low byte into DPL and 0x0A plus the carry into DPH, then returns, so DPTR = 0x0A27 + 0x17 * A and A ends holding the high byte of that address. No memory access. The C returns the high-byte expression alone and drops both pointer stores.

name: zero_xdata_0a14_step_17
comment: Builds the address 0x0A14 + 0x17 * A (B = 0x17, mul AB, add 0x14 into DPL, then 0x0A plus the carry into DPH) and clears A, but has no ret of its own: control continues at 0x971B, which writes that zero to the XDATA byte at the address just built, and then at 0x971C, which sets DPTR = 0x0A15 + 0x17 * R7. So a call here clears one XDATA byte and returns with a second pointer in DPTR, built from R7 rather than from A. The C shows the store and a second carry expression without that distinction.

name: write_a_to_dptr
comment: Writes the current A to the XDATA byte at DPTR: a single instruction, with no ret, so control continues at 0x971C, which replaces A with R7 and builds DPTR = 0x0A15 + 0x17 * R7 before returning. Entered by falling through from 0x970D, the value stored is the zero that address cleared A to. The C's pointer parameter is its reading of the DPTR write, and it shows neither the fall-through nor R7 as the index.

name: dptr_0a15_plus_17_times_r7
comment: Takes the byte in R7, multiplies it by B = 0x17, adds 0x15 to the low byte into DPL and 0x0A plus the carry into DPH, then returns, leaving DPTR = 0x0A15 + 0x17 * R7 and A holding the high byte of that address. No memory access. The C's first parameter is the same multiply with R7 passed in as an argument.

name: dptr_07d4_then_fall_through
comment: One instruction: DPTR = 0x07D4. The listing has no ret, so control continues at 0x972E, which loads R0 to R3 with 0x04, 0x05, 0x06 and 0x07, reads that XDATA byte, multiplies it by B = 0x17 and returns the product in A with the high byte in B. The C's DAT_EXTMEM_07d4 * 0x17 is that product, but it shows neither the read nor the four register loads.

name: load_r0_r3_then_read_dptr_times_17
comment: Loads R0 = 0x04, R1 = 0x05, R2 = 0x06 and R3 = 0x07, reads the XDATA byte at the incoming DPTR, multiplies it by B = 0x17 and returns the product in A with the high byte in B. The pointer is not set here, so the address multiplied is the caller's; entered from 0x972B it is 0x07D4. The C's *param_1 * 0x17 is the same product with the movx read written as a pointer dereference and the four register loads dropped.

name: dptr_07d1_then_tail_0faf
comment: Loads DPTR = 0x07D1 and reads that XDATA byte into A, then, with no ret of its own, continues at 0x9740, which multiplies the byte by B = 0x5E, adds 0xFC into DPL and 0x08 plus the carry into DPH, and jumps to 0x0FAF (the address the export labels read4xdata_to_r4_r7). A call here therefore passes 0x08FC + 0x5E * the byte at XDATA 0x07D1 as the pointer in DPTR, and control does not come back through 0x973C. What 0x0FAF then reads is not shown in this listing.

name: dptr_from_a_mul_5e_add_fc_tail_jump_0faf
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by 0x5E, adds 0xFC, stores the low byte in DPL and 0x08 plus the add's carry in DPH, so DPTR lands in the 256-byte window 0x08FC-0x09FB; the high byte of the product is discarded. It then tail-jumps to 0x0FAF, which is not decoded here. The .c names that target read4xdata_to_r4_r7, which is where DPTR is passed.

name: load_a_from_r7_9750
comment: One instruction, mov A,R7, with no ret; the listing ends at 0x9751 where a separate Ghidra entry begins. The .c body here is byte-for-byte the same text as 9751.c, 9764.c, 9768.c, 9772.c and 97F3.c, so it is boilerplate in this region and does not describe these bytes. Whether this is a whole entry or a function-boundary artefact is not determinable here.

name: dptr_from_a_mul_17_add_29
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by 0x17, adds 0x29, stores the low byte in DPL and 0x0A plus the add's carry in DPH, leaving DPTR within 0x0A00-0x0BFF. The high byte of the product is discarded and nothing dereferences DPTR; at the ret A holds the byte written to DPH, 0x0A or 0x0B.

name: read_xdata_07d4_into_r3
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x07D4, reads that byte from XDATA and copies it to R3. The listing is three instructions, has no ret, and stops at 0x9764 where a separate entry begins, so nothing after the copy is shown.

name: dptr_from_a_mul_17_add_17_first_half
comment: Loads B with 0x17 and executes mul AB, leaving the low product byte in A; the high byte is discarded. The listing ends at 0x9768, where a separate entry holds the rest of the same sequence (add A,#0x17 through ret), so this entry covers only the first two instructions of one address computation.

name: dptr_from_a_add_17_second_half
comment: Adds 0x17 to the product byte left in A by the entry at 0x9764, stores it in DPL, then computes A = 0x0A + carry and stores that in DPH before returning. The entry begins mid-sequence, at the add rather than at the mul, and no address is dereferenced before the ret.

name: read_xdata_07d4_into_a
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x07D4 and reads the byte at that XDATA address into A. The listing is two instructions, has no ret, and stops at 0x9776 where a separate entry begins. The .c body is the same region-wide boilerplate seen at 9750.c and does not correspond to these two instructions.

name: dptr_from_a_mul_17_add_1b
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by 0x17, adds 0x1B, stores the low byte in DPL and 0x0A plus the add's carry in DPH, leaving DPTR within 0x0A00-0x0BFF. The high byte of the product is discarded and DPTR is not dereferenced; at the ret A holds the DPH value.

name: call_0faf_0f00_0dbc_then_r3_23
comment: Stores A into DPH, then calls 0x0FAF, 0x0F00 and 0x0DBC in that order, clears A and loads R3 with 0x23. The entry starts mid-sequence -- its DPL is set by instructions not in this listing -- and has no ret, so what this address is for is not determinable here. The .c shows the same three calls in the same order.

name: clr_carry
comment: A single clr CY with no ret; the listing ends at 0x9793 where a separate entry begins. That entry copies A into R2, R1 and R0 and tail-jumps to 0x0F0E, so this instruction is the carry-clearing preamble of the same sequence, but the two halves are not separately callable and neither returns.

name: copy_a_to_r0_r1_r2_tail_jump_0f0e
comment: Copies A into R2, R1 and R0 in turn, then tail-jumps to 0x0F0E rather than returning to its own caller. The entry begins at 0x9793 with the carry already cleared by the single clr CY listed at 0x9792. 0x0F0E is not decoded here.

name: load_a_from_r7_9799
comment: One instruction, mov A,R7, with no ret; the listing ends at 0x979A where a separate entry begins and which is itself complete, ending in its own ret. The .c here describes the 0x979A block instead and so does not describe this byte. Whether this is a whole entry or a function-boundary artefact is not determinable here.

name: read_xdata_table_byte_idx_a_mul_17_add_14
comment: Multiplies the accumulator -- loaded from R7 by the entry at 0x9799 -- by 0x17, adds 0x14, builds DPTR from 0x0A00 plus the low sum and its carry, then reads the byte at that XDATA address into A and returns. The high byte of the product is discarded, so the address reached is confined to 0x0A00-0x0BFF.

name: dptr_from_a_mul_17_add_2c
comment: Loads A from R7, multiplies by 0x17, adds 0x2C, stores the low byte in DPL and 0x0A plus the add's carry in DPH, and returns without ever dereferencing DPTR. The high byte of the product is discarded, so the caller has to use DPTR for the result; A holds 0x0A or 0x0B on return.

name: load_a_from_r7_97b8
comment: One instruction, mov A,R7, with no ret; the listing ends at 0x97B9 where a separate entry begins and which is itself complete, ending in its own ret. The .c here reproduces the 0x97B9 block instead and so does not describe this byte. Whether this is a whole entry or a function-boundary artefact is not determinable here.

name: read_xdata_byte_at_r4_minus_3_page_01
comment: Saves A to R4, computes 1 into R5 with clr A / add A,#0x01, which also clears the carry, then sets A = R4 - 3 via addc A,#0xFD and forms DPTR with DPL = R5 = 0x01 and DPH = that byte. It reads the byte at DPTR into A and returns, so the address reached is ((R4-3) << 8) | 0x01, one byte into a page selected by R4.

name: dptr_page_sel_from_r6_minus_3_first_half
comment: Saves the incoming A to R6, then computes A = 1 via clr A / add A,#0x01, which also clears the carry. The listing stops at 0x97CB, where a separate entry holds the rest of the same sequence (mov R7,A, the addc, the DPL/DPH stores, the read and the ret), so this entry covers only the first three instructions.

name: read_xdata_byte_at_r6_minus_3_page_01
comment: Takes the 1 that 0x97C7 left in A into R7, restores A to R6, adds 0xFD with the carry clear to give R6 - 3, and forms DPTR with DPL = R7 = 0x01 and DPH = R6 - 3, then reads the byte at DPTR into A and returns. The address reached is ((R6-3) << 8) | 0x01.

name: dptr_from_a_mul_5e_add_04_tail_jump_0faf
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by 0x5E, adds 0x04, stores the low byte in DPL and 0x09 plus the add's carry in DPH, so DPTR lands in the 256-byte window 0x0904-0x0A03, discarding the high byte of the product. It then tail-jumps to 0x0FAF, which is not decoded here; the .c names that target read4xdata_to_r4_r7.

name: test_r7_bit_5
comment: Loads A from R7 and masks it with 0x20, leaving 0x20 if bit 5 was set and 0x00 otherwise. The listing is two instructions, has no ret, and stops at 0x97E8 where a separate entry begins, so whether these two instructions are the whole entry is not determinable here. The .c agrees with them.

name: clear_r4_r5_r6_return_a
comment: Saves the incoming A to R7, clears A and stores 0 into R6, R5 and R4 in turn, then reloads A from R7 and returns, so the entry returns its argument byte and leaves R4, R5 and R6 zero. The .c reports only the returned byte and omits the three register clears.

name: dptr_from_a_mul_17_add_23_first_half
comment: Loads B with 0x17 and executes mul AB, leaving the low product byte in A; the high byte is discarded. The listing ends at 0x97F3, where a separate entry holds the rest of the same sequence (add A,#0x23 through ret), so this entry covers only the first two instructions.

name: dptr_low_from_a_add_23_no_dph_store
comment: Adds 0x23 to the product byte left in A by 0x97EF, stores the result in DPL, then computes A = 0x0A + carry and returns. Unlike the other entries that build a 0x0A00-based address, this one never executes mov DPH,A, so the high address byte keeps whatever value it held on entry and DPTR is only half-formed. The .c does not show the missing DPH store.

name: dptr_from_a_mul_17_add_28
comment: Loads A from R7, multiplies by 0x17, adds 0x28, stores the low byte in DPL and 0x0A plus the add's carry in DPH, and returns without dereferencing DPTR. The high byte of the product is discarded, so the address reached is confined to 0x0A00-0x0BFF; A holds 0x0A or 0x0B on return.

name: call_0faf_0f00_0dbc_return_zero
comment: Calls 0x0FAF, 0x0F00 and 0x0DBC in that order, clears A and returns, so the entry's result is always 0. The return value of each call is discarded. The .c agrees with these five instructions.

name: call_0bc4_keep_result_in_r7
comment: Calls 0x0BC4 and saves the returned byte in R7. The listing is two instructions, has no ret, and stops at 0x984D where a separate entry begins; the .c here additionally contains the call listed at 0x984D and the DPTR/tail-jump listed at 0x9850, so it describes the chain rather than these two instructions alone. What this address is for is not determinable here.

name: call_0eeae
comment: A single lcall 0xEEAE with no ret; the listing ends at 0x9850, where a separate entry loads DPTR with 0xD9EF and tail-jumps to 0x10F1. The .c here shows both that call and that tail-jump, so it describes the chain rather than this one instruction. Neither 0x0BC4 nor 0x0EEAE is decoded here.

name: load_dptr_d9ef_tail_jump_10f1
comment: Loads DPTR with 0xD9EF and tail-jumps to 0x10F1, passing the address in DPTR rather than in a register. The .c names 0x10F1 and shows the same DPTR argument, but that target is not decoded here, so what it does with 0xD9EF is not established.

name: call_0d8f_write_00_04_to_07da_07db
comment: Calls 0x0D8F, then clears A, loads DPTR with 0x07DA, writes 0x00 there, increments DPTR to 0x07DB and writes 0x04, and finally loads R5, R6 and R7 with 0 before returning. These are addresses in the PD image's own XDATA space, which is separate from the EC firmware's map, so no EC register is implied by them. The .c shows the call and the two XDATA writes but omits the three register clears.

name: read_xdata_byte_to_r7
comment: Reads the byte at the address the caller left in DPTR and copies it into both A and R7. The listing is two instructions with no ret; the *param_1 * 2 the C reports is its reading of the whole routine, whose multiply and DPTR write are in the entries at 0x9885 and 0x9888.

name: set_multiplier_2
comment: One instruction, mov B,#0x2, which supplies the multiplier for the MUL AB in the next entry. The listing has no ret of its own and the bytes run straight into 0x9888, so this looks like one routine cut in two.

name: mul_ab_into_dptr
comment: Multiplies A by B, stores the 16-bit product in DPTR -- low byte to DPL, high byte to DPH -- and returns. The C reports a char multiplication and drops both the DPTR write and the high byte, so the product left in DPTR is the only visible result of these instructions.

name: load_dptr_07d0
comment: One instruction: DPTR = 0x07D0, the address the read in the next entry (0x98A4) is made from. That 0x07D0 is the ITE8850-PD image's own XDATA, not the EC's: ec/annotations/registers.yaml records all 254 of its sites for that address in the PD image and none in the EC firmware, so this listing is not evidence about the EC byte of the same address.

name: read_xdata_byte
comment: A single movx A,@DPTR, reading the byte at 0x07D0 -- the address loaded by the entry at 0x98A1, and the PD image's own byte, not the EC's (ec/annotations/registers.yaml). The multiply the C prints belongs to the next entry.

name: mul_by_0c_return_r6r7
comment: Loads B with 0x0C, multiplies the accumulator, and returns the 16-bit product in R6 (high) : R7 (low). The accumulator is the byte read at 0x98A4. The C returns a single char and loses the high byte held in R6.

name: call_0d8f_then_take_r7
comment: Calls 0x0D8F, which is not decoded in this file pair, then moves R7 into the accumulator; the listing stops at 0x98B0, where the +1 and the shared tail the C prints continue. R7 is whatever the call left, so what this routine goes on to divide is not fixed by these two instructions.

name: inc_r7_carry_to_r6_setup_0005
comment: Adds 1 to R7 and keeps the carry out of that add in R6 -- clr A leaves CY alone, so rlc A yields exactly the carry. Loads R4 = 0x00 and R5 = 0x05 and tail-jumps to 0x0C8C, handing it R7, R6 and that divisor pair; 0x0C8C is not decoded in this file pair. The C prints the same 0,5 constants plus a 0xFE-carry test that no instruction here contains.

name: load_dptr_0004
comment: One instruction: DPTR = 0x0004, the address still in place when the routine tail-jumps to 0x0BC4 from the next entry (0x98C1). Nothing is read or written here, and 0x0BC4 is not decoded in this file pair, so what the constant addresses is not determined.

name: add_r6r7_to_r1r2_tail_0bc4
comment: Adds the 16-bit pair R6:R7 into R1:R2 -- R1 += R7, then R2 += R6 with the carry -- and tail-jumps to 0x0BC4 with the DPTR loaded at 0x98BE. No memory access happens in these instructions. The C's three arguments and its carry-shift expression are not in the listing; what is handed over is the register pair itself.

name: store_a_to_r2
comment: One instruction: A into R2, the high byte of the 16-bit pair this routine returns. The listing has no ret and runs straight into 0x98E0, which completes the arithmetic. The C's subtraction with a carry shift is not in these bytes.

name: add_5_to_r2r1
comment: Adds 5 to the 16-bit value in R2:R1, R1 being the low byte: R1 += 5, then clr A / addc A,R2 leaves R2 holding R2 plus the carry, and the pair is returned. The C reads the same bytes as a subtraction, so the listing is what this row follows.

name: pass_r6_and_a_to_0d70
comment: Copies the accumulator into R7, loads the accumulator from R6 and B from R7, then tail-jumps to 0x0D70, so that callee is entered with B:A holding the old accumulator in B and the old R6 in A. Nothing is read from memory and 0x0D70 is not decoded in this file pair. The C's two parameters are its own reconstruction of that register shuffle.

name: dptr_001d_tail_0d38
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x001D and tail-jumps to 0x0D38 with no other work, so the whole routine is an argument setup for that callee. The C shows the same thing as a call carrying 0x1D. 0x0D38 is not decoded in this file pair, so what it does with the address is not determined.

name: dptr_0011_tail_0d8f
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0011 and tail-jumps to 0x0D8F -- the same callee the entry at 0x98AD calls -- with a different constant. The C shows a call carrying 0x11. 0x0D8F is not decoded in this file pair.

name: dptr_001f_return_a0_b2
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x001F, clears the accumulator, loads B with 0x02 and returns. Neither clr A nor mov B,#0x02 touches the carry flag, so the CY handed back is the one the caller arrived with. The C reports only the 0 returned in A and drops both the B load and the address.

name: add_r6r7_to_r1r2_tail_0c58
comment: Adds the 16-bit pair R6:R7 into R1:R2 -- R1 += R7, then R2 += R6 with the carry -- copies R5 into the accumulator and tail-jumps to 0x0C58, which is not decoded in this file pair. Same 16-bit add as the entry at 0x98C1 with a different tail target; the C's four arguments and carry-shift expression are not in the listing.

name: call_10fd_then_dptr_0007
comment: Calls 0x10FD with R0-R7 passed through unchanged, then loads DPTR with 0x0007 and returns without loading A, so the returned value is whatever the call left there. 0x10FD is not decoded in this file pair. The C shows the call and drops the DPTR load.

name: dptr_0021_tail_0c58
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0021 and tail-jumps to 0x0C58, the same tail as the entry at 0x9936, with a different constant. The C shows a call carrying 0x21. 0x0C58 is not decoded in this file pair.

name: dptr_0010_tail_0c58
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0010 and tail-jumps to 0x0C58. Two instructions, no ret of its own, no other register touched. The C shows a call carrying 0x10.

name: call_10fd_dptr_0004_tail_0bc4
comment: Calls 0x10FD, loads DPTR with 0x0004 and tail-jumps to 0x0BC4. Neither 0x10FD nor 0x0BC4 is decoded in this file pair, so what the call does and what the 0x0004 base addresses are not determined here. The C shows both calls but not the DPTR load.

name: load_a_from_r7_9987
comment: One instruction: A = R7, the first operand of the multiplication whose other operand the next entry loads. The listing has no ret and the C's call to a routine the export names add_full_product_to_dptr is not in these two bytes, nor is that routine decoded in this file pair.

name: set_multiplier_60
comment: One instruction: B = 0x60. No multiply, store or ret appears here; the C for these two entries shows a call to a routine the export names add_full_product_to_dptr, which is not in this listing, so what the loaded multiplier is used for is not determined from these bytes.

name: dbl_a_add_dph_write_dph
comment: Doubles the accumulator, adds DPH to it and writes the result back to DPH, returning the new DPH in A. DPL and every other register are untouched and no memory is accessed, so the routine's only visible effect is on the high byte of a pointer the caller has already started. The C reports the same arithmetic as a return value and drops the write to DPH.

name: add_r5_to_dptr
comment: Adds the single byte in R5 to the 16-bit DPTR: DPL += R5, then clr A / addc A,DPH leaves DPH holding DPH plus the carry. Only one byte of R5 is used, so the addend is zero-extended. The C prints a subtraction with a carry shift, which is not in this listing.

name: read_xdata_inc_r7_carry_r6_tail_0c8c
comment: Reads the byte at DPTR and adds 1 to it, leaving the incremented byte in R7 and the carry out of that add in R6, so R6 is 1 only when the byte read was 0xFF. Loads R4 = 0x00 and R5 = 0x06 and tail-jumps to 0x0C8C with those four registers; 0x0C8C is not decoded in this file pair. The C prints the increment and the 0,6 pair, plus a 0xFE-carry test that no instruction here contains.

name: a_r3_b_60_tail_10bc
comment: Loads A from R3 and B with 0x60, then tail-jumps to 0x10BC without a ret of its own, so those two registers are the operands the callee is entered with. The C prints that as a non-returning call to a routine the export names add_full_product_to_dptr. The file header records that this boundary came from a call-target byte scan, an upper bound, so these three instructions may not be the whole routine.

name: load_a_from_r7_stub
comment: One instruction: A = R7, and the listing has no ret. The next entry (0x9A91) loads B with 0x60 and DPTR with 0x04A4 and then returns without using any of the three, so what this stub is for is not determinable from these two listings. The file header records the boundary as a hypothesis from a call-target byte scan, so it may not be a whole routine either.

name: set_b_60_dptr_04a4_then_ret
comment: Loads B with 0x60 and DPTR with 0x04A4 and returns, with no read, no write and no call: the A that 0x9A90 loaded from R7 and both constants are simply handed back to the caller. Nothing in these two listings says what that is for, so the role is not determined. 0x04A4 is the PD image's own XDATA and has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: dptr_add_0d0e_via_122f
comment: Loads DPTR with 0xFFFF and calls 0x122F, which adds the direct-RAM pair 0x0D:0x0E to DPTR (leaving 0x0D0D) and copies the resulting low byte into the direct address 0x0E before returning. The listing holds no return instruction of its own, so how control leaves 0x9ACD after that call is not shown here; the decompiled C's 'subroutine does not return' warning is Ghidra's, and 0x122F's own listing has three returns.

name: set_dptr_0d0e_9add
comment: Loads DPH with 0x0D and DPL with 0x0E, i.e. sets DPTR to the constant 0x0D0E, and returns. Nothing in these two instructions shows what that address pair is for, so the role is left open; the decompiled C renders the body as a bare return, which drops both stores.

name: set_b_67
comment: One instruction, mov B,#0x67, which sets the multiplier register and then runs straight into the next function entry at 0x9C1B (this listing is three bytes, ending 0x9C1A with no ret). No MUL AB follows inside this listing, and the same 0x67 constant appears in the neighbouring entries 0x9C45, 0x9CFB and 0x9D39, so what it selects is not determined here.

name: read_xdata_to_r6_set_dptr_069a
comment: Reads the byte at @DPTR into A, copies it to R6, then sets DPTR to 0x069A and B to 0x67. The listing is eight bytes ending 0x9C4C with no ret and the next function entry is 0x9C4D, so this is one routine cut in two; the decompiled C's call to add_full_product_to_dptr is not what these bytes do.

name: load_1byte_to_r6
comment: 1-byte load, returned in R6, leaving 0x67 in B. Reached by lcall from the 0x8F94 site. The 0x67 is recorded as the instruction's literal, not as a decoded unit

name: read_xdata_to_r7_set_dptr_066c
comment: Reads the byte at @DPTR into A, copies it to R7, sets B to 0x67 and DPTR to 0x066C, then returns. The decompiled C reports only the byte read, dropping the B and DPTR stores that the instructions perform.

name: set_b_67_dptr_066e
comment: Sets B to 0x67 and DPTR to 0x066E, then returns. No memory is touched and no other value is examined, so what this pair of constants selects is not determinable from this listing; the decompiled C renders it as a bare return.

name: stash_args_dispatch_code_table
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x0A69, R5 to 0x0A6A and R2/R3 to 0x0A6B/0x0A6C, then calls 0x119C, which pops the return address into DPTR and jumps through a code-space table, so control does not come back to 0xA34E. The bytes between 0xA34E and 0xA36D in this listing are therefore not a fall-through path and are not decoded further; the decompiled C's calls to 0xA000, 0xA5B3 and 0xE757 sit inside that region. The block at 0xA435 reloads R2/R3 from XDATA 0x0A6B/0x0A6C, reads the four bytes at 0x0A6D with 0x0FAF into R4..R7, writes them to XDATA 0x0836 with 0x1041, reloads R5/R7 from 0x0A6A/0x0A69 and tail-jumps to 0x4C27.

name: dispatch_on_state_07d0
comment: Reads XDATA 0x07D0: if the byte is zero it calls 0x98A5, 0x9850 and 0x98C1 and stores 0x98C1's return value in XDATA 0x07D1, and if that byte then compares equal to the value 0x98BE returns it tail-jumps to 0xA678, which increments 0x07D0 and re-enters this address. If the byte is non-zero it tail-jumps to 0xA681 instead, which clears R7 and returns. Otherwise it calls 0x98E0, 0x9885 and 0x0D38 and tests the A|B result of that 16-bit read. The listing stops at 0xA5B0 mid-sequence (0xA5B1..0xA5B2 are not shown), and the longer body the decompiled C renders starts at 0xA5B4, which is listed under 0xA5B3. registers.yaml's 0x07D0 row names it from the EC side and records that all of its references in this PD image belong to a different program's XDATA, so no EC meaning is carried over.

name: and_16bit_fields_write_07d2_07d3
comment: Adds R6:R7 into R2:R1 (R1 the low byte, 0x98DF continues the call), then ANDs the 16-bit value returned by 0x0D38 with the one returned by 0x991A into R6 and R7 and stores them to XDATA 0x07D2 and XDATA 0x07D3. If either of those two bytes is non-zero it increments the byte at XDATA 0x07D0, passes it through 0x996F, 0x9920 and 0x9975 to build ((R7 & 0x7F) << 1) | (0x9975 result & 1) and stores that to XDATA 0x0004, writes 5 to XDATA 0x0021, then calls 0xEEAE three times with the 0x9975 result rotated right one bit and with the bytes at 0x07D2 and 0x07D3, and returns R7 = 1. If both bytes are zero it writes R5 to XDATA 0x07D1 and tail-jumps back to 0xA58F, the loop body of 0xA571. The entry itself is questionable: the byte at 0xA5B3 (0x6C, XRL A,R4) is the last byte of the ljmp 0xA66C that begins at 0xA5B1, so the code proper starts at 0xA5B4. registers.yaml's 0x07D0/0x07D1 row is an EC-side name not carried over to this image's XDATA.

name: inc_07d0_reenter_a571
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA 0x07D0, adds 1 to it, writes it back and tail-jumps to 0xA571, so it is that routine's back edge over this byte. registers.yaml records 0x07D0 as an EC address whose 254 references all lie in this PD image and says nothing is established about its EC-side meaning, so none is claimed here.

name: zero_r7_return
comment: Sets R7 to 0 and returns. It is the tail-call target of 0xA571 for the case where the byte at XDATA 0x07D0 is not zero, but nothing else appears in this three-byte listing, so what the cleared R7 is for is not determinable here. registers.yaml's 0x07D0 row is an EC-side name whose sites in this image it attributes to a different program's XDATA.

name: load_dptr_be16_from_0abf
comment: Reads XDATA 0x0ABF into R6 and XDATA 0x0AC0 into DPL, copies R6 into DPH and tail-jumps to 0x0FBB, i.e. it hands the big-endian 16-bit value stored at 0x0ABF to that routine as DPTR. The decompiled C's argument rendering of the same two bytes is correct here. Neither the two bytes it reads nor 0x0FBB is described in any annotation, and the routine it jumps to is not decoded here.

name: shift_r4_r7_right_then_sub_0x30
comment: Calls 0x0F1F, which shifts the 32-bit value in R4..R7 (R4 most significant, R7 least) right by the R0 count the caller left, then adds 0xFFFFFFD0 to R4..R7 with R7 as the low byte, i.e. subtracts 0x30 from that same 32-bit value. Returns with the adjusted value still in R4..R7; no memory is touched and the decompiled C's carry algebra is a restatement of the same add/adc chain.

name: ascii_string_not_code
comment: The thirteen bytes at this address are printable ASCII (the tail "r 3", NUL, "Set Ver 2") in a run of NUL-terminated strings that continues with "Prover:0" at 0xA89D, so this address holds data, not instructions. The decompiled C built from it is an artefact of decoding the string as code (it even reports an unreachable block at 0xB058) and is not a reading of any function; nothing is decoded further.

name: event_dispatch_ff80_ffe0
comment: Clears IE.7, the global interrupt enable, at bit address 0xAF, on entry and sets it again at 0xA9BE, so the body runs with interrupts masked, and dispatches on bits of 0xFF80. Bit 7 of 0xFF80 with bit 3 of 0xFFE0 writes 8 to 0xFFE0, adds 0x00D3 to 0x0208 and 0x0209, calls 0xEA67 and writes 0x00D5 to 0xFFD0 and 0x00D4 to 0xFFD1; bit 2 of 0xFFE0 with bit 2 of 0xFFE1 clear calls 0xF5D1, sets bit 2 of 0xFFE1 and writes 4 to 0xFFE0. Bits 5, 0 and 1 of 0xFF80 write 0x40 to 0xFFE0 or call 0xF786 or 0xF7B4, and bit 3 gates a five-way test of 0xFFE2: 0x98, 0x84, 0x88 or 0xA0 writes 0x5A to 0x020A; 0xBC clears 0x00BD from 0x00BC and calls 0xF5D1 if zero; 0xBE with 0x00BE == 0x55 writes 1 to 0x0AE8; 0xE2 calls 0xF477. 0xFFE0 ends at 0x10. Every 0xFFxx address here is XDATA by encoding and not by spelling (#181); none is in registers.yaml. [Corrected in place, issue #181, the wrong version left visible: it read "PSW.EA (direct address 0xAF)" and "the pattern of an interrupt routine". 0xAF is a bit address and the bit is IE.7 (`CLR bit` / `SETB bit`), and the last instruction is `ret` (0x22) not `reti` (0x32), so this masks interrupts rather than being a vector. pd-xdata-overlap.md 5.3.1.]

name: build_masked_indexed_table_bytes
comment: Stores R7 in XDATA 0x07D7, calls 0xE458 and reads the byte back, and from then on addresses bytes through 0x9028, 0x906D, 0x907E, 0x9066 and 0x909A, each of which loads DPTR with (R6 - 3 + carry) as the high byte and the index passed in A as the low byte. It writes 0xFF, 0x20, 0x4B or 0x44 to, or masks with 0xFC, 0xF7 or 0xEF, the byte those indices select, with the indices built from XDATA 0x07D7 as 0, 4, 5, 6, 0x13, 0x15, 0x63 and 0x64. A four-byte read at XDATA 0x08FC + X*0x5E through 0x0FAF is reduced to its low bit for the branches, which also call 0xEC5E (twice), 0xB8DB and 0xBBE7; the routine ends with a ret. The decompiled C's arithmetic on *param_1 is Ghidra's misreading of the index expressions, not a different code path.

name: load_r0_r3_4_5_6_7
comment: Loads R0 with 0x04, R1 with 0x05, R2 with 0x06 and R3 with 0x07. The listing is eight bytes ending 0xACBE with no ret and runs straight into the next function entry at 0xACBF, so the code these four constants feed is not shown here; the decompiled C's comparison against 0xCA is Ghidra's reading of the entry at 0xACC0, not of these bytes.

name: read_xdata_at_dptr_acbf
comment: One instruction, movx A,@DPTR, which reads the byte at the caller's DPTR into A. The listing has no ret and the next function entry is 0xACC0, which multiplies A by 0x17 to form a DPTR, so this is the read half of one routine cut in two; the decompiled C's multiply and compare belong to that next entry.

name: index_a_by_23_add_0a35
comment: Multiplies A by 0x17, adds 0x35 to the low byte, computes the high byte as 0x0A plus the carry and loads DPTR, i.e. DPTR = 0x0A35 + A*0x17, then returns. The XDATA table that address indexes is not described in any annotation. This entry is the tail of the sequence begun at 0xACB7 (the R0..R3 loads) and 0xACBF (the read).

name: set_dptr_07d6
comment: One instruction, mov DPTR,#0x07D6. The listing ends there with no ret and the next function entry is 0xACD1, so the read and the table index that use this pointer are listed separately; the decompiled C's comparison against 0xD3 is the 0xACD3 entry's arithmetic, not this one's.

name: read_xdata_to_a_r7
comment: Reads the byte at @DPTR into A and copies it to R7. The listing is two bytes ending 0xACD2 with no ret and the next function entry is 0xACD3, which turns A into the address 0x0A2C + A*0x17, so the two entries are one sequence Ghidra has cut in two.

name: index_a_by_23_add_0a2c
comment: Multiplies A by 0x17, adds 0x2C to the low byte, computes the high byte as 0x0A plus the carry and loads DPTR, i.e. DPTR = 0x0A2C + A*0x17, then returns. It has the same shape as the entries at 0xACC0 (base 0x0A35) and 0xACE6 (base 0x0A2D); none of those tables is described in any annotation, and the decompiled C reports the multiply without the DPTR it produces.

name: set_dptr_07d1
comment: One instruction, mov DPTR,#0x07D1. The listing has no ret and the next function entry is 0xACE4, so what is done with the byte at 0x07D1 is not shown here. registers.yaml names 0x07D0/0x07D1 as the EC-side DSDT fields DBD1/DBD2 and records that references in the ITE8850-PD image are a different program's XDATA, so that name is not carried over.

name: read_xdata_to_r3
comment: Reads the byte at @DPTR into A and copies it to R3. The listing is two bytes ending 0xACE5 with no ret and the next function entry is 0xACE6, which turns A into DPTR = 0x0A2D + A*0x17, so this is the read half of that split sequence.

name: index_a_by_23_add_0a2d
comment: Multiplies A by 0x17, adds 0x2D to the low byte, computes the high byte as 0x0A plus the carry and loads DPTR, i.e. DPTR = 0x0A2D + A*0x17, then returns. Same shape as 0xACC0 (base 0x0A35) and 0xACD3 (base 0x0A2C), all three with a 0x17 stride; none of these tables is described in any annotation.

name: write_r7_to_dptr
comment: Copies R7 into A and writes it to @DPTR. The listing is two bytes ending 0xACF5 with no ret and the next function entry is 0xACF6, which computes DPTR = 0x08FC + A*0x5E, so the address stored to is whatever the caller left and this is the store half of that sequence; the decompiled C's read4xdata call and & 1 belong to the following entries.

name: index_a_by_5e_add_08fc
comment: Multiplies A by 0x5E, adds 0xFC to the low byte and computes the high byte as 0x08 plus the carry, i.e. preparing DPTR = 0x08FC + A*0x5E, the same 0x5E-stride table the entry at 0x909A walks. The listing stops at 0xACFF with no store to DPH and no ret, and the next entry is 0xAD01, so the completion of that address is not shown here.

name: read4xdata_bit0_to_a
comment: Loads DPH from A, calls 0x0FAF, which reads the four bytes at DPTR into R4..R7, and takes bit 0 of the fourth of those bytes into A. The listing ends at 0xAD07 with no ret, so whether the result is also copied to R7 is not shown here; it is the tail of the address sequence begun at 0xACF6.

name: zero_extend_a_into_r4_r7
comment: Takes the incoming A, copies it to R7, clears R6, R5 and R4, then reloads A from R7 and returns. The result is a four-byte value in R4:R7 whose only non-zero byte is R7, with A equal to the input. The .c returns the byte unchanged and drops the R4-R6 clears.

name: dptr_0900_plus_5e_times_xdata_byte
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA[DPTR], multiplies it by 0x5E, adds 0x04 to the low product byte, and forms DPTR from that byte with 0x09 plus the add's carry in DPH, so DPTR is 0x0900 or 0x0A00 plus it. The high byte of the product is discarded. The listing has no ret and runs up to 0xAD1E, where the next entry begins, so DPTR is still live state when that entry calls 0x0FAF. The .c reads these bytes as a four-byte XDATA read into R4:R7, which they do not do.

name: call_0faf_then_clear_r3
comment: Calls the routine at 0x0FAF, then clears A and stores 0 in R3. The listing has no ret and ends at 0xAD22, where the next entry begins at 0xAD23, so what this address is for is not determinable here. 0x0FAF is not decoded in this shard; the .c shows the same call followed by a second call that the listing does not contain.

name: load_r2_from_a
comment: One instruction, mov R2,A, with no ret; the listing ends at 0xAD23 and the next entry begins at 0xAD24, which copies A to R1 and R0, clears the carry and tail-jumps to 0x0F0E. Whether this is a separate entry or a function-boundary artefact is not determinable here. The .c renders it as a call the listing does not have.

name: copy_a_to_r0_r1_tail_jump_0f0e
comment: Copies A into R1 and R0 in turn, clears the carry, and tail-jumps to 0x0F0E rather than returning, so 0x0F0E's return is this entry's return. R2 was loaded from A by the single instruction listed separately at 0xAD23. 0x0F0E is not decoded here; the .c reports the two moves and drops the tail-jump.

name: read_xdata_07d1_into_a
comment: Loads DPTR with the XDATA address 0x07D1 and reads that byte into A. The listing has no ret and stops at 0xAD2D, where the next entry begins; that entry multiplies the byte left in A by 0x17 and builds a DPTR from it, so A is the input to the following computation. 0x07D1 is a byte in the PD image's own XDATA map and this listing says nothing about what it holds, so it is left unnamed.

name: dptr_0a39_plus_17_times_a
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by 0x17, adds 0x39 to the low product byte, and stores that byte in DPL with 0x0A plus the add's carry in DPH, so DPTR is 0x0A00 or 0x0B00 plus it. The high byte of the product is discarded and no address is dereferenced; on return A holds the DPH value. The .c renders the sequence as a comparison and loses the pointer.

name: set_dptr_07d0
comment: One instruction, mov DPTR,#0x07D0, with no ret; the listing ends at 0xAD3E and the next entry begins at 0xAD3F with the movx that reads the byte this pointer selects, so the two are halves of one sequence. The .c instead reads the byte here and multiplies it by 0x17, which is the work the next entry does. 0x07D0 is the PD image's own XDATA byte and is left unnamed here.

name: read_dptr_byte_then_dpl_17x_plus_31
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA[DPTR] into A and R3, multiplies A by 0x17, adds 0x31 to the low product byte and stores that in DPL, then computes A = 0x0A (the clr A has already cleared the carry) and returns. DPH is never stored, so this entry builds only the low byte of the pointer set up at 0xAD3C and leaves the high byte as the caller left it; A on return holds 0x0A. The .c reads the same bytes as a comparison and drops the R3 copy.

name: call_0faf_0f00_0dbc_return_0
comment: Calls 0x0FAF, then 0x0F00, then 0x0DBC in that order, clears A and returns 0. Nothing is read from or written to XDATA here and no register is set up beforehand, so the three callees see whatever the caller left. All three are outside this file pair and are not decoded in this shard; the .c shows the same three calls in the same order.

name: set_r3_ff_dptr_0a86_call_10e8
comment: Loads R3 with 0xFF, loads DPTR with the XDATA address 0x0A86 and calls 0x10E8. The listing ends at 0xAD60 with no ret, so execution continues at 0xAD60, which is not part of this export. The .c names the callee store_3byte_r3r2r1, but that routine's body is not in this file pair, its behaviour is not decoded here, and R2 and R1 are not set by these instructions.

name: dptr_08fb_plus_5e_times_a
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by 0x5E, adds 0xFB to the low product byte, and stores that byte in DPL with 0x08 plus the add's carry in DPH, so DPTR is 0x0800 or 0x0900 plus it. The high byte of the product is discarded and nothing is dereferenced; on return A holds the DPH value. The .c renders the sequence as a comparison and loses the pointer.

name: dptr_0a3d_plus_17_times_a
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by 0x17, adds 0x3D to the low product byte, and stores that byte in DPL with 0x0A plus the add's carry in DPH, so DPTR is 0x0A00 or 0x0B00 plus it. The high byte of the product is discarded and nothing is dereferenced; on return A holds the DPH value. The .c renders the sequence as a comparison and loses the pointer.

name: read_07d1_07d2_into_r7_r5
comment: Reads XDATA 0x07D1 into A and R7, increments DPTR to 0x07D2, reads that byte into A and R5, and returns, with A holding the 0x07D2 value. R6 and R4 are left as they were. The .c returns only the second byte and drops both register copies.

name: read_07d2_into_r7_r5_zero
comment: Loads DPTR with XDATA 0x07D2, reads that byte into A and R7, then clears A and R5, so R5 is left 0 whatever the byte held, and returns with A = 0. It is the single-byte form of the two-byte read at 0xAD83. The .c drops the read entirely and returns 0.

name: call_1041_then_return_07d1
comment: Calls 0x1041, then loads DPTR with the XDATA address 0x07D1, reads that byte into A and returns it. DPTR is reloaded after the call, so the pointer the callee used is not the one used for the read. 0x1041 is not decoded in this shard; the .c shows the same order.

name: read_07d1_into_r7_r5_zero
comment: Loads DPTR with XDATA 0x07D1, reads that byte into A and R7, then clears A and R5, so R5 is left 0 whatever the byte held, and returns with A = 0. It is the same shape as 0xAD8C, which does the same to 0x07D2. The .c drops the read entirely and returns 0.

name: call_0faf_then_test_r7_bit2
comment: Calls 0x0FAF, then takes R7 into A and masks it with 0x04, so the return value is 0x04 exactly when bit 2 of R7 is set and 0 otherwise. No XDATA is touched and the other bits of R7 do not affect the result. The .c shows the same mask but takes the input from a parameter rather than from R7 after the call.

name: copy_0809_to_080a_then_dispatch_0805
comment: Points DPTR at XDATA 0x0803 and calls 0x393D, then copies XDATA 0x0809 to 0x080A and points DPTR at 0x0806 for a call to 0x10C8. It zeroes the pair 0x080B/0x080C, then with DPTR = 0x0001 calls 0x0BC4, keeps the result in R6, calls 0x0BAB and keeps that in R5, masks R5 with 0x1F and writes the result to 0x080C, leaving 0x080B at 0. It then adds 2 to R1 (the clr A before the addc A,R2 clears the carry, so R2 comes back holding its own old value and R1's carry-out is dropped), reads XDATA 0x0805, calls 0x119C, loads R6 with 0x7A and tail-jumps to 0xA8AE. There is no ret; the .c renders that tail-jump as a call to a routine it names dispatch_code_table, whose body is not in this file pair, as is the case for every callee here (0x393D, 0x10C8, 0x0BC4, 0x0BAB, 0x119C).

name: write_07d1_then_call_chain
comment: Stores R7 into XDATA 0x07D1, calls 0xACE6, saves DPTR on the stack, calls 0x0FAF, sets R7 |= 0x01, copies R4 into A, restores DPTR and calls 0xAD94, keeping that result in R3; it then calls 0xACF6 and branches to 0xAED3 when the result is zero. The other path loads R7 = 0x03, pushes direct address 0x07 (R7 in register bank 0) and calls 0x104D with DPTR = 0x0A98; the 0xAED3 path instead calls 0xACE4, 0xADA4 and 0xAD09, and on a non-zero result from 0xAD09 repeats the same R7 = 3, push, DPTR = 0x0A98, 0x104D sequence, while a zero result calls 0x104D with DPTR = 0x0A98 and no push. All three exits are followed by three bytes the linear decode reads as NOP and then an ajmp, to 0xA8D0 on the two failure paths and to 0xA890 on the third, and every lcall 0x104D here is followed by the four bytes 00 00 00 01, so whether those belong to the call as inline arguments or are instructions is not settled by this listing. There is no ret, and the long tail through 0xF5D1, 0xFFE0, 0xFF80 and 0xEA67 in the .c is only reached by following that ajmp out of this entry, so it is not part of these bytes.

name: call_c1dd_store_r7_then_call_122f
comment: Calls 0xC1DD, then writes R7 to the XDATA byte at whatever DPTR holds at that moment (this listing does not say what that address is), then loads DPTR with 0xFFFE and calls 0x122F. There is no ret, so execution continues at 0xB07F, which is not part of this export. The .c reports the same three steps and adds a does-not-return warning on 0x122F that these bytes do not show.

name: load_a_with_03
comment: Two bytes, mov A,#0x03, with no ret; the listing ends at 0xB155 and the next entry begins at 0xB156 with mov DPTR,#0x083D. The .c attributes to this address a write of 3 to XDATA 0x083D and a call to 0x122F with DPTR = 0xFFFC, neither of which is in these two bytes (that is its reading of the entry that follows). What this instruction is for is not determinable here.

name: set_dptr_083d
comment: One instruction, mov DPTR,#0x083D, with no ret; the listing ends at 0xB158 and the next entry in the export begins at 0xB172, so the 0x1A bytes in between are not decoded here. The .c writes through that pointer and then calls 0x122F with DPTR = 0xFFFC, which this listing does not contain. Whether 0x083D is read or written after the pointer load is not determinable from this entry.

name: store_first_handoff_helper
comment: The other of the two handoff helpers that begins by storing: the file groups it with the 18 entry points carrying 1-3 sites each and records that all of those but this one begin movx a,@dptr. Its body is not decoded here and its exact site count is not stated

name: read_dptr_byte_to_r7_then_add_b0
comment: Reads the byte at XDATA[DPTR] into A and R7, then adds 0xB0 to that value in A. The listing has no ret and stops at 0xB175, where the next entry begins, so nothing in these bytes acts on the sum. The .c turns it into a comparison against 0x4F, but no compare or branch appears here; any use of the sum is outside this listing.

name: make_dptr_from_a_low_byte
comment: Copies the incoming A into DPL, then clears A (which also clears the carry) and rotates it left through carry, giving A = 0 and CY = 0, and stores that in DPH. DPTR therefore comes out as 0x00nn with nn the byte that was in A; the rlc contributes only the zero, and any carry the caller meant to propagate is lost at the clr A. The .c returns PSW bit 7, which is not what these instructions do.

name: write_dptr_byte_set_00bd_bit0_clear_ff62_bit3
comment: Writes A to the XDATA byte at the caller's DPTR, then reads XDATA 0x00BD, sets bit 0 and writes it back, then reads XDATA 0xFF62, clears bit 3 and writes it back, returning with A holding the 0xFF62 value. What either flag byte means is not decoded here. The .c draws the first store as a pointer parameter, which matches only because DPTR is the caller's.

name: set_dptr_0a00_plus_a
comment: Copies the incoming A into DPL, then computes A = 0x0A (the clr A has already cleared the carry, so the addc adds nothing) and stores it in DPH, giving DPTR = 0x0A00 + A. No address is dereferenced and any carry from the caller's own addition is discarded; on return A holds 0x0A. The .c returns PSW bit 7 instead.

name: read_xdata_0800_table_stride_77
comment: Multiplies the incoming A by 0x77, adds 0xD5 to the low product byte, and stores that byte in DPL with 0x08 plus the add's carry in DPH, so DPTR is 0x0800 or 0x0900 plus it; it then reads the byte at that XDATA address into A and returns. The high byte of the product is discarded, so only the low byte of the sum reaches the address. The .c builds a pointer from the caller's byte alone and loses the read.

name: unresolved_0xB1F2
comment: Unresolved: lcalls the 3-byte loader 0x10C8 with the DPTR it was given, sets A=1 and jumps to 0x0C46. The file says the remaining control flow was not traced and deliberately did not follow the second level, so this name records a handoff and nothing more

name: clear_r3_r2_r1
comment: Loads R3, R2 and R1 with 0x00 in turn and returns. R0 and R4-R7 are left as they were, so only three of the eight general registers are cleared, and A and B are untouched. The .c renders it as an empty void body.

name: read_xdata_at_r6r7_minus_3
comment: Takes the incoming A into R7, loads A from R6 and adds 0xFD, which is -3, together with whatever carry is in CY, then forms DPTR with DPL = R7 and DPH = that result. It reads the byte at that XDATA address into A, copies it to R4 and returns, so with the carry clear the address reached is three below the R6:R7 pair the caller passed. The .c drops the R4 copy and the intent of the subtraction.

name: load_r3_r0_jmp_0f0e
comment: Loads R3..R0 from A, clears carry and tail-jumps to 0x0F0E with no intervening RET. Its R3 clobber does not invalidate the writer's source because 0x4DD6 loads R3 again

name: broadcast_a_to_r0_r2_then_sub_r4_r7
comment: Copies the accumulator into R0, R1 and R2, clears the carry, and tail-jumps to 0x0F0E, which subtracts R4..R7 from R0..R3 byte by byte with subb and ORs the four difference bytes together, leaving the low difference in A and the borrow in CY. What the caller's registers hold, and what the caller does with A and CY, is not visible in this listing.

name: add_ab_then_r7_page
comment: Calls 0x10BC to add A x B to DPTR, loads R7 into A and falls into the 0xB267 page add; it writes no R7, which is what lets the index loaded at 0x4D8D survive to 0xB2AE

name: mul38_of_xdata_0832
comment: Loads XDATA[0x0832], multiplies by 0x38 and returns A = low8(product) with the high product in B, leaving DPTR at 0x0832; the file states it is not itself a pointer construction. Its index load is a fresh read, not a reuse of an earlier one

name: mov_a_from_r7
comment: One instruction: loads the accumulator from R7. There is no ret, so control falls straight through into B2A7, which writes that accumulator to XDATA at the incoming DPTR and then reads four bytes back from 0x07D8. It is a separate function only because the decompiler split that fall-through.

name: write_a_to_dptr_then_read4_from_07d8
comment: Writes the accumulator to XDATA at the incoming DPTR, then loads DPTR with 0x07D8 and tail-jumps to 0x0FAF, which reads four consecutive XDATA bytes from that address into R4, R5, R6 and R7 and returns DPTR one past the last. ec/annotations/registers.yaml lists 0x07D8 as MODE_TCC_OFFSET_DEFAULT but records PD-image sites as a different program's XDATA, so that name is not applied here.

name: mul38_ptr_0946
comment: Construction entry for the 0x38 multiply at 0xB2B1: returns P = 0x0946 + low8(A_entry x 0x38) in DPTR, discarding the product's high byte B but keeping the base carry in DPH, and writing no R0-R7 register

name: add_a_ptr_0946
comment: Independently entered add-only suffix of the 0x38 construction: returns P = 0x0946 + A_entry and executes no MUL. Counting it as running the multiply at 0xB2B1 would erase this separate entry that the census deliberately preserves

name: read3_from_07d5_into_r3_r1
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x07D5 and tail-jumps to 0x10C8, which reads three consecutive XDATA bytes into R3, R2 and R1 in that order (0x07D5, 0x07D6, 0x07D7) and returns with DPTR at 0x07D7. The decompiled C passes 0x07D5 as an argument instead of showing either the address load or the three MOVX reads; what 0x07D5 holds is not established here.

name: mul38_ptr_0976
comment: Same shape as 0xB2AE with base 0x0976: returns P = 0x0976 + low8(A_entry x 0x38) in DPTR. At index 5 it discards B=01 and does not produce the full-product address 0x0A8E

name: dptr_from_097c_plus_carry
comment: Forms a 16-bit pointer: DPL gets A+0x7C and DPH gets 0x09 plus the carry out of that add, so DPTR = 0x097C, or 0x097D when the low byte wrapped. Returns the computed DPH in the accumulator. The address formed is not dereferenced here, and the decompiled C reads the pair as a signed expression against 0x83 rather than as an address.

name: dptr_from_097d_plus_carry
comment: The same pointer construction as 0xB2E1 with base 0x097D instead of 0x097C: DPL gets A+0x7D, DPH gets 0x09 plus the carry, and the computed DPH is returned. The adjacent address is not written or read by these eight instructions, and nothing here says what 0x097D is for.

name: read3_from_dptr_then_set_dptr_0002
comment: Calls 0x10C8, which reads three consecutive XDATA bytes from the caller's DPTR into R3, R2 and R1, then overwrites DPTR with 0x0002 and returns. That new DPTR is not used again in this listing and what it is left pointing at is not established here. The decompiled C shows only the call, with neither the read nor the DPTR write.

name: read_0832_and_multiply_by_38
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0832, reads the byte there into A, multiplies it by 0x38, and returns with A holding the low product byte and B the high byte. R7 receives the byte read, and DPTR is left at 0x0832. No other register is written, so the product is a return value rather than a pointer; 0x0832 has no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: write_07d2_then_dispatch_on_07d1
comment: Stores R5 in XDATA 0x07D2 (the C names that store's source param_1; the instruction moves R5), then calls 0xACF4 with DPTR at 0x07D1. A nonzero accumulator from that call takes one path; a zero accumulator falls through to a second test on the byte at 0x07D2, and both paths index arrays at 0x08F6 and 0x08E8 by low8(XDATA[0x07D1] x 0x5E) and test ACC bits through jnb 0xe1, 0xe2 and 0xe3. Every exit returns 0 or 1 in R7. The decompiled C reads those three jnb bits as shifts of the XDATA byte just fetched; the disassembly addresses ACC, and which reading is right is not settled here.

name: write_r7_at_0d0d_then_load_0d0b
comment: Calls 0x717C, which loads DPTR with 0xFFFF and jumps into 0x122F; 0x122F adds 0x0D0E to DPTR with carry, so DPTR wraps to 0x0D0D on return and R7 is written to that XDATA address. DPTR is then reloaded with 0xFFFD and 0x7059 (a bare lcall to the same 0x122F) leaves it at 0x0D0B. There is no ret in the listing, so control continues past the last instruction rather than back to the caller.

name: write_r7_and_r3r2r1_to_0803
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x0803, increments DPTR to 0x0804, and calls 0x10E8, which stores R3, R2 and R1 at the three XDATA bytes starting at DPTR. So four bytes, 0x0803 through 0x0806, are written, the first from R7 and the remaining three from R3:R2:R1. There is no ret in the listing; the decompiler's does-not-return warning is this fall-through, not a proven non-returning call.

name: write_07d4_07d5_then_return_0_or_1
comment: Stores R5 in XDATA 0x07D5 and R7 in XDATA 0x07D4, calls 0x9740, and passes (R7 & 1) to 0x97E8. A nonzero result from that takes a short path that increments R5, calls 0xB074 with R2 = 0x11 and R3 = 0x94, and returns 1 or 0 from R7. The other path branches on the byte at 0x07D5; when it is nonzero the routine indexes 0x0A2D + low8(XDATA[0x07D4] x 0x17) through 0x0FAF, tests bit 2 of the fourth byte, and on a set bit calls 0xF739, 0x9772, 0x982F and 0x9793 with R3 = 0x64 and the carry set. Every exit returns 0 or 1 in R7; what the flag stands for is not established here.

name: branch_on_ram_r5_then_set_indirect_bits
comment: Copies the internal-RAM byte at fixed address 0x07 into R4 and the byte at fixed address 0x05 into R3 (opcodes 0xAC and 0xAD, mov Rn,direct), then branches on whether R3 equals 1. Both arms build indirect XDATA addresses through 0x9028, which forms DPTR as (R6 << 8) + A + 0xFFFD, and rewrite the bytes they land on: the R3 == 1 arm forces bits 0xF0 or 0x0F into the byte at field 5, calls 0x915E, then applies anl #0xdf / orl #0x02 or anl #0xfd / orl #0x20 to the next byte, writes the first result at field 6 and 0x03 at field 7; the other arm calls 0x915F, ORs 0x22 into the field-5 byte and rewrites the field-7 byte as anl #0xfe / orl #0x02. It ends by copying the internal-RAM byte at fixed address 0x04 into R7, calling 0x9106 with it, turning that call's result into 0 or 1 in R7, writing R4..R7 to XDATA 0x07DA-0x07DD, writing R3 to 0x07DE, and jumping to 0xF775.

name: write_07d6_07d7_07d8_07d9_then_store_07df
comment: Writes R5 to XDATA 0x07D6, R3 to 0x07D7, and 0 to both 0x07D8 and 0x07D9, leaving DPTR at 0x07DA. It then calls 0xACD3 with A = R7 and copies the byte that call leaves at DPTR into 0x07DA, sets R3:R2:R1 to 0x01, 0x07, 0xD9, loads DPTR with 0x07DF and calls 0x10E8, writing those three bytes to 0x07DF, 0x07E0 and 0x07E1. ec/annotations/registers.yaml lists 0x07D8-0x07DA as MODE_TCC_OFFSET_DEFAULTS but records PD-image sites as a different program's XDATA, so that name is not applied here.

name: forwarder_9926_985d_cfa0
comment: Calls 0x9926, then jumps to 0xC0DF, which calls 0x985D, sets R4 = 0xC0, and jumps to 0xC0EB; there 0xCFA0 is called and the function returns. The two sjmp instructions skip the bytes 0xC0B4-0xC0DE, so that block is not reached by this entry. Nothing about what the three callees do is visible in this listing.

name: store_0845_0847_then_return_ff_or_00
comment: Writes R4 to XDATA 0x0846, R5 to 0x0847 and R7 to 0x0845, then subtracts 1 from the accumulator; if the byte just stored was not zero there is no borrow and control jumps to the end, which loads R7 with 0xFF and returns. On the zero path it calls 0x9850, builds a 16-bit value in R1:R2 from the incoming R1:R2 plus 0x1B plus twice the byte at 0x0845, calls 0x0D0D, and ORs the two bytes read back from 0x0846/0x0847 into the results of 0x0D0D, 0x9909, 0x991A, 0x9888 and 0x0D38; if that OR chain comes out zero it also reaches 0xC19E and returns 0xFF, otherwise it writes through 0x98A4/0x9850, stores a byte at 0x0848, calls 0x987F and 0x98AD, and returns R7 = 0. The two return values, 0xFF and 0x00, are the only outputs.

name: call_0e54_with_dc_then_reenter_with_26
comment: Loads R0..R3 with 0, 0, 0, 0xDC and calls 0x0E54, then rebuilds R4..R7 by adding 0xED to R7 and 0xFF with carry to R6, R5 and R4, which is a 16-bit subtract of 0x13 from the value that call returned in R7 and R6. It then loads R0..R3 with 0, 0, 0, 0x26 and tail-jumps back into 0x0E54. The arithmetic 0x0E54 itself performs is not decoded here; this listing shows only the two constants 0xDC and 0x26 being passed and the 0x13 adjustment between the two calls.

name: set_dptr_0d0e_c1d6
comment: Two instructions: writes 0x0D into DPH and 0x0E into DPL, so DPTR is left holding 0x0D0E, and returns. The accumulator and every R register are untouched, so the function's entire effect is on DPTR. The decompiled C renders the body as empty, and nothing here says what 0x0D0E is subsequently used for.

name: load_dptr_fffe_into_0d0c
comment: Loads DPTR with 0xFFFE and calls 0x122F, which adds 0x0D0E to DPTR with carry: 0xFFFE + 0x0D0E wraps to 0x0D0C. 0x122F then stores the low byte into direct address 0x0E and, because the computed high byte equals 0x0D, returns on the path that leaves direct 0x0D and bit 0xAF alone. There is no ret of its own, so control continues past the lcall.

name: write_a_to_dptr_then_fall_into_c1f0
comment: A single instruction: stores the accumulator into XDATA at the incoming DPTR. There is no ret, so execution falls through into C1F0, which loads DPTR with 0xFFFF and jumps to 0x122F. The decompiled C's does-not-return warning is this fall-through, and its reading of the store as a write through a pointer parameter is not supported: MOVX @DPTR takes no pointer argument.

name: load_dptr_ffff_into_0d0d
comment: Loads DPTR with 0xFFFF and tail-jumps to 0x122F, which adds 0x0D0E with carry: 0xFFFF + 0x0D0E wraps to 0x0D0D, and 0x122F stores the low byte into direct 0x0E before returning on its high-byte-equals-0x0D path. There is no ret of its own, so control leaves through 0x122F.

name: cmp32be_0827_against_00001388
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x0827 and calls 0x0FCB, which reads four consecutive XDATA bytes into R0, R1, R2 and R3, then loads R4..R7 with 0x00, 0x00, 0x13 and 0x88, clears the carry and tail-jumps to 0x0F0E. 0x0F0E subtracts R4..R7 from R0..R3 byte by byte and ORs the four differences, so this is a 32-bit big-endian comparison of XDATA 0x0827-0x082A against 0x00001388, returning the low difference in A and the borrow in CY. The decompiled C drops both the constant and the XDATA address.

name: read_byte_at_ffdc_plus_a
comment: Forms a 16-bit address from the incoming accumulator: the low byte is A+0xDC and the high byte is 0xFF plus the carry out of that add, so the address is 0xFFDC + A modulo 0x10000. It loads that into DPTR and returns the byte found there in A. The decompiled C reads the same bytes as a signed offset from 0xDC; the high-byte immediate 0xFF is what fixes the base at 0xFFDC.

name: write_080d_then_branch_on_70e7
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x080D and tests R5: when R5 is zero it calls 0x104D, a computed jump through DPTR, with DPTR at 0x0815, and tail-jumps to 0xE1E0 with R5 = 0x55. Otherwise it calls 0x70E7 twice and takes one of four arms, each of which calls 0x104D the same way and then calls 0xE1E0 with R5 set to 0x66, 0x44, 0x77 or 0x88, followed by 0x700D or 0x7014 with R2 = 0xD6; one of those arms copies four bytes from XDATA 0x080F to 0x0815 through 0x0FAF and 0x1041. All arms converge on 0x718D and 0xF4AB before returning. The four bytes at 0xC2B6 (13 88 90 08) disassemble as instructions but read as inline data here and are not decoded; the decompiled C's P1 = param_1 rests on that reading.

name: write_07d0_then_run_indexed_state_chain
comment: Stores R7 in XDATA 0x07D0 and immediately uses that byte as an index: DPTR is built as 0x08F8 + low8(XDATA[0x07D0] x 0x5E), and when the byte there is zero 0x8A4A is called with R7 holding that value. It then calls 0xEE8B on 0x07D0, calls 0xB3ED when the result is 1, and after 0xF739, 0xAD75, 0xAD4D and 0xAD24 with R2 = 3 and R3 = 0xE8 either writes four bytes at 0x07D0 through 0x1041 or falls through to a second chain that calls 0xAD3C, 0x0FAF and 0xAD09 and, when bit 1 of the fourth byte read is set, calls 0xC398 and then 0xB311 and 0xD72E if 0xB311 returns 1. The routine has several exits and no single return value. ec/annotations/registers.yaml records the PD image's 0x07D0 as an index or state variable and says it establishes nothing about the EC's own 0x07D0.

name: set_r7_r5_from_iram_then_read_07d0
comment: Copies the internal-RAM byte at fixed address 0x03 into R7 (opcode 0xAF, mov R7,direct, which the Ghidra listing prints as mov R7,0x03), calls 0xF75C, then copies the internal-RAM byte at fixed address 0x07 into R5 (opcode 0xAD). It finishes by reading XDATA 0x07D0 and returning that byte in R7, with DPTR left at 0x07D0. The direct addresses are fixed, not indirect through R3, so the decompiled C's reading of the first assignment as the constant 3 is a coincidence of the same number appearing in the opcode's operand byte.

name: write_00b8_pattern_then_copy_ffc0_to_00d5
comment: Loads R1:R2 with 0x00B0, R3 = 1, R7 = 0x20, R6 = 0 and R5 = 0 and calls 0x128D, which in that mode reloads DPTR from R2:R1 and writes the accumulator 0x21 times, so 0x00B0 through 0x00D0 is cleared. It then writes the constants 0x88, 0x51, 0x04 and 0x8D to XDATA 0x00B8-0x00BB, and runs the pair 0xA742, 0xA75D, 0x0F32 (a left shift of R4..R7 by R0 bits) and 0x0EF3 (an OR of R4..R7 with R0..R3) three times, subtracting 0x30 from the 32-bit little-endian value in R4..R7 in the middle, and stores the result little-endian to 0x00B6-0x00B7. It finishes by copying XDATA 0xFFC0 and 0xFFC1 to 0x00D6 and 0x00D7 and XDATA 0xFFC2 to 0x00D5, then returns. What 0xFFC0-0xFFC2 are is not established here.

name: latch_07d2_07d3_then_zero_23_bytes
comment: Latches R7 and R5 into XDATA 0x07D2 and 0x07D3, then makes a fixed run of calls (0xAD67, 0xF668, 0xB73F, 0xE15A, 0xB9A1, 0xEE68), several of which re-read XDATA 0x07D2 into R7, followed by 0xAD8C feeding 0xD83D, 0xD013 and 0xF65E. It then computes 0x0A00 + (XDATA 0x07D2 * 0x17 + 0x2A) with MUL AB into R1:R2 and calls 0x128D with R3 = 1, R5 = 0, R6 = 0 and R7 = 0x17, whose loop stores 0x17 zero bytes at that address. It finishes by reloading DPTR with 0x07D2, calling 0xAD3F and moving the result into DPH, calling 0x104D, and jumping to 0xC0AF.

name: store_a_at_dptr_and_r7_at_0800_plus_a
comment: The listing is 15 bytes long and has no ret: it stores A to whatever XDATA address the caller left in DPTR, sets direct byte 0xA4 to 0xA4, forms DPTR as 0x0800 plus (A + 0x8B) with the carry into the high byte, stores R7 there, and ends on MOV A,R6. The decompile continues well past the end of this listing with writes to a 0x0834-indexed table and a call to 0xB19F that these bytes do not show.

name: compare_55_then_mark_0819
comment: The bytes 0xC819 to 0xC86F in this listing are the tail of the function before it, and the DJNZ at 0xC88F and the failure branch of the compare at 0xC886 both point back into them, so the two bodies overlap as one loop. Within 0xC873 it stores R7 at XDATA 0x0819, calls 0x119C with A = R5, and runs a carry/rotate sequence over R5, R0, @R1 and direct byte 0x77 (the listing renders opcode 0xC8 as XCH A,R0, which the 8051 encoding gives as XCH A,R5) ending in a compare of A against 0x55. On a match it stores 0x55 through @R1, calls 0x96FB, ORs 0x08 into XDATA 0x0819 and returns; the decompile's later writes to the 0x0834 * 0x77 table belong to the 0xC819 bytes, not to this function.

name: dispatch_on_r3_then_add_product_to_0699
comment: Stores R7, R5 and R3 into XDATA 0x0814, 0x0815 and 0x0816, then dispatches on R3 by adding 0xFB and 0xFA to it: R3 = 1 first adds XDATA 0x0814 * 0x67 to a DPTR of 0x0675, R3 = 5 jumps past that, and R3 = 0x0B calls 0xDCC7 instead, the 1 and 5 paths then calling 0x9D39 and falling into a call to 0x9C1B. If XDATA 0x0815 is zero it also calls 0x9CFB first. Every path ends at a call to 0x9C1B with DPTR = 0x0699, B = 0x67 and A = XDATA 0x0814, and the listing has no ret of its own.

name: store_0803_0805_then_jump_c808
comment: Stores R7 into XDATA 0x0803, R5 into XDATA 0x0804 and 0 into XDATA 0x0805, and returns immediately if R3 is 0x0D. Otherwise it re-reads XDATA 0x0803 into R1, calls 0x34EF with that byte, then 0x349B, 0x38D3 and 0x11C2, exchanges the last result with R3, ANDs it with R5, and jumps to 0xC808.

name: call_122f_with_dptr_fffd_cc36
comment: Sets DPTR = 0xFFFD and calls 0x122F, and the listing ends there: this body has no ret of its own and touches nothing else. The decompile's warning that the subroutine does not return is not supported by these two instructions - 0x122F's own listing ends in a RET.

name: store_0a94_0a97_then_add_0a94_times_60
comment: Stores R5, R2, R3 and R7 into XDATA 0x0A95, 0x0A96, 0x0A97 and 0x0A94, reads four bytes from XDATA 0x0A98 into R4:R7 with 0x0FAF, and calls 0x3883, which sets B = 0x60 and DPTR = 0x0400, then 0x10BC, which adds A * B to DPTR with A = the byte stored at 0x0A94. The listing ends on that call with no ret of its own, so the address left in DPTR is the only result these bytes show.

name: store_4_at_07d6_then_branch_on_991a
comment: Stores R4:R7 as four bytes at XDATA 0x07D6, calls 0x9850 and then 0x991A, and branches on A | B being non-zero. The non-zero side re-reads the four bytes at 0x07D6, calls 0x0F1F with R0 = 0x18, 0x9958 with A = 0 and 0x0C58 with R7 = XDATA 0x07DA and then with the smaller of XDATA 0x07DA and 0x10, before running through 0xF598, the byte at XDATA 0x07DB, 0x995F, 0x984D with R7 = 0xA1, 0x9958, 0x9849, 0x10FD and 0x0BC4, and returning R7 = 1; the zero side goes straight to 0x9850, 0x995F with A = 0 and 0xEEAE with R7 = 0xA0, returning 0. Both sides finish at 0xEEAE.

name: latch_07d4_07d5_and_call_7014_with_63_or_6c
comment: Latches R7 and R5 into XDATA 0x07D4 and XDATA 0x07D5; on R5 == 1 it calls 0x714F, reads four bytes at the saved DPTR into R4:R7, sets bit 1 of the R7 byte, calls 0x7063 with A = R4 and that byte, then sets bit 0 of the byte at DPTR and calls 0x7014 with R1 = 0x63, R2 = 0xD6 and R3 = 0xFF. The other path clears those same two bits and calls 0x7014 with R1 = 0x6C instead, and passes A = 9 rather than 8 to 0x718D. Both paths then call 0xF4AB, read XDATA 0x07D4 through 0x6FAD, and only if that comes back zero read XDATA 0x07D5 into R5 and call 0xBBE7.

name: decrement_00e2_and_tail_jump_to_d07b
comment: Reads XDATA 0x00E2, subtracts one with the carry preset and returns the result in A as soon as it does not borrow, that is whenever the byte was 1 or more. When the byte was 0 it reads a 16-bit value into R6:B through 0x0CF7 with DPTR = 0x0AE3, returns R6 unchanged if that value is below 100, and otherwise zeroes XDATA 0x0AE3 and XDATA 0x0AE4, calls 0xB159 with DPTR = 0x07D0 and A = 6, calls 0x104D and jumps to 0xD07B. That target is not an instruction boundary in 0xD013's listing - it is the second byte of the JNZ at 0xD07A - so the byte executed there is 0x08 (INC R0) before the MOV DPTR,#0x07D5, the read, LCALL 0xBBE7 and RET tail.

name: require_nonzero_from_b074
comment: Latches R7 into XDATA 0x07D6 and then makes up to three calls to 0xB074, returning R7 = 1 only if every call it makes comes back non-zero and R7 = 0 at the first zero. When R5 == 1 the argument pairs R2, R3, R5 are 0x11, 0x94, 0 and then 0x15, 0x7C, 1, both with R7 = XDATA 0x07D6, and the second is skipped if the first returns zero. Otherwise it calls 0x9740 and then, if R6 & 0x40, makes the single call 0x11, 0x94, 1, or if that bit is clear calls 0x97D5 and then 0x06, 0x07, 1 with R7 = XDATA 0x07D6.

name: inc_r0_then_reti
comment: The whole listing is INC R0 followed by RETI: no register, no memory location and no branch is touched, and RETI pops a return address and the PSW high byte rather than the single return address an LCALL pushed, so this is not a body that returns through an ordinary call. What the two bytes are for, or whether they are code at all, is not shown here.

name: return_one_when_arg_matches_queried_values
comment: Copies the caller's R7 into R6, zeroes R7, reads XDATA at 0x01 + (R7 - 3) * 0x100 - the byte read is never tested - and branches on direct bit 0xE0. When that bit is clear it calls 0xB21E with A = 9, keeps the top nibble of the result and returns 1 if that nibble is zero while the low nibble of R4 is not, or if the nibble is non-zero while the low nibble of R4 is 0. When the bit is set it calls 0xB21E with A = 8 and returns 1 only if the result is 0x31 or R4 is 1, 0x10 or 0x13; every other path sets R7 = 0 and returns, so the decompile's subtraction results are not values these instructions produce.

name: store_4_zero_bytes_at_0904_plus_0809_times_5e
comment: Latches R7, R4 and R5 into XDATA 0x0809, 0x080A and 0x080B, then compares the pair R5:R4 against 0x7C15 by subtraction with the carry preset. When it is not below that value the function re-reads XDATA 0x080A and XDATA 0x080B into R4 and R5, calls 0x06B1 with A = 0, then 0x05A6 with R0 = 0x3F, R1 = 0x4C, R2 = 0xCC, R3 = 0xCD, and 0x06EA; otherwise, if either of those two bytes is non-zero, R6 and R7 become 0x11 and 0x94. Both paths finish by zeroing R4 and R5, forming DPTR from XDATA 0x0809 * 0x5E plus 4 with the carry added to 0x09, and calling 0x1041, which stores the four zero bytes there.

name: copy_0841_to_0984_when_083c_matches_097f
comment: Stores R7 into XDATA 0x083C, reads the four bytes at XDATA 0x083D into R4:R7 and, if either of the last two is non-zero, re-reads them and calls 0xC0EF with R4 = 0x06, R5 = 0x07 and R7 = XDATA 0x083C. It then reads XDATA 0x097F into R7 and compares R7 with XDATA 0x083C - opcode 0xB5 is CJNE direct,A,rel, so the direct byte is R7 and the branch is taken only when the two are equal, which is what the decompile's comparison of 0x083C with R7 also concludes - and only then loads the four bytes at XDATA 0x0980, ANDs them with the four at XDATA 0x083D through 0x0FCB and 0x0EE6, and, if any of the four results is non-zero, sets XDATA 0x097E to 0x01 and copies four bytes from XDATA 0x0841 to XDATA 0x0984 with 0x0FAF and 0x1041.

name: poll_0208_0209_then_spin
comment: Calls 0xF7B2, 0xEBBB and 0xF7B3, then loops: XDATA 0x0208 is cleared and 0xF79F called when it is non-zero, XDATA 0x0209 is cleared and 0xE543 followed by 0xF79C called when it is 0x0A or more, 0xE902 is called with the difference and then 0xF7B7, and the loop repeats while XDATA 0x0AE8 is zero. 0xF79C is a two-byte LJMP to 0xD085 and 0xF79F an LJMP to 0x4402, which is what the decompile means by its two thunks. When XDATA 0x0AE8 becomes non-zero the function calls 0xE2E4 and returns to the top of the loop unless R7 is non-zero; when R7 is non-zero it writes 0xAA to XDATA 0x00BE, clears bit 6 of XDATA 0xFFD3, calls 0x3FEA with R1 = 0x77, R2 = 0xF2 and R3 = 0xFF, and then spins on a jump to itself. The decompile's param_1 exit test has no counterpart here, because the loop back to 0xDA4D is unconditional.

name: mov_dptr_07cf_and_call_10e8
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x07CF and calls 0x10E8, and the listing ends there: this body has no ret of its own and writes nothing itself. The decompile renders the call as a three-byte store with the constant 1999, which is 0x07CF, but no store appears in these bytes.

name: loop_c901_per_index_0x07d0
comment: Stores R7 into XDATA 0x07CF, calls 0x128D with R1 = 0x61, R2 = 0x06, R3 = 0x01, R5 = 0, R6 = 0x01 and R7 = 0x67, and clears XDATA 0x07D0. It then loops while XDATA 0x07D0 is below XDATA 0x07CF, calling 0xC901 twice per pass - first with R3 = 1, R5 = 0 and R7 = 0, then with R7 = XDATA 0x07D0, R3 = 0x0B and R5 = 1 - and setting bit 0 of the byte at XDATA 0x0666 through 0x9C18 before incrementing the counter. The exit leaves the difference XDATA 0x07D0 minus XDATA 0x07CF in A, which is the return value.

name: call_122f_with_dptr_fffe
comment: Sets DPTR = 0xFFFE and calls 0x122F, and the listing ends there: this body has no ret of its own and touches nothing else. As at 0xCC36, the decompile's warning that the subroutine does not return is not supported by the two instructions shown.

name: store_then_clear_0817_and_add_r6_times_0x67
comment: Stores R7 into XDATA 0x0817, calls 0x9C45, then writes 0 over XDATA 0x0817 again. It finishes by setting B = 0x67, taking A from R6, loading DPTR = 0x069B and calling 0x9C4D, which the listing shows as a jump into 0x10BC. There is no ret of its own, so what executes after that call is not shown here.

name: loop_256_passes_over_07cf
comment: Clears XDATA 0x07CF, calls 0x128D with R1 = 0xE3, R2 = 0x08, R3 = 0x01, R5 = 0, R6 = 0 and R7 = 0x5E, and clears XDATA 0x08F8. Its loop then calls 0x70F8 with DPTR = 0x07CF, writes 0x02 over XDATA 0x07CF, calls 0xF28D, calls 0x70D7 with the same DPTR and stores R4:R7 there with 0x1041, and when 0x6FAF returns zero calls 0xE8D4 with the direct byte 0x03 in R7. It increments XDATA 0x07CF and repeats until that byte reads zero again, i.e. 256 passes, which is what the listing's compare-with-1-and-carry loop does rather than the decompile's sign test.

name: store_0x14_at_0810_and_write_0000
comment: Calls 0xC1F0, then 0xC1EF with A = R7, then 0xC1D6 with R4, R5 and R6 zero and R7 = 0x14, advances DPTR twice, and calls 0x0FCB, 0x0DC9 and 0xC1D6 again. It writes R7 (0x14) at the address 0xC1D6 leaves and, if the next byte there is zero, re-selects an address with 0xC1D6, clamps that byte to 0x3F, ORs in bits 6 and 7 of 0xC23A's result, and writes the byte to XDATA 0x0000. The listing ends by loading DPTR = 0x0006 and jumping to 0x122F, which has a RET of its own, so unlike the decompile's warning this path does return.

name: init_sequence_then_ljmp_128d
comment: Sets bit 6 of XDATA 0xFFD3, calls 0xC62B and 0xF2FB, clears bit 0 of XDATA 0xFF88, sets bit 4 of XDATA 0xFFD5, then calls 0xDF6A, 0xDB89 with R1 = 0x80, R2 = 0x00 and R3 = 0x01, 0xEED1 with A = 0, 0xC755 with R5 = 1 and R7 = 0, and 0xDBD9 with R7 = 1. It never returns: the last act is a jump to 0x128D with R1 = 0xE5, R2 = 0x0A, R3 = 0x01, R5 = 0xFF, R6 = 0x00 and R7 = 0x01, which on the R3 = 1 path of 0x128D writes the single byte 0xFF at DPTR = 0x0AE5. It is called from 0xEBBB, which 0xDA44 calls before entering its poll loop.

name: set_0832_through_5874_58ab_ed46_56cb
comment: Latches R7 into XDATA 0x0832, sets R6 = 0 and R7 = 0x77, pushes those two registers across a call to 0x5874 with R5 = 0, then calls 0x128D and 0x584A with DPTR = 0x0832. It pushes R2 and R1 across 0x58AB, re-reads XDATA 0x0832 into R7, restores R1 and R2 and calls 0xED46, then calls 0x567C and 0x56CB with A = 1 and ORs 0x04 into the result before storing it back to XDATA 0x0832.
