So the byte left at XDATA 0x0832 is 0x56CB's return value with bit 2 forced on; what the intermediate calls contribute is not visible from these bytes alone.

name: copy_0815_to_081b_then_call_c873
comment: Copies the caller's R7 into R1 and, when R5 is 0x99, calls 0x6FC5 with A = R1, clears bit 1 of the byte that call selects, then computes DPTR as 0x0800 plus (R1 * 0x5E + 0xE6) with the carry into the high byte and sets bit 5 of that byte. It then calls 0x6FAF with A = R1 and returns unless that comes back zero, in which case it copies four bytes from XDATA 0x0815 to XDATA 0x081B with 0x0FAF and 0x1041, restores R7 and R5 from the stack, and calls 0xC873. The decompile's signed -0x67 is the same test on R5, read as 0x99.

name: poll_d78a_for_indices_0_and_1
comment: Runs R2 from 0 up to 1; on each pass it sets R7 to R2 - opcode 0xAF is MOV Rn,direct and direct 0x02 is R2, which the listing prints as MOV R7,0x02 - and calls 0xD78A, and if R7 comes back non-zero it adds R2 * 0x60 to a DPTR it sets to XDATA 0x0424 through 0x10BC. The loop therefore makes exactly two calls to 0xD78A, with R7 = 0 and then 1, and returns with R7 = 1.

name: dptr_fffe_then_122f_at_e323
comment: Six bytes, no return of its own: MOV DPTR,#0xFFFE then LCALL 0x122F. Nothing at this address reads or writes memory, and the call at 0xE326 returns to 0xE329, which is outside this listing, so what the caller eventually sees depends on bytes this file does not show. The C body's "WARNING: Subroutine does not return" is Ghidra's annotation on the call, not a property of these two instructions.

name: store_07d8_and_dispatch_07da
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x07D8; if R7 was zero it then read-modify-writes XDATA 0xFFD5 twice, first ORing in bit 0 and then bit 5. It finishes by loading DPTR with 0x07DA and calling 0x104D, and the four NOPs the .asm shows at 0xE470-0xE473 are the argument bytes that call consumes. The .c's while(true) loop, its P1_0 test and its chain of calls to 0xC7E5/0x56A0/0x5842/0x57EB/0x567B/0xA210 are Ghidra's reading of those argument bytes, not of decoded instructions: the .asm shows NOP, RR A and a DJNZ R0 whose target 0xE46F lands inside the preceding three-byte LCALL. Only the trailing MOV R5,#1 / LJMP 0xD435 at 0xE490 reads as code past the dispatch.

name: dptr_fffe_then_122f_at_e4d0
comment: Six bytes, no return of its own: MOV DPTR,#0xFFFE then LCALL 0x122F, byte-for-byte the same two instructions as 0xE323. The call at 0xE4D3 returns to 0xE4D6, outside this listing, so the fall-through destination is not shown here. What the shared DPTR value of 0xFFFE selects is not decoded further.

name: count_07cf_and_conditional_call_122d
comment: Clears XDATA 0x07CF, writing zero to it twice at the same address, then loops: read 0x07CF into R7, exit at 0xE551 once it is nonzero, and otherwise call 0xB1E3, OR its result into the byte at XDATA 0x07D0 (reached by the INC DPTR at 0xE558) and, if that OR is nonzero, call 0xB217 and then 0x122D with DPH taken from a second 0xB1E3 result and DPL from XDATA 0x07D0. Each pass increments 0x07CF at 0xE576, so on its own the loop body runs exactly once. registers.yaml records 0x07D0 here as belonging to the PD image's own XDATA, not to the EC's 0x07D0 of the same number, so no EC-side name applies to these accesses.

name: store_080e_and_accumulate_r6
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x080E, calls 0xF755 and discards its return, then builds R6 as the rotate-left-by-3 of R7 masked with 0xF8. It re-reads 0x080E into R7, calls 0x70BB, loads that call's A into DPH, reads the byte at the resulting DPTR into R5 and sets R6 to (that byte doubled) OR the rotated value. It then pushes the direct byte of R6, calls 0xF75C, pops that byte back into A, and sets R6 to the popped value ORed with the byte 0xF75C returns in R7. It ends by calling 0x6FAD with DPTR=0x080E and, only if that returns zero, setting R5=0x06 and calling 0xE877; the DPTR values the helpers leave are not shown in this listing.

name: store_080f_0810_and_pick_f50e_arg_on_carry
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x080F and R5 to XDATA 0x0810, the following byte, and keeps the 0x080F value in both R5 and R6. It calls 0x9028 with A=0x67, then read-modify-writes the byte at the DPTR that call leaves: OR in bit 2, then clear bit 3, in a single accumulate. It then calls 0x90D6 with the saved 0x080F byte and selects R5=3 if that call left the carry flag set and R5=2 if it cleared it, then calls 0xF50E and returns. The .c takes the branch from a local variable initialised to zero and applies the bit 2/bit 3 edit to 0x080F itself, neither of which the .asm shows.

name: store_3byte_r3r2r1_at_0803
comment: Two instructions: MOV DPTR,#0x0803 then LCALL 0x10E8, which the C body already names store_3byte_r3r2r1 and which writes R3, R2 and R1 to consecutive bytes from DPTR. This address itself moves no data and has no return of its own. Nothing here indicates what R1-R3 hold on entry.

name: reset_07c9_block_then_flag_00d3_1
comment: Twenty-nine instructions and no `mov DPTR` into 0xFF00-0xFFFF: this routine writes only the 0x07C9 block and the 0x00D3 flag, and the two runs of `inc DPTR` off 0x07C9 and 0x00D4 are what put 0x07CA-0x07CC and 0x00D5 in the census. It zeroes 0x07C9 and 0x07CA, writes 1 to 0x07CB, and only if XDATA 0x0945 is non-zero reads 0x07CA into R7 with R5 = 0 and calls 0xF63F. It then writes 0x00D4 = 0, 0x00D5 = 0x2E and 0x00D3 = 1, and returns. It shares pd-001 with the 0xFFxx addresses only through the 0x07C9 block, not through a 0xFFxx access of its own -- which is why it is one of the two `FUN_CODE_` entries the census could not classify by reading it. The only `lcall 0xea67` in the committed `.asm` tree is A8AE!A8ED, and `AE9C.c` shows a call to it as well: that one sits on the `lcall 0x104D` inline-argument idiom findings.md 3b records as defeating linear framing, so it is a decompiler reading rather than a second call site. What 0x07C9-0x07CC and 0x00D3-0x00D5 hold is not established here, and 0x07CC's status vocabulary is issue #32's.

name: init_sequence_with_ea_cleared
comment: Clears the global interrupt enable at bit address 0xAF, sets the interrupt-priority register at direct address 0xB8 to zero, and zeroes XDATA 0xFFDF and 0xFF42. It then read-modify-writes XDATA 0xFF4A to set bit 0 and calls six routines in order: 0xF6FB, 0xF6F3, 0xEFB9, 0xF781, 0xDFFA and 0xC62B. It sets bit 0xAF again and returns, so the whole call sequence runs with interrupts disabled. The roles of the six callees are not resolved here.

name: pick_00d0_or_00d1_then_tail_with_dp_0002
comment: Calls 0x9ACD and branches on the byte at the DPTR it leaves: if that byte is zero it stores the following byte to XDATA 0x00D0, and if it is nonzero it calls 0x9ADD and stores that call's following byte to XDATA 0x00D1 instead. It then makes an unconditional third call to 0x9ADD and, if the following byte of that one is nonzero, writes 0 to XDATA 0x00D2. The function ends by loading DPTR=0x0002 and tail-jumping to 0x122F, with no return of its own. The .c models the pointer as a parameter and gates 0x00D2 on the value just written to 0x00D0 or 0x00D1, which is a third, separate call in the .asm.

name: set_or_clear_bits_0_5_via_9028
comment: Sets R4=0x07 and branches on R5 being exactly 1. Both arms load R6 with 0x07 and call 0x9028 with A=0x1E, then modify the byte at the DPTR that call leaves: the R5==1 arm ORs in bit 0 and then bit 5, and every other R5 value ANDs out bit 0 and then bit 5. Each arm returns immediately after its two read-modify-writes, with no common tail, and the address behind 0x9028 is not shown in this listing. The .c writes through a parameter pointer, which the .asm does not have.

name: set_or_clear_bits_1_2_6_via_9028
comment: Same shape as 0xEC36, differing only in the bits: R4=0x07, R6=0x07, a call to 0x9028 with A=0x1E, and then bit 1 and bit 2 ORed in when R5==1, or cleared with masks 0xF9 and 0xBF otherwise. Each arm returns without a common tail, and the address 0x9028 leaves in DPTR is not in this listing.

name: store_3byte_r3r2r1_at_0861
comment: Two instructions: MOV DPTR,#0x0861 then LCALL 0x10E8, the routine the C body names store_3byte_r3r2r1 and which writes R3, R2 and R1 to consecutive bytes from DPTR. This address itself moves no data and has no return of its own. The 0x0861 block is not described further here.

name: set_bit3_and_bits2_3_from_r5
comment: Sets R4=0x07 and branches on R5 being exactly 1: the true arm calls 0x90C0 and ORs bit 3 into the byte at the DPTR it returns, the false arm calls the same helper and clears bit 3 there. Both arms then call 0x9023, clear bits 2 and 3 of the byte at that DPTR with mask 0xF3, and write back (R5 & 3) << 2 ORed with the cleared byte, so R5's low two bits become the new bit 2-3 field. The addresses the two helpers return are not in this listing, and the .c applies both edits to the same parameter pointer, which the .asm does not do.

name: setup_04a3_r3_7_then_call_10bc
comment: Sets R3=0x07 and DPTR=0x04A3, calls 0x9A1B, and passes A=R3=0x07 to 0x998F, then 0x99D4, then 0x9A91 again with A=R3. The last instruction is LCALL 0x10BC, which the C body names add_full_product_to_dptr and which adds A*B to DPTR, so this address neither returns nor supplies B itself. The .c passes BANK0_R7 to 0x998F and 0x9A91 where the .asm passes the constant 0x07, and it omits the DPTR=0x04A3 load entirely.

name: stage_07d4_07d5_then_call_ef59
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x07D4 and, via one INC DPTR, R5 to XDATA 0x07D5, then calls 0xEF79. It reads 0x07D5 back and uses it only as the branch condition: on 1 it reloads R7 from XDATA 0x07D4 and sets R5=1, otherwise it reloads the same R7 and sets R5=0. It then calls 0xEF59 with that register pair and returns. The .c passes the comparison result to 0xEF59 as an argument, which is what the two register loads amount to but is not how the value is produced here.

name: write_r7_at_0x0260_plus_0bab_result
comment: Loads R3=0x01, R2=0x02 and R1=0xFF and calls 0x0BAB; if the returned byte is 0x9F it calls 0x0C46 with A cleared. It then calls 0x0BAB again with the same registers and forms DPTR by adding 0x60 to the returned byte into DPL and adding 0x02 plus the carry into DPH, so the destination is 0x0260 plus that byte and can reach the next 0x100 page. R7 is written there, A is set to 0x01 and control tail-jumps to 0x0BF1. The .c's `CONCAT11(...,bVar2+0x60)` reads the same address but its carry expression is the decompiler's noise.

name: write_ff_clear_bit7_write_ff
comment: Loads R5=0x07, R6=0x07 and R7=0x00, then makes three separate helper calls and writes through each of the DPTRs they leave. 0xF3EB called with A=0x0F gives a pointer that is filled with 0xFF; 0xF3E2 called with A=0x15 gives a pointer whose byte is masked with 0x7F, clearing bit 7; 0xF3E0 called with A=0x00 gives a third pointer that is also filled with 0xFF, after which the function returns. The three addresses behind those helpers are not in this listing. The .c collapses all three onto one parameter pointer.

name: stage_07d6_call_715e_6faf_tail_e5b3
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x07D6, calls 0x715E, and then writes R5 to the byte at the DPTR that call left rather than reloading 0x07D6 first. It calls 0x6FAF with A=R7; only when that returns zero does it reload XDATA 0x07D6 into R7 and call 0xED90. Either way it finishes by reloading 0x07D6 into R7 and tail-jumping to 0xE5B3, so there is no return instruction here. The .c's assumption that the R5 write lands on 0x07D6 depends on 0x715E preserving DPTR, which this listing does not show.

name: stage_07d6_call_716c_6faf_tail_e5b3
comment: Structurally identical to 0xEF59, with 0x716C in place of 0x715E and 0xCBB0 in place of 0xED90: write R7 to XDATA 0x07D6, call 0x716C, write R5 at the DPTR that call left, and gate a single call on 0x6FAF(A=R7) returning zero. Both arms end by reloading 0x07D6 into R7 and tail-jumping to 0xE5B3. The .c's claim that the R5 write lands on 0x07D6 depends on 0x716C preserving DPTR, which this listing does not show.

name: clear_0ffd3_ff88_ffe1_bits_then_ffd0_2e
comment: Nineteen instructions, all of it read-modify-write on the 0xFFxx window, and the one function in pd-001 besides A8AE and C62B that names a 0xFFxx address as a `mov DPTR` operand: it clears bit 4 of 0xFFD3, writes 0x2E to 0xFFD0 and 0 to 0xFFD1 (that one by `inc DPTR`, so no `mov DPTR` names it), clears bit 7 of 0xFF88 and clears bit 3 of 0xFFE1, then returns. Three of the bits it clears are the same bits A8AE tests, which is what ties the two together in the cluster. It is called once in the tree, from EBBB!EBD5, inside the init sequence that runs with the global interrupt enable cleared. The roles of the five addresses and of the constants 0x2E and 0xEF/0x7F/0xF7 are not established here.

name: stage_07d6_chain_tail_f351
comment: Writes R7 to XDATA 0x07D6, calls 0x7021 and then 0x7182, reloads 0x07D6 into R7 and calls 0xF126. It then reloads 0x07D6, passes it in A to 0x7140, takes the byte 0x7140 leaves at @DPTR into R7 and tail-jumps to 0xF351, so this address has no return of its own. The .c's argument order for the final call matches, but it shows no return value being taken from 0x7140, which the MOVX at 0xF04F does.

name: set_or_clear_bit0_via_9028
comment: Branches on R5 being zero. Both arms set R6=R7, clear A, add 0x04 and call 0x9028; the R5==0 arm then ORs bit 0 into the byte at the DPTR that call returns, and the R5!=0 arm clears bit 0 with mask 0xFE. Each arm returns immediately, so the two are independent. The address behind 0x9028 is not in this listing, and the file carries a caveat that the function boundary came from a call-target byte scan and so this may not be the whole function.

name: gate_on_6f96_then_tail_122f_with_dp_000a
comment: Calls 0x6F96 and skips the whole body if it returns nonzero. When it returns zero the function calls 0x7108, 0x7045, 0x7108, 0x7045, 0x7108 and finally 0xCC36, in that order, with no register or memory setup between the pairs. Both paths then load DPTR=0x000A and tail-jump to 0x122F, so there is no return of this address's own. The .c drops the DPTR load, and the file carries a caveat that the boundary came from a call-target byte scan and may not cover the whole function.

name: read_04a3_then_call_9a90
comment: Loads DPTR with 0x04A3, calls 0x9987, reads the byte at that address into R6, then calls 0x9A90 and 0x998B. The listing ends at that third call with no RET, so what follows is not shown here; the C's warning that 0x9A90 does not return is not settled by these instructions.

name: write_07d6_then_table_entry_then_0_3
comment: Stores the R7 byte at XDATA 0x07D6, then calls 0xF3CC with R4 = 0 and R5 = 0x7F, which stores 0x00 then 0x7F at 0x08EF + the low byte of R7 x 0x5E. It reloads DPTR with 0x07D6, calls 0x70A3, then overwrites 0x07D6 with 0x00 and 0x07D7 with 0x03, so the caller's value at 0x07D6 does not survive the call.

name: dptr_eaf9_index_04
comment: Computes a table address from R7: A is doubled twice (R7 x 4 in byte arithmetic), 0xF9 is added for DPL and 0xEA plus the carry forms DPH, giving 0xEAF9 + 4 x R7 wrapping inside 16 bits. It hands that DPTR to 0x0FBB, then returns R6 with bit 1 set. What 0x0FBB does with the pointer is not decoded here.

name: write_ffda_ffdb_10_ffd8_48_ff40_bit1
comment: Writes 0x10 to XDATA 0xFFDA and to 0xFFDB, reads 0xFF40, ORs 0x02 into it and writes it back, then writes 0x48 to XDATA 0xFFD8. Three fixed XDATA bytes and one bit set, with no other location read and no branch; what these bytes are is not decoded here.

name: gate_6f96_then_ljmp_122f
comment: Calls 0x6F96 and, only when it returns zero, calls 0x705C, increments the DPTR that 0x705C left, calls 0x10C8 and then 0xF723. Either way it sets DPTR to 0x0004 and ends with ljmp 0x122F, so this routine has no RET of its own and reaches 0x122F with DPTR = 0x0004.

name: store_r4r5_at_08ef_index_5e
comment: Multiplies R7 by 0x5E with MUL AB, adds 0xEF to the low product byte for DPL and 0x08 plus the carry for DPH, giving 0x08EF + low8(R7 x 0x5E); the high product byte left in B is discarded. It then stores R4 at that address and R5 at the next byte up, leaving DPTR on the second byte written.

name: unresolved_0xF3E0
comment: One instruction, ADD A,#0x0D, and no RET. The entry is a fragment of a longer straight-line block: the adjacent entry 0xF3E2 begins with MOV R7,A and the two run together to the RET at 0xF3EA, so on its own this address does not show what A holds on entry or what the sum is used for.

name: dptr_high_r6_low_a
comment: Loads R7 with the incoming A, computes R6 + 0xFD + carry into DPH and puts the saved A into DPL, building DPTR = (R6 + 0xFD + C):A with no memory access. R7 is clobbered, which is the only behavioural difference from the same sequence at 0xF3EB; the carry this consumes is whatever the caller left set.

name: dptr_high_r6_low_r3
comment: The same DPTR construction as 0xF3E2 -- DPH = R6 + 0xFD + carry, DPL = the incoming A -- but it parks the low byte in R3 instead of R7, so it clobbers R3 where 0xF3E2 clobbers R7. No read or write, and it consumes the incoming carry as-is.

name: zero_084c_call_8814_821b
comment: PUSH 0x03 saves R3, A is cleared, XDATA 0x084C is written with 0x00, and R3, R2 and R1 are each set to 0 before 0x8814 is called with A and R1-R3 all zero. POP 0x03 restores the caller's R3 and 0x821B is called before the RET; the value 0x8814 returns in A is not used here.

name: write_07d6_then_set_1
comment: Stores R7 at XDATA 0x07D6, calls 0xABBF, reloads DPTR with 0x07D6, reads the byte back and passes it in A to 0x96ED, then writes 0x01 over 0x07D6. Whatever 0xABBF left in 0x07D6 is what 0x96ED is handed; nothing here says what either call does with it.

name: call_0180_if_00e2_is_1
comment: Reads XDATA 0x00E2 and returns immediately unless it equals exactly 0x01. On that one value it reads XDATA 0x0300 into R5, clears R7 and calls 0x0180 with A = 0. Any other value of 0x00E2, including values with other bits set alongside, does nothing.

name: store_4bytes_to_0a82
comment: Writes R7, R5, R2 and R3 in that order to XDATA 0x0A82 through 0x0A85, one byte each, then sets R7 to 0x01 and returns. The .c pairs these four bytes with its parameters in the opposite order to the registers the listing stores, so the register names are used here. The .asm notes this boundary came from a call-target byte scan, so it may not be the whole routine.

name: call_70c7_with_0_then_5c_tail_f55c
comment: With DPTR loaded from 0x07D6 it calls 0x70C7 with A = 0, then again with A = 0x5C, reads the byte at the DPTR 0x70C7 left into R5, and ends with ljmp 0xF55C -- there is no RET here. 0x70C7 is outside this listing, so whether it writes through 0x07D6 or only moves DPTR is not determined by these instructions.

name: return_1_if_dptr_byte_ge_02
comment: Passes A (from R7) to 0x350B, reads the byte at the DPTR that call left, clears the carry, subtracts 0x02 and branches on the borrow: no carry, i.e. the byte is 0x02 or greater, returns R7 = 1, otherwise R7 = 0. The decompiled C returns the same expression from both branches and so loses this distinction.

name: set_bits_6_7_from_r5
comment: Calls 0x9021, reads the byte at the DPTR it leaves and keeps its low six bits in R3, then takes R5 through SWAP and two RLCs and masks with 0xC0, which places the low two bits of R5 into bits 7 and 6 -- the carry entering the first RLC only reaches bit 0 and is masked away. The byte is written back with those two bits replaced and the low six preserved.

name: write_r5_then_f763_if_6faf_zero
comment: Calls 0x70C8, stores R5 at the DPTR it leaves, then calls 0x6FAF with A = R7 and, if that returns zero, calls 0xF763 before the RET. DPTR is not set in this listing before the 0x70C8 call, so the address written depends on what that routine leaves there.

name: return_1_if_acc_bits_2_3_set
comment: Calls 0x7121 and tests bit address 0xE3 (ACC.3) and then 0xE2 (ACC.2) of the byte it returns in A. Both set returns R7 = 1, either one clear returns R7 = 0, and the other six bits of A are not examined.

name: set_00bd_bit1_clear_ff42_bit7
comment: Reads XDATA 0x00BD, ORs 0x02 into it and writes it back, then reads XDATA 0xFF42, clears bit 7 with AND #0x7F and writes it back. Both writes are unconditional and no other location is touched; what either byte is, is not decoded here.

name: return_1_if_56f1_byte_zero
comment: Passes A (from R7) to 0x56F1, reads the byte at the DPTR that call left, and returns R7 = 1 if that byte is zero and R7 = 0 if it is not. The decompiled C drops the comparison entirely and shows only the call, so the boolean this actually returns does not appear in the C at all.

name: set_ff42_bit7_if_00bd_zero
comment: Reads XDATA 0x00BD and returns without writing if it is not zero. Only when 0x00BD is zero does it read XDATA 0xFF42, OR in 0x80 and write the byte back, so this and 0xF598 touch the same pair of bytes from opposite conditions.

name: call_e458_then_r4r5r6r7_03120100
comment: Calls 0xE458 and then loads R7 = 0x00, R6 = 0x01, R5 = 0x12 and R4 = 0x03 before returning, with no memory access of its own and DPTR left as 0xE458 left it. Those four registers are the only output; what they mean and what 0xE458 does are not decoded here.

name: store_r7r5r3_to_080d
comment: Writes R7, then R5, then R3 to XDATA 0x080D, 0x080E and 0x080F, incrementing DPTR between stores, and returns with DPTR on 0x080F. Three single-byte stores, no read and no comparison; the .c maps its parameters to these three bytes in a different order than the registers the listing stores.

name: store_r7r5_0_to_07d2_if_6faf_zero
comment: Calls 0x6FAF with A = R7; a nonzero return goes straight to the RET with R7 cleared to 0 and nothing written. On a zero return it stores R7 at XDATA 0x07D2, R5 at 0x07D3 and 0x00 at 0x07D4, leaving DPTR on 0x07D4. The .c pairs these bytes with its parameters in the opposite order to the registers the listing stores.

name: store_r7_to_07cc_r5_to_0945
comment: Writes the whole R7 byte to XDATA 0x07CC and the whole R5 byte to XDATA 0x0945, then returns with no read and no comparison and DPTR left on 0x0945. registers.yaml names 0x07CC USB_C_POWER_PRIORITY (bit 7) but records that every reference to it sits in this PD image and its status as present-untested, so that name is that file's hypothesis, and this is a full-byte write rather than a bit-7 write; 0x0945 is not documented.

name: call_f109_if_6faf_zero
comment: Calls 0x6FAF with A = R7 and returns immediately if it returns nonzero; on a zero return it calls 0xF109 and then returns. The same three-instruction shape as 0xF65E, 0xF668 and 0xF672, which call 0xEC5E, 0xEC36 and 0xF610 from the same position.

name: call_ec5e_if_6faf_zero
comment: Calls 0x6FAF with A = R7 and returns immediately if it returns nonzero; on a zero return it calls 0xEC5E and then returns. Identical in shape to 0xF654, 0xF668 and 0xF672, which call 0xF109, 0xEC36 and 0xF610 from the same position.

name: call_ec36_if_6faf_zero
comment: Calls 0x6FAF with A = R7 and returns immediately if it returns nonzero; on a zero return it calls 0xEC36 and then returns. Identical in shape to 0xF654, 0xF65E and 0xF672, which call 0xF109, 0xEC5E and 0xF610 from the same position.

name: call_f610_if_6faf_zero
comment: Calls 0x6FAF with A = R7 and returns immediately if it returns nonzero; on a zero return it calls 0xF610, which in this same set stores R7, R5 and R3 to XDATA 0x080D, 0x080E and 0x080F, and then returns. Identical in shape to 0xF654, 0xF65E and 0xF668, which call 0xF109, 0xEC5E and 0xEC36 from the same position.

name: clear_ffc6_bit5
comment: Loads DPTR with 0xFFC6, reads that byte, clears bit 5 (0x20) with ANL A,#0xDF and writes it back. It is a read-modify-write of a single bit and nothing else: no other address is touched and no call is made. The meaning of that bit in this program's XDATA is not decoded here.

name: set_ffc6_bit2
comment: Loads DPTR with 0xFFC6, reads that byte, sets bit 2 (0x04) with ORL A,#0x04 and writes it back. It is a read-modify-write of a single bit, the same one-byte read-modify-write shape as the neighbouring bit-clear at 0xF6F3 but on a different bit. The meaning of that bit is not decoded here.

name: chain_96ff_then_0c46
comment: Loads A from R7, calls 0x96FF, reads the XDATA byte at whatever DPTR that call left, then tail-jumps to 0x0C46 with the byte in A. The ljmp means it never returns to its own caller. Neither 0x96FF nor 0x0C46 is decoded here, so the address read and what 0x0C46 does with A are not determinable from this listing.

name: call_returns_with_dptr_loaded
comment: Called immediately before seven of the eight 0x07D0 sites that decode with no movx in the window - those sites are lcall 0xF739 ; mov dptr,#0x07d0 ; ret - so this file describes it only as returning with DPTR left pointing at the byte. Its body is not decoded here

name: read_dptr_byte_via_715e
comment: Loads A from R7, calls 0x715E, then reads the XDATA byte at the DPTR that call left, puts it in R7 and returns. The read is the only access this function makes; the address read is whatever 0x715E computes, and 0x715E is not decoded here.

name: read_dptr_byte_via_716c
comment: Loads A from R7, calls 0x716C, then reads the XDATA byte at the DPTR that call left, puts it in R7 and returns. Identical in shape to the byte-at-0xF755 reader but through a different callee (0x716C instead of 0x715E); that callee is not decoded here.

name: store_r5_at_dptr_via_97fb
comment: Calls 0x97FB, then writes R5 to the XDATA byte at the DPTR that call left and returns. The store is the only access this function makes; the address written is whatever 0x97FB computes, and 0x97FB is not decoded here.

name: clear_sfr_88_set_sfr_a8
comment: Two bit operations and a return: clears bit address 0x88 and sets bit address 0xA8 in the bit-addressable space, with no read first. The decompiler renders the pair as IT0 = 0 and EX0 = 1, but the listing only gives the raw bit addresses 0x88 and 0xA8, and the SFR names for this image are not independently confirmed here.

name: tailcall_7b14_with_r7_zero

name: seed_07d3_gfid_and_08xx_defaults
comment: Masks XDATA 0x073C with 0x06 and sets bit 0 of it, sets bit 1 of 0x1605, bit 6 of 0x1607 and bit 4 of 0x1603, runs the counted Timer 1 delay at 0x0EA2 with R7 = 200 and then with R7 = 5, and writes 0x40 to 0x1646 -- then picks XDATA 0x07D3's GFID field from two bits: bit 2 of 0x1666 and bit 4 of 0x166A select one of 0x30, 0x40, 0x50 or 0x70, i.e. GFID = 3, 4, 5 or 7. All four stores write the whole byte, so the low nibble is zero on each of them. It goes on to set or clear bit 4 of 0x07A4 from bit 6 of 0x1665, write 0x00/0x10/0x23/0x25 into 0x083A/0x083B/0x08B8/0x08B9, set bit 3 of 0x0832 and bits 6-7 of 0x0456, and clear bit 1 of 0x0782. 0x1665, 0x1666 and 0x166A have no entry in ec/annotations/registers.yaml, and the DSDT names the 0x07D3 field GFID (dsdt.dsl:52254-52256) without expanding it, so what the four values select is not established here.

name: reset_xdata_flags_and_07d5_to_ff
comment: A whole-machine reset pass. It copies a short CODE run into internal RAM 0xB7/0xB8 and back, sets bit 4 of 0x075E, calls the 0x074C nibble router, clears bit 2 of 0x0741 and later bit 7, then masks a long list of single bits across 0x07C5, 0x07C6, 0x07A6, 0x0741, 0x073C, 0x045A, 0x072D, 0x0471, 0x0442 and 0x0456; zeroes 96 bytes from 0x0F00 to 0x0FAF; zeroes 0x0787 and 0x0786; clears bits 1 and 0 of 0x0743; clears bit 5 of 0x07C5; sets 0x0788 and 0x07D5 to 0xFF; and ends with R7 = 0xE1 and a tail jump to 0x83D6. There is no ret in this listing, so how control comes back is not shown here, and the function boundary is a call-target byte scan -- an upper bound (ec/annotations/bank-call-audit.md 1). 0x07D5 is the DSDT's DBAP, which the ASL publishes as DBAP * 8 to NPCF.AMAT; 0xFF as its reset value is a reading of these surroundings, not a decode of what the value means. Of the addresses named, 0x07C6, 0x07A6, 0x0741, 0x0743, 0x0786 and 0x045A have entries in ec/annotations/registers.yaml and 0x07C5, 0x075E, 0x0787, 0x0788, 0x0F00, 0x073C, 0x072D, 0x0471, 0x0442 and 0x074C do not.

name: compute_level_blocks_086b_086c_086e
comment: Three near-identical blocks in one 627-byte body, one per profile, each writing its own result byte. Block one (0x9DA0-0x9E88) seeds 0x0865-0x0869 all from 0x08C0, then overrides 0x0866 from 0x0783, 0x0867 from 0x0872, 0x0868 from 0x0873 and 0x0869 from 0x0874 when the source is non-zero; it calls 0xBBF2 (0x0865 minus 0x0866) and 0xBD34 and 0xBD3D (the result byte minus 0x0867 and minus 0x0868), each of which returns its difference with the borrow in CY, and stores the smaller of the running result and the 0x0869 cap into 0x086B. It then clamps 0x086B three times -- to 0x23, 0x14 and 0x0F -- each clamp guarded by bit 7 of 0x0751 together with a different pairing of bits 1 and 0 of 0x07C6. Block two (0x9E89-0x9FA2) repeats it from 0x08C1 with overrides 0x0784, 0x087A, 0x087B, 0x087C, and the same three clamps routed through 0xBC7B and 0xBC7E instead of inline, storing the result in 0x086C; its third clamp reads and writes 0x0A47, which is then compared against 0x09EF and, on a change, passed to 0xA73F with R7=0xBC. Block three (0x9FA3-0xA00D) repeats it a third time from 0x08C3 with overrides 0x0785, 0x088A, 0x088B, storing into 0x086E with NO clamp at all -- it is the same fold and stops at the ret. 0x0865-0x0869 are therefore a working set reused by all three blocks, and 0x086B, 0x086C and 0x086E are the three results. Nothing here fixes the units of any of the six, so none is named; what the EC does with the three results is a live question. The three clamp constants and MANUAL_FAN_CTRL are named in ec/annotations/registers.yaml.

name: seed_0872_087a_088a_then_select_level
comment: Clears bit 3 of 0x0723 and bit 1 of 0x0985, calls 0x94D0 with R7=1 (the copy_code_table_into_0730_07a7 the other block also calls with 1), and then seeds the three per-profile override sources in one run: 0x08C0 into 0x0872, 0x08C1 into 0x087A and 0x08C3 into 0x088A. It clears 0x080C and takes one of several early exits -- bit 0 of 0x0490 set, or 0xB9D8 (read_06e6_xor_01) returning zero, both go to the 0xA04A block that calls 0xBC85, writes 0x64 to 0x08AF, clears bit 1 of 0x0983 and returns; bit 5 of 0x0476 with 0x0398 equal to 0xA5 clears 0x080C and 0x081D instead. Past those, the balance of the body compares a 16-bit value from 0x0608 against thresholds 0x44, 0xB1, 0x75, 0xEB and 0xE0 and the byte 0x2E, calling 0xB9C6, 0xBEF0 and 0xBEC8 and 0xBED2 along the way, and several of those arms tail-call select_code_table_entry_and_store_0872_087a_088a -- the code table that actually fills the three override bytes. This listing does not contain that routine's body, so the arm is recorded as a call and not decoded further. What the 0x08xx seeds are in any unit is not determined here. This is part of the same mechanism as the block computation at 0x9D9B, which reads the bytes this one seeds, but it writes 0x0872/0x087A/0x088A and not the 0x086x results themselves.

name: stage_0862_0865_into_1c12_1c14
comment: Three stores and two reads, 21 bytes, no branching: it stores the accumulator to 0x1C14, copies 0x0862 to 0x1C13 and 0x0865 to 0x1C12, and returns. The accumulator is the caller's; nothing here computes it. Same shape as the routine at 0xD304 one call site away, which stages the same two source bytes into 0x1C36-0x1C38 instead -- so the selector byte and the level byte reach two separate destinations, one per case-table handler. What reads either trio downstream is not established by this listing.

name: stage_0862_0865_into_1c36_1c38
comment: Three stores and two reads, 21 bytes, no branching: it stores the accumulator to 0x1C38, copies 0x0862 to 0x1C37 and 0x0865 to 0x1C36, and returns. Byte-for-byte the same shape as the routine at 0xD2EF, with every destination differing by 0x24, and it is called from the case-0x36/0x37/0x38/0x39 handlers at 0xD239 and 0xD25F where 0xD2EF is not. What reads this trio downstream is not established by this listing.
